61.s: Which of the following pairs correctly states the number of subjects in the Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules, respectively?
61.x: The Eleventh Schedule contains 29 subjects relating to Panchayats, while the Twelfth Schedule contains 18 subjects relating to municipalities.
61.tq: Keep the Panchayat and municipal Schedule counts in their constitutional order.
xs: The **Eleventh Schedule** has **29** subjects (panchayats) and the **Twelfth Schedule** **18** (municipalities) — option **(2)**: 29 and 18.
Option (1) reverses them — the classic trap.
xa: **Neither Schedule transfers anything by itself**; Art. **243G/243W** say the State "**may**" devolve.
Panchayat taxing powers: **243H**; municipal equivalent: **243X**.
The 3Fs: **Functions**, **Funds**, **Functionaries**.

61.s: Which one of the following best describes the standard condition of 3F devolution in practice?
o: Staff are answerable to local bodies, while functions and funds are retained by the Union.
Functions, funds and functionaries are fully transferred to local bodies in an untied form.
Funds are untied, but functions remain exclusively with State departments.
Functions are devolved on paper, funds arrive tied to schemes, and staff report to State line departments.
61.x: The standard finding is that functions exist on paper, funds are commonly tied to schemes, and functionaries continue to report to State line departments.
61.tq: Compare the formal position with the operational reality across all three Fs.
xs: In practice, **functions are devolved on paper**, **funds arrive tied to schemes**, and **staff report to State line departments** — option **(4)**.
The ideal — **untied** funds and staff answerable to the local body — is what is missing, so option (2) is wrong.
xa: Result: PRIs are **reduced to implementing agencies**.
ULBs **depend on tied grants**; own revenue only **~0.3% of GDP**.
**Roadmap for Panchayati Raj** lists weak 3F devolution, **bureaucratic control**, **tied funds**, **dependence on grants**, **reluctance to tax**.

61.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a reason for the underperformance of Panchayati Raj Institutions in the government's Roadmap for Panchayati Raj?
o: Weak devolution of the three Fs
61.x: The Roadmap identifies weak 3F devolution, bureaucratic control, tied funds, dependence on grants and reluctance to tax. Complete financial autonomy is not listed and contradicts the identified constraints.
61.tq: Find the option that reverses the diagnosed weakness instead of merely naming one.
xs: **Complete financial autonomy** is NOT a reason — panchayats actually **depend on grants** — option **(1)**.
The **Roadmap** lists: **weak 3F devolution**, **bureaucratic control**, **tied funds**, **dependence on grants**, **reluctance to tax**.
xa: ULB own revenue is only **~0.3% of GDP**.
Funds **arrive tied** to schemes; staff report to **State line departments**.

61.s: The constitutional planning bodies intended to integrate plans at the district and metropolitan levels are, respectively:
o: DPC under Article 243ZD and MPC under Article 243ZE
MPC under Article 243ZD and DPC under Article 243ZE
DPC under Article 243G and MPC under Article 243W
DPC under Article 280 and MPC under Article 281
61.x: The District Planning Committee is provided under Article 243ZD, while the Metropolitan Planning Committee is provided under Article 243ZE.
61.tq: Match the planning body, territorial level and Article number in sequence.
xs: **DPC under Article 243ZD** (district) and **MPC under Article 243ZE** (metropolitan) — option **(1)** is correct; both exist for **integration of plans**.
Option 2 swaps them; **243G/243W** cover devolution of functions, not planning committees.
xa: **243K / 243ZA**: **SEC** for panchayats / municipalities.
**243E/243U**: **5-year term**; elections within **6 months** of dissolution.
**243D**: women's reservation floor of **one-third**.

61.s: Which constitutional arrangement ended the practice of postponing local elections at will?
o: Appointment of Special Officers for every local body
Elections held at the discretion of the State Government
A three-year term renewable by the State Government
A five-year term, with elections before expiry or within six months of dissolution, under the SEC
61.x: The five-year term with elections before expiry or within six months of dissolution, conducted by the State Election Commission, made local government a permanent institution after 1993.
xa: Term: **243E** (panchayats) / **243U** (municipalities); SEC: **243K** / **243ZA**.
**Special Officers** run AP local bodies whose terms lapsed.
16th FC grants go only to **properly constituted** local bodies.

61.s: Article 243D sets a constitutional floor for the reservation of seats for women in Panchayats. Andhra Pradesh, like many other States, reserves:
61.x: Article 243D guarantees at least one-third of seats for women, but many States, Andhra Pradesh included, give 50%. One-third is only the constitutional minimum; 40% and 25% are not the AP figure.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** reserves **50 per cent of the seats** for women — option **(3)**.
**One-third** is only the constitutional floor under **Art. 243D**; many States give **50%**.
xa: Proxy problem: "**sarpanch pati**"; it **falls markedly in a second term**.
AP Cabinet (**18 Aug 2026**): **34%** BC reservation rural, **33⅓%** urban.

61.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about constitutional devolution to local bodies?
o: The Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules transfer subjects automatically without legislative action
These Articles say the State Legislature 'may' devolve powers and responsibilities
61.x: The Schedules do not transfer subjects automatically; Articles 243G and 243W use the discretionary 'may'.
xa: Likewise **243H/243X** (taxing powers) use "**may**".
This discretion is the **root cause** of weak devolution.
**DPC (243ZD)** and **MPC (243ZE)** are meant to **integrate plans**.

61.s: Which one of the following is the single most important source of own revenue for Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)?
61.x: Property tax is the main own-source revenue of ULBs, although it remains under-assessed and under-collected.
61.tq: Directly identify the principal own-source revenue item.
xs: **Property tax** is the **single most important own revenue** of ULBs — option **(3)**.
It is **under-assessed** and **under-collected**, and property registers are **outdated**.
xa: ULB own revenue is only **~0.3% of GDP**.
**GST** cost ULBs ~**19%** of own revenue (**octroi**, **entry tax**).
**SVAMITVA** gives a **property-tax baseline** for rural homes.

61.s:
With reference to the finances of Urban Local Bodies, consider the following statements:
1. Their own-source revenue is only about 0.3% of GDP.
2. Cities produce about 67% of GDP.
3. Cities receive more than half of the country’s tax revenue.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
61.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because cities receive less than 1% of tax revenue, despite producing about two-thirds of GDP.
61.tq: Find the reversed comparison in the revenue-share statement.
xs: Statement 1 correct: ULB own revenue is only **~0.3% of GDP**.
Statement 2 correct: cities produce **~2/3 (about 67%) of GDP**.
Statement 3 wrong: cities get **<1%** of tax revenue. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: **GST** cost ULBs ~**19%** of own revenue (octroi, entry tax).
ULBs **depend on tied grants**; property registers outdated.
**Weak balance sheets** keep most bodies out of the bond market.

61.s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission grants for 2026–31, the urban share increased from 36% to:
61.x: The urban share rises to 45%, with grants split 80% basic and 20% performance.
xa: 16th FC (**2026-31**): rural **₹4.4 lakh crore**, urban **₹3.6 lakh crore** (~**₹75,000 crore** a year).
15th FC urban: about **₹1.2-1.3 lakh crore** (about **0.12-0.13%** of GDP).
Grant conditions: **properly constituted** LBs, **audited accounts**, **timely SFCs**.

61.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: State Election Commissioner – Removed like a High Court Judge
Chief Election Commissioner – Removed like a High Court Judge
State Election Commissioner – Appointed by the President
Elections to Municipalities – Conducted by the Election Commission of India
61.x: Under Article 243K the State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and removable only like a High Court Judge; the CEC is removed like a Supreme Court Judge.
xa: **243K** for panchayats; **243ZA** for municipalities.
SEC + **5-year term** + **6-month rule** made local government **permanent**.
**Before 1993**, States postponed local polls at will.

61.s: In debates on local devolution, Janmabhoomi committees and secretariats are criticised as:
o: Constitutional planning bodies integrating local plans
Parallel bodies weakening the centrality of PRIs
61.x: The criticism is that PRIs act mainly as implementing agencies, while parallel bodies such as Janmabhoomi committees and secretariats reduce their centrality.
xa: Other parallel bodies: **DRDAs**, **SHGs**, **MPLADS/MLA LADS**, **parastatals/SPVs**.
**DPC (243ZD)** and **MPC (243ZE)** are meant for **integration of plans**.

61.s: Which of the following is identified as an arrangement that bypasses elected local bodies?
61.x: DRDAs, user groups, SHGs and MPLADS/MLA LADS bypass elected local bodies; DPCs and MPCs are constitutional planning bodies.
xa: Under **MPLADS/MLA LADS**, **legislators pick the works**.
**Parastatals** and **SPVs** also bypass elected bodies and citizen participation.
The proposed **District Development Council** was criticised as a **parallel executive**.

61.s: Village and ward secretariats and volunteers were introduced in Andhra Pradesh in:
61.x: They were introduced in 2019, after the Janmabhoomi committees of 2014-19; both were criticised as parallel to gram panchayats and wards.
xa: When terms lapse, AP local bodies are run by **Special Officers**.
AP gives **50%** women's reservation (Art. **243D** floor is **one-third**).
AP was showing a **local-body poll push** with **direct Mayor elections**.

61.s:
With reference to MPLADS, consider the following statements:
1. The Member of Parliament recommends works, which the Implementing District Authority executes.
2. RTI applies to works under the scheme.
3. The Member of Parliament executes the works directly.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
61.x: Under MPLADS the MP only recommends works and the Implementing District Authority executes them; RTI applies and eSAKSHI is the associated portal.
xa: MPLADS/MLA LADS are criticised as bypassing PRIs because **legislators pick the works**.
Other parallel bodies: **DRDAs**, user groups, **SHGs**, **parastatals/SPVs**.

61.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated condition associated with the Sixteenth Finance Commission’s local-body grants?
o: Timely constitution of State Finance Commissions
Permanent appointment of Special Officers in place of elected bodies
61.x: The conditions include properly constituted local bodies, published audited accounts and timely State Finance Commissions. Permanent replacement of elected bodies by Special Officers is not a condition.
61.tq: Find the institutional arrangement that contradicts the grant conditions.
xs: **Permanent Special Officers** is NOT a condition — option **(4)**; the 16th FC wants **properly constituted** (elected) bodies.
The conditions are: **properly constituted local bodies**, **audited accounts published**, **timely SFCs**.
xa: Problem: **SFC reports** are often **ignored**.
This is why AP is **rushing polls** — **₹12,150 crore** at stake.
16th FC: **80% basic / 20% performance**; urban share **45%**.

61.s: Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA), begun in 2018-19, strengthens Panchayati Raj Institutions mainly for achieving:
61.x: RGSA aims to strengthen PRIs so that they can contribute to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals.
xa: Focus on **117 aspirational districts** + convergence with **Mission Antyodaya**.
**Revamped RGSA: 1 April 2022 – 31 March 2026**, co-terminus with the **XV FC**.
**BRGF** was merged into RGSA (APPSC-GS **2018**).

61.s: The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet decision of 18 August 2026 provided ____ reservation for Backward Classes in rural local bodies.
61.x: It provided 34% BC reservation in rural local bodies and 33⅓% in urban local bodies, with direct election of Mayors and chairpersons.
xa: ⚠ BC reservation **34%** rural vs **33⅓%** urban — do not swap.
AP **Mandal and Zilla Parishads** were due by **23 Sep 2026**.
AP gives **50%** reservation for women.

61.s:
Assertion (A): Delayed local-body elections can jeopardise the flow of Central grants to local bodies.
Reason (R): The Sixteenth Finance Commission links grants with properly constituted local bodies, audited accounts and timely State Finance Commissions.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
61.x: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the grant conditions explain why failure to constitute elected local bodies and related institutions can put Central funds at risk.
61.tq: Test whether the financial consequence is directly explained by the stated grant conditions.
xs: **Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
R is true: the **16th FC** ties grants to **properly constituted** local bodies, **published audited accounts** and **timely SFCs**.
A follows from R: delayed polls put grants at risk — that is why AP is **rushing polls**, with **₹12,150 crore** at risk if not done by **October**.
xa: AP **Mandal and Zilla Parishads** were due by **23 Sep 2026**; **Special Officers** in charge.
AP Cabinet (**18 Aug 2026**) also approved **direct election** of Mayors and municipal chairpersons.
Problem: **SFC reports** are often **ignored**.

61.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about proxy representation of elected women in Panchayats?
o: 'Sarpanch pati' refers to a male relative exercising power in the elected woman's name
Proxy behaviour falls markedly in a second term
Online trolling and intimidation are other problems faced by women leaders
Proxy behaviour increases markedly when the woman enters a second term
61.x: Proxy behaviour falls markedly, not increases, when the woman representative enters a second term.
xa: Responses: **capacity building**, **Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan**, **Model Women-Friendly GPs**.
**Sushil Kumar** committee (report **2025**) recommended **exemplary penalties** in proven proxy cases.

61.s: Which measure is identified as a response to proxy participation by male relatives in women-led Panchayats?
o: Conducting Panchayat meetings without elected representatives
Appointing Special Officers to run Panchayats
Exemplary penalties in proven proxy cases
61.x: Capacity building of elected women and exemplary penalties in proven proxy cases were identified as responses.
xa: The penalties came from the **MoPR advisory committee** chaired by **Sushil Kumar** (report **2025**).
Proxy behaviour **falls markedly in a second term**.
Other responses: **Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan**, **Model Women-Friendly GPs**.

61.s: The Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan is aimed at:
o: Strengthening participation of elected women representatives
61.x: Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan and Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats strengthen participation of elected women representatives.
xa: **Capacity building** is the third response listed.
Constitutional floor **one-third** (**243D**); AP gives **50%**.

61.s: Which programme was merged into the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan?
61.x: The Backward Regions Grant Fund (BRGF) was merged into RGSA (APPSC-GS 2018). RGSA converges with Mission Antyodaya rather than absorbing it; SVAMITVA and MPLADS are separate schemes.
61.tq: Use the programme-merger relationship to distinguish RGSA from associated initiatives.
xs: The **Backward Regions Grant Fund (BRGF)** was **merged into RGSA** — option **(2)** (APPSC-GS **2018**).
RGSA only **converges with Mission Antyodaya**; **SVAMITVA** and **MPLADS** are separate.
xa: RGSA covers **non-Part IX** areas too.
Focus on **117 aspirational districts**.

61.s: The funding pattern under RGSA is correctly represented by which one of the following?
o: Centre:State is 40:60, with 90:10 for Union Territories
Centre:State is 75:25, with no separate pattern for Union Territories
Centre:State is 60:40, 90:10 for North-Eastern and hilly States, and 100% Central funding for Union Territories
61.x: The normal Centre-State ratio is 60:40; it is 90:10 for North-Eastern and hilly States, while Union Territories receive 100% Central funding.
61.tq: Separate the normal ratio from the special ratios for difficult terrain and Union Territories.
xs: RGSA funding: **Centre:State 60:40** for general States, **90:10 for North-Eastern and hilly States**, **100% Central** for **Union Territories** — option **(4)** is correct.
The other options give ratios (50:50, 40:60, 75:25) that are not the RGSA pattern.
xa: RGSA aims to strengthen **PRIs** to achieve the **SDGs**.
Revamped RGSA runs **1 April 2022 – 31 March 2026**, co-terminus with the **XV Finance Commission**.
FY25: **35 lakh+** trained; **Training of Trainers** on **own-source revenue**.

61.s: The revamped RGSA is co-terminus with which period?
o: The Fifteenth Finance Commission period, from 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026
The Fourteenth Finance Commission period, from 2015 to 2020
The Sixteenth Finance Commission period, from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2027
The Fifteenth Finance Commission period, from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2026
61.x: The revamped RGSA runs from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2026 and matches the period of the Fifteenth Finance Commission. The 1 April 2021 starting date is incorrect.
61.tq: Discriminate between the close starting dates 1 April 2021 and 1 April 2022.
xs: The **revamped RGSA** runs **1 April 2022 – 31 March 2026**, co-terminus with the **Fifteenth Finance Commission** — option **(4)**.
⚠ "**1 April 2021** to 31 March 2026" (option 1) is the known wrong date (UPSC **2026** trap).
xa: Phase 1 of RGSA launched **2018-19**.
**BRGF** was merged into RGSA.

61.s: Which one of the following correctly describes eGramSwaraj?
o: It provides only online auditing of Panchayat accounts.
It executes works recommended under MPLADS.
It combines Panchayat planning, accounting and reporting.
It prepares property records for rural homes.
61.x: eGramSwaraj integrates Panchayat planning, accounting and reporting. Online auditing is the specific function of AuditOnline, while property records are associated with SVAMITVA.
61.tq: Distinguish the complementary digital platforms by their precise functions.
xs: **eGramSwaraj** integrates panchayat **planning, accounting and reporting** — option **(3)**.
**Online audit** is **AuditOnline**; property records come from **SVAMITVA**.
xa: eGramSwaraj was launched with SVAMITVA on **24 April 2020**.
**SVAMITVA** is implemented by the **Survey of India**.

61.s: A major concern about State Finance Commission reports is that they are:
o: Prepared by the Union Finance Commission
61.x: State Finance Commission reports are often ignored, which weakens fiscal devolution to local bodies.
xa: Other conditions: **properly constituted** local bodies and **published audited accounts**.
The SEC (not the SFC) conducts local polls, **appointed by the Governor**.

61.s: The recommendation to establish a Local Body Ombudsman was made by the:
o: First Administrative Reforms Commission in its Sixth Report
Second Finance Commission in its Local Finance Report
Second Administrative Reforms Commission in its Sixth Report
61.x: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended a Local Body Ombudsman in its Sixth Report, titled Local Governance, published in 2007.
61.tq: Discriminate between the First and Second ARC, a standard institutional trap.
xs: The **Local Body Ombudsman** was recommended by the **Second Administrative Reforms Commission**, **6th Report "Local Governance"** (**2007**) — option **(4)**.
⚠ The **UKPSC 2012** key marked the **First ARC**; the standard answer is the **Second ARC**.
The **V. Ramachandran** Committee (**2013**) dealt with delivery of public goods through panchayats.
xa: **Sushil Kumar** committee (report **2025**): ending **proxy participation**.
**Devolution Index** report: **Ministry of Panchayati Raj** with **IIPA**.

61.s: The report titled “Status of Devolution to Panchayats in States” is published by the:
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, prepared with the National Institute of Urban Affairs
Ministry of Panchayati Raj, prepared with IIPA
Ministry of Rural Development, prepared with NIRDPR
Ministry of Finance, prepared with the Finance Commission
61.x: The Devolution Index report is published by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj and is prepared with the Indian Institute of Public Administration.
61.tq: Identify the publishing ministry and distinguish it from related rural-development institutions.
xs: "**Status of Devolution to Panchayats in States**" (Devolution Index) is published by the **Ministry of Panchayati Raj**, **prepared with IIPA** — option **(2)** is correct.
**NIRDPR** (Hyderabad) is the national **training** institute, not the publisher.
xa: Devolution concerns the **3Fs** — **functions, funds, functionaries**.
Root cause of weak devolution: Art. **243G/243W** say the State "**may**" devolve.
**Eleventh Schedule**: **29** subjects; **Twelfth Schedule**: **18**.

61.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the role of the Collector in Panchayati Raj administration?
o: Balwantrai Mehta — made the Collector the Zilla Parishad chairman
Hanumantha Rao — recommended complete abolition of the Collector’s role
Ashok Mehta — made the Collector the Zilla Parishad chairman
G.V.K. Rao — kept the Collector central without modification
61.x: Balwantrai Mehta made the Collector the chairman of the Zilla Parishad. Later committees split on the Collector's role, and none of them (Ashok Mehta, Hanumantha Rao or G.V.K. Rao) is correctly paired with the statement shown, so only A is correctly matched.
61.tq: Avoid swapping committee recommendations concerning the Collector.
xs: **Balwantrai Mehta** made the **Collector** the **Zilla Parishad chairman** — option **(1)**.
Later committees **split** on the Collector's role.
xa: **Democratic decentralisation** is Balwant Rai Mehta's term — power to **elected** local bodies.
**Block offices**: sarpanches depend on them for **approvals and funds**.
The proposed **District Development Council** was criticised as a **parallel executive**.

61.s: Which Programme has been merged with RGSA, a Central Government Scheme from 2015-16....
61.src: APPSC 2018 Question Papers and Keys for Mains Exams

62.s: Which one of the following is the “National Voters’ Day”?
62.x: To encourage young voters to take part in the political process, the Government of India has decided to celebrate January 25 every year as ‘National Voters Day.’ It started on January 25, 2011 to mark the commission’s foundation day.

62.s: Article 324, which provides for the Election Commission of India, lies in Part ____ of the Constitution.
62.x: Article 324 lies in Part XV (Articles 324-329).
xa: The ECI was **set up on 25 January 1950**; its seat is **Nirvachan Sadan, New Delhi**.
Its training arm is **IIIDEM**, New Delhi.
**25 January** is also **National Voters' Day**, observed since **2011**.

62.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners?
o: The CEC and the ECs have equal powers and differences are settled by majority
The CEC has a permanent veto over the decisions of the ECs
The CEC alone takes all substantive decisions of the Commission
The ECs can overrule the CEC only with the President's approval
62.x: The CEC and the other Election Commissioners have equal powers, and differences are resolved by majority decision.
62.tq: Discriminate between the chairing role of the CEC and unequal voting power.
xs: **The CEC and the ECs have equal powers** and **differences are settled by majority** — option **(1)** is correct.
So the CEC has no veto and cannot decide alone; the CEC only **presides**.
xa: **T.N. Seshan v Union of India (1995)** upheld the **multi-member body + majority rule**.
Salaries: **CEC and ECs equal**, on a par with a **Supreme Court judge**.
⚠ But removal differs: CEC like an **SC judge**; ECs only on the **CEC's recommendation**.

62.s: The CEC and Election Commissioners receive equal salaries on a par with:
o: a judge of a High Court
a judge of the Supreme Court
62.x: They are paid on a par with a Supreme Court judge, and their service conditions cannot be varied to their disadvantage.
xa: Tenure: **6 years or 65**; **no reappointment** under the 2023 Act.
**CEC and ECs have equal powers**; differences settled by **majority**.

62.s: Under Article 324(1), the ECI's superintendence does NOT extend to elections to:
62.x: Article 324(1) covers Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President; Panchayat and municipal polls come under the State Election Commissions.
xa: ECI does not conduct the elections of **Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Deputy Chairman** — the House elects them.
**Art. 71**: President/VP election disputes go to the **Supreme Court**.
The **State Election Commissioner** is appointed by the **Governor**.

62.s: The Model Code of Conduct rests on which provision, and applies from when?
o: Article 324; from the announcement of the election schedule
Article 324; from the start of polling
Representation of the People Act, 1951; from the announcement of the schedule
Representation of the People Act, 1951; from the declaration of results
62.x: The MCC is not a statute; it rests on Article 324 and applies from the announcement of the election schedule (Harbans Singh Jalal, 1997).
xa: The start date comes from **Harbans Singh Jalal (1997)**.
**T.N. Seshan** enforced the MCC strictly in **1991**.
A petition said the PM's broadcast during Assembly polls violated **Part VII of the MCC** (conduct of the party in power).

62.s: The 2022 delimitation of Jammu and Kashmir was conducted by a Commission headed by Justice:
62.x: The J&K delimitation (2022) was done by a Commission under Justice Ranjana Desai, while Assam was delimited by the ECI.
xa: The ECI decides constituencies under the **Delimitation Commission Act**.
**Art. 329(a)**: delimitation laws cannot be questioned in court.

62.s: Which body decides every step of the election process, from the announcement of the schedule to the declaration of results?
62.x: The ECI decides every step from announcement to results; Panchayat and municipal polls belong to the State Election Commissions.
xa: It can **cancel polls** for rigging or booth capturing.
It **recognises parties** and **allots symbols**.

62.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 71 – Disputes on Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections
Article 329(b) – Bar on questioning delimitation in court
Article 329(a) – Challenge to an election only by election petition
62.x: Article 71 covers disputes on Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections; 329(a) bars court challenges to delimitation and 329(b) requires an election petition.
xa: MP/MLA election petitions → **High Court**, appeal to the **Supreme Court**.
**Art. 103** / **Art. 192**: ECI advises on MPs' / MLAs' disqualification.

62.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: District Collector – District Election Officer/District Returning Officer
Election Commission of India – Conducts elections to Parliament and State Legislatures
State Election Commission – Conducts elections to Panchayats and municipalities
Chief Electoral Officer – Conducts elections to Panchayats and municipalities
62.x: The Chief Electoral Officer is the State-level officer under the ECI's control; local-body elections are conducted by the State Election Commission.
xa: The SEC is appointed by the **Governor** and removed like an **HC judge**.
AP SEC: **Anil Chandra Punetha**.

62.s: National Voters' Day, observed since 2011, falls every year on:
62.x: National Voters' Day is 25 January, the ECI's foundation day (25 January 1950).
xa: **V.S. Ramadevi** (**1990**) was the first and only woman CEC.
**T.N. Seshan** was the **10th CEC** (**1990-96**); he enforced the MCC strictly in **1991**.
The opposition's removal motion against **Gyanesh Kumar** is the first against a CEC appointed under the **2023 Act**.

62.s: There is a demand that the expenses of the Election Commission of India be charged on the:
62.x: Critics note the ECI's dependence on DoPT, Law and Home Ministries and demand its expenses be charged on the Consolidated Fund.
xa: Listed flaws: the Constitution prescribes **no qualifications** and **no term** for members.
**Salary equal to a Supreme Court judge**; service conditions cannot be varied to their disadvantage.

62.s: In which year did the election commission of India celebrate its Golden Jubilee?
Two Election Commissioners were added in 1989 after which Amendment lowered the voting age from 21 to 18?
62.x: The 61st Amendment lowered the voting age from 21 to 18, after which two Election Commissioners were added in 1989.
xa: **Jan 1990**: EC posts abolished; single-member again.
**Oct 1993 onwards**: multi-member (**CEC + 2 ECs**), decisions by majority.
From **1950** to **Oct 1989**, the ECI was a **single-member** body (CEC only).

62.s: V.S. Ramadevi, the first woman Chief Election Commissioner of India, served in:
62.x: V.S. Ramadevi served as CEC in 1990; T.N. Seshan was the tenth CEC.
xa: First CEC: **Sukumar Sen**.
Current CEC: **Gyanesh Kumar**, the **26th CEC**.

62.s: With reference to the Election Commission of India, which pair is correctly matched?
62.x: The Golden Jubilee was observed in 2001; the Diamond Jubilee was in 2010 and 75 years were completed in 2025.
xa: The ECI was **set up on 25 January 1950**; **National Voters' Day** (**25 January**) is observed since **2011**.
Seat: **Nirvachan Sadan, New Delhi**; training arm: **IIIDEM**, New Delhi.
Two ECs were first added on **16 Oct 1989** after the **61st Amendment** lowered the voting age from **21 to 18**.

62.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Election Commission of India is a multi-member body.
II. The ECI has been a multi-member body continuously since 1 October 1993.
III. The Chief Election Commissioner and the two Election Commissioners receive salaries equivalent to those of Supreme Court Judges.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
62.x: All three are correct: the ECI has been a three-member body continuously since 1 October 1993, and its members are paid like Supreme Court judges.
62.tq: Recall the 1993 change to a multi-member Commission.
n: The Election Commission of India consists of one Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India has been a multi-member body continuously since 1 October 1993. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The salary of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners is equivalent to the salary of Supreme Court Judges. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xs: All three statements **I, II and III** are correct — option **(1)**.
I and II: the ECI is a **multi-member** body (**CEC + 2 ECs**), continuously since **1 October 1993**.
III: the CEC and ECs get **salary** equal to **Supreme Court Judges**.
xa: It began as a **single-member** body; **two ECs were added in 1989** after the **61st Amendment**.
**T.N. Seshan v Union of India (1995)** upheld the multi-member body and majority rule.
Service conditions cannot be varied to their disadvantage.

62.s: The reservoir of power under Article 324 may be used by the Election Commission primarily when:
o: A State Election Commission requests it in every case
No law holds the field on the matter concerned
A law already completely occupies the field
The President delegates legislative power to it
62.x: Article 324 operates as a reservoir where no law holds the field; it cannot ordinarily override an existing law governing the matter.
62.tq: Apply the condition attached to residual constitutional power.
xs: Art. 324's "**reservoir of power**" is usable only where **no law holds the field** — option **(2)** is correct.
This was held in **Mohinder Singh Gill v. CEC (1978)**; where a law occupies the field, the ECI must follow it.
xa: The **MCC is not a statute** — it rests on **Art. 324**.
**SIR** of rolls is ordered under **Art. 324** + **Section 21, RPA 1950**.
**T.N. Seshan v UoI (1995)** upheld the **multi-member** Commission.

62.s: The constitutional validity of the multi-member Election Commission and the majority rule was upheld in which case?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner
ADR v. Election Commission of India
T.N. Seshan v. Union of India
62.x: The Supreme Court upheld the multi-member structure and majority rule in T.N. Seshan v. Union of India (1995).
62.tq: Use the case-name association to distinguish institutional-structure litigation from election-process cases.
xs: **T.N. Seshan v Union of India (1995)** upheld the **multi-member body + majority rule** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Mohinder Singh Gill (1978)** is the "**reservoir of power**" case, not this one.
xa: The ECI has been **multi-member since Oct 1993**.
**Anoop Baranwal (2023)**: interim panel of **PM + LoP + CJI**.
**Harbans Singh Jalal (1997)**: MCC applies from the day the schedule is announced.

62.s: In Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India (2023), the interim selection panel directed by the Constitution Bench consisted of:
o: Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Chief Justice of India
Prime Minister, Law Minister and Chief Justice of India
President, Prime Minister and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
Prime Minister, Speaker of the Lok Sabha and Chief Justice of India
62.x: Until Parliament enacted a law, the Constitution Bench directed selection by a panel comprising the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition or leader of the largest opposition party in the Lok Sabha, and the Chief Justice of India.
62.tq: Separate the interim judicial mechanism from the later statutory mechanism.
xs: **Anoop Baranwal (2023)**: **PM + Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha + CJI** — option **(1)** is correct.
This was a **Constitution Bench** order, to apply **until Parliament legislates**.
xa: Where there is no LoP, the **largest opposition party leader** sits.
⚠ The **2023 Act** replaced the **CJI** with a **Union Cabinet Minister**.
**May 2026**: SC said the CJI's place was **only temporary**, pending a law.

62.s: Which one of the following was the principal change made by the 2023 Act in relation to the interim mechanism in Anoop Baranwal?
o: The entire Selection Committee was replaced by the Search Committee.
The Prime Minister was replaced by the President.
The Leader of Opposition was replaced by the Law Minister.
The Chief Justice of India was replaced by a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
62.x: The 2023 Act replaced the Chief Justice of India on the selection panel with a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
62.tq: Discriminate between the CJI in the interim panel and the Cabinet Minister in the statutory panel.
xs: The 2023 Act replaced **the Chief Justice of India** with **a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister** — option **(4)** is correct.
The **PM** and the **LoP** stay on the panel.
xa: Criticism: the government now has a **2-1 majority**.
**Jaya Thakur v UoI (2024)** challenges the Act — **pending** as of May 2026.
SC (May 2026) questioned the lack of "**one absolutely neutral person**".

62.s: The Election Commission recognises political parties and allots election symbols under the:
62.x: Party recognition and symbol allotment are governed by the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968, issued under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 and Article 324.
62.tq: Match a power with its exact legal instrument and year.
xs: Parties are recognised and symbols allotted under the **Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968** — option **(2)** is correct.
The Order was issued under the **RPA 1951** + **Art. 324**.
xa: The ECI settles **symbol and recognition disputes** like a court — a **quasi-judicial** function.
It **cannot review a result** and **does not try election petitions**.

62.s: The Search Committee for Election Commissioners under the 2023 Act is headed by the:
62.x: The Search Committee is headed by the Law Minister, has two Secretary-rank members and shortlists five names.
xa: The **Selection Committee** — **PM (chair)**, **LoP**, a **Union Cabinet Minister** — may pick names **outside the shortlist**.
The **President** appoints on the Selection Committee's recommendation.
The Act is **Act No. 49 of 2023**, replacing the **1991 Act**.

62.s:
Regarding the Selection Committee under the CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023, consider:
1. It may select names outside the Search Committee's shortlist.
2. It recommends names for appointment by the President.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
62.x: The Selection Committee may choose names outside the Search Committee's shortlist, and it recommends names to the President for appointment.
xa: Members: **PM (chair)**, **Leader of Opposition** (or largest opposition party leader) in the Lok Sabha, a **Union Cabinet Minister** nominated by the PM.
Criticism: this gives the government a **2-1 majority**.
The Search Committee shortlists **5** names under the **Law Minister**.

62.s: The Tarkunde Committee on electoral reforms was set up by:
62.x: Jayaprakash Narayan set up the Tarkunde Committee, which proposed a three-member Election Commission.
xa: **Anoop Baranwal (2023)** adopted the same **PM + LoP + CJI** panel as an interim measure.
The ECI became a **three-member** body from **Oct 1993**.

62.s:
Assertion (A): The Constitution places post-retirement restrictions on the CAG under Article 148(4).
Reason (R): The Constitution expressly bars retiring Election Commissioners from any further government appointment.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
62.x: A is true (as with the UPSC Chairman under Article 319), but the Constitution has no express bar for retiring Election Commissioners.
xa: ⚠ Some notes say the CEC cannot hold office of profit after retirement — the Constitution has **no such bar**.
The Constitution also prescribes **no qualifications** and **no term** for members.

62.s: The Election Commission advises the Governor on disqualification of members of State Legislatures under Article:
62.x: The ECI advises the Governor under Article 192 and the President under Article 103; anti-defection cases go to the Speaker or Chairman.
xa: This is the ECI's **advisory** function.
⚠ Disqualification (Art. 103/192) → ECI advises; anti-defection → Speaker/Chairman.

62.s: At the district level, Returning and Presiding Officers are appointed by the:
62.x: Each State has a Chief Electoral Officer, while at district level the Collector/District Election Officer appoints Returning and Presiding Officers.
xa: The CEO is appointed by the **ECI** from **senior civil servants** of the state.
⚠ CEO appointment: APP says **by the CEC**; IYB says **by the Commission**.

62.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Chief Electoral Officer is removed like a High Court judge
The State Election Commission functions under Articles 243K and 243ZA
The Chief Electoral Officer functions under the Representation of the People Act, 1950
The State Election Commissioner is removable only like a High Court judge
62.x: The Chief Electoral Officer is removed by the Election Commission; only the State Election Commissioner has High Court judge-like protection.
xa: The SEC is appointed by the **Governor**; the CEO by the **ECI**.
AP SEC: **Anil Chandra Punetha**, for local-body polls.

62.s: The challenged composition of the Selection Committee under the 2023 Election Commission law gives the government a majority of:
62.x: Petitions by ADR and Jaya Thakur challenge the 2:1 government majority; the Supreme Court said the CJI's place had been only temporary, pending a law.
xa: **Anoop Baranwal v Union of India** (**2023**): until Parliament legislates, **PM + LoP + CJI** choose the CEC and ECs.
The **2023 Act** (**Act No. 49 of 2023**) replaced the **CJI with a Union Cabinet Minister**.
A **Search Committee** headed by the **Law Minister** shortlists **5** names; the Selection Committee may pick from outside it.
**Jaya Thakur v Union of India** (**2024**) was still **pending** as of May 2026.

62.s: Which of the following elections is NOT conducted by the Election Commission of India?
62.x: Panchayat elections at all three tiers are conducted by the State Election Commission.
n: The Election Commission of India conducts elections to the Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India conducts elections to the Rajya Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India conducts elections to State Legislative Assemblies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India conducts elections to State Legislative Councils. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India conducts elections for the President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India conducts elections for the Vice-President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India does not conduct local body elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The State Election Commission conducts Panchayat elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The State Election Commission conducts Municipal elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India conducts elections to the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India conducts elections to State Legislative Assemblies and Councils. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The Election Commission of India conducts elections for the President and Vice-President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The State Election Commission conducts elections to Gram Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The State Election Commission conducts elections to Panchayat Samitis. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The State Election Commission conducts elections to Zilla Parishads. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xa: SEC basis: **Articles 243K and 243ZA**.
⚠ ECI also does **not** conduct elections of **Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Deputy Chairman** (chosen by the House itself).
SECs operate under the respective **State Panchayati** and **State Municipal** laws.

62.s: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office:
o: In the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge
In the same manner as a High Court judge
By the President on the advice of the Prime Minister
On the recommendation of the Union Law Minister
62.x: The CEC is removable like a Supreme Court judge; Election Commissioners and Regional Commissioners only on the CEC's recommendation.
xa: CEC grounds: **proven misbehaviour or incapacity**; **special majority** in both Houses.

62.s: A motion for removal of the Chief Election Commissioner must be supported by at least how many signatures when initiated in the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha, respectively?
62.x: The motion requires the signatures of at least 100 members in the Lok Sabha or 50 members in the Rajya Sabha.
62.tq: Keep the House-wise numerical requirements in their correct order.
xs: A CEC removal motion needs **100** Lok Sabha or **50** Rajya Sabha signatures — option **(1)** is correct.
This mirrors the procedure for a **Supreme Court judge**.
xa: Grounds: **proven misbehaviour or incapacity**; **special majority** in both Houses.
The Opposition's removal motion against **Gyanesh Kumar** was the first against a CEC appointed under the 2023 Act.
ECs are removed only **on the CEC's recommendation** (**Section 11** of the 2023 Act).

62.s: Which of the following does the Constitution NOT prescribe for members of the Election Commission?
o: Removal of the CEC in the manner of a Supreme Court judge
Superintendence of elections vested in the Commission
62.x: The Constitution prescribes no qualifications and no fixed term for members of the Election Commission.
xa: The **2023 Act** fills the gap: **Secretary to GoI** rank; **6 years or 65**.
Criticism: ECI depends on **DoPT, Law and Home Ministries**; no power over **inner-party democracy** or **party finances**.
Demand: charge its expenses on the **Consolidated Fund**.

62.s: An Election Commissioner holds office for six years or until attaining the age of ____, whichever is earlier.
62.x: The ECI has one CEC and two ECs, appointed by the President, each serving six years or until age 65.
n: The Election Commission of India consists of one Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The President of India appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners is six years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xa: **CEC and ECs have equal powers**; differences settled by **majority**.
The **2023 Act** bars **reappointment**.
**Salary** equals that of a **Supreme Court judge**.

62.s: The removal safeguard for the Chief Election Commissioner is provided under which provision of the Constitution?
62.x: Article 324(5) protects the CEC: they can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge.
n: Article 324(5) provides the removal safeguard for the Chief Election Commissioner. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xs: The CEC's removal safeguard is in **Article 324(5)** — option **(3)** is correct.
The CEC is removed only in the **same manner** and on the **same grounds** as a **Supreme Court judge**.
**Art. 324(1)** vests **superintendence, direction and control** of elections; **243K/243ZA** concern **State Election Commissions**.
xa: Removal motion needs **100 Lok Sabha or 50 Rajya Sabha** signatures; **special majority** in both Houses.
Other ECs are removed by the **President** only **on the CEC's recommendation**.
⚠ CEC like an **SC judge**; SEC like an **HC judge**.

62.s: The head of a State Election Commission can be removed only in the manner of a:
62.x: A State Election Commissioner is removed like a High Court judge, while the CEC is removed like a Supreme Court judge.
n: The State Election Commission conducts elections to Municipalities. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The State Election Commission conducts elections to Municipal Corporations. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The head of the Election Commission of India is removed like a Supreme Court Judge. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The head of the State Election Commission is removed like a High Court Judge. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xa: **AP SEC:** **Anil Chandra Punetha**.
SEC head is appointed by the **Governor**; ECI members by the **President**.
President/VP election disputes go to the **Supreme Court** (**Art. 71**).

62.s: Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls is ordered under:
o: Article 280 and Section 21 of the Delimitation Act, 2002
Article 324 and Section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950
Article 243K and Section 11 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
Article 326 and Section 62 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
62.x: Special Intensive Revision is ordered under Article 324 and Section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
62.tq: Match the electoral exercise with both its constitutional and statutory bases.
xs: **SIR** is ordered under **Article 324** and **Section 21 of the RPA 1950** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Art. 243K** is the **SEC** (local bodies), and **Art. 280** is unrelated to rolls.
xa: The ECI **prepares and revises electoral rolls**.
AP angle: **ASR district's 100% SIR digitalisation**.

62.s: A challenge to an election result after it has been declared must be made through:
o: A review by the Election Commission
62.x: The Election Commission cannot review a declared result and does not try election petitions; challenges follow the election-petition route.
xa: The ECI decides **party and symbol disputes** and advises on disqualification.
**Art. 329(b)**: challenge only by an **election petition**.

62.s: The State Election Commission for municipal elections is provided under Article:
62.x: Article 243ZA covers municipal elections; 243K covers Panchayat elections and 324 the ECI.
n: Articles 243K and 243ZA relate to the State Election Commission's local body election functions. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
The constitutional basis of the Election Commission of India is Article 324 in Part XV. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Article 326 provides universal adult suffrage for Lok Sabha elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Article 326 provides universal adult suffrage for Legislative Assembly elections. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xa: ⚠ ECI is **not** for panchayat or municipal polls — those go to the **SEC**.
ECI sits in **Part XV** (**Articles 324 to 329**); SECs in **Parts IX and IX-A**.

62.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Lok Sabha Speaker and Deputy Speaker are chosen internally by the Lok Sabha under Article 93.
The Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman is chosen internally under Article 89(2).

n: The Lok Sabha chooses its Speaker and Deputy Speaker internally under Article 93. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]

xs: The incorrect statement is that the **ECI elects the Chairman of a Legislative Council** under **Article 182** — option **(3)**.

62.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the election reforms of the T.N. Seshan era?
o: Transfer of election petitions from High Courts to the Election Commission
Strict enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct in 1991
Introduction of Electors Photo Identity Cards
62.x: Election petitions were not transferred to the Election Commission; they are tried by the High Courts in the case of Parliamentary and State Legislature elections. The other three measures were associated with the Seshan era.
62.tq: Find the institutional power wrongly transferred to the Election Commission.
xs: **Transfer of election petitions from High Courts to the Election Commission** was never a Seshan-era reform — so option **(1)** is the answer.
**Art. 329(b)** petitions are tried by the **High Court**, with appeal to the **Supreme Court**; the **ECI does not try election petitions**.
Seshan era: **strict MCC enforcement in 1991**, arrest of violators and **removal of partisan police officers**.
**Electors Photo Identity Cards** were also introduced in the Seshan era.
xa: **T.N. Seshan** was the **10th CEC** (**1990-96**), the reform-era CEC.
The **MCC is not a statute**; it rests on **Art. 324** and applies from the day the schedule is announced (**Harbans Singh Jalal, 1997**).
**T.N. Seshan v Union of India** (**1995**) upheld the **multi-member body** and majority rule.
⚠ **ECI cannot review a result**; it decides **party and symbol disputes** and advises on disqualification.

63.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

63.s: A candidate's security deposit is forfeited when the candidate secures less than:

xs: The **security deposit** is forfeited below **one-sixth** of valid votes — option **(2)**.

**NOTA** has no electoral effect: even if NOTA leads, the **highest-scoring candidate** wins.

63.s: The constitutional principle underlying delimitation is best expressed as:
o: One State, one vote, one value
One district, one representative, one value

One person, one vote, one value

xs: Delimitation rests on **"one person, one vote, one value"** — option **(4)**.

any address selected by the elector
the last place of employment in India only
the address of the Indian passport

Sikkim, for Buddhist monks in the Sangha seat

63.s: The constitutional authority for conducting State Legislative Assembly elections is the:

Article 325 prohibits discrimination in electoral rolls on the basis of race. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Article 325 prohibits discrimination in electoral rolls on the basis of caste. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Article 325 prohibits discrimination in electoral rolls on the basis of sex. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]

xa: Every citizen aged **18+** may vote unless disqualified.

o: Duration of the Houses of Parliament
63.x: Articles 83 and 85 concern Parliament's term and sessions, 172 and 174 the States', and 356 President's Rule; all may need amending.

Simultaneous elections may require amendment of Article 85. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Simultaneous elections may require amendment of Article 172. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Simultaneous elections may require amendment of Article 174. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
Simultaneous elections may require amendment of Article 356. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xa: The first four general elections (**1951-52, 1957, 1962, 1967**) were **simultaneous** with Assembly polls.
**Bypolls** must be held within **6 months** of a vacancy.
Universal adult suffrage: **Article 326**.

63.s: The voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 years by the:

The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988, lowered the voting age. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]

The minimum age for Panchayat and Municipality elections is 21 years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 91-94]

63.s:

The right to vote is not a Fundamental Right. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
The right to vote is a legal or statutory right. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]

63.s: Under the old Rule 49-O, a voter:
o: Entered the booth but refused to vote before the Presiding Officer
Voided the result by majority rejection
Pressed the NOTA button on the EVM

Under old Rule 49-O, an abstaining voter refused to vote before the Presiding Officer. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
Under the full international right to reject, voters reject all candidates. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
Under the full international right to reject, rejection is made via the ballot or EVM. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]

NOTA **preserves** secrecy.

63.x: A candidate with one-sixth or less of the valid votes forfeits the deposit.
n: NOTA does not determine the election outcome by itself. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]

Abstention under old Rule 49-O did not affect the winning tally. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
Under the international right to reject, re-election is mandated if rejection crosses a threshold of more than 50%. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
xa: ⚠ Trap: "election cancelled if NOTA gets the highest votes" is **false**.
NOTA applies only to **direct Lok Sabha** and **Assembly** elections.

Old Rule 49-O was struck down as ultra vires. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #66 · pp 176-178]
xa: Rule 49-O did **not affect** the **winning tally**.

63.s: Which additional areas are included in the Presidential electoral college through the 70th Constitutional Amendment Act?

xs: The **70th Constitutional Amendment Act** added **Delhi and Puducherry** to the President's electoral college — option **(1)**.

o: The Election Commission of India under Article 324
State Election Commissions under Articles 243K and 243ZA
The Chief Electoral Officer of the State under Article 325
63.x: Panchayat and municipal polls are run by the State Election Commissions under Articles 243K (panchayats) and 243ZA (municipalities), not by the ECI. Article 324 vests control of Parliament, State legislature, President and VP elections in the ECI; Article 325 provides one general electoral roll; Article 329 bars courts in electoral matters. The CEO and Delimitation Commission do not conduct local polls.

xs: **State Election Commissions** under **Articles 243K and 243ZA** conduct **panchayat and municipal** polls — option **(2)**.

The **Delimitation Commission** fixes seats and boundaries; it conducts no elections.
xa: **Article 325** = one general electoral roll; **Article 329** = bar on courts in electoral matters.
**Art. 243K** covers **panchayats**; **Art. 243ZA** covers **municipalities**.

63.s: The freeze on the inter-State allocation of Lok Sabha seats on the basis of the 1971 Census was first imposed by which Amendment, and until when?

63.s:

The Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides scrutiny procedures. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]

63.s: Election expense accounts are dealt with in which Sections of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?

xa: Expense accounts reach the **District Election Officer** within **30 days** (**Sec. 78**).
**Sec. 29A, RPA 1951** = registration of political parties.
**Sec. 126** bars opinion polls in the **48 hours** before close of poll; **Sec. 126A** governs exit polls.

63.s: An election held after a legislature is dissolved before the expiry of its normal term is called a:
63.x: A mid-term election follows premature dissolution; a by-election fills a single vacancy, ordinarily within six months.
xa: Bypoll exceptions: remaining term **under one year**, or ECI (consulting the Centre) certifies difficulty.

63.s: The Delimitation Commission is constituted under:
o: A notification of the Election Commission
A resolution of the Rajya Sabha
An executive order of the President

63.s: Reservation of one-third of seats for women, under the 106th Amendment, is linked to Article:
63.x: Article 334A relates to the women's one-third reservation; Article 330 covers SC/ST seats in the Lok Sabha and 331 the former Anglo-Indian nomination.
xa: ⚠ **330 / 332** = SC/ST seats; **331 / 333** = Anglo-Indians (ended).

63.s: Which Lok Sabha constituency in Andhra Pradesh is reserved for Scheduled Tribes?
63.x: Araku is the ST-reserved constituency; Amalapuram and Tirupati are SC-reserved.
xa: AP's **4** SC seats: **Amalapuram, Bapatla, Chittoor, Tirupati**.

63.s: In a constituency reserved for Scheduled Castes, who can vote?
o: Only voters belonging to Scheduled Castes
Only voters belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
Only voters belonging to Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes

xa: AP has **4** SC + **1** ST Lok Sabha seats; Telangana **3** SC + **2** ST.

63.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about women's reservation under the 106th Amendment?
o: It provides one-third reservation of seats
It operates immediately, irrespective of census and delimitation

xa: Tamil Nadu's resolution sought the women's quota from **2029** without linking it to delimitation.

63.s: The number of Scheduled Caste-reserved seats in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly is:
63.x: Andhra Pradesh has 29 SC and 7 ST Assembly seats; Telangana has 19 SC and 12 ST.
xa: AP's ST Lok Sabha seat: **Araku**; Telangana's: **Adilabad, Mahabubabad**.
Telangana's SC Lok Sabha seats: **Peddapalle, Warangal, Nagarkurnool**.

63.s: Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies under Article 334 has been extended up to 2030 by which Amendment?
63.x: The 104th Amendment (Act of 2019, in force January 2020) extended SC/ST seat reservation under Article 334 to 2030 and ended Anglo-Indian nomination. xs: The **104th Amendment** extended SC/ST reservation to **2030** — option **(2)**.
Act of **2019**, in force **Jan 2020**; it also **ended** Anglo-Indian nomination.
The **106th** gave women one-third (**Art. 334A**); the **84th** extended the delimitation freeze.
xa: **Art. 334** originally provided **10 years** (till **1960**).

63.s: Under Section 78 of the RPA 1951, election expense accounts must be filed with the District Election Officer within:
63.x: Section 78 requires expense accounts to reach the DEO, usually the Collector, within 30 days.
xa: **Observers** (general, police, expenditure) are appointed by the ECI under **Sec. 20B**.

63.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the election machinery?
o: Booth Level Officers now carry standard photo identity cards
The Chief Electoral Officer assists the Election Commission in each State or UT
Electoral Registration Officers and Booth Level Officers are associated with electoral rolls
The Election Commission has no control over officers deployed on poll duty
63.x: The Election Commission controls officers on poll duty and may transfer them or act against partisan conduct.
xa: **Returning Officer** conducts the poll and declares results.
**DEO** (usually the Collector) receives expense accounts within **30 days**.

63.s: For State Party recognition on seat share, a party needs three per cent of Assembly seats or ____ seats, whichever is more.
63.x: One alternative criterion is three per cent of Assembly seats or three seats, whichever is more.
xa: A fifth route: **1** Lok Sabha seat for every **25** from the state.
Recognition is under the **Election Symbols Order, 1968**; registration under **Sec. 29A**.

63.s: A party is eligible for National Party recognition if it is recognised as a State party in at least ____ States.
63.x: State-party recognition in four or more States is one of the alternative criteria under the Election Symbols Order, 1968.
xa: PYQ APPSC-G2 **2025**: all listed national-party conditions were valid → key "**None of the above**".
State Party routes include **8%** of valid votes, and **1** Lok Sabha seat for every **25** from the state.
Recognition is under the **Election Symbols Order, 1968** (an ECI order, not an Act).

63.s: For a Lok Sabha general election, the notification under Section 14 of the RPA 1951 is issued by the:
63.x: The President notifies Lok Sabha polls on the ECI's recommendation; the ECI fixes the schedule and nomination dates.
xa: ⚠ **Sec. 14** = President (Lok Sabha); **Sec. 15** = Governor (Assembly).
**Bypolls** must be held within **6 months** of a vacancy.

63.s: The authority of the Model Code of Conduct is associated with the Election Commission's plenary power under Article:
63.x: The Model Code is a set of ECI guidelines supported by Article 324, not a statute enacted by Parliament.
xa: SC in **Mohinder Singh Gill v CEC (1978)**: Art. 324 = "**reservoir of power**".
MCC comes into force **from the announcement of the schedule** (**Harbans Singh Jalal v UoI (1997)**).

63.s: Which of the following ECI initiative – purpose pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: SVEEP – Voter education and electoral participation
cVIGIL – Assistance and facilities for voters with disabilities
Saksham – Assistance and facilities for voters with disabilities
Voter Helpline – Registration, corrections, roll search and complaints
63.x: cVIGIL is for reporting Model Code violations through geo-tagged photographs or videos; Saksham assists voters with disabilities.
xa: cVIGIL promises action within **100 minutes**.
SVEEP was launched in **2009**; the ECI partnered **Indian Railways** (APPSC **2019**).
**ECINET** merges **40+** ECI apps and websites.

63.s: Persons in preventive detention may vote through:
o: A special booth in the jail
63.x: Persons in preventive detention, along with service voters, special voters and electors on election duty, are covered by postal-ballot provisions.
xa: Absentee voters: seniors **85+** (raised from **80**), **benchmark disability (40%+)**, essential-service staff on duty.
Overseas electors enrol at their **passport address** (**Sec. 20A**).

63.s: The age threshold for senior citizens in the absentee-voter postal ballot category is:
63.x: The senior-citizen threshold is 85 years or above, raised from 80 years.
xa: Persons with **benchmark disability (40%+)** and **essential-service staff** on duty also qualify.
Postal ballot also covers **service voters** and those in **preventive detention**.

63.s: The grounds for declaring an election void are listed in which Section of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
63.x: Section 100 lists grounds such as disqualification of the returned candidate, corrupt practice and improper rejection of a nomination.
xa: Petition tried by the **High Court** (**Sec. 80A**), filed within **45 days** (**Sec. 81**).
Electoral offences now sit in **BNS Chapter IX (Sections 169-177)**.

63.s: The 17th Lok Sabha was elected in:
63.x: The 17th Lok Sabha was elected in 2019; 2014 elected the 16th and 2024 the 18th.
xa: First general election: **1951-52**.
NOTA first used in a Lok Sabha poll in **2014**.

63.s: Southern States fear population-based delimitation would shift Lok Sabha seats towards States such as:
63.x: Population-based delimitation would shift representation towards more populous States such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan.
xa: **Tamil Nadu** resolution (**17 Aug 2026**): permanent freeze at **543** + **2.2:1** Lok Sabha-Rajya Sabha ratio.
The freeze on inter-State seats dates from the **42nd Amendment (1976)** on the **1971 Census**.

63.s: IIIDEM, which trains election managers, is an institute of the:
63.x: IIIDEM belongs to the Election Commission, a permanent independent constitutional body constituted in 1950.
xa: SC in **State of Karnataka v Prathik Parasrampuria (2026)**: removing black money from elections = **core ECI duty**.
**Art. 324** vests superintendence, direction and control of elections in the ECI.

63.s: Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the disqualification for conviction continues for how long after release?
63.x: Under the RPA 1951 the disqualification continues for six years after release. Three, five and ten years are distractors.
63.tq: Recall the six-year period after release.
n: The disqualification for conviction continues for six years after release. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
xs: Under the **RPA 1951**, disqualification continues for **six years** after release — option **(2)**.
It applies to one convicted and sentenced to at least **two years**, during imprisonment and **six years** after.
xa: RPA 1951 **Sec. 8** deals with **disqualifications**.
RPA 1951 also covers **corrupt practices** and **election petitions**.
**Sec. 77-78** = expense accounts.

63.s:
Arrange the following milestones relating to the Model Code of Conduct in chronological order:

A. Part VII relating to the party in power was added
B. The Code was first drafted by the Kerala Government
C. The Code was revised
D. The Code was formalised by the Election Commission

Select the correct sequence.
63.x: The sequence is 1960 drafting by Kerala, 1968 formalisation by the ECI, 1974 revision, and 1979 addition of Part VII.
63.tq: Fix the earliest and latest milestones first, then place the 1968 and 1974 events.
xs: Order: **B** (Kerala draft, **1960**) → **D** (formalised by ECI, **1968**) → **C** (revised, **1974**) → **A** (Part VII added, **1979**) — option **(1)**.
Options (2) and (4) wrongly put the **1968** formalisation before the **1960** Kerala draft.
xa: **1991**: MCC enforced with rigour by CEC **T.N. Seshan**.
MCC was first used in the **1960 Kerala** Assembly election.
⚠ **1960** = MCC in Kerala; indelible ink = **1962**.

63.s: The Model Code of Conduct was first drafted and used in the 1960 Assembly election of:
63.x: The Code was first used in Kerala in 1960, formalised by the ECI in 1968 and strictly enforced by T.N. Seshan in 1991.
xa: The MCC was revised in **1974**.
It is lifted once results are declared.

63.s: Which one of the following is NOT a restriction under Part VII of the Model Code of Conduct?
o: Introducing new schemes or grants after announcement of polls
Using official machinery or transport for campaigning
Continuing ordinary official visits without combining them with electioneering
63.x: Part VII (party in power) bars combining official visits with electioneering, using official machinery or transport, and announcing new schemes or grants once polls are announced (options A, B, C). Ordinary official visits not combined with electioneering are not restricted, so D is the answer.
63.tq: Find the option that does not describe a prohibited act under the specific part of the Code.
xs: **Ordinary official visits not combined with electioneering** are not barred — option **(4)**.
**Part VII** curbs: no **official visits with electioneering**, no use of **official machinery/transport**, no **new schemes or grants** once polls are announced.
xa: **Part VII** on the "**party in power**" was added in **1979**.
Sanctions go up to **suspension/withdrawal of recognition** under **Para 16A** of the Symbols Order.
A 2026 petition alleged the **PM's national broadcast** breached MCC Part VII.

63.s: In which case did the Supreme Court describe Article 324 as a “reservoir of power”?
o: Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
63.x: In Mohinder Singh Gill v. CEC (1978), the Supreme Court described Article 324 as a reservoir of power.
63.tq: Match the constitutional principle with the case that established or described it.
xs: **Mohinder Singh Gill v CEC (1978)** called Art. 324 a "**reservoir of power**" — option **(1)**.
It lets the ECI act where **Parliament has not legislated**.
xa: The **MCC**'s authority rests on this **plenary power under Art. 324**.
**Kuldip Nayar**: right to vote = **statutory right**; **PUCL (2013)**: **NOTA** on EVMs.

63.s: Under which provision can the Election Commission suspend or withdraw the recognition of a political party for violating the Model Code of Conduct?
o: Paragraph 16A of the Election Symbols Order, 1968
63.x: Sanctions for MCC violations range from censure up to suspension or withdrawal of recognition under Paragraph 16A of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968. Section 29A deals with party registration, Section 126A with exit polls, and Article 329 bars courts in electoral matters.
63.tq: MCC teeth = Para 16A, Symbols Order 1968.
xs: **Paragraph 16A of the Election Symbols Order, 1968** allows suspension/withdrawal of recognition — option **(2)**.
**Sec. 29A** = party registration; **Sec. 126A** = exit polls; **Art. 329** = bar on courts.
xa: Sanctions under the MCC range from **censure** up to **suspension/withdrawal of recognition**.
The Symbols Order is an **ECI order, not an Act**.

63.s: When does the Model Code of Conduct come into force?
o: Immediately upon the formal announcement of the election schedule by the ECI
After the completion of nomination and scrutiny
After Parliament approves the election schedule
When the election results are declared
63.x: The Model Code of Conduct takes effect as soon as the ECI announces the election schedule, and lasts until the results.
63.tq: Recall when the Model Code starts.
n: The Model Code of Conduct comes into force immediately upon the ECI's formal announcement of the election schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
xs: The **Model Code of Conduct** comes into force **immediately upon the formal announcement of the election schedule** by the ECI — option **(1)**.
Held in **Harbans Singh Jalal v UoI (1997)**, **P&H HC**; it is lifted once **results are declared**.
xa: The MCC is **not statutory**; it rests on the ECI's plenary power under **Art. 324**.
First drafted by **Kerala** (**1960**); formalised by the ECI in **1968**; **Part VII** (party in power) added **1979**.
Enforced with rigour by CEC **T.N. Seshan** in **1991**.

63.s: The indelible election ink used in India is manufactured by which organisation and is based on which substance?

xa: Formula from the **National Physical Laboratory**; applied on the **left forefinger**.
First used in the **1962** general election.

63.s: The key chemical in the indelible ink used in Indian elections is:
63.x: Silver nitrate is the key chemical; the formula comes from the National Physical Laboratory and it is applied on the left forefinger.
xa: Manufacturer: **Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd** (Karnataka).
First used in **1962**.

63.s: Indelible ink was first used in the Indian general election of:
63.x: Indelible ink was first used in the 1962 general election. The claim that it was first used in Mysore in 1960 is incorrect.
63.tq: Reject the nearby but incorrect preliminary-use year.
xs: Indelible ink was first used in the **1962** general election — option **(3)**.
**1952** is the 1st Lok Sabha; **1957** and **1967** were other early general elections.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "first used in **1960** in Mysore" is wrong — **1960** = MCC in **Kerala**.
Made by **Mysore Paints and Varnish Ltd**; **silver nitrate** based.

63.s: The Supreme Court directed the inclusion of a NOTA option on all Electronic Voting Machines in:
o: Harbans Singh Jalal v Union of India, 1997
Mohinder Singh Gill v Chief Election Commissioner, 1978
Kuldip Nayar v Union of India, 2006
63.x: In PUCL v Union of India on 27 September 2013, the Supreme Court directed that a NOTA button be provided on all EVMs.
63.tq: Match the election-related judicial direction with the correct case and year.
xs: **PUCL v Union of India (27 September 2013)** ordered a **NOTA** button on all EVMs — option **(1)**.
**Harbans Singh Jalal** = MCC from schedule announcement; **Mohinder Singh Gill** = Art. 324 "reservoir of power"; **Kuldip Nayar** = vote a statutory right.
xa: PUCL (2013) also linked the **secret vote** to **Art. 19(1)(a)**.
NOTA symbol: ballot with a **black cross**, designed by **NID, Ahmedabad**.

63.s: The NOTA symbol, a ballot paper with a black cross, was designed by:
o: The National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad
63.x: The NOTA symbol was designed by NID Ahmedabad; it was first used in a Lok Sabha election in 2014.
xa: In 2014 NOTA took **1.1%** of votes (over **6 million**).
