73.s: Which one of the following is specifically associated with the functions of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
o: Appointment of State Human Rights Commissioners
Protection of minor forest produce ownership and tribal mineral and water rights
73.x: The NCST deals, among other matters, with ownership of minor forest produce, mineral and water rights, and rehabilitation of displaced tribal communities.
73.tq: Identify the commission from a distinctive cluster of subject-specific responsibilities.
xs: The NCST's extra work includes **minor forest produce ownership** and **mineral and water rights** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It also covers **rehabilitation of displaced tribals**.
xa: NCST: **Art. 338A**, **89th Amendment, 2003**, set up **19 Feb 2004**.
First NCST chairperson: **Kunwar Singh**.
Governments must **consult** the NCST on major policy matters (**Art. 338A(9)**).

73.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the civil-court powers of the National Commission while investigating a matter?
o: It can summon and examine a person on oath
It can require the discovery and production of documents
It can requisition public records from a court or office
It cannot issue commissions for the examination of witnesses
73.x: The Commission can issue commissions for examining witnesses, along with summoning persons, requiring documents, receiving affidavits and requisitioning records.
xa: APPSC-G1 **2022** keyed "all of these".
**NHRC** and **NCM** also have civil-court powers in inquiries.
⚠ APPCA (**Jun 2026**) says NCM has "no automatic civil-court powers"; the **NCM Act** does give them.

73.s: Who was the first chairperson of the separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes constituted in 2004?
73.x: Kunwar Singh was the first NCST chairperson (2004); Suraj Bhan headed the first separate NCSC and S.H. Ramdhan the combined commission (1992).
xa: The combined commission came from the **65th Amendment, 1990**.
Separate bodies: **NCST** w.e.f. **19 Feb 2004**, separate NCSC also from **2004**.
Current **NCBC** chair: **Niranjan Jyoti** (**2026**).

73.s: As of 2026, who heads the National Commission for Backward Classes?
73.x: Niranjan Jyoti was appointed Chairperson of the NCBC in 2026. Harjit Singh Grewal heads the National Commission for Minorities. Kunwar Singh and Suraj Bhan were the first chairpersons of the NCST and NCSC respectively.
73.tq: NCBC 2026: Niranjan Jyoti; NCM: Harjit Singh Grewal.
xs: **Niranjan Jyoti** heads the **NCBC** (appointed **2026**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Harjit Singh Grewal** heads the **NCM**; **Kunwar Singh** and **Suraj Bhan** were the first NCST and NCSC chairpersons.
xa: NCBC composition: Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and **three** members (**2026**).
The NCBC is under **Art. 338B** (**102nd Amendment Act, 2018**).
First chair of the combined SC/ST commission: **S.H. Ramdhan** (**1992**).

73.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional NCBC?
o: It is appointed by State Governors and exercises the powers of a tribunal.
It is appointed by the President and possesses powers of a civil court.
It is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and possesses criminal-court powers.
It is appointed by the Prime Minister and functions only as an advisory body without legal powers.
73.x: The Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and members of the constitutional NCBC are appointed by the President, and the Commission has civil-court powers.
73.tq: Apply the ‘who appoints and what powers’ test to avoid authority and function swaps.
xs: The constitutional NCBC is **appointed by the President** and has **powers of a civil court** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Not State Governors, the Speaker or the PM; and it has civil, not criminal, court powers.
xa: Composition: **Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson** + **3** members (**102nd Amendment**).
Civil-court powers under **Art 338(8)**, **338A** and **338B**.
Current chair: **Niranjan Jyoti** (**2026**).

73.s: Which of the following is NOT the function of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes ?
o: To investigate and monitor all matters relating to the safeguards provided for the Scheduled Castes under the Constitution
To submit the report to the Prime Minister related to the protection of Scheduled Castes
To inquire into specific complaints with respect to the deprivation of rights and safeguards of the Scheduled Castes
To advise on the planning process of socioeconomic development of the Scheduled Castes
73.x: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes submits its reports to the President of India, not to the Prime Minister. The President then places these reports before Parliament along with action taken by the government.

73.s: Who is the present Chairman of National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
Through which Constitutional Amendment Act, was the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) given status of constitutional body?
Article 338 of the Indian Constitution mandates formation of which of the following Commissions?
Under which Article of the Constitution of India, has the National Commission for Scheduled Castes been constituted?
73.x: Article 338 of the Constitution, originally provided for the establishment of a Special Officer for Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes (SCs and STs) to look into any issues pertaining to constitutional safeguards for the SCs and STs and to report to the President on their workings. Later, the 65th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1990, provided for the establishment of a high-level multi-member National Commission for SCs and STs in the place of a single Special Officer for SCs and STs. Again, the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2003, bifurcated the combined National Commission for SCs and STs into two separate bodies, namely, the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (under Article 338) and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (under Article 338-A).

73.s: Which of the following Constitutional Amendments is related to the formation of the National Commission for Backward Classes in India?
73.x: The One Hundred and Second (102nd) Amendment of the Constitution granted constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC). The amendment has inserted Article 338B, forming a commission for Socially and Educationally Backward Classes. Shri Hansraj Gangaram Ahir assumed charge as chairperson for the Commission on 02-12-2022 till now.

73.s: The Provision of National Commission for Scheduled Tribes is given in which Article of the Constitution?
73.x: The provision of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes has been made by Article 338-A. Originally, there was only Article 338 for the establishment of a commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (both), but the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 bifurcated the combined commission into two separate bodies. Article 338A was inserted for a separate commission for Scheduled Tribes. Article 338 now only provides for a commission for Scheduled Castes. The commissions constituted under Article 338 and 338A consist of a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and three other members.

73.s: Article 338 of the Indian Constitution deals with
Which Constitutional Amendment bifurcated the Combined National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes into two separate bodies?
73.x: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes was bifurcated into the National Commission for Scheduled Castes and the National Commission for Scheduled tribes through the 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003. The two commissions have been constituted under Article 338 and Article 338A, respectively.

73.s: Under which Article of the Constitution the Separate Scheduled Tribe Commission was established?
73.x: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes was established by amending Article 338 and inserting a new Article 338A in the Constitution through the Constitution (89th Amendment) Act, 2003.

74.s: Which body was set up in 2007 under a law enacted in 2005?
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
74.x: The NCPCR was set up in 2007 under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005.
xa: The NCPCR is one of the **WCD Ministry's** three statutory bodies, with the **NCW** and **CARA**.
It monitors the **RTE Act 2009**, **POCSO Act 2012** and **JJ Act 2015**.
The **NHRC** came under the **Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993** on **12 October 1993**.

74.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
74.x: The NCBC acquired constitutional status under the 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018, and Article 338B. The 89th Amendment Act, 2003, relates to the separation of the NCSC and NCST.
74.tq: Find the institution-amendment mismatch rather than the correctly matched statutory bodies.
xs: **NCBC — 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003** is wrongly matched — option **(1)**.
The NCBC became constitutional under **Art. 338B** by the **102nd Amendment 2018**; the **89th Amendment (2003)** split the NCSC and NCST.
The other pairs are right: **CVC** got the **CVC Act 2003** (earlier a **1964** resolution) and the **NCM** came under the **NCM Act, 1992**.
xa: Before 2018 the NCBC was **statutory** under the **NCBC Act 1993**.
The **89th Amendment** inserted **Art. 338A** for the **NCST**; separate bodies from **2004**.
Exam angle: "which of these is NOT a constitutional body" — only **NCSC, NCST, NCBC** are constitutional commissions.

74.s: The National Commission for Women was constituted in:
74.x: The NCW was constituted in January 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.
xa: First NCW chairperson: **Jayanti Patnaik** (**1992**); present: **Vijaya Rahatkar**.
⚠ **Rekha Sharma** was the chairperson in July **2023** (G2-GS 2023 key).
The NCW is one of the **WCD Ministry's** three statutory bodies, with **NCPCR** and **CARA**.

74.s: The NCPCR is a statutory body established under the
o: Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
74.x: The NCPCR was established under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005, although it monitors the implementation of several other child-related laws.
74.tq: Match the institution with its constituting statute rather than a law it monitors.
xs: The NCPCR is a statutory body under the **Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005** — option **(2)**.
It was set up in **2007**.
The **JJ Act 2015**, **POCSO Act 2012** and **RTE Act 2009** are Acts it monitors, not its parent Act.
xa: **SCPCRs** also come under the **CPCR Act 2005**.
The NCPCR checks laws against the **UNCRC**; India acceded in **1992**.
It is one of the **WCD Ministry's** statutory bodies with **NCW** and **CARA**.

74.s: Which of the following pairs regarding the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis is correctly matched?
o: Governing Act now in force — NCSK Act, 1993
74.x: The NCSK Act, 1993 lapsed in 2004, after which the NCSK continued as a non-statutory body under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
xa: Its tenure is extended by **government resolution**.
Jan **2022**: extended **three years** to **31 March 2025**; next to **31 March 2028**.
⚠ UPSC notes still call it a "statutory body".

74.s: Which statement regarding the National Human Rights Commission is correct?
o: It is a Statutory Body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
It is a Constitutional Body governed by Article 263.
It is a Constitutional Body governed by Article 338.
It is an Extra-Constitutional Body established by a Cabinet Resolution.
74.x: The NHRC is a statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. It has no Article of the Constitution behind it.
74.tq: Classify a body by where its power comes from: Constitution, statute or order.
n: Pairing the National Human Rights Commission with a constitutional Article is false. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The National Human Rights Commission is a statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
xs: The NHRC is a **Statutory Body** under the **Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993** — option **(1)**.
It was set up on **12 October 1993**, first through an **Ordinance of 28 Sep 1993**.
⚠ Pairing the NHRC with a **constitutional Article** is **false**; only **NCSC (Art. 338)**, **NCST (Art. 338A)** and **NCBC (Art. 338B)** are constitutional commissions.
**Article 338** belongs to the **NCSC**, not the NHRC.
xa: The same **PHRA 1993** also provides for the **State Human Rights Commissions**.
The NHRC conforms to the **Paris Principles** (Paris, **Oct 1991**; endorsed by the UNGA on **20 Dec 1993**).
The **NCBC** has been constitutional since **2018** (**102nd Amdt**); it was earlier statutory under the NCBC Act **1993**.
The **CVC** began by a **1964 resolution** and became statutory by the **CVC Act 2003**.

74.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: National Human Rights Commission — Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
Central Information Commission — Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
74.x: The NHRC and SHRCs come from the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. The Lokpal comes from the 2013 Act, the NGT from the 2010 Act and the CIC from the RTI Act, 2005.
n: The National Human Rights Commission and State Human Rights Commissions are statutory bodies under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Lokpal and Lokayuktas are statutory bodies under the Act of 2013. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The National Green Tribunal is a statutory body under the Act of 2010. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
The Central Information Commission is a statutory body under the Right to Information Act, 2005. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
xa: **Zonal Councils** are statutory under the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956** (**Section 15**).
**CVC** → **Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003**; **NCPCR** → CPCR Act, **2005** (set up **2007**).
⚠ Exam angle: "NHRC is constitutional" is a trap — it is **statutory**.

74.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The NCST is provided for under Article 338A.
2. The NCBC is provided for under Article 338B.
3. The National Commission for Women is provided for under Article 338C.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
74.x: The NCST (Article 338A) and NCBC (Article 338B) are constitutional bodies. The NCW is a statutory body under the NCW Act, 1990, not under any Article 338C.
xa: Only **NCSC, NCST and NCBC** are constitutional commissions; the **Finance Commission** (Art. **280**) is also constitutional.
⚠ Older notes still call the NCBC "statutory" — it has been constitutional since **2018** (statutory from **1993**).
The **65th Amendment (1990)** created a combined SC/ST Commission; the 89th split it, separate bodies from **2004**.

74.s: State Human Rights Commissions are established under the:
o: Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
74.x: SHRCs are set up under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993; human-rights functions in Delhi remain with the NHRC.
xa: SHRC jurisdiction covers only **State List and Concurrent List** subjects.
⚠ SHRC members are **appointed by the Governor** but **removed only by the President**.
After **2019**, an SHRC chair may be a former **Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court**.

74.s: After the 2019 amendment, the term of office of the NHRC Chairperson and members is:
o: Five years or until the age of 70
Three years or until the age of 70
Three years or until the age of 65
Five years or until the age of 65
74.x: Since 2019 the term is three years or until 70, whichever is earlier; earlier it was five years.
xa: Before 2019: chair only an **ex-CJI**, **2** human-rights members, term **five years** or age 70.
Removal is by the **President** after an **SC inquiry** for misbehaviour or incapacity.
The 2019 amendment added the **NCBC**, **NCPCR** chairs and the **Chief Commissioner for PwD** as deemed members.

74.s: Which of the following was NOT added as a deemed member of the NHRC by the 2019 amendment?
o: Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes
Chairperson of the National Commission for Women
Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
74.x: The NCW chairperson was already a deemed member before 2019; the amendment added the NCBC and NCPCR chairpersons and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities.
xa: Post-2019 NHRC: Chair + **3** members + deemed members; **3 years** or **70**.
The chair may now be a former **CJI or a Judge of the Supreme Court**.
At least **one** of the human-rights members must be a **woman**.

74.s:
Consider the following statements about the recommendations of the NHRC:
1. They are binding on the government.
2. The government is required to respond to them.
3. The Commission cannot compel implementation of its recommendations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: NHRC recommendations are not binding. However, the government must respond, and the Commission cannot compel their implementation.
74.tq: Separate the duty to respond from the power to compel implementation.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1 wrong: NHRC recommendations are **not binding**.
Statements 2 and 3 correct: the **government must respond**, but the Commission **cannot compel** implementation.
xa: In inquiries the NHRC has the powers of a **civil court**.
Example: notices to the AP **DGP** and **Chief Secretary** on the Sai Krishna **custodial death** (**28 Jun 2026**), citing **Art. 21**.
It cannot inquire into a matter **after one year** of the incident.

74.s: In which year was CEDAW adopted?
74.x: CEDAW was adopted in 1979; the Convention against Torture followed in 1984.
xa: The **UN Convention on the Rights of the Child** dates from **1989**; India acceded in **1992**.
**10 Dec** is **Human Rights Day**, marking the UDHR.
The **Paris Principles** (Oct **1991**) were endorsed by the UNGA on **20 Dec 1993**.

74.s: Under the 2019 amendment relating to State Human Rights Commissions, the Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission may be:
o: A former Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court
Only a serving Chief Justice of India
74.x: After the 2019 amendment, the Chairperson may be a former Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court.
74.tq: Watch the qualifying words ‘former’ and ‘High Court’ in eligibility questions.
xs: After the **2019** amendment an SHRC chair may be a **former Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court** — option **(2)**.
Earlier only a former **Chief Justice** of a High Court could chair it.
The parallel change for the **NHRC**: former **CJI or a Judge of the Supreme Court**.
xa: SHRC members are appointed by the **Governor** and removed only by the **President**.
The selection committee: **CM**, Speaker, Home Minister, Leader of Opposition (+ Council Chairman and LoP where a Council exists).
SHRCs take only **State List and Concurrent List** matters.

74.s:
Assertion (A): The National Commission for Women may appoint committees for particular purposes.
Reason (R): The National Commission for Women has no power to regulate its own procedure.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
74.x: The NCW can appoint committees and co-opt outsiders, and it may also regulate its own procedure, so R is false.
xa: NCW functions are listed in **Section 10** of the NCW Act, 1990.
It handles **complaints** and takes **suo motu notice**; commissions **special studies**.
It holds **Jan Sunwai** public hearings.

74.s: Who chairs the selection committee for appointing the NHRC Chairperson and members?
74.x: The Prime Minister chairs the six-member committee, which includes the Union Home Minister and the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
xa: Other members: the **Lok Sabha Speaker** and the **Leaders of Opposition in both Houses**.
The NHRC is appointed by the **President**; the **NCW** and **NCM** by the **Central Government**.
For an **SHRC**, the **Governor** appoints on a committee of the **CM**, Speaker, Home Minister and Leader of Opposition.

74.s: The NHRC cannot inquire into a matter after what period from the date of the alleged violation?
74.x: The NHRC cannot inquire into a complaint after one year from the date of the alleged violation.
xa: In inquiries the NHRC has **civil court** powers: summon witnesses, call for documents.
Recommendations are **not binding**; the government must respond.
Limited role over the **armed forces**.

74.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the removal of the Chairperson or a member of the NHRC on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity?
o: Removal by the Prime Minister on the advice of the selection committee
Removal by the President after an inquiry by the Supreme Court
Removal by Parliament through a special-majority resolution only
Removal by the Central Government by a simple order
74.x: For misbehaviour or incapacity, the President removes an NHRC member after the Supreme Court inquires into the charge. A is wrong because the PM chairs the selection committee but does not remove anyone. C is wrong because no parliamentary resolution is needed. D describes the NCW, whose members the Centre can remove.
74.tq: NHRC: President appoints and removes (after SC inquiry); NCW and NCM: Centre.
xs: An NHRC member is removed **by the President after an inquiry by the Supreme Court** for **misbehaviour or incapacity** — option **(2)**.
The **PM** only chairs the selection committee; he does not remove anyone.
Removal **by the Centre** is the rule for the **NCW**, not the NHRC.
xa: NHRC: Chair + **3** members + deemed members; **3 years** or **70**.
⚠ **SHRC** members are appointed by the **Governor** but removed only by the **President**.
The selection committee includes the **Lok Sabha Speaker**, **Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman**, both **LoPs** and the **Home Minister**.

74.s: Who is the common Chairman of the Zonal Councils?
74.x: The Union Home Minister chairs all the Zonal Councils.
74.tq: Recall who chairs the Zonal Councils.
n: The Home Minister is the common Chairman of the Zonal Councils. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #65 · pp 172-176]
xs: The **Union Home Minister** is the **common Chairman** of the **Zonal Councils** — option **(1)**.
The Zonal Councils are **statutory** bodies under the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**, **Section 15**.
xa: Other statutory bodies: **NHRC** (PHRA **1993**), **Lokpal** (Act of **2013**), **NGT** (Act of **2010**), **CIC** (RTI Act **2005**).
The **Finance Commission** is **constitutional** (**Art. 280**), unlike the Zonal Councils.
The **Union Home Minister** also sits on the **NHRC** appointment committee chaired by the **PM**.

74.s: A State Human Rights Commission may inquire into a matter only when it relates to
o: Any matter regardless of its legislative list
The State List or the Concurrent List and is not already before the NHRC or another statutory commission
Only matters already decided by a court
74.x: The jurisdiction of an SHRC extends to matters in the State List and Concurrent List, but it cannot inquire into a matter already pending before the NHRC or another statutory commission.
74.tq: Apply both jurisdictional limits: legislative list and prior institutional consideration.
xs: An SHRC may inquire only into **State List or Concurrent List** matters **not already before the NHRC or another statutory commission** — option **(2)**.
So the **Union List** alone or "any matter" are wrong.
It also will not take a case already pending elsewhere.
xa: SHRCs are set up under the **PHRA 1993**.
The **2019 amendment** lets the Centre give **UT** functions to SHRCs; **Delhi** stays with the NHRC.
⚠ SHRC: **appointed by the Governor**, **removed by the President**.

74.s: The Chairperson and members of a State Human Rights Commission are appointed by ______ but can be removed only by ______.
74.x: The Governor appoints SHRC members on the recommendation of a committee of the Chief Minister, Speaker, Home Minister and Leader of Opposition (plus the Council Chairman and its LoP where a Council exists). Only the President can remove them. A reverses the two roles. The Chief Minister chairs the committee but does not appoint, and the State Legislature has no power to remove.
74.tq: SHRC: Governor appoints, President removes (like SPSC).
xs: SHRC members are appointed by **the Governor** but removed only by **the President** — option **(2)**.
The Governor acts on a committee of the **CM**, **Speaker**, **Home Minister** and **Leader of Opposition**.
The CM only sits on the committee; the **State Legislature** has no removal role.
xa: Where a Council exists, the **Council Chairman** and its **LoP** join the committee.
For the **NHRC**, the **President** appoints on a committee chaired by the **PM**.
After **2019** the SHRC chair is a former **Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court**.

74.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Human Rights Commission functions from:
74.x: The Andhra Pradesh State Human Rights Commission works from Kurnool.
74.tq: Use location discrimination among major Andhra Pradesh cities.
xs: The **AP State Human Rights Commission** works from **Kurnool** — option **(3)**.
It is an SHRC under the **PHRA 1993**.
Its members are appointed by the **Governor** and removed only by the **President**.
xa: The **AP Commission for Backward Classes** rests on the **AP Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993** and is a permanent body.
The NHRC sought reports from the AP DGP, Chief Secretary and **AP SHRC** on **Gade Sai Krishna's** custodial death (**28 Jun 2026**).
SHRCs take only **State List and Concurrent List** matters.

74.s: Reports of State commissions constituted under State laws are submitted to the:
o: Governor and laid before the State Legislature
Chief Minister and laid before the Union Cabinet
High Court and laid before the Legislative Council only
74.x: Reports of State commissions go to the Governor and are laid before the State Legislature.
74.tq: Apply the State-level reporting chain and reject the Union-level authority trap.
xs: Reports of State commissions go to the **Governor** and are **laid before the State Legislature** — option **(2)**.
These commissions are created by **State laws**, so their reports stay within the State.
The President, Parliament and Union Cabinet have no role in the notes for State commission reports.
xa: ⚠ **Art 338(9)** and **338A(10)** do not create State commissions; they make the **Union and States consult** the national commission.
AP: the **AP State Commission for SCs and STs Act, 2003**; the body was **reconstituted in 2016**.
AP State SC Commission chairman **K.S. Jawahar** took **196 petitions** in SPSR Nellore (**28 Aug 2026**).

74.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Women:
1. Its Chairperson, Members and Member-Secretary are appointed by the President of India.
2. It consists of a Chairperson, five Members and a Member-Secretary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
74.x: Statement 2 is correct: the NCW has a Chairperson, five Members (at least one SC and one ST) and a Member-Secretary. Statement 1 is wrong: all of them are nominated by the Central Government, not appointed by the President (contrast the NHRC, appointed by the President). So '2 only'.
74.tq: NHRC = President; NCW and NCM = Central Government.
xs: Only statement 2 is correct — the NCW has a **Chairperson, five Members and a Member-Secretary** — so option **(1)**, **2 only**.
Statement 1 is wrong: all of them are **nominated by the Central Government**, not appointed by the **President**.
⚠ Contrast: the **NHRC** is appointed by the **President**; **NCW** and **NCM** are appointed by the **Central Government**.
xa: The NCW is a **statutory body** under the **NCW Act, 1990**, constituted in **January 1992**.
Among the five Members, at least **1 SC** and **1 ST**; term **3 years**, removal by the Centre.
The **NCM** has a Chair + Vice-Chair + **5 members** (7 in all), also appointed by the **Central Government, not the President**.
NCW is one of the **WCD Ministry**'s three statutory bodies, with **NCPCR** and **CARA**.

74.s:
With regard to the National Commission for Minorities, which of the following statements is correct?
1. It is appointed by the Central Government.
2. Its members are appointed by the President.
3. Five members including the Chairperson belong to minority communities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: The NCM is appointed by the Central Government, not by the President. Five of its seven members, including the Chairperson, are from minority communities.
74.tq: Separate the appointing authority from the composition requirement.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: the NCM is appointed by the **Central Government**.
Statement 2 wrong: it is **not** appointed by the **President**.
Statement 3 correct: **5 including the chair** must be from minorities.
xa: NCM: Chair + Vice-Chair + **5 members** (**7** in all); term **3 years**.
The **Vice-Chair** post was added by the **1995** amendment.
⚠ **NHRC** = appointed by the **President**; **NCW** and **NCM** = **Central Government**.

74.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the National Commission for Women?
o: Suggesting amendments to laws affecting women
Taking suo motu notice where women’s rights are denied
Commissioning special studies on discrimination and atrocities against women
Enforcing criminal sentences imposed by courts
74.x: The NCW reviews laws, suggests amendments, takes suo motu notice and commissions special studies; it does not enforce criminal sentences imposed by courts.
xa: It reviews constitutional and **legal safeguards** for women and advises on policy.
The **Central Government must consult the NCW** on all major policy matters affecting women.
**Jan Sunwai**: the NCW's public hearings of women's grievances.

74.s: In the context of women’s rights, ‘Jan Sunwai’ refers to:
o: An annual financial audit of women’s commissions
A public hearing of women’s grievances
A legislative session on gender budgeting
74.x: Jan Sunwai refers to public hearings held to hear and address women’s grievances.
xa: The AP zones included **Nellore**, **Guntur**, **Vijayawada** and **Rajamahendravaram**.
AP Mahila Commission chairperson: **Rayapati Sailaja**.
The NCW takes **complaints and suo motu notice** under **Section 10** of its Act.

74.s: The NCPCR’s mandate includes examining whether laws and policies are in conformity with the
o: Paris Agreement and the Constitution alone
Convention against Torture and the Geneva Conventions
Constitution of India and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights alone

74.s: Which of the following correctly explains the relevance of Articles 338(9) and 338A(10)?
o: They directly establish all State commissions.
They empower the President to appoint all State commission members.

74.x: Articles 338(9) and 338A(10) concern consultation with the National Commissions on major policy matters; they do not create State commissions.

xs: **Art 338(9)** and **338A(10)** require the **Union and States to consult** the national commission on policy matters — option **(4)**.

State commissions are created by **State laws** and report to the **Governor**.

74.s: Who was the Chairperson of the National Commission for Women in July 2023?

NCW: Chairperson + **5 members** + Member-Secretary, nominated by the **Central Government**.
NCW term: **3 years**.

74.s: In 2026, which commission began a full review of proposals relating to de-reservation of posts?

The **89th Amendment (2003)** split the combined SC/ST Commission created by the **65th Amendment (1990)**.
⚠ **Art 338(9)** makes the Union and States **consult** the NCSC on policy.

74.x: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) is a Statutory body. It was established in 1993 under a legislation enacted by the Parliament. 75.s: The first Lokpal Bill was presented in the Parliament in–
75.x: The first Lokpal Bill was presented in 1968 during the fourth Lok Sabha, where it was passed in 1969, but before it could be passed by the Rajya Sabha, the Lok Sabha was dissolved, and the bill lapsed.

75.s: Who coined the term ‘Lokpal’?
75.x: The word ‘Lokpal’ was coined by Dr. L.M. Singhvi.
75.tq: Test the person associated with the exact origin of a term.
xs: The term **Lokpal** was coined by **Dr. L.M. Singhvi** in **1963** — option **(3)**.
Lokpal is the Indian equivalent of the **Ombudsman** at the Union; the State equivalent is the **Lokayukta**.
The Ombudsman itself began in **Sweden in 1809**.
xa: The **first Lokpal Bill** was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** in **1968**.
The **First ARC (1966-70)** recommended a **Lokpal** for the Union and a **Lokayukta** in every State.
⚠ **1809** Sweden ombudsman ≠ **1766** Sweden RTI law.

75.s: The institution of Ombudsman was first established in which country in 1809?
75.x: The Ombudsman institution was first set up in Sweden in 1809. Sweden’s 1766 law is associated with the right to information, not the origin of the Ombudsman institution.
75.tq: Use the date-place pair and distinguish it from the nearby 1766 Swedish fact.
xs: The **Ombudsman** was first set up in **Sweden in 1809** — option **(1)**.
⚠ Sweden's **1766** law is about RTI, not the Ombudsman.
India's equivalents are the **Lokpal** (Union) and **Lokayukta** (State).
xa: The term Lokpal was coined by **Dr. L.M. Singhvi** (**1963**).
First Lokayukta in India: **Maharashtra, 1971**; first State law: **Odisha, 1970**.
First Lokpal Bill: **1968**.

75.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the Indian equivalents of the Ombudsman at the Union and State levels respectively?
75.x: Lokpal is the Ombudsman institution at the Union level, while Lokayukta performs the corresponding role at the State level.
75.tq: Discriminate between the two similar terms by matching them with Union and State levels.
xs: The Union and State equivalents of the Ombudsman are the **Lokpal and Lokayukta** — option **(1)**.
The **Lokpal** works at the Union level; the **Lokayukta** in the States.
The **CVC** came from the **Santhanam Committee**; it is not the Ombudsman.
xa: The **First ARC** recommended this two-tier model in **1966**.
The term Lokpal was coined by **Dr. L.M. Singhvi**.
Every State had to set up a Lokayukta within **one year** under **Section 63** of the **2013** Act.

75.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the First Administrative Reforms Commission from the Santhanam Committee?
o: The First ARC recommended the CVC, whereas the Santhanam Committee recommended the Lokpal.
The First ARC recommended a two-tier Lokpal-Lokayukta system, whereas the Santhanam Committee recommended the CVC and the CBI.
The Santhanam Committee recommended the Lokayukta for States, whereas the First ARC recommended only the CBI.
Both bodies recommended only the Lokpal at the Union level.
75.x: The First ARC recommended Lokpal at the Union level and Lokayukta in the States. The Santhanam Committee was associated with the CVC and the CBI, not the Lokpal.
75.tq: Separate closely associated anti-corruption bodies by assigning each recommendation to the correct committee.
xs: The **First ARC** recommended a **two-tier Lokpal-Lokayukta** system; the **Santhanam Committee** recommended the **CVC and the CBI** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **Santhanam** → CVC + CBI; **First ARC** → Lokpal + Lokayukta.
The Santhanam Committee did not recommend the Lokpal.
xa: Santhanam Committee: **1962-64**, chaired by **K. Santhanam**.
The ARC's interim report "**Problems of Redressal of Citizens' Grievances**" (**1966**) carried the two-tier idea.
The **Second ARC (2007)** strongly reiterated the Lokpal recommendation.

75.s: In which year did the First Administrative Reforms Commission recommend a two-tier Lokpal-Lokayukta system?
75.x: The First ARC made the recommendation in 1966; the Second ARC reiterated it in 2007.
xa: Santhanam recommended the **CVC** and **CBI**, not the Lokpal.
First ARC chair: **Morarji Desai**, later **K. Hanumanthaiya**.
The first Lokpal Bill followed in **1968**.

75.s: In which year did the Lok Sabha pass the First Lokpal Bill?
75.x: The First Lokpal Bill, introduced in the Lok Sabha, was passed by it in 1969 and lapsed on the dissolution of that Lok Sabha.
xa: Exam angle: options mix **1968** (introduced) with **1969** (passed by the Lok Sabha) — read the verb.
Final passage came in **December 2013**, after the **Anna Hazare** movement.

75.s: In which year did Parliament pass the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill?
75.x: Parliament passed the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill in December 2013, after the Bill's re-introduction in 2008.
xa: The Rajya Sabha passed it on **17 December 2013** and the Lok Sabha on **18 December 2013**.
President's assent: **1 January 2014**; in force: **16 January 2014**.
The Lokpal began functioning on **27 March 2019**.

75.s: The India Against Corruption movement was led by
75.x: India Against Corruption was led by Anna Hazare and was central to the 2011 civil society campaign for the Jan Lokpal Bill.

xs: **India Against Corruption (IAC)** was led by **Anna Hazare** — option **(1)**.

**Shanti Bhushan** and **Prashant Bhushan** sat on the civil-society side of the drafting panel; **Pranab Mukherjee** chaired it for the Government.
xa: Fasts: **Jantar Mantar (April 2011)** and **Ramlila Maidan (August 2011)**.
Civil-society members also included **Arvind Kejriwal** and **Justice N. Santosh Hegde**.
The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill was passed in **December 2013**.

75.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the dates associated with the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013?
o: Assent was given on 1 January 2014 and the Act came into force on 16 January 2014.
Assent was given on 16 January 2014 and the Act came into force on 1 January 2014.
Both assent and commencement took place on 1 January 2014.
Both assent and commencement took place on 16 January 2014.

xs: **Assent** came on **1 January 2014** and the Act **came into force** on **16 January 2014** — option **(1)**.
⚠ TH (**23 Mar 2026**) wrongly gives 1 January 2014 as commencement — that is the assent date.
**16 January 2014** is the APPSC key (APPSC **2019**, G2 **2025**).
xa: Parliament passed it on **17 December 2013** (Rajya Sabha) and **18 December 2013** (Lok Sabha).
The Lokpal actually began functioning on **27 March 2019**.
The Lokpal is a **statutory body**, not constitutional.

75.s: The Inquiry Wing of the Lokpal conducts preliminary inquiry into offences under the:
75.x: The Inquiry Wing conducts preliminary inquiries into offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
75.tq: Use the statutory subject of the inquiry rather than the name of the investigating wing alone.
xs: The Inquiry Wing makes preliminary inquiries into offences under the **Prevention of Corruption Act** (PCA) — option **(2)**.
It is headed by a **Director of Inquiry** (**Section 11**).
Its report after a reference is due in **60 days**.
xa: SC **split verdict** on **Section 17A** of the PCA (prior approval before investigation), **22 Jan 2026**.
Justice **K.V. Viswanathan** upheld 17A only with a **binding opinion of the Lokpal/Lokayukta**; Justice **B.V. Nagarathna** held it unconstitutional.
AP's **ACB** investigates **Prevention of Corruption Act** offences.

75.s: Which one of the following is the principal role of the Anti-Corruption Bureau in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Receiving complaints and submitting recommendations to the Governor
Investigating offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, including trap and disproportionate-assets cases
Advising departments on disciplinary matters without investigating offences
Exercising superintendence over the Central Bureau of Investigation in all cases
75.x: The Anti-Corruption Bureau is a police investigating agency that investigates Prevention of Corruption Act offences, including trap and disproportionate-assets cases.

xs: The ACB's main role is **investigating offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act**, including **trap** and **disproportionate-assets** cases — option **(2)**.
Receiving complaints and recommending to the Governor is the **Lokayukta's** role.
Advising departments is the **State Vigilance Commission's** role.
xa: AP ACB head (IG level): **R. Jayalakshmi** (Apr **2026**).
Many Lokayuktas depend on the **state police/ACB** for investigation.
The State Vigilance Commission dates from **1964**.

75.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. First Lokpal Bill introduced
B. Sweden established the first ombudsman
C. Maharashtra established the first Lokayukta
D. First Lokpal appointed in India
75.x: Sweden’s first ombudsman dates to 1809, the first Lokpal Bill to 1968, Maharashtra’s first Lokayukta to 1971, and India’s first Lokpal appointment to 2019.
75.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two middle events by year.
xs: The order is **B, A, C, D** — option **(1)**.
B: Sweden's first ombudsman, **1809**; A: first Lokpal Bill, **1968**.
C: Maharashtra's first Lokayukta, **1971**; D: first Lokpal appointed, **2019**.
xa: The term Lokpal was coined by **Dr. L.M. Singhvi** in **1963**.
Odisha passed the first Lokayukta law in **1970**.

75.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The institution of Ombudsman was first created in Sweden in 1809.
2. The First Administrative Reforms Commission was set up in 1966.
3. The First Administrative Reforms Commission recommended Lokpal and Lokayuktas.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
75.x: All three are correct: the Ombudsman began in Sweden (1809), and the First ARC (1966) recommended Lokpal and Lokayuktas.
n: The institution of Ombudsman was first created in Sweden in 1809. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
The First Administrative Reforms Commission was established in 1966. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
The First Administrative Reforms Commission recommended the establishment of Lokpal and Lokayuktas. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Morarji Desai submitted the interim report of the First Administrative Reforms Commission on Lokpal and Lokayuktas. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xa: The First ARC proposed **two tiers**: **Lokpal** for the Union and a **Lokayukta in every State**.
Desai was later replaced by **K. Hanumanthaiya** after he joined the Cabinet.

⚠ **1809** Sweden ombudsman ≠ **1766** Sweden RTI law.

75.s: The Lokpal is a:
o: Body created by a Constitutional Amendment
75.x: The Lokpal is established by statute and is not a constitutional body.

75.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Lokpal is correct?
o: The Lokpal may inquire into a complaint filed at any time after the alleged offence.
A Chairperson or member of the Lokpal may simultaneously be an MP or MLA.

75.x: A Chairperson or member of the Lokpal cannot be a Member of Parliament or a Member of a Legislative Assembly. The Act also covers public servants outside India and bars complaints filed after seven years from the alleged offence.

xs: A Lokpal Chairperson or member **cannot be an MP or MLA** — option **(4)**.
Option 1 wrong: complaints made **after seven years** from the alleged offence are barred.
Option 3 wrong: the Act covers public servants **in and outside India** (UKPSC **2025** key).
xa: Term: **5 years or age 70**, whichever earlier; **no reappointment**.
Chairperson eligibility: former **CJI**, an **SC judge**, or an eminent person with **25 years'** experience.

75.s: An eminent person may be appointed Chairperson of the Lokpal if he or she has at least ____ years' experience in specified fields.

Present chair: **Justice A.M. Khanwilkar**, a retired SC judge.

75.s: The term of office of the Chairperson or a member of the Lokpal is
o: six years irrespective of age, with one reappointment
eight years or until attaining 70 years of age, whichever is later
five years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is later, with reappointment permitted
five years or until attaining 70 years of age, whichever is earlier, with no reappointment
75.x: The term is five years or until the age of 70, whichever is earlier, and reappointment is not permitted. A member may become Chairperson within the total five-year period.
75.tq: Watch the reversed comparison words 'earlier' and 'later' and the reappointment trap.
xs: The term is **five years or age 70**, whichever is **earlier**, with **no reappointment** — option **(4)**.
A member may become Chairperson within a **5-year** total.
The other options' terms do not match the Act.
xa: Bar: a Chairperson or member **cannot be an MP or MLA**.
The **Rajasthan** Lokayukta's tenure was cut from **8** years to **5** years (APPSC G1 **2018** key).
AP's new Lokayukta has a **5-year term** (**20 Aug 2026**).

75.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Selection Committee of the Lokpal?

3. The Act applies only to public servants posted within India.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
75.x: The Leader of the Opposition and an eminent jurist sit on the Selection Committee. Statement 3 is wrong: the Act also covers public servants outside India.
n: The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha is a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
An eminent jurist is a member of the Lokpal Selection Committee. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The minimum age for the Lokpal is 45 years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
The Lokpal Act covers public servants outside India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #22 · pp 52-55]
xa: Selection Committee chair: the **Prime Minister**; the **Rajya Sabha Chairman** is **not** a member.
Lokpal strength: **Chairperson + not more than 8 members**; **50%** judicial and at least **50%** from SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women.
Term: **5 years or age 70**, whichever earlier; no reappointment.
A Chairperson or Member cannot be an **MP or MLA**.

75.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the declaration of assets under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas law?
o: The original law covered the public servant, spouse and dependent children
The 2016 amendment placed the form and manner of declaration in the Constitution
The declaration was required within 30 days of entering office
After 2016, the form and manner are prescribed by the Central Government
75.x: The 2016 amendment left the form and manner to be prescribed by the Central Government, not by the Constitution.
xa: The **2016** amendment filled "a small gap" in the Act (UPSC Governance).
The **2013** Act also amended the **DSPE Act** (CBI Director's committee; a **Directorate of Prosecution**).
The Lokpal is a **statutory body**.

75.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Search Committee for the Lokpal?
o: It prepares a panel for consideration
It is constituted by the Selection Committee
It may have fewer than seven persons
At least half its members must be from SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women
75.x: The Search Committee must have at least seven persons.
xa: The Selection Committee is chaired by the **PM**.
The **President** makes the appointment.
The Lokpal bench itself must be at least **50%** from these groups.

75.s: The Lokpal consists of a Chairperson and not more than ____ members.
75.x: The Lokpal has a Chairperson and up to eight members, at least half of whom must be judicial members.
xa: At least **50%** must also be from **SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women** — the two 50% rules apply together.
Present bench: **6 members** against a sanctioned **8** (Jun **2026**).
Term: **5 years or age 70**.

75.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the jurisdiction of the Lokpal?
o: Central officials of Groups A, B, C and D — Group C and D complaints are referred to the CVC
Members of Parliament — all speeches and votes in Parliament are subject to inquiry
NGOs — covered only when they receive foreign contribution below ₹10 lakh
Indian public servants abroad — excluded because jurisdiction ends outside India
75.x: The Lokpal’s jurisdiction covers central officials of Groups A, B, C and D, while complaints against Group C and D officials are sent to the CVC, which reports back to the Lokpal. Parliamentary speeches and votes are excluded, NGOs are covered above the stated threshold, and public servants outside India are included.
75.tq: Separate closely related jurisdictional exceptions and administrative routes.
xs: **Central officials of Groups A, B, C and D** are covered, with **Group C and D** complaints going to the **CVC** — option **(1)**.
The CVC reports back to the Lokpal.
Option 2 wrong: anything said or any vote **in Parliament** is excluded; option 3 wrong: NGOs are covered above **₹10 lakh**; option 4 wrong: servants **outside India** are covered.
xa: The **PM** is covered with safeguards.
Bodies set up by an **Act of Parliament** or funded by government are covered.
Criticism: Group C/D in practice left to the **CVC**.

75.s: Which of the following categories of organisations comes within the Lokpal’s jurisdiction when the stated condition is fulfilled?
o: Only organisations receiving domestic donations above ₹10 lakh
Only constitutional bodies receiving no government funding
Every private company, irrespective of funding
NGOs, trusts and societies receiving foreign contributions above ₹10 lakh
75.x: NGOs, trusts and societies receiving foreign contributions above ₹10 lakh come within the stated jurisdiction of the Lokpal.
75.tq: Focus on both the organisation category and the exact monetary threshold.
xs: **NGOs, trusts and societies** receiving **foreign contribution above ₹10 lakh** (FCRA) are covered — option **(4)**.
The test is **foreign** contribution, not domestic donations.
Bodies set up by an **Act of Parliament** or **funded by government** are also covered.
xa: Central officials of **Groups A, B, C and D** are covered.
**Union Ministers** and **MPs** are covered.
Public servants **in and outside India** are covered.

75.s: Allegations against the Prime Minister relating to which of the following are excluded from the Lokpal's jurisdiction?
o: International relations, security, public order, atomic energy and space
75.x: All these areas, namely international relations, security, public order, atomic energy and space, are excluded from the Lokpal's jurisdiction over the Prime Minister.
xa: An inquiry against the PM needs the **full bench** and a **two-thirds** majority.
It is held **in camera**.
Complaints are barred **after seven years**.

75.s: An allegation against the Prime Minister relates to a matter not covered by the statutory exclusions. Which condition is required for an inquiry by the Lokpal?
o: Approval by the Union Cabinet through an open hearing
Prior approval of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha alone
Approval by the full Bench with at least a two-thirds majority, with the proceedings held in camera
Approval by a simple majority of any two members, in public proceedings
75.x: An inquiry against the Prime Minister requires approval of the full Bench by at least a two-thirds majority, and the inquiry is held in camera.
75.tq: Apply the special procedural safeguards to a concrete jurisdictional situation.
xs: An inquiry against the PM needs the **full Bench** with at least a **two-thirds majority**, held **in camera** — option **(3)**.
Neither the **Cabinet** nor the **Rajya Sabha Chairman** has a role.
A simple majority or public proceedings would not satisfy the safeguard.
xa: Excluded subjects: **international relations**, **security**, **public order**, **atomic energy and space**.
Lokpal: Chairperson + up to **8** members.
The Lokpal has **civil court** powers: summon persons, requisition records.

75.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the jurisdiction of the Lokpal?
o: It applies to Indian public servants both within and outside India
It extends to Union Ministers and Members of Parliament
It covers anything said or any vote given by an MP in Parliament
It covers bodies set up by an Act of Parliament or funded by the government
75.x: Anything said or any vote given by an MP in Parliament is outside the Lokpal's jurisdiction.
xa: NGOs with **foreign contribution above ₹10 lakh** are covered.
⚠ UPSC **2025** key marks the "not posted abroad" statement wrong.
Groups **A, B, C and D** officials are covered.

75.s: A preliminary inquiry under the Lokpal framework is ordinarily to be completed within:
75.x: A preliminary inquiry ordinarily takes 90 days, extendable by 90 more days for reasons recorded in writing.
xa: Inquiry Wing report: **60 days**.
Investigation: **6 months** + **6 months**.
Trial: **1 year**, extendable up to **2 years**.

75.s: Under the Lokpal framework, a trial by the Special Court is ordinarily to be completed within
o: six months, extendable by six months
one year, extendable up to two years
75.x: The Special Court trial has a one-year limit extendable up to two years. Six months plus six months is the investigation limit; 90 plus 90 days is the preliminary inquiry; 60 days is the Inquiry Wing's report.
75.tq: 60 days report, 90+90 inquiry, 6+6 months investigation, 1-2 years trial.
xs: A Special Court trial takes **one year**, extendable up to **two years** — option **(2)**.
**Six months + six months** is the investigation limit.
**90 + 90 days** is the preliminary inquiry; **60 days** the Inquiry Wing's report.
xa: The **Prosecution Wing** files cases before the **Special Court**.
It is headed by a **Director of Prosecution**.
The Lokpal can attach property even while **prosecution is pending**.

75.s:
While appointing a Lokayukta, the Governor generally consults which of the following?
1. Chief Justice of the High Court
2. Leader of the Opposition
3. Chief Election Commissioner
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: The Governor generally consults the Chief Justice of the High Court and the Leader of the Opposition. The Chief Election Commissioner is not part of this consultation process.
75.tq: Separate the prescribed consultation authorities from an unrelated constitutional authority.
xs: Items **1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)**.
The Governor generally consults the **Chief Justice of the High Court** and the **Leader of the Opposition**.
The **Chief Election Commissioner** has no role.
xa: The appointing authority is the **Governor** (APPSC key).
Reports go to the **Governor** annually.
Lokayuktas rely on **state investigating agencies**.

75.s: The recommendations of Lokayuktas are binding in:
75.x: Lokayukta recommendations are advisory in many States and binding only in some, not in every State.
xa: Weakness: many Lokayuktas have **no independent investigating wing**.
Karnataka is an exception with its own **Lokayukta Police** wing.
Criticism: executive attempts to **dilute powers** (e.g. **Delhi**).

75.s:
Assertion (A): In Andhra Pradesh, the Lokayukta deals with complaints against higher functionaries and the Upa-Lokayukta with the remaining functionaries.
Reason (R): The Chief Minister and Members of the Legislative Assembly are covered by the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
75.x: Both are true: the two bodies have differentiated functions and coverage includes the CM and MLAs, but coverage does not explain the division of work.
xa: Features: informal procedure, easy access, almost free and prompt service, **independence from executive control**.
⚠ It is **not** an interpreter of the Constitution (APPSC **2019** PYQ).
AP is among States with **Lokayukta + Upa-Lokayukta**, with Rajasthan, Karnataka and Maharashtra.

75.s: Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act is associated with the issue of:
o: Publication of the Corruption Perceptions Index
Appointment of the Central Vigilance Commissioner
General consent of States for all CBI investigations
Prior approval before investigating certain decisions or recommendations by public servants
75.x: Section 17A concerns prior approval for investigation in specified circumstances involving decisions or recommendations of public servants. Its interpretation has been the subject of a Supreme Court split verdict and debate over 'sanction paralysis'.
75.tq: Distinguish prior approval under the PCA from State general consent under the DSPE Act.
xs: **Section 17A** of the PC Act concerns **prior approval before investigation** of public servants — option **(4)**.
It was the subject of an SC **split verdict** (**22 Jan 2026**).
Justice **K.V. Viswanathan** upheld it only with a **binding opinion of the Lokpal/Lokayukta**.
xa: Justice **B.V. Nagarathna** held 17A unconstitutional.
The Lokpal's **Inquiry Wing** handles preliminary inquiries into **PCA** offences.
Criticism: the Lokpal has **no power of prior sanction**.

75.s: Who is the first Lokpal of our country?
75.x: On March 23rd, 2019, Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose was sworn in as the country's first Lokpal. President Ram Nath Kovind administered the oath to him. On 10th March 2024, Justice Ajay Manikrao Khanwilkar has been appointed as the Chairperson, Lokpal of India.

75.s: Who is the first Lokpal of our country?
75.x: The Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC) of India (1966-1970) recommended the setting up of two special authorities designated as 'Lokpal' and 'Lokayukta' for the redressal of citizen's grievances. According to the ARC, the chairperson and members shall be appointed by the President after obtaining the recommendations of a selection committee consisting of – (a) the Prime Minister – Chairperson (b) the Speaker of the Lok Sabha (c) the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha (d) the Chief Justice of India or a Judge of the Supreme Court nominated by him. (e) one eminent jurist. Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose was appointed the first Lokpal of India (a retired Supreme Court Judge). On 10th March, 2024 Ajay Manikrao Khanwilkar (retired Justice) has been appointed as the chairperson, Lokpal of India. 5. Who among the following has been appointed as the Chairperson of Lokpal of India in 2024? (a) Shri Justice Sanjay Yadav (b) Shri Justice Lingappa Narayana Swamy (c) Shri Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose (d) Shri Justice Ajay Manikrao Khanwilkar U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2024 Ans. (d) In year 2024, the former Judge of the Supreme Court of India, Justice Ajay Manikrao Khanwilkar was appointed as the Head of the Lokpal of India. He assumed the post on 10 March, 2024. Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghosh was the first Head of the India’s Lokpal. 6. Establishment of Lokpal and Lokayukta in India was recommended by – (a) Sarkaria Commission (b) Administrative Reforms Commission (c) Law Commission (d) Thakkar

75.s: The Lokpal actually began functioning on:
75.x: Although the Act came into force in 2014, the Lokpal began functioning on 27 March 2019 after its Chairperson and members were appointed.
75.tq: Distinguish commencement of an Act from the date on which an institution began functioning.
xs: The Lokpal actually began functioning on **27 March 2019** — option **(2)**.
This was after the chairperson and members were appointed.
**16 January 2014** is commencement, **1 January 2014** assent and **17 December 2013** Rajya Sabha passage.
xa: First Lokpal: **Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose**, appointed **17 March 2019** (UPSC notes: **19** March).
Criticism: the **2013** Act → first Lokpal only in **2019** shows delay.
Second chair: **Justice A.M. Khanwilkar** since **10 March 2024**.

75.s: Section 11 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, requires the establishment of
o: a vigilance wing headed by the CVC and an audit wing headed by the CAG
an inquiry wing headed by a Director of Inquiry and a prosecution wing headed by a Director of Prosecution
a judicial wing headed by the Chief Justice of India and a police wing headed by the CBI Director
a parliamentary wing headed by the Speaker and a prosecution wing headed by the Attorney General
75.x: Section 11 requires an inquiry wing headed by a Director of Inquiry and a prosecution wing headed by a Director of Prosecution.
75.tq: Match each statutory wing with its specifically designated head.
xs: **Section 11** requires an **inquiry wing** headed by a **Director of Inquiry**; a **prosecution wing** is headed by a **Director of Prosecution** — option **(2)**.
The prosecution wing files cases before the **Special Court**.
Both wings were **still being staffed** (parliamentary standing committee, **23 Mar 2026**).
xa: The Inquiry Wing was recently set up with **3 SPs** (general, economic/banking, cyber).
The Lokpal has **superintendence and direction** over the **CBI** in cases it refers.
It can **attach and confiscate** corruptly acquired property.

75.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the powers associated with the Lokpal?
o: Its Prosecution Wing files cases before the Special Court
It exercises superintendence and direction over the CBI in cases it refers
Tainted property can be attached only after the prosecution is over
It may summon persons and requisition records like a civil court
75.x: Property acquired by corrupt means can be attached and confiscated even while the prosecution is pending.
xa: It can also direct protection of documents and recommend **transfer/suspension** and disciplinary action.
⚠ The **CVC Act 2003** gives the CVC superintendence over the CBI in PCA cases generally; the Lokpal only in cases it refers.
Criticism: **dependence on the CBI**.

75.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: First Lokpal — Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose
Lokpal inquiry and prosecution wings — fully staffed from the commencement of the Act
Group C and D complaints — Central Vigilance Commission
75.x: The Lokpal’s inquiry wing under Section 11 and its prosecution wing were reported as still not fully staffed. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
75.tq: Find the overstated institutional claim containing the false completion detail.
xs: **Inquiry and prosecution wings — fully staffed from the commencement of the Act** is NOT correct — option **(3)**.
A parliamentary standing committee found both **still being staffed**; the **Director of Inquiry** appointment "in process" (**23 Mar 2026**).
The other pairs are right: first Lokpal **Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose**; began work **27 March 2019**; **Group C and D** complaints go to the **CVC**.
xa: Ghose left office on **27 May 2022**; the post was then vacant for about **two years**.
The Inquiry Wing was set up under **Section 11** with **3 SPs**.
Criticism: more than a decade after the Act, staffing is incomplete.

75.s: Who has been the second Chairperson of the Lokpal since 10 March 2024?
75.x: Justice Ajay Manikrao Khanwilkar, a retired Supreme Court judge, became the second Chairperson of the Lokpal on 10 March 2024.
75.tq: Distinguish the Chairperson from the judicial members of the bench.
xs: **Justice A.M. Khanwilkar** (**Ajay Manikrao Khanwilkar**) has been the second Lokpal chair since **10 March 2024** — option **(4)**.
He is a retired **SC judge**, appointed after a gap of nearly two years (UPPSC **2024** key).
**Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose** was the first; **Ritu Raj Awasthi** and **Lingappa Narayana Swamy** are judicial members.
xa: Ghose was appointed **17 March 2019** and left on **27 May 2022**.
Present bench: **6 members** against a sanctioned **8**.
Non-judicial members: **Sushil Chandra**, **Pankaj Kumar**, **Ajay Tirkey**.

75.s: Who was appointed the first Lokpal of India in March 2019?
75.x: Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose, a retired Supreme Court judge, became the first Lokpal in March 2019. Khanwilkar is the present (second) Chairperson since 2024; Santosh Hegde was Karnataka Lokayukta; Ritu Raj Awasthi is a judicial member.
75.tq: First Lokpal = P.C. Ghose (2019); second = Khanwilkar (2024).
xs: **Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose**, a retired **Supreme Court judge**, became the first Lokpal in **March 2019** — option **(3)**.
**Justice A.M. Khanwilkar** is the present (second) chair since **2024**.
**Justice N. Santosh Hegde** gave Karnataka's **Bellary** report; **Ritu Raj Awasthi** is a judicial member.
xa: APPSC answer for the first Lokpal's year: **2019** (APPSC **2018** key).
The Lokpal **started work** on **27 Mar 2019**.
Ghose left office on **27 May 2022**.

75.s: Which of the following correctly states the distinction between the Central Vigilance Commission and the Lokpal in relation to the Central Bureau of Investigation?
o: The CVC has superintendence over the CBI generally in Prevention of Corruption Act cases, whereas the Lokpal has it only in cases referred by the Lokpal.
The Lokpal has general superintendence, while the CVC acts only in cases referred by the Lokpal.
The Lokpal has superintendence over the CBI in every Prevention of Corruption Act case.
Neither the CVC nor the Lokpal has any relationship with the CBI.
75.x: The CVC Act, 2003 gives the CVC superintendence over the CBI in Prevention of Corruption Act cases generally. The Lokpal exercises such a role only in cases referred by it.
75.tq: Compare the scope words ‘generally’ and ‘only in cases it refers’.
xs: The **CVC** has superintendence over the **CBI** in **PCA cases generally**; the **Lokpal** only in **cases it refers** — option **(1)**.
The CVC's power comes from the **CVC Act 2003**.
So options 2-4 misstate the split.
xa: The **Santhanam Committee (1962-64)** recommended the **CVC** and **CBI**.
**Group C and D** complaints go from the Lokpal to the **CVC**, which reports back.
The 2013 Act amended the **DSPE Act** (CBI Director's committee; Directorate of Prosecution).

75.s:
Assertion (A): The first Lokpal Bill was presented in 1968.
Reason (R): Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose was the first Lokpal of India.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
75.x: Both are true but unrelated: the first Lokpal Bill was presented in 1968, while Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose became the first Lokpal only in 2019 under the 2013 Act.
75.tq: A later appointment cannot explain an earlier Bill.
n: The first Lokpal Bill was presented in 1968. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose was the first Lokpal of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xs: Both statements are true but unrelated — option **(2)**: R is **not** the correct explanation of A.
A: the **first Lokpal Bill** was introduced in **1968**, in the **Lok Sabha** (4th Lok Sabha).
R: **Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose** became the **first Lokpal** only in **2019**, under the **2013** Act.
xa: The 1968 Bill was **passed by the Lok Sabha** in **1969** but **lapsed** when that House was dissolved.
⚠ Read the verb: **1968** = first introduced; **1969** = first passed by the Lok Sabha.
The term **Lokpal** was coined by **Dr. L.M. Singhvi** in **1963**.
Present Lokpal: **Justice A.M. Khanwilkar**, since **10 March 2024**.

75.s: A complaint is made more than seven years after the alleged offence. Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the Lokpal:
o: can inquire only if the complaint concerns a Union Minister
cannot inquire into it after the statutory seven-year period
can inquire only after approval of the Rajya Sabha Chairman
must inquire into it because there is no limitation period
75.x: The Lokpal cannot inquire into a complaint made after seven years from the alleged offence.
75.tq: Apply the statutory time limit to a filing scenario.
xs: The Lokpal **cannot inquire** into a complaint made **after seven years** from the alleged offence — option **(2)**.
So there is a limitation period; it is not a Union Minister or Rajya Sabha Chairman exception.
The bar is **7 years** from the alleged offence.
xa: Inquiry Wing report after reference: **60 days**.
Preliminary inquiry: **90 days**, plus **90 days** with **reasons in writing**.
Investigation: **6 months**, extendable by **6 months**.
75.fixed: bar applies after expiry of seven years; 'seven years after' is ambiguous

75.s: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act required every State to establish a Lokayukta within:
o: Six months of the Act’s assent
Two years of the first Lokpal appointment
One year of the commencement of the Act
Five years of the establishment of the Central Vigilance Commission
75.x: Every State was required to set up a Lokayukta within one year of the commencement of the Act.
75.tq: Test the exact time limit and its starting point.
xs: Every State had to set up a Lokayukta within **one year of commencement** of the Act — option **(3)**.
This is **Section 63** of the **2013** Act.
Each State does so by **its own State law**.
xa: By **2013**, **21 States and 1 UT (Delhi)** already had Lokayuktas.
There is **no uniform model**; CDI asks the Centre to encourage a **uniform, robust model**.
The Act came into force on **16 January 2014**.

75.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the uniformity of Lokayukta institutions in India?
o: All States follow an identical Act and identical jurisdiction.
The Chief Justice of India determines the jurisdiction of every Lokayukta.
Each State establishes the institution under its own Lokayukta Act, resulting in differences in jurisdiction and coverage.
The Union Government appoints all Lokayuktas under one central law.
75.x: Lokayuktas are established under the respective State Acts, and there is no uniformity among States regarding jurisdiction, coverage of the Chief Minister or judicial qualifications.
75.tq: Reject the absolute uniformity claim and apply the federal institutional arrangement.
xs: Each State sets up its Lokayukta under **its own Lokayukta Act**, so jurisdiction and coverage differ — option **(3)**.
There is no uniformity in jurisdiction, **cover of the CM**, or **judicial qualification**.
Lokayuktas are appointed by the **Governor**, not the Union Government.
xa: CDI asks the Centre to encourage a **uniform, robust model**.
The CM is covered in **HP, AP, MP, Gujarat** but excluded in **Maharashtra, UP, Rajasthan, Bihar, Odisha**.
Judicial qualification is required in **UP, HP, AP, Gujarat, Odisha, Karnataka, Assam**.

75.s: The annual consolidated report of a State Lokayukta is submitted to the
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
75.x: The Lokayukta submits an annual consolidated report to the Governor.
75.tq: Test the reporting relationship by identifying the constitutional recipient.
xs: The Lokayukta submits an **annual consolidated report to the Governor** — option **(1)**.
The Governor is also the appointing authority.
In AP the Lokayukta/Upa-Lokayukta **reports to the Governor**.
xa: AP annual report **2025**: **7,431** cases handled, **3,654** disposed.
Recoveries facilitated: **₹15.29 crore**.
Nearly half the disposals concerned the **Revenue Department**.

75.s: Which of the following pairs of State and Lokayukta arrangement is correctly matched?
o: Uttar Pradesh — Officials designated as Lokpal
75.x: Punjab has officials designated as Lokpal. Bihar and Uttar Pradesh have only a Lokayukta, while Maharashtra has a Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta.
xa: Lokayukta + Upa-Lokayukta also in **Rajasthan, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh**.
**Himachal Pradesh** also has a Lokayukta only; **Odisha** also designates officials as "Lokpal".
⚠ This three-way pattern was **not** what the **First ARC** suggested.

75.s: Which State reduced the tenure of its Lokayukta from 8 years to 5 years?
75.x: Rajasthan cut its Lokayukta's tenure from eight to five years (APPSC G1 2018 key). Maharashtra, Karnataka and Bihar are not cited for this change.
75.tq: Rajasthan: 8 -> 5 years.
xs: **Rajasthan** cut its Lokayukta's tenure from **8 years to 5 years** — option **(3)**.
This is the APPSC G1 **2018** key.
Rajasthan's Lokayukta Act dates from **1973**.
xa: Rajasthan's **Section 7** keeps sexual harassment, caste discrimination and violence outside the Lokayukta's investigation.
Rajasthan has a **Lokayukta + Upa-Lokayukta** but needs **no judicial qualification**.
AP's new Lokayukta has a **5-year term**.

75.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the Karnataka Lokayukta model?
o: It was created under the Karnataka Lokayukta Act, 1971, without a police wing.
It was established under the Karnataka Lokayukta Act, 2013, with no investigative role.
It functions only as an advisory body under the Central Lokpal.
It was created under the Karnataka Lokayukta Act, 1984, and has its own Lokayukta Police wing.
75.x: The Karnataka Lokayukta was established under the Karnataka Lokayukta Act, 1984, and has its own Lokayukta Police wing.
75.tq: Combine the exact year with the distinctive institutional feature to reject near-date traps.
xs: Karnataka's Lokayukta was created under the **Karnataka Lokayukta Act, 1984** and has its own **Lokayukta Police** wing — option **(4)**.
**1971** is Maharashtra's year; **2013** is the central Lokpal Act.
It is not under the Lokpal; each State has **its own State law**.
xa: **Bellary** illegal iron ore mining report by **Justice N. Santosh Hegde** (**2011**).
Lokayukta Police caught **Shirahatti BJP MLA Chandru Lamani** taking a **₹5 lakh** bribe (**22 Feb 2026**).
Karnataka requires a **judicial qualification** and has an **Upa-Lokayukta**.

75.s: The Bellary illegal iron ore mining report of 2011 was associated with:
75.x: The Bellary illegal iron ore mining report was prepared under Justice N. Santosh Hegde in 2011.
75.tq: Match the report with its author while avoiding confusion with other Lokayukta-related names.
xs: The **Bellary** illegal iron ore mining report (**2011**) was by **Justice N. Santosh Hegde** — option **(3)**.
**Chandru Lamani** was caught in a **₹5 lakh** trap case; **Morarji Desai** chaired the First ARC; **Dr. L.M. Singhvi** coined "Lokpal".
Hegde was then the **Karnataka** Lokayukta.
xa: The report led to the **CM's resignation** and the arrest of **G. Janardhana Reddy**.
Mining leases were cancelled and thousands of crores recovered.
Hegde was also on the civil-society side of the **April 2011** Joint Drafting Committee.

75.s: The Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act was enacted in
75.x: The governing law is the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1983.
75.tq: Discriminate between the founding State Act and later central anti-corruption legislation.
xs: The **AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act** was enacted in **1983** — option **(2)**.
It was amended by the **AP Lokayukta (Amendment) Act, 2024**.
**1973** is Rajasthan's Act; **2013** the central Lokpal Act.

77.s: Which of the following districts constituted the original group of Aspirational Districts in Andhra Pradesh?
77.x: The original aspirational districts of Andhra Pradesh were Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam and YSR Kadapa.
77.tq: Recall the exact state-specific district combination.
xs: AP's original aspirational districts were **Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam and YSR Kadapa** — option **(3)**.
Visakhapatnam's agency area now lies in **ASR district**.
⚠ Lists naming **Kurnool** and **Anantapur** are WRONG.
xa: Current list (**2025-26**): **Alluri Sitharama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam, YSR Kadapa**.
Vizianagaram's poverty headcount: **8.66%**.
ASR's literacy is the lowest at **44.67%**.

77.s: Which of the following is the current set of Aspirational Districts of Andhra Pradesh mentioned for the 2025-26 State Survey?
o: Alluri Sitarama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam and YSR Kadapa
77.x: The current set mentioned is Alluri Sitarama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam and YSR Kadapa. Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam belong to the earlier list, while Kurnool and Anantapur are not included in the current set.
77.tq: Separate the earlier district list from the current list by focusing on the changed names.
xs: The current AP list is **Alluri Sitarama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam and YSR Kadapa** — option **(4)**.
**Vizianagaram** and **Visakhapatnam** belong to the original list.
⚠ **Kurnool** and **Anantapur** are not ADP districts (APPCA note is wrong).
xa: Visakhapatnam's agency area now lies in **ASR district**.
ASR literacy: **44.67%** (lowest).
Lagging regions: **North Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema**.

77.s:
Consider the following statements regarding regional disparities in Andhra Pradesh:
1. North Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema are identified as lagging regions.
2. The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 provided for a special package for seven backward districts.
3. These seven districts comprise three districts of Rayalaseema and four of North Coastal Andhra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
77.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the split is 4 Rayalaseema + 3 North Coastal, not 3 + 4. Hence '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' omits a true statement and the options with 3 include a false one.
77.tq: 7 backward districts = 4 Rayalaseema + 3 North Coastal (bigger region, bigger share).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **North Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema** are the lagging regions.
Statement 2: the **AP Reorganisation Act 2014** gave a special package for **7 backward districts**.
Statement 3 wrong: the split is **4 Rayalaseema + 3 North Coastal**.
xa: AP's ADP districts include **Parvathipuram Manyam** and **ASR** (North Coastal) and **YSR Kadapa** (Rayalaseema).
Vizianagaram poverty headcount: **8.66%**.
ASR literacy: **44.67%**.

78.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the forms of decentralisation?
o: Delegation transfers powers to elected local governments with their own revenue
Deconcentration shifts work to field offices of the same government
Delegation entrusts tasks to semi-autonomous bodies
Devolution transfers powers to elected local governments with their own mandate and revenue
78.x: Delegation entrusts tasks to semi-autonomous bodies; transferring powers to elected local governments with their own mandate and revenue is devolution.
xa: Under deconcentration the Centre keeps **full control** — the weakest form.
Delegated power **can be withdrawn at will**; devolved power cannot.
Devolution was attempted by the **73rd and 74th Amendments**.

78.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the corresponding dimension of decentralisation?
o: Political decentralisation — power to implement through staff and functions
Administrative decentralisation — power to decide through elected local bodies
Fiscal decentralisation — power to spend and raise funds and taxes
Political decentralisation — power to transfer grants from the Union
78.x: Fiscal decentralisation concerns the power to spend and raise funds and taxes. Political decentralisation concerns decision-making, while administrative decentralisation concerns implementation through staff and functions.
78.tq: Start from the sure pair and reject options that interchange decision-making, implementation and finance.
xs: **Fiscal decentralisation — power to spend and raise funds and taxes** is correct — option **(3)**.
**Political** decentralisation is the power to **decide** through elected local bodies.
**Administrative** decentralisation is the power to **implement** through staff and functions.
xa: India transferred **political** power, some **administrative** power and the **least fiscal** power.
Elected local bodies can be **powerless without fiscal decentralisation**.
The **3Fs**: **Funds, Functions, Functionaries**.
