78.s: Which statement most accurately describes the fiscal dimension of India's decentralisation experience?
o: Only fiscal power was transferred to local governments
Fiscal power was transferred more extensively than political power
Political, administrative and fiscal powers were transferred in equal measure
Political power was transferred, some administrative power followed, but fiscal power was transferred the least
78.x: India transferred political power, some administrative power and the least fiscal power. This uneven transfer is a central feature of the decentralisation gap.
78.tq: Read the relative comparison carefully and identify the correct ranking of transferred powers.
xs: India transferred **political** power, **some administrative** power and **fiscal power the least** — option **(4)**.
Devolving Schedule subjects, taxes and grants was **voluntary** for States — the gap.
So the transfers were not equal, and fiscal was the smallest.
xa: Without **fiscal decentralisation**, elected bodies can be **powerless**.
Incomplete **3Fs** leave PRIs as **implementing agencies**.
Fiscal dimension = power to **spend and raise** funds and taxes.

78.s: A State has regularly elected local bodies, but they lack adequate funds to perform their assigned functions. Which conclusion most accurately follows from the principle of decentralisation?
o: Without fiscal decentralisation, elected local bodies may remain powerless.
Fiscal decentralisation necessarily eliminates the role of State Governments.
Local bodies become constitutionally invalid if they lack sufficient funds.
Election alone automatically ensures effective local self-government.
78.x: Political decentralisation through elections is insufficient by itself. Local bodies require fiscal decentralisation and adequate financial powers to exercise their responsibilities effectively.
78.tq: Apply the distinction between elected institutions and the financial capacity required to make decentralisation effective.
xs: **Without fiscal decentralisation, elected local bodies may remain powerless** — option **(1)**.
Election gives **political** decentralisation but not the power to **spend and raise** funds.
India transferred the **least fiscal** power.
xa: The **3Fs**: **Funds, Functions, Functionaries**.
Incomplete devolution leaves PRIs as **implementing agencies**.
Devolving taxes and grants is **voluntary** for States.

78.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of decentralisation?
78.x: Autonomy, people's participation and empowerment of local communities are features of decentralisation. Instilling non-confidence among local communities is not a feature.
78.tq: Find the one negative formulation that does not belong to the standard features.
xs: **Instilling non-confidence among local communities** is NOT a feature — option **(4)**.
The features are **autonomy**, **people's participation** and **empowerment of local communities**.
This trap appeared in BPSC **2020**.
xa: Arguments for decentralisation: **proximity and information**, **participation**, **accountability and speed**, **political education**.
**Participation** turns subjects into citizens.
Decentralisation transfers authority **downward**.

78.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principle of subsidiarity?
o: Every function must be performed by the Union Government for uniformity
Local bodies may perform only those functions expressly delegated temporarily by the Centre
A function should be performed at the lowest level competent to do so and move upward only when that level cannot perform it
The highest tier should decide all functions and lower tiers should implement them
78.x: Subsidiarity assigns a function to the lowest competent level and permits movement to a higher level only when the lower level cannot perform it adequately.
78.tq: Apply the lowest-competent-level test to the institutional scenario.
xs: **Subsidiarity**: a function is done at the **lowest level competent to do it**, moving up only if that level cannot — option **(3)**.
The **2nd ARC** used it to divide functions among the **three tiers**.
Options giving everything to the Union or the top tier are the opposite.
xa: The **3Fs** are **Funds, Functions, Functionaries**.
Incomplete devolution leaves PRIs as **implementing agencies**.
⚠ Power that can be withdrawn at will is **delegation**, not devolution.

78.s: In the context of Panchayati Raj Institutions, the three Fs stand for:
78.x: The three Fs are Funds, Functions and Functionaries. Effective devolution requires all three rather than merely assigning responsibilities on paper.
78.tq: Use the standard acronym expansion as a direct institutional recall question.
xs: The **3Fs** are **Funds, Functions, Functionaries** — option **(2)**.
Incomplete devolution of these leaves PRIs as **implementing agencies**.
The other expansions are not used.
xa: **Subsidiarity**: function at the **lowest competent level**.
India transferred the **least fiscal** power.
Devolving subjects, taxes and grants is **voluntary** for States.

78.s:
Assertion (A): Local Self-Government is an exercise in democratic decentralisation.
Reason (R): It promotes community participation and local accountability.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
78.x: Both are true: local self-government is democratic decentralisation precisely because it brings people's participation and accountability to the local level. R explains A.
78.tq: Ask whether participation and accountability explain decentralisation.
n: Local self-government is an exercise in democratic decentralisation. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Local self-government involves community participation. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Local self-government involves local accountability. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xs: Both are true and R is the correct **explanation** of A — option **(1)**.
**Democratic decentralisation** means **community participation** and **local accountability** — not central control or mere administration.
So local self-government is democratic decentralisation because it brings participation and accountability to the local level.
xa: **Decentralisation** = authority transferred **downward**; **centralisation** = decisions at the **apex**.
Features of decentralisation: **autonomy, people's participation and empowerment** of local communities.
⚠ Weakest form = **deconcentration**; strongest = **devolution** (attempted by the **73rd and 74th Amendments**).
Three dimensions: **political** (decide), **administrative** (implement), **fiscal** (spend and raise).

78.s: Which of the following is NOT a functional area of local government?
78.x: Public health, sanitation and water supply are local functions; judicial review belongs to the higher courts.
n: Local self-government includes public health. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Local self-government includes sanitation. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Local self-government includes water supply. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Judicial Review is not a local-government function. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xa: **Rural development** is another listed local function.
⚠ Maintenance of **public order** is **not** a local-government function either.
⚠ Instilling **non-confidence** among local communities is **not** a feature of decentralisation (BPSC 2020).
Test: if the transferring authority can take power back at will → **delegation, not devolution**.

78.s: The Gandhian conception of village self-government is best represented by which one of the following?
o: A centralised planned state based on heavy industry
A republic of self-sufficient villages with decentralised economic and political power
A system of village administration controlled by departmental headquarters
A local-government system limited to implementation of centrally prepared plans
78.x: Gandhi advocated Gram Swaraj, conceived as a republic of self-sufficient villages with decentralised economic and political power.
78.tq: Use the direct contrast between the Gandhian and Nehruvian models.
xs: Gandhi's **Gram Swaraj** was a **republic of self-sufficient villages** with **decentralised economic and political power** — option **(2)**.
A **centralised planned state with heavy industry** was the **Nehruvian** view.
Gandhi wanted **self-contained villages**, cottage industry, **swadeshi, sarvodaya and trusteeship**.
xa: The **Gandhian Plan (1944)** by **Sriman Narayan Agarwal** reflected Gram Swaraj.
**Art. 40** was a compromise between **Gandhi** and **Ambedkar**.
⚠ **Ambedkar** saw the village as a seat of **caste domination**.

78.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Nehruvian approach to state and development?
o: A centralised planned state with emphasis on heavy industry
A state without central planning or national industrial priorities
A republic of self-sufficient villages based on cottage industries
Complete fiscal autonomy for village panchayats from the beginning of planning
78.x: The Nehruvian approach favoured a centralised planned state with heavy industry, as reflected in the National Planning Committee and the Bombay Plan.
78.tq: Use the ideology-based contrast and connect Nehruvian planning with heavy industry.
xs: The Nehruvian approach was a **centralised planned state** with **heavy industry** — option **(1)**.
It was like the **NPC** and **Bombay Plan**.
A republic of self-sufficient villages is **Gandhi's** Gram Swaraj.
xa: The **Community Development Programme (1952)** was run **top-down**.
Yet Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj at **Nagaur (Rajasthan)** on **2 Oct 1959**.
In the **1960s** planning grew more centralised.

78.s: On 4 November 1948, B.R. Ambedkar described the Indian village as which of the following?
o: The primary constitutional unit protected from all central authority
A seat of caste domination and a sink of localism, ignorance, narrow-mindedness and communalism
A model of decentralised economic and political power
78.x: Ambedkar criticised the village as a seat of caste domination and called it a sink of localism, a den of ignorance, narrow-mindedness and communalism on 4 November 1948.
78.tq: Use the exact descriptive expression and the associated date as the recall cue.
xs: Ambedkar called the village a seat of **caste domination** and "a **sink of localism**, a **den of ignorance, narrow-mindedness and communalism**" — option **(3)**.
He said this in the Constituent Assembly on **4 Nov 1948**.
A republic of self-sufficient villages is **Gandhi's** view.
xa: Ambedkar preferred **the individual** as unit of the republic.
**Art. 40** reconciled the two views: panchayats **named but non-justiciable**.
Gandhi's model: **Gram Swaraj**.

78.s: Article 40, on organising village panchayats, is a:
78.x: Article 40 is a Directive Principle in Part IV; it is non-justiciable.
xa: Art. 40 asks the State to **organise village panchayats** as **units of self-government**.
The **73rd Amendment** gave it practical shape.
It balanced **Gandhi's** Gram Swaraj with **Ambedkar's** reservations.

78.s: Article 40 is generally regarded as a compromise between which two perspectives?
o: The Gandhian advocacy of panchayats and Ambedkar's reservations about the village
The Union List and the State List
The Nehruvian advocacy of heavy industry and the Gandhian advocacy of cottage industry
78.x: Article 40 represented a compromise: panchayats were named as an objective, reflecting the Gandhian position, but the provision was made non-justiciable, accommodating Ambedkar's reservations.
78.tq: Identify the constitutional compromise by linking the institutional provision with the two contrasting viewpoints.
xs: **Art. 40** is a compromise between **Gandhian advocacy of panchayats** and **Ambedkar's reservations about the village** — option **(1)**.
Panchayats were **named** (Gandhi) but made **non-justiciable** (Ambedkar).
Heavy industry vs cottage industry is the **Nehru-Gandhi** contrast, not Art. 40.
xa: Ambedkar: village = **caste domination**; preferred unit = **the individual**.
Gandhi: **Gram Swaraj**.
The **73rd Amendment** gave Art. 40 its practical shape.

78.s: Despite favouring a centralised planned state, Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj at
78.x: Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj at Nagaur in Rajasthan on 2 October 1959. Andhra Pradesh followed on 1 November 1959; 1952 is the Community Development Programme year; January 1957 is when the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was appointed.
78.tq: Nagaur, 2 Oct 1959 - Rajasthan first, AP next.
xs: Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj at **Nagaur, Rajasthan, on 2 October 1959** — option **(1)**.
This was despite his preference for a **centralised planned state**.
**1952** is the **Community Development Programme** year.
xa: The CDP was run **top-down**.
The Nehruvian model resembled the **NPC** and **Bombay Plan**.
**Rajiv Gandhi's 64th Amendment Bill** came in **1989**.

78.s: Why did the 64th Amendment Bill of 1989 fail to become law?
o: It passed the Lok Sabha but failed in the Rajya Sabha amid fears of centralisation
It was rejected by the Supreme Court for violating Article 40
It failed to secure passage in the Lok Sabha because it opposed decentralisation
It lapsed because the State legislatures refused to ratify it unanimously
78.x: The 64th Amendment Bill, associated with Rajiv Gandhi, passed the Lok Sabha but failed in the Rajya Sabha because of fears that it would promote centralisation.
78.tq: Track the legislative chamber and the specific reason for failure rather than merely recalling the year.
xs: The **64th Amendment Bill (1989)** **passed the Lok Sabha but failed in the Rajya Sabha** amid **fears of centralisation** — option **(1)**.
⚠ It failed in the **Rajya Sabha**, not the Lok Sabha.
It was **Rajiv Gandhi's** Bill.
xa: The **V.P. Singh Bill (1990)** lapsed.
The **73rd and 74th Amendments** finally attempted devolution.
**Art. 40** got practical shape from the 73rd Amendment.

78.s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to organise Village Panchayats as units of self-government?
78.x: Article 40, a Directive Principle, tells the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government. Articles 243A, 243B and 243G came much later with the 73rd Amendment.
78.tq: Discriminate Article 40 (directive) from Part IX (the 73rd Amendment).
n: Article 40 of the Directive Principles of State Policy directs the State to organize Village Panchayats as units of self-government. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243A deals with the Gram Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243B provides for a three-tier system and exemption. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243G deals with the powers and responsibilities of Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xs: **Article 40** (DPSP) directs the State to organise **Village Panchayats** as units of self-government — option **(1)**.
It sits in **Part IV** and is **non-justiciable** — a compromise between **Gandhi** and **Ambedkar**.
The **73rd Amendment** gave Article 40 its **practical shape**.
xa: The **64th Amendment Bill (1989)** passed the Lok Sabha but **failed in the Rajya Sabha**.
The **V.P. Singh Bill (1990)** lapsed.
Ambedkar called the village "a sink of localism, a den of ignorance" (**4 Nov 1948**) and preferred **the individual**.
Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj at **Nagaur** (Rajasthan) on **2 Oct 1959**.

78.s: Which of the following was an argument advanced in favour of centralisation in India after Independence?
o: Local bodies possess complete knowledge of local needs
Nation-building after Partition required unity and security
78.x: Nation-building after Partition, along with the requirements of unity and security, was an argument for centralisation. The other options are arguments for decentralisation.
78.tq: Use the for-versus-against comparison and identify the nation-building rationale.
xs: **Nation-building after Partition**, unity and security was an argument for centralisation — option **(4)**.
Accountability and speed, participation, and local knowledge are arguments **for decentralisation**.
Other centralising arguments: a **single command** for heavy industry and food security, weak local **capacity**, **elite capture**.
xa: In the **1960s** planning grew more centralised and people's participation was diluted.
The **Community Development Programme (1952)** was run **top-down**.
The **Nehruvian** model was a **centralised planned state** with heavy industry.

78.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the arguments advanced in India in favour of centralisation?
o: Planned heavy industry was said to need a single command
Food security was said to need a single command
Weak local capacity was used as an argument for centralisation
Elite capture by dominant local castes was cited as a reason for decentralisation
78.x: The risk of elite capture by locally dominant castes was cited in favour of centralisation, not decentralisation.
xa: The other centralising argument: **nation-building after Partition**, unity and security.
Counter-arguments: **proximity**, **participation**, **accountability and speed**, **political education**.
Planning-era India: **deliberate centralisation** through Five-Year Plans and the **CDP**.

78.s: The power to take back an entrusted authority at will is the decisive test distinguishing which of the following?
78.x: If the transferring authority can withdraw the power at will, the arrangement is delegation rather than devolution. Devolved powers are not ordinarily withdrawable at will by the transferring authority.
78.tq: Apply the confusable-pair test by focusing on the power of withdrawal.
xs: The power to take authority back **at will** separates **devolution from delegation** — option **(1)**.
If it can be withdrawn at will → **delegation, not devolution**.
Devolution, the **strongest form**, cannot be withdrawn at will.
xa: Devolution goes to **elected local governments** with their own mandate and revenue.
The three dimensions: **political** (decide), **administrative** (implement), **fiscal** (spend and raise).
⚠ **Weakest = deconcentration**.

78.s: What is the principal consequence of incomplete devolution of the three Fs to Panchayati Raj Institutions?
o: They remain primarily implementing agencies rather than planning units
They replace the State legislature in rural areas
They become fully autonomous planning governments
They acquire complete control over State taxation
78.x: Without adequate funds, functions and functionaries, Panchayati Raj Institutions remain implementing agencies instead of becoming effective planning units.
78.tq: Trace the institutional consequence of an incomplete transfer of resources, responsibilities and personnel.
xs: With incomplete 3Fs, PRIs remain **implementing agencies**, not **planning units** — option **(1)**.
The 3Fs: **Funds, Functions, Functionaries**.
They do not replace the State legislature or control State taxes.
xa: Local bodies can be elected but **powerless without fiscal decentralisation**.
India gave **political** power, some **administrative** and **least fiscal** power.
The **2nd ARC** invoked **subsidiarity** for the three tiers.

78.s: Which of the following best illustrates historical village autonomy in the Andhra Pradesh region?
o: The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 under Article 253
The 12-Ayagar village administration associated with the Kakatiyas and Vijayanagara
The transfer of all local functions to the Union Government
The Justice Kurian Joseph committee on Union-State relations
78.x: The traditional 12-Ayagar village administration under the Kakatiyas and Vijayanagara is cited as an example of historical village autonomy in the Andhra region.
78.tq: Identify the historical institution by linking the distinctive administrative term with the dynasties associated with it.
xs: The **12-Ayagar** village administration of the **Kakatiyas** and **Vijayanagara** shows historical village autonomy — option **(2)**.
The **SWM Rules, 2026** are criticised as centralising.
The **Justice Kurian Joseph committee** dealt with Union-State relations.
xa: SWM Rules: in force **1 Apr 2026**, under **Art. 253**.
Gandhi's **Gram Swaraj** also idealised self-sufficient villages.
⚠ **Ambedkar** saw the village as a seat of **caste domination**.

78.s: Which one of the following is not an attribute of a Local Government?
o: Power to raise finances by taxation
78.x: The statutory status, participation of local community and power to raise funds by taxation are the attributes of local government, but Central control is not one of them because the objective of the establishment of local governments is decentralization of power.

78.s: Which one of the following Articles directs the State Governments to organize the Panchayats?
78.x: Article 40- "to organise village Panchayats and endow them with necessary powers and authority, to enable them to function as units of self - government. Article 33- Under Rights to Constitutional Remedies (Fundamental Rights), Power of Parliament to modify the rights conferred by this part in their application of forces, etc. Article 48- To prohibit the slaughter of cows, calves and other milch and draught cattle and to improve their breeds. Article 50- Separation of the Judiciary from the Executive.

79.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of local self-government?
o: Election by and accountability to local people
A defined local area and functions
79.x: Local self-government does not possess sovereignty or legislative supremacy. Its features include local accountability, defined functions, own funds and autonomy within State law.
79.tq: Locate the constitutional attribute that belongs to the sovereign State rather than a local body.
xs: **Sovereignty or legislative supremacy** is NOT a feature of local self-government — option **(2)**.
Its features: elected by and **accountable to local people**, a **defined local area and functions**, **own funds and taxing powers**, **autonomy within State law**.
It acts within **State law**, so it cannot be sovereign.
xa: **Judicial powers** are also not a feature — **Nyaya Panchayats** are separate.
**Control by a central department** is deconcentration, not local self-government.
Definition: transfer of power to **elected local bodies**.

79.s: Which one of the following was NOT a recommendation associated with the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee?
o: Constitutional status for Panchayati Raj Institutions
79.x: The committee recommended a three-tier system, genuine transfer of power and adequate resources. Constitutional status for PRIs was associated with later recommendations, particularly those of the L.M. Singhvi Committee.
79.tq: Find the recommendation belonging to a later committee rather than the committee under examination.
xs: **Constitutional status for PRIs** was NOT a Balwant Rai Mehta recommendation — option **(4)**.
Mehta recommended a **three-tier PRI**, **genuine transfer of power** and **adequate resources**.
Constitutional status came from the **Committee on Policy and Programmes (1988)**.
xa: That 1988 committee also sought a **5-year term**, **direct elections** and **State Finance and Election Commissions**.
The Mehta Committee was appointed **Jan 1957** and reported **Nov 1957**.
The **NDC** accepted it in **Jan 1958**.

79.s: In the context of the Ashok Mehta Committee, the provision concerning supersession of a local body was that:
o: Elections should be held only after five years of supersession
There should be no supersession, or elections should be held within six months
Supersession could continue indefinitely without elections
Supersession should be decided by the Union Cabinet
79.x: The committee recommended no supersession, or that polls should be conducted within six months if supersession occurred.
79.tq: Focus on the precise time limit and the alternative safeguard in a recommendation.
xs: **Ashok Mehta** sought **no supersession**, or **polls within 6 months** — option **(2)**.
He also wanted **compulsory taxation powers** and **social audit**.
He made the **district** the first point of decentralisation.
xa: The Ashok Mehta Committee sat in **1977-78**.
⚠ **Dantwala (1978) = block**; **Hanumantha Rao (1984) = district**.
**G.V.K. Rao (1985)**: "**grass without roots**".

79.s: The expression “grass without roots” was used in the context of which observation?
o: Development had become bureaucratised, requiring restoration of the Zila Parishad’s role
Municipal corporations had become financially autonomous
Village communities had acquired excessive judicial powers
79.x: The G.V.K. Rao Committee observed that development had become bureaucratised—described as “grass without roots”—and called for restoration of the Zila Parishad’s role.
79.tq: Match the distinctive phrase with the correct committee diagnosis.
xs: "**Grass without roots**" meant **development had become bureaucratised**, so the **Zila Parishad's** role should be restored — option **(1)**.
This was the **G.V.K. Rao (1985)** committee.
The other options do not match.
xa: **Ashok Mehta** made the **district** the first point of decentralisation.
**Hanumantha Rao (1984)**: **district planning** with the **Collector** coordinating.
The **1988** committee sought **constitutional status** for PRIs.

79.s:
The Committee on Policy and Programmes (1988) recommended which of the following?
1. Constitutional status for PRIs
2. A five-year term for PRIs
3. State Finance Commissions and State Election Commissions
79.x: The 1988 Committee recommended constitutional status, a five-year term, direct elections, and State Finance and Election Commissions.
xa: **Balwant Rai Mehta (1957)**: **adequate resources** and genuine transfer of power.
**Ashok Mehta (1977-78)**: **no supersession** or polls within **6 months**.
**G.V.K. Rao (1985)**: "**grass without roots**".

79.s: The Hanumantha Rao Committee (1984) recommended district planning coordinated by the:
79.x: The Hanumantha Rao Committee wanted the Collector to coordinate district planning.
xa: **Art. 243ZD** now provides a **District Planning Committee**.
**Ashok Mehta** made the **district** the first point of decentralisation.
**G.V.K. Rao (1985)**: restore the **Zila Parishad's** role.

79.s: Which committee recommended block-level planning in 1978?
79.x: The Dantwala Committee (1978) recommended block-level planning. The Hanumantha Rao Committee (1984) recommended district planning with the Collector coordinating it; G.V.K. Rao (1985) spoke of 'grass without roots'; Ashok Mehta (1977-78) made the district the first point of decentralisation.
xs: The **Dantwala Committee (1978)** recommended **block-level** planning — option **(2)**.
**Hanumantha Rao (1984)** recommended **district planning** with the Collector.
**G.V.K. Rao (1985)** spoke of "**grass without roots**"; **Ashok Mehta** made the **district** the first point.
xa: Both Dantwala and Hanumantha Rao put the basic planning function at the **district** level (UPSC).
**Art. 243ZD**: District Planning Committee.
Ashok Mehta sat in **1977-78**.

79.s: SabhaSaar, in the context of Gram Sabha functioning, is associated with:
o: Conduct of elections to Jammu and Kashmir DDCs
Collection of property tax by Zilla Parishads
Preparation of Gram Sabha minutes using an artificial intelligence tool
79.x: SabhaSaar is an AI tool associated with Gram Sabha minutes.
79.tq: Use the function of a named digital tool to distinguish it from unrelated Panchayati Raj activities.
xs: **SabhaSaar** is an **AI tool** for **Gram Sabha minutes** — option **(4)**.
It was noted in the **ES 2025-26** with **e-GramSwaraj**.
The Survey also discussed PRI **own-source revenue**.
xa: A report flagged **low Gram Sabha participation** (**1 Jul 2026**).
J&K **DDCs'** term ended **24 Feb 2026**.
**RGSA** trains PRI members.

79.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rajasthan was the first State to introduce Panchayati Raj.
2. Panchayati Raj was first inaugurated at Nagaur.
3. Andhra Pradesh followed Rajasthan on 1 November 1959.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: All three statements are correct. Rajasthan inaugurated Panchayati Raj at Nagaur on 2 October 1959, and Andhra Pradesh followed on 1 November 1959.
79.tq: Combine place, sequence and dates, checking whether all three linked statements are supported.
xs: All three statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(4)**.
**Rajasthan** was first, at **Nagaur**, on **2 Oct 1959**.
**Andhra Pradesh** followed on **1 Nov 1959**.
xa: The rollout followed the **Balwant Rai Mehta** recommendations, accepted by the **NDC** in **Jan 1958**.
AP has **13 Zilla Parishads** (May **2026**).
The three tiers: **Gram Panchayat**, **Panchayat Samiti**, **Zila Parishad**.

79.s: Local self-government can be best explained as an exercise in
79.x: UPSC 2017 keyed 'democratic decentralisation': power is transferred to elected local bodies. Federalism is about Union-State division; delegation can be withdrawn at will; direct democracy is citizens deciding without representatives.
xs: Local self-government is best explained as an exercise in **democratic decentralisation** (UPSC **2017**) — option **(2)**.
It means transferring power to **elected local bodies** for people's participation.
It is not **federalism** or **delegation**; local bodies have **autonomy within State law**.
xa: The term was coined by the **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee**.
PRIs were adopted to **decentralise the power of democracy** (UPPSC **2016**).
The fundamental objects: **people's participation in development** + **democratic decentralisation**.

79.s: Panchayati Raj Institutions brought which significant change in village governance?
o: Abolition of local participation in development
Direct control by Parliament over village decisions
79.x: PRIs brought formal representation of weaker sections in village governance and were adopted to decentralise democratic power.
79.tq: Test the social consequence of an institution rather than its organisational structure.
xs: PRIs brought **formal representation of the weaker sections** in village governance (APPSC **2019**) — option **(4)**.
They were adopted to **decentralise the power of democracy** (UPPSC **2016**).
They widened participation rather than abolishing it.
xa: Fundamental objects: **people's participation in development** + **democratic decentralisation** (UPSC **2015**).
Post-73rd needs: decentralisation of **decision-making**, **the system as a whole** and **administrative powers**.
⚠ **Not judicial powers** (BPSC **2022**).

79.s:
Assertion (A): Democratic decentralisation was a fundamental objective of Panchayati Raj.
Reason (R): Financial mobilisation was the primary constitutional objective of Panchayati Raj.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
79.x: The fundamental objectives were people's participation in development and democratic decentralisation; financial mobilisation was not, so R is false.
xa: PRIs brought **formal representation of the weaker sections** (APPSC **2019**).
They were adopted to **decentralise the power of democracy** (UPPSC **2016**).
The Mehta Committee held **local public participation** indispensable.

79.s: After the 73rd Amendment, which of the following is NOT considered necessary for effective Panchayati Raj?
o: Decentralisation of the system as a whole
79.x: The needs identified are decentralisation of decision-making, of administrative powers and of the system as a whole, not of judicial powers.
xa: PRIs brought **formal representation of the weaker sections**.
Fundamental objects: **people's participation** + **democratic decentralisation**.
Local bodies have no **sovereignty or legislative supremacy**.

79.s: The constitutional trace of the idea of Gram Swaraj is found in:
79.x: The constitutional trace of Gram Swaraj is found in Article 40, a Directive Principle of State Policy concerning village panchayats.
79.tq: Distinguish the Article associated with village self-government from nearby decentralisation provisions.
xs: The constitutional trace of Gram Swaraj is **Article 40** (DPSP) — option **(4)**.
**Art. 243ZD** is the **District Planning Committee**.
Gram Swaraj = a **self-reliant village republic**.
xa: The **1988** Committee on Policy and Programmes sought **constitutional status** for PRIs.
The **RGSA** was revamped for **1 Apr 2022 to 31 Mar 2026**.
**SVAMITVA** launched on **24 Apr 2020**.

79.s: Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan, which trains members of Panchayati Raj Institutions, is implemented by the:
79.x: RGSA is implemented by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj from 2018-19 to train PRI members.
xa: Revamped for **1 Apr 2022 to 31 Mar 2026**.
Funding: **60:40**; NE and hill States **90:10**.
ES **2025-26** noted **e-GramSwaraj** and **SabhaSaar**.

79.s: The District Planning Committee is constitutionally recognised as a coordinating body under:
79.x: The District Planning Committee is a constitutional coordinating body under Article 243ZD.
79.tq: Match the institution with its exact constitutional Article rather than a related Panchayati Raj provision.
xs: The **District Planning Committee** is a constitutional coordinating body under **Article 243ZD** — option **(2)**.
**Art. 40** is the DPSP trace of Gram Swaraj.
District planning was recommended by **Hanumantha Rao (1984)**.
xa: **Dantwala (1978)** wanted **block-level** planning.
J&K **DDCs'** term ended **24 Feb 2026** with no fresh polls.
AP has **13 Zilla Parishads**.

79.s:
Consider the following statements about Kerala's People's Plan Campaign:
1. It was launched on 17 August 1996.
2. About 60-70% of plan funds were devolved to local bodies under it.
3. T.M. Thomas Isaac has proposed a 'People's Plan Campaign 2.0' with student internships and an online portal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
79.x: Statement 1 is correct (launched 17 Aug 1996). Statement 2 is wrong: about 35-40% of plan funds were devolved, not 60-70%. Statement 3 is correct: Thomas Isaac proposed PPC 2.0. So '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with 2 include the false figure.
79.tq: Kerala PPC: 1996, roughly one-third (35-40%) of plan funds, Isaac's 2.0.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1: Kerala's **People's Plan Campaign** began on **17 Aug 1996**.
Statement 2 wrong: about **35-40% of plan funds** were devolved, not 60-70%.
Statement 3: **T.M. Thomas Isaac** proposed "**People's Plan Campaign 2.0**" with student internships and an online portal.
xa: The campaign turned **30** in Aug **2026**.
Isaac's proposal came on **25 Aug 2026**.
The **Scandinavian** model of **high local taxes** is the benchmark for fiscal decentralisation.

79.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Scandinavian model of local government?
o: Strong municipalities delivering most welfare services with high local taxes
Local councils functioning only through parliamentary committees
Village bodies exercising judicial supremacy over the State
Weak municipalities dependent mainly on central grants
79.x: The Scandinavian model is characterised by strong municipalities, delivery of most welfare services and high local taxes; it is treated as a benchmark for fiscal decentralisation.
79.tq: Identify the model through its combination of municipal strength, welfare delivery and local taxation.
xs: The **Scandinavian** model has **strong municipalities** delivering most **welfare services** with **high local taxes** — option **(1)**.
It is the benchmark for **fiscal decentralisation**.
Councils as **creatures of Parliament** with committees is the **British** model.
xa: British councils follow the **ultra vires** rule.
India's municipal model derives from the **British** (Ripon's boards).
Kerala devolved about **35-40%** of plan funds to local bodies.

79.s: Which one of the following is a characteristic of the British model of local government?
o: Local bodies deliver most welfare services through high local taxes
Municipalities possess complete sovereignty independent of Parliament
Local councils are creatures of Parliament and operate under the ultra vires rule
All local councils are governed through Gram Panchayats
79.x: In the British model, local councils are creatures of Parliament and are subject to the ultra vires rule; the model also uses a committee system.
79.tq: Distinguish parliamentary creation and ultra vires from the fiscal characteristics of the Scandinavian model.
xs: In the **British** model, local councils are **creatures of Parliament** under the **ultra vires** rule — option **(3)**.
It also uses a **committee system**.
High local taxes and welfare delivery mark the **Scandinavian** model.
xa: India's municipal model derives from the British (**Ripon's boards**).
Local self-government has no **sovereignty or legislative supremacy**.
The Scandinavian model is the benchmark for **fiscal decentralisation**.

80.s: Which of the following pairs of rural reconstruction project and person is correctly matched?
80.x: Sriniketan was Rabindranath Tagore’s project. Gurgaon was F.L. Brayne’s, Marthandam was Spencer Hatch’s and Baroda was V.T. Krishnamachari’s.
xa: Tagore worked at Sriniketan with **Leonard Elmhirst**.
**Sevagram** – **Mahatma Gandhi** (Wardha, 1930s); **Nilokheri** – **S.K. Dey** (**1948**).
**Etawah pilot project** – **Albert Mayer** (Uttar Pradesh, **1948**).
**Firka Development Scheme** – T. Prakasam's Madras ministry, **1946**.

80.s: Which of the following pairs of rural development project and person is correctly matched?
80.x: Marthandam was associated with Spencer Hatch. Sevagram was Mahatma Gandhi’s, Etawah was Albert Mayer’s and Nilokheri was S.K. Dey’s.
xa: ⚠ **Trap (UPPSC 2023):** "Sevagram - **Vinoba Bhave**" is a WRONG pair; Sevagram belongs to **Gandhi**.
S.K. Dey later became **Union Minister of Community Development**.
Albert Mayer was an **American planner**.
**Gurgaon** – F.L. Brayne (**1920**); **Sriniketan** – Tagore (**1921**).

80.s: Which phase of the Five Year Plan framework gave Panchayati Raj Institutions a new lease of life, although it did not become an official Plan of India?
80.x: The Sixth Five Year Plan, associated with the Janata Government’s 1978-1983 plan, gave Panchayati Raj a new lease of life but was dropped after 1980 and did not become an official Plan of India.
80.tq: Use the unusual qualification about an unofficial Plan to identify the correct Plan phase.
xs: The **Sixth Five Year Plan** gave PRIs a new lease of life but "could not become an official plan of India" — option **(2)** (APPSC-G2 2017 key).
It was the Janata government's **1978-83** plan, dropped after **1980**.
xa: It matches the Ashok Mehta report of **1978**.
Post-1977 panchayats on Ashok Mehta lines = "**Second Generation Panchayats**".
The **1978-83** revival phase was shaped by this committee.

80.s: The Grow More Food Inquiry Committee, constituted in 1952, was chaired by:
80.x: V.T. Krishnamachari chaired the Grow More Food Inquiry Committee constituted in 1952.
80.tq: Apply the wrong-person trap by distinguishing the committee chairman from later Panchayati Raj committee chairmen.
xs: The Grow More Food Inquiry Committee (**1952**) was chaired by **V.T. Krishnamachari** — so option **(3)** is correct (APPSC-G2 2008 key).
**Balwant Rai Mehta** (1957), **Ashok Mehta** (1977-78) and **G.V.K. Rao** (1985) headed later Panchayati Raj committees — they are the keyed distractors.
The committee found the campaign **too narrow** and called for an **integrated village-development** approach.
xa: It recommended a nationwide **extension organisation**, which led to the **CDP (1952)** and the **NES (1953)**.
V.T. Krishnamachari is also linked with the **Baroda** rural project of **1932**.
The **Grow More Food campaign** itself began in **1943**.

80.s: The principal recommendation of the Grow More Food Inquiry Committee was to establish:
o: A separate constitutional court for villages
80.x: The Committee found the campaign too narrow and recommended an integrated village-development approach supported by a nationwide extension organisation.
80.tq: Identify the institutional recommendation that connects the inquiry with the later rural extension system.
xs: The Grow More Food Inquiry Committee's principal recommendation was a **nationwide extension organisation** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It found the Grow More Food campaign **too narrow** and wanted an **integrated village-development approach**.
That extension organisation took shape as the **Community Development Programme (1952)** and the **National Extension Service (1953)**.
xa: Chairman: **V.T. Krishnamachari** (APPSC-G2 2008 key); distractors were Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta, G.V.K. Rao.
The **NES** was a lighter, extension-staff version that spread the CDP pattern (**block, BDO, VLW**) nationwide.
The CDP was launched on **2 October 1952**, in the **First Five Year Plan (1951-56)**.

80.s: The Community Development Programme represented a step towards implementing which provision of the Directive Principles of State Policy?
o: Article 50 relating to separation of judiciary from executive
Article 44 relating to a Uniform Civil Code
80.x: The programme was viewed as a step towards implementing Article 40 of the Constitution, which directs the State to organise village panchayats.
80.tq: Apply the article-subject association and distinguish the relevant Directive Principle from neighbouring provisions.
xs: The CDP was a step towards the Directive Principles (**Part IV**), especially **Article 40** on village panchayats — option **(2)**.
It aimed at **public participation** in village development, putting the DPSP into practice.
xa: PR evolution: CDP's development schemes → self-government; **Art. 40** (DPSP) → justiciable **Part IX**.
The **73rd Amendment, 1992** added **Part IX** (**Art. 243-243O**) and the **Eleventh Schedule** (**29** items).
The 73rd Amendment came into force on **24 April 1993**.

80.s: The Community Development Programme was launched in India in which year?
80.x: The CDP was launched on 2 October 1952 (Gandhi Jayanti) during the First Five Year Plan. 1950 is the Constitution/Planning Commission year, 1957 the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee and 1959 the launch of Panchayati Raj.
xs: The CDP was launched in **1952** (2 October, Gandhi Jayanti) — option **(2)**.
⚠ **1957** = Balwant Rai Mehta Committee; **1959** = Panchayati Raj launched; **1953** = NES.
xa: It came during the **First Five Year Plan (1951-56)**, starting with **55 community projects**.
The **IADP** came in **1960** (pilot in **7** districts).
Exam angle: the year is asked directly — **1952**, not 1950/1957/1959.

80.s: The basic aim of the Community Development Programme was:
o: Development of villages through public participation
Establishment of Nyaya Panchayats in every village
A two-tier system of rural government
80.x: The CDP aimed to develop villages and raise rural living standards through public participation.
xa: Objective in full: raise the **standard of living of the rural population** through **public participation**.
Its lack of real people's participation later led to the **Balwant Rai Mehta** review (**1957**).
Unit: the **block**, with a **BDO** and **Village Level Workers**.

80.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Extension Service:
1. It was launched in 1953.
2. It supported the Community Development Programme.
3. It replaced the objective of public participation with exclusive government control.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the Community Development approach aimed at public participation, although it was later criticised as government-imposed.
80.tq: Spot the reversed meaning in the statement that converts a participatory programme into an exclusively governmental one.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: the **NES** was launched in **1953** (BPSC 2022 key).
Statement 2: it was the **extension arm** complementing and supporting the **CDP**.
Statement 3 wrong: the approach aimed at **public participation**; it was only later criticised as **imposed by government**.
xa: The NES was a lighter, extension-staff version that spread the **block, BDO, VLW** pattern nationwide; intensive CD blocks came later.
The NES grew out of the **Grow More Food Inquiry Committee's** call for an extension organisation.
The **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee** reviewed both CDP and NES in **1957**.

80.s: The Village Level Worker, also known as the Gram Sevak, is best described as a:
o: Political representative elected to the Panchayat Samiti
Single-purpose revenue official for one village
Multipurpose extension worker for a group of villages
Judicial officer appointed to a Nyaya Panchayat
80.x: A Village Level Worker or Gram Sevak served as a multipurpose extension worker for a group of villages.
80.tq: Discriminate between the administrative, developmental and judicial roles associated with village institutions.
xs: The **Village Level Worker (Gram Sevak)** was a **multipurpose extension worker for a group of villages** — option **(3)**.
He was not elected, not a single-purpose revenue official, and not a judicial officer of a **Nyaya Panchayat**.
xa: The **BDO** headed the block team of extension officers.
**Block** = unit of planning and development (about **100 villages**).
The block later became the base of the **Panchayat Samiti** in the Rajasthan-AP pattern.

80.s: Under the Community Development Programme, the unit of planning and development headed by the Block Development Officer was the:
80.x: The block, covering about 100 villages, was the CDP’s unit of planning and development, headed by the BDO.
xa: The block later became the base of the **Panchayat Samiti** in the Rajasthan-AP pattern.
**Dantwala (1978)** reported on **Block-Level Planning**; **Hanumantha Rao (1984)** on **District Planning**.
Gram Sabha = "**embodiment of direct democracy**" (Singhvi).

80.s: What was the principal finding of the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee regarding rural development?
o: Public participation was indispensable for development
District-level bureaucracy alone could ensure development
Administrative centralisation was indispensable for development
Private agencies should replace local bodies in development
80.x: The committee’s main finding was that public participation is indispensable for development.
80.tq: Identify the central principle rather than a structural detail of the committee’s recommendations.
xs: The committee's main finding: **public participation was indispensable for development** — option **(1)**.
Its remedy was **democratic decentralisation** — transfer of power and resources to elected bodies, the opposite of centralisation or bureaucratic control.
xa: The CDP and NES were seen as **imposed by government** with little people's participation.
The decentralisation scheme "later came to be known as **Panchayati Raj**".
Balwant Rai Mehta first used the term "**democratic decentralisation**" (APPSC 2019).

80.s: A major criticism of the Community Development Programme was that it:
o: Was implemented without any administrative unit
Was confined exclusively to urban municipalities
Had no agricultural or social components
Was imposed by the government with inadequate people’s participation
80.x: The programme was criticised for being government-imposed and for involving the people insufficiently. This weakness contributed to the review by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee.
80.tq: Link the criticism of implementation with the later institutional review it prompted.
xs: The CDP was criticised as **imposed by the government with inadequate people's participation** — option **(4)**.
The other options are false: it had a unit (the **block**), was rural, and had **agricultural** and **social education** components.
xa: This weakness led to the **Balwant Rai Mehta** review in **January 1957**.
The committee's remedy: **democratic decentralisation** through three-tier elected bodies.
Later decline causes: **bureaucratisation**, poor finances, irregular elections, weak devolution.

80.s: The G.V.K. Rao Committee dealt primarily with:
o: Administrative arrangements for rural development and poverty alleviation programmes
Election disputes of urban local bodies
80.x: The full title associated with the G.V.K. Rao Committee was ‘Administrative Arrangements for Rural Development and Poverty Alleviation Programmes’.
80.tq: Match the committee with its distinctive official subject rather than a general Panchayati Raj theme.
xs: G.V.K. Rao reviewed "**Administrative Arrangements for Rural Development and Poverty Alleviation Programmes**" — option **(1)**.
**Panchayat statistics** = **V.R. Rao (1960)**; constitutional recognition = **L.M. Singhvi**.
xa: Set up in **1985** by the **Planning Commission**.
Finding: PRIs had become "**grass without roots**".
CGPSC 2021: "G.V.K. Rao - administrative arrangements" is a correct pair.

80.s: Under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment, which of the following is the correct constitutional range dealing with Panchayati Raj Institutions?
80.x: Panchayats are dealt with in Part IX of the Constitution, covering Articles 243 to 243O.
80.tq: Use the constitutional Part and Article-range distinction.
xs: Panchayats: **Part IX**, **Articles 243–243O** — option **(3)**.
Added by the **73rd Amendment, 1992**, in force **24 April 1993**.
xa: It also added the **Eleventh Schedule** with **29** items.
Thungon (**1988**) first proposed a list of PR subjects in the Constitution.
Part IX made PRIs **justiciable**, replacing reliance on **Art. 40** (DPSP).

80.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
80.x: The Food for Work programme is associated with 1977. ICDS was listed as 1975, TRYSEM as 1979 and DWCRA as 1982.
80.tq: Use nearby programme years as distractors and verify the exact programme-year association.
xs: **Food for Work — 1977** is correct — option **(3)**.
xa: **IADP** = **1960** (pilot in **7** districts).
**IRDP** = 1978-79; nationwide **2 Oct 1980**.

80.s: Which of the following was the first major rural development programme after independence?
80.x: The Community Development Programme (1952) was the first major rural development programme after independence; the National Extension Service followed in 1953 and Panchayati Raj in 1959.
80.tq: Pick the earliest programme in the rural-development sequence.
n: The Community Development Programme of 1952 was the first major rural development programme after independence. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xs: The **Community Development Programme** (**1952**) was the first major rural development programme after independence — option **(4)**.
It was launched on **2 October 1952**, during the **First Five Year Plan**.
The **National Extension Service** came later, in **1953**; **Panchayati Raj** was launched in **1959**.
xa: The CDP began with **55 community projects**; its unit was the **block**.
It is called the "**Mother of social development programmes**".
**Social education** was a CDP component — ⚠ not part of NAEP, IRDP or National Literacy Mission (APPSC 2019).
Its objective: **development of village through public participation** (APPSC 2018 key).

80.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Community Development is wrongly matched?
o: V.T. Krishnamachari – Chairman of the Grow More Food Inquiry Committee
Jawaharlal Nehru – Launched the CDP and inaugurated Panchayati Raj at Nagaur
S.K. Dey – Built Nilokheri and served as Union Minister of Community Development
80.x: Albert Mayer was the American planner behind the Etawah Pilot Project; Nilokheri is associated with S.K. Dey.
xa: Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj at **Nagaur** on **2 Oct 1959**.
**Balwant Rai Mehta** = **architect / father of Panchayati Raj**.
⚠ The name 'Panchayati Raj' is credited to **M.K. Gandhi** (UPPSC 2017 key), not Nehru.

80.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee?
o: It examined the working of the Integrated Rural Development Programme
It examined the working of the Community Development Programme
It examined the working of the National Extension Service
80.x: It examined the Community Development Programme (1952) and the National Extension Service (1953); IRDP was outside its terms of reference.
xa: Appointed by the **Government of India** in **January 1957**; report **November 1957**.
Main finding: **local people's participation** is indispensable.
Remedy: **democratic decentralisation** → three-tier elected bodies, later called **Panchayati Raj**.

80.s: The democratic decentralisation recommended by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee consisted essentially of:
80.x: The recommended remedy was democratic decentralisation through elected three-tier local bodies, which later came to be known as Panchayati Raj.
80.tq: Link the remedy proposed by the reviewing committee with its institutional form.
xs: Democratic decentralisation meant **three-tier elected local bodies** — option **(4)**.
Tiers: **Gram Panchayat** (village), **Panchayat Samiti** (block), **Zila Parishad** (district), "organically linked" by **indirect elections**.
xa: It meant genuine transfer of **power and responsibility** with **adequate resources**.
The scheme "later came to be known as **Panchayati Raj**".
⚠ **Nyaya Panchayat** is NOT one of the three tiers (UPPSC 2024).

80.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the election pattern recommended by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee?
o: Indirect elections at all three levels
Direct elections at all three levels
Direct election to the Gram Panchayat and indirect elections to the Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad
Direct elections to the Gram Panchayat and Zila Parishad, with indirect election to the Panchayat Samiti
80.x: The committee recommended direct election to the village Panchayat, while the Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad were to be constituted through indirect elections.
80.tq: Discriminate between direct election at the base and indirect election at the higher tiers.
xs: Balwant Rai Mehta: **direct** election to the **Gram Panchayat**, **indirect** elections to the **Panchayat Samiti** and **Zila Parishad** — option **(3)**.
⚠ "Direct elections to both village panchayat and Zila Parishad" is a keyed **false** statement (APPSC 2019).
xa: The three tiers were "**organically linked**" through indirect elections (UPSC).
**Gadgil (1988)** later proposed **direct elections at all levels**.
**Ashok Mehta** wanted **political parties** to take part at all levels.

80.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the roles assigned by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee?
o: Panchayat Samiti—supervisory body; Zila Parishad—village-level implementation body
Panchayat Samiti—advisory body; Zila Parishad—executive body
Panchayat Samiti—executive body; Zila Parishad—advisory, coordinating and supervisory body
Panchayat Samiti—judicial body; Zila Parishad—legislative body
80.x: The Panchayat Samiti was recommended as the executive body, whereas the Zila Parishad was assigned advisory, coordinating and supervisory functions.
80.tq: Use role-based comparison to distinguish the executive Samiti from the coordinating Zila Parishad.
xs: **Panchayat Samiti — executive body**; **Zila Parishad — advisory, coordinating and supervisory body** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Making the **Zila Parishad the executive body** was something the committee did **NOT** recommend (APPSC 2019).
xa: The block was the **basic unit of planning and development** for the Panchayat Samiti.
The **District Collector** was to chair the **Zila Parishad**.
Under **Ashok Mehta** the roles flipped: **Zila Parishad** = executive body.

80.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee's recommendations?
o: The transfer of functions should come with adequate resources
The District Collector should chair the Zila Parishad
Planning and development functions should go to Panchayati Raj bodies
The Zila Parishad should be the executive body
80.x: The Committee made the Panchayat Samiti, not the Zila Parishad, the executive body.
xa: APPSC 2019 keyed "**c and d only**": all planning and development to these bodies + Collector as ZP chairman.
⚠ **Collector as ZP chairman** = BRM; **Collector as ZP CEO** = **Thungon**; **DDC as ZP CEO** = **G.V.K. Rao**.

80.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee's recommendations?
o: Direct election to the Zila Parishad
The Panchayat Samiti as the executive body
The District Collector as chairman of the Zila Parishad
80.x: The Committee did not recommend direct election to the Zila Parishad; it recommended three tiers with the Panchayat Samiti as the executive body.
xa: Two tiers came from **Ashok Mehta (1978)** — Zila Parishad + **Mandal Panchayat**.
⚠ **3 – block – Collector chairman** = BRM; **2 – district – parties** = Ashok Mehta.

80.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
80.x: G.R. Rajagopalan was associated with Nyaya Panchayats, not Panchayat elections. K. Santhanam was associated with Panchayat elections in 1965.
80.tq: Find the swapped subject by comparing specialist panels with their narrowly defined functions.
xs: **G.R. Rajagopalan — Panchayat Elections** is wrong — option **(4)**: Rajagopalan (**1962**) studied **Nyaya Panchayats**.
PR elections were studied by **K. Santhanam** (**1965**).
Correct pairs: **G. Ramachandran** — Training Centres (**1969**); **M.L. Jain** — Budgeting and Accounting (**1963**); **R.K. Khanna** — Audit and Accounts (**1966**).
xa: **V.R. Rao (1960)** — Panchayat Statistics; ⚠ sounds statistical but IS a PR committee.
**R.R. Diwakar (1963)** — **Gram Sabha**.
⚠ **CGPSC 2021:** "PR Training - **A.S. Trivedi**" is a WRONG pair (training = **G. Ramachandran**).

80.s:
Which of the following contributed to the decline of Panchayati Raj Institutions?
1. Poor finances
2. Irregular elections and supersession
3. Excessive independence from the development administration
80.x: Poor finances and irregular elections/supersession were causes. Excessive independence was not; the problem was bureaucratic detachment from Panchayati Raj.
xa: **Ashok Mehta** set a **six-month** limit for elections after supersession.
**Thungon (1988)**: fixed **5-year** term; supersession at most **6 months**.

80.s: The V.R. Rao Committee of 1960 is associated with:
80.x: Although its name may suggest a statistical body outside the Panchayati Raj field, the V.R. Rao Committee was associated with Panchayat Statistics and was a Panchayati Raj committee.
80.tq: Resolve the look-alike committee trap by recalling its specific Panchayat-related subject.
xs: The **V.R. Rao Committee (1960)** dealt with the **Rationalisation of Panchayat Statistics** — option **(1)**.
⚠ It sounds statistical but **IS** a PR committee (CGPSC 2021: "V.R. Rao - statistics" is a correct pair).
**Centre-State relations** = **Sarkaria**; **electoral reforms** = **Dinesh Goswami** and **Tarkunde** — not PR committees.
xa: **S.D. Mishra (1961)** — Working Group on Panchayats and Cooperatives.
**Vishwa Raman (1961)** — PR Administration.
**C. Rangarajan** headed the **National Statistical Commission** — not a PR committee.

80.s:
With reference to the Ashok Mehta Committee, consider the following statements:
1. It recommended a two-tier Panchayati Raj structure.
2. It proposed a four-year term for the Panchayati Raj bodies.
3. It retained the three-tier structure without modification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: The Committee proposed replacing the three-tier structure with a two-tier system and recommended a four-year term. It did not retain the three-tier structure unchanged.
80.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the principal structural recommendation.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
1 and 2: Ashok Mehta proposed a **two-tier system with four years of term** (APPSC-G2 2023 and 2025 key).
3 wrong: the two tiers came **in place of** the three tiers.
xa: Tiers: **Zila Parishad** (district, executive) + **Mandal Panchayat** (**15,000-20,000** people).
UPPSC 2023 key "only (1)": the **district**, not the block, was the unit.
⚠ The **73rd Amendment (1992)** went back to **three tiers** (two only in states under **20 lakh** population).

80.s: With reference to the Ashok Mehta Committee, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Zila Parishad — Body for a group of villages
Mandal Panchayat — Body for a group of villages
80.x: The Mandal Panchayat covered a group of villages. The Zila Parishad was the district-level executive body; the committee was appointed in December 1977 and reported in August 1978.
xa: The report made **132 recommendations**.
Appointed by the **Janata government** of PM **Morarji Desai**.
Mandal Panchayat population: **15,000-20,000**.

80.s: According to the Ashok Mehta Committee, the first point of decentralisation below the State level was to be the:
80.x: The Committee treated the district as the first point of decentralisation under popular supervision below the State level.
80.tq: Separate the district-based recommendation from the commonly associated block-level structure.
xs: The **District** was the first point of decentralisation below the State — option **(2)**.
⚠ UPPSC 2023 trap: Ashok Mehta made the **district**, **not the block**, the unit.
xa: The block (Samiti executive) was the unit under **Balwant Rai Mehta**.
**G.V.K. Rao (1985)** also made the **district** the basic unit of planning.
**Dantwala (1978)** = **block**-level planning; **Hanumantha Rao (1984)** = **district** planning.

80.s: The Ashok Mehta Committee on Panchayati Raj (1977) was appointed by the Janata Government headed by Prime Minister:
80.x: The Janata Government of Morarji Desai appointed the Ashok Mehta Committee in December 1977 (APPSC-G2 2008 key). Rajiv Gandhi's government appointed the L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986); Indira Gandhi and Charan Singh are distractors.
80.tq: Ashok Mehta = Janata / Morarji Desai; Singhvi = Rajiv Gandhi.
xs: The Janata Government of PM **Morarji Desai** appointed the Ashok Mehta Committee (**December 1977**) — option **(2)** (APPSC-G2 2008 key).
**Rajiv Gandhi's** government appointed the **L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986)**.
xa: The report came in **August 1978** with **132 recommendations**.
The **Sixth Five Year Plan** (Janata's **1978-83** plan) gave PRIs a new lease of life.
It was dropped after **1980** and "could not become an official plan of India" (APPSC-G2 2017).

80.s: If a Panchayati Raj body was superseded under the Ashok Mehta Committee's recommendation, elections were to be held within:
80.x: The Committee recommended that elections should be conducted within six months if a Panchayati Raj body was superseded.
80.tq: Distinguish the prescribed election deadline from other common constitutional time limits.
xs: Elections within **six months** of supersession — option **(4)**.
This six-month limit was Ashok Mehta's answer to **irregular elections + supersession**.
xa: **Thungon (1988)** also set supersession at most **6 months**, with a fixed **5-year** term.
Ashok Mehta also wanted a **Minister for Panchayati Raj** in the state cabinet.
Elections run by the **Chief Electoral Officer** of the state.

80.s:
With reference to the Ashok Mehta Committee, consider the following recommendations:
1. Constitutional recognition for Panchayati Raj Institutions
2. A Minister for Panchayati Raj in the State Council of Ministers
3. Elections to Panchayati Raj bodies on a non-party basis
Which of the above were recommended by the Committee?
80.x: The Committee sought constitutional recognition for PRIs and a Minister for Panchayati Raj in the State cabinet. Statement 3 is wrong: it wanted official participation of political parties at all levels of panchayat elections. So the answer is '1 and 2 only'.
80.tq: Ashok Mehta = party-based elections, not non-party polls.
xs: **1 and 2** were recommended — option **(1)**.
1: **Constitutional recognition** for PRIs (sanctity, stature, continued functioning).
2: A **Minister for Panchayati Raj** in the state cabinet.
3 wrong: it wanted **official participation of political parties** at **all levels**.
xa: ⚠ **L.M. Singhvi** is keyed as the committee that "**first suggested constitutional status**" (APPSC 2018); older notes credit Ashok Mehta too.
Other points: **regular social audit**, **compulsory taxation**, **SC/ST reservation by population**.

80.s: The principal political reason for the failure to implement the Ashok Mehta Committee recommendations was that:
o: The Supreme Court declared the recommendations unconstitutional
The Janata government fell before completing its term
The Planning Commission rejected the report immediately
The State governments unanimously implemented an alternative model
80.x: The Janata government fell before completing its term, and consequently the Centre took no action on the recommendations.
80.tq: Connect policy non-implementation with the political fate of the sponsoring government.
xs: The **Janata government fell before completing its term** — option **(2)**.
So the **Centre took no action** on the report.
xa: The ideas survived in states: **West Bengal**, **Karnataka**, and AP's **Mandal Praja Parishads** (**1986**).
The **two-tier plan** was never adopted nationally.
The **73rd Amendment (1992)** returned to **three tiers**.

80.s: Panchayats formed after 1977 broadly on the lines suggested by the Ashok Mehta Committee are known as:
80.x: Panchayats formed after 1977 on the lines of the Ashok Mehta recommendations are referred to as Second Generation Panchayats.
80.tq: Discriminate between the generation label and descriptive institutional terms.
xs: Post-1977 panchayats on Ashok Mehta lines are "**Second Generation Panchayats**" — option **(3)**.
They followed the Ashok Mehta report (**August 1978**).
xa: **West Bengal** adopted Ashok Mehta's model.
"**Grass without roots**" = **G.V.K. Rao's** phrase for PRIs.
Gram Sabha = "**embodiment of direct democracy**" (Singhvi).

80.s:
Assertion (A): The G.V.K. Rao Committee treated the district as the basic unit of planning.
Reason (R): The G.V.K. Rao Committee recommended that a District Development Commissioner act as Chief Executive Officer of the Zila Parishad.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
80.x: Both are recommendations of the G.V.K. Rao Committee, but naming a DDC as CEO does not explain why the district was made the planning unit.
xa: It also called for **decentralised field administration** and **regular elections**.
Set up in **1985** by the **Planning Commission**.
G.V.K. Rao cut the **Collector's** development role.

80.s:
Which of the following was/were associated with the Gadgil Committee (1988)?
1. Constitutional status for Panchayati Raj Institutions
2. Reservations in Panchayati Raj Institutions
3. Serving as the model for the 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill
80.x: The Gadgil Committee recommended constitutional status, direct elections and reservations, and its ideas were the model for the 64th Amendment Bill.
xa: Gadgil: **Congress Party** Committee on Policy and Programmes (**1988**).
It also proposed a **State Finance Commission** + **State Election Commission**.
PRIs to **levy taxes**.

80.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: G.V.K. Rao — Direct elections at all three levels
Thungon — Collector as Chief Executive Officer of the Zila Parishad
80.x: Direct elections at all three levels were associated with the Gadgil recommendations. G.V.K. Rao focused on administrative arrangements, district planning and the District Development Commissioner.
80.tq: Find the committee whose central administrative focus does not fit the electoral recommendation.
xs: **G.V.K. Rao — Direct elections at all three levels** is wrong — option **(1)**: direct elections at all levels were **Gadgil's** idea.
G.V.K. Rao stood for **ZP pivotal**, **district planning** and the **DDC**.
Correct pairs: **Singhvi** — regular elections; **Gadgil** — **State Election Commission**; **Thungon** — **Collector as ZP CEO**.
xa: ⚠ **DDC as ZP CEO** = G.V.K. Rao; **Collector as ZP chairman** = Balwant Rai Mehta.
G.V.K. Rao did urge **regular elections** to PRIs.

80.s: Which one of the following expressions is most closely associated with the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee?
80.x: Democratic decentralisation was the central idea associated with the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee, along with the recommendation of a three-tier system.
80.tq: Discriminate between closely related committee slogans and subjects.
xs: **Democratic decentralisation** is the BRM hallmark — option **(4)** (first used the term, APPSC 2019).
**Revitalisation for democracy and development** = **L.M. Singhvi**; **administrative arrangements** = **G.V.K. Rao**; **district planning under the Collector** = **Hanumantha Rao**.
xa: The scheme "later came to be known as **Panchayati Raj**".
BRM's structure: **three tiers**, organically linked by **indirect elections**.

80.s:
Consider the following pairs of early Panchayati Raj committees and their subjects:
1. S.D. Mishra (1961) - Working Group on Panchayats and Cooperatives
2. Vishwa Raman (1961) - Nyaya Panchayats
3. R.R. Diwakar (1963) - Gram Sabha
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
80.x: Pair 1 is correct. Pair 2 is wrong: Vishwa Raman dealt with PR Administration; Nyaya Panchayats was G.R. Rajagopalan (1962). Pair 3 is correct. Hence '1 and 3 only'; every other option includes the wrong pair 2 or leaves out pair 3.
80.tq: Nyaya Panchayats = Rajagopalan; Gram Sabha = Diwakar; Administration = Vishwa Raman.
xs: Pairs **1 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
1: **S.D. Mishra (1961)** — Working Group on **Panchayats and Cooperatives** — correct.
2 wrong: **Vishwa Raman (1961)** = **PR Administration**; Nyaya Panchayats = **G.R. Rajagopalan (1962)**.
3: **R.R. Diwakar (1963)** — **Gram Sabha** — correct.
xa: **V.R. Rao (1960)** — Panchayat Statistics.
**M.L. Jain (1963)** — Budgeting and Accounting.

80.s: Which one of the following sets contains only recommendations associated with the Ashok Mehta Committee?
o: Constitutional recognition, free and fair elections and viable Gram Panchayats
Three tiers, indirect elections above the village level and Collector as Zila Parishad chairman
Two tiers, four-year term and participation of political parties in Panchayat elections
Zila Parishad as pivotal body, decentralised field administration and District Development Commissioner as its Chief Executive Officer
80.x: Two tiers, a four-year term and party participation in panchayat elections are all Ashok Mehta recommendations. Option A belongs to L.M. Singhvi, option B to Balwant Rai Mehta and option D to G.V.K. Rao.
80.tq: Identify the committee by a cluster of recommendations rather than by one isolated fact.
xs: **Two tiers, four-year term, party participation** — all **Ashok Mehta** — option **(3)**.
Option 1 = **L.M. Singhvi**; option 2 = **Balwant Rai Mehta**; option 4 = **G.V.K. Rao**.
xa: Ashok Mehta also: **compulsory taxation**, **social audit**, **Minister for Panchayati Raj**.
Superseded PRIs → elections **within six months**.
Mandal Panchayat population: **15,000-20,000**.

80.s: Which of the following statements about the role of the District Collector in Panchayati Raj committee recommendations is correct?
o: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee made the Collector chairman of the Zila Parishad, while several later committees sought to reduce the Collector’s development role
The Collector’s development role was increased by the Ashok Mehta Committee and G.V.K. Rao Committee
Hanumantha Rao Committee was the only committee to reduce the Collector’s development role
The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee excluded the Collector from the Zila Parishad, while all later committees made the Collector its executive head
80.x: Balwant Rai Mehta proposed the District Collector as chairman of the Zila Parishad, but the Balwant Rai Mehta, First ARC, Ashok Mehta and G.V.K. Rao bodies are identified as cutting the Collector’s development role. Hanumantha Rao was the exception.
80.tq: Handle an apparent contradiction by separating the chairmanship recommendation from the wider development role.
xs: BRM made the **Collector chairman of the Zila Parishad**, while later committees **cut the Collector's development role** — option **(1)**.
Role cut by: **BRM** (despite ZP chair), **First ARC**, **Ashok Mehta**, **G.V.K. Rao**.
Exception: **Hanumantha Rao (1984)**, who kept the Collector as primary coordinator of district planning.
xa: **Thungon (1988)**: **Collector as ZP CEO**.
G.V.K. Rao wanted a **District Development Commissioner** instead.

80.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Thungon Committee – District Development Commissioner as Zila Parishad CEO
Hanumantha Rao Committee – Collector as main coordinator of district planning
G.V.K. Rao Committee – District Development Commissioner as Zila Parishad CEO
L.M. Singhvi Committee – Constitutional status and Nyaya Panchayats for village clusters
80.x: The Thungon Committee proposed the District Collector, not a District Development Commissioner, as Zila Parishad CEO.
xa: ⚠ **Collector as ZP chairman** = **Balwant Rai Mehta**.
Thungon also wanted a **list of PR subjects** in the Constitution.

80.s:
Assertion (A): The National Extension Service came after the Community Development Programme.
Reason (R): The Community Development Programme was launched in 1952 and the National Extension Service in 1953.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
80.x: CDP began in 1952 and NES in 1953, which is exactly why NES followed CDP.
xa: **Food for Work 1977**; **TRYSEM 1979**; **DWCRA 1982**.
**IADP 1960** (pilot in **7** districts).

80.s: Which of the following statements about the Ashok Mehta Committee is correct?
o: It rejected constitutional recognition and recommended only official nominations
It recommended abolition of all elected rural institutions
It confined its recommendations exclusively to municipal corporations
It was the first committee to seek constitutional recognition and party-based elections for Panchayati Raj Institutions
80.x:
The Ashok Mehta Committee was significant for being the first to seek constitutional recognition and party-based elections for Panchayati Raj Institutions.
⚠ Sources differ: most prep texts: Ashok Mehta (1978) first sought constitutional status; APPSC 2018 key: L.M. Singhvi (1986). This key follows the standard view.
80.tq: Identify the committee through its distinctive recommendation rather than its appointment details.
xs: The Ashok Mehta Committee was the **first to seek constitutional recognition and party-based elections** for PRIs — option **(4)**.
It wanted constitutional recognition for **sanctity, stature, continued functioning**, and **official participation of political parties** at all levels.
xa: It shaped the **1978-83** revival phase.
⚠ Notes differ: APPSC 2018 key credits **L.M. Singhvi (1986)** as the committee that "**first suggested constitutional status**".
The Janata government fell, so the Centre took **no action**.

80.s: The Ashok Mehta Committee envisaged regular social audit by:
o: A district-level agency and a committee of legislators
The Gram Sabha and the Supreme Court jointly
80.x: The Committee proposed regular social audit by a district-level agency together with a committee of legislators.
80.tq: Identify the combination of bodies assigned the audit function.
xs: Regular social audit by **a district-level agency and a committee of legislators** — option **(2)**.
It was one of Ashok Mehta's **132 recommendations** (August 1978).
xa: Other points: **compulsory taxation**, **party participation**, **Minister for Panchayati Raj**.
**SC/ST reservation by population**.
Superseded body → elections within **6 months**.

80.s: Which one of the following committees was concerned with block-level planning?
80.x: The Dantwala Committee, appointed in 1978, dealt with block-level planning.
80.tq: Match the planning level with the committee specifically associated with it.
xs: The **Dantwala Committee (1978)** reported on **Block-Level Planning** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **Hanumantha Rao (1984)** = **district** planning; **G.V.K. Rao (1985)** = administrative arrangements; **L.M. Singhvi (1986)** = revitalising PRIs.
xa: Hanumantha Rao kept the **Collector** as primary coordinator of district planning.
Dantwala too kept the Collector central to district planning.
The block was the CDP's unit (about **100 villages**).

80.s: The phrase ‘grass without roots’ was used in the context of Panchayati Raj Institutions by the:
80.x: The G.V.K. Rao Committee observed that Panchayati Raj Institutions had become ‘grass without roots’.
80.tq: Use the distinctive quotation to separate committees with overlapping rural-development concerns.
xs: "**Grass without roots**" was the phrase of the **G.V.K. Rao Committee** — option **(1)**.
It meant development had become **bureaucratised** and cut off from PR.
xa: Remedy: **Zila Parishad** pivotal; **district** = basic unit of planning.
**District Development Commissioner** = ZP CEO.
It also urged **regular elections** to PRIs.

80.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the G.V.K. Rao Committee from the L.M. Singhvi Committee?
o: G.V.K. Rao focused on Gram Sabhas, while L.M. Singhvi focused on district bureaucracy
G.V.K. Rao focused on administrative arrangements, while L.M. Singhvi focused on revitalising PRIs for democracy
G.V.K. Rao focused on constitutional recognition, while L.M. Singhvi focused on taxation powers
Both committees had identical objectives and key units
80.x: G.V.K. Rao examined the administrative set-up for rural development, whereas L.M. Singhvi focused on revitalising Panchayati Raj Institutions as instruments of democracy.
80.tq: Separate committees by focus rather than by their common connection with Panchayati Raj.
xs: G.V.K. Rao = **administrative arrangements** for rural development; L.M. Singhvi = **revitalising PRIs for democracy** — option **(2)**.
Key unit: G.V.K. Rao = **district / Zila Parishad**; Singhvi = **Gram Sabha** and viable gram panchayats.
xa: Big idea: G.V.K. Rao = **DDC as ZP CEO**; Singhvi = **constitutional recognition**.
G.V.K. Rao **1985** (Planning Commission); Singhvi **1986** (Rajiv Gandhi government).

80.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation associated with the L.M. Singhvi Committee?
o: Abolition of the Gram Sabha as an institution of direct democracy
Regular, free and fair elections to Panchayati Raj Institutions
Constitutional recognition of Panchayati Raj Institutions
Nyaya Panchayats for clusters of villages
80.x: The Singhvi Committee supported the Gram Sabha as the embodiment of direct democracy; it did not recommend its abolition. It also supported constitutional recognition, regular elections and Nyaya Panchayats for clusters of villages.
