80.tq: Find the option that reverses a stated recommendation while the other three retain the committee’s approach.
xs: **Abolition of the Gram Sabha** was not Singhvi's idea — option **(1)**: he called the Gram Sabha the "**embodiment of direct democracy**".
He did recommend **constitutional recognition**, **regular, free and fair elections** and **Nyaya Panchayats** for **clusters of villages**.
xa: He wanted villages reorganised to make **gram panchayats viable**, with more money for them.
**Judicial tribunals** in each state for PR election and dissolution disputes.
**R.R. Diwakar (1963)** studied the **Gram Sabha**.

80.s: The Gadgil Committee of 1988 was set up by the:
80.x: The Gadgil Committee was set up by the Congress party in 1988 and its recommendations fed into the draft constitutional amendment proposals.
80.tq: Identify the political origin of the committee instead of confusing it with a governmental commission.
xs: The **Gadgil Committee (1988)** was set up by the **Congress Party** (Committee on Policy and Programmes) — option **(3)**.
The **Planning Commission** set up **G.V.K. Rao (1985)**.
xa: Gadgil "**fed into draft amendment proposals**" — model for the **64th Amendment Bill**.
It proposed **direct elections at all levels** and a **State Election Commission**.
**Thungon (1988)** was a sub-committee of Parliament's Consultative Committee.

80.s: The principal objection raised by opponents to the 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill was that it would
o: remove the system of reservation in local bodies
centralise power and bypass the States
80.x: Opponents feared that the 64th Bill would centralise power and bypass the States in matters relating to Panchayati Raj.
80.tq: Identify the specific political objection rather than the broad objective of the Bill.
xs: Opponents feared the 64th Bill would **centralise power and bypass the States** — option **(3)**.
The Centre would deal directly with local bodies over the states' heads, though "**Local Government**" is a **State List** subject.
xa: Moved by **Rajiv Gandhi** govt, **July 1989**; **passed Lok Sabha**, **defeated in Rajya Sabha** (October 1989).
No special majority → it **lapsed**.
The 64th Bill = **legislative origin of the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992** (BPSC 2020 key).

80.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Balwant Rai Mehta Committee — Two-tier system with a four-year term
Ashok Mehta Committee — Three-tier system with the block as the main planning unit
G.V.K. Rao Committee — Zila Parishad as the pivotal body
L.M. Singhvi Committee — District Collector as chairman of the Zila Parishad
80.x: The G.V.K. Rao Committee regarded the Zila Parishad as the pivotal institution. The two-tier, four-year model belonged to the Ashok Mehta Committee; the three-tier block-based model and Collector as Zila Parishad chairman were associated with Balwant Rai Mehta.
80.tq: Use distinctive recommendations to eliminate committees with swapped identities.
xs: **G.V.K. Rao — Zila Parishad as pivotal body** is correct — option **(3)**.
**Two-tier, four-year term** = **Ashok Mehta**; **three tiers with block** = **Balwant Rai Mehta**.
**Collector as ZP chairman** = **Balwant Rai Mehta**, not Singhvi.
xa: G.V.K. Rao (**1985**): **district** = basic unit of planning; **DDC** = ZP CEO.
⚠ **DDC as ZP CEO** = G.V.K. Rao; **Collector as ZP CEO** = **Thungon**.

80.s: Which combination of committees is associated with the principal blueprint of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment?
o: Balwant Rai Mehta, Hanumantha Rao and Dantwala
G.V.K. Rao, K. Santhanam and R.R. Diwakar
Ashok Mehta, S.D. Mishra and Rajagopalan
80.x: The L.M. Singhvi, Thungon and Gadgil Committees collectively contributed to the blueprint of the 73rd Amendment, including constitutional status, election and financial institutions, tenure and reservation.
80.tq: Start from the distinctive three-committee combination linked with constitutionalisation.
xs: **L.M. Singhvi, Thungon and Gadgil** = blueprint of the **73rd Amendment** — option **(2)**.
They gave **constitutional status**, **SEC**, **SFC**, **5-year term** and **reservation**.
xa: Singhvi **1986**; Thungon and Gadgil **1988**.
Gadgil was the model for the **64th Amendment Bill**.
**Balwant Rai Mehta (1957)** gave **three tiers**; **Hanumantha Rao** and **Dantwala** were planning committees.

80.s: Which Bill was the first attempt to provide constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions?
80.x: The Constitution (64th Amendment) Bill was the first attempt to confer constitutional status on Panchayati Raj Institutions. It failed in the Rajya Sabha in 1989.
80.tq: Distinguish the first failed constitutional attempt from the later successful amendment.
xs: The **64th Amendment Bill** was the **first attempt** at constitutional status for PRIs — option **(4)**.
Moved **July 1989** by **Rajiv Gandhi**; passed Lok Sabha, **defeated in Rajya Sabha** (October 1989).
xa: It was the **legislative origin of the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992** (BPSC 2020 key).
The **131st Amendment Bill, 2026** was defeated in the **Lok Sabha** on **17 April 2026** — special majority still decisive.

80.s:
Arrange the following committees in chronological order of their constitution:
A. L.M. Singhvi Committee
B. Balwant Rai Mehta Committee
C. G.V.K. Rao Committee
D. Ashok Mehta Committee
80.x: Balwant Rai Mehta (1957), Ashok Mehta (1977), G.V.K. Rao (1985), L.M. Singhvi (1986): B, D, C, A.
80.tq: Order the Panchayati Raj committees by year.
n: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was established in 1957. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Ashok Mehta Committee was established in 1977. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The G.V.K. Rao Committee was established in 1985. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The L.M. Singhvi Committee was established in 1986. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
xs: Correct order: **B, D, C, A** — option **(3)**.
xa: After Singhvi came **P.K. Thungon** and **Gadgil** (both **1988**).
**Dantwala (1978)** → block-level planning; **Hanumantha Rao (1983)** → district planning.
The **Ashok Mehta** Committee was set up by the **Janata Government**; **L.M. Singhvi** by the **Rajiv Gandhi Government**.
**G.V.K. Rao** was set up by the **Planning Commission**.

80.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Ashok Mehta Committee – Three-tier Panchayati Raj
L.M. Singhvi Committee – Constitutional status and greater financial resources
Balwant Rai Mehta Committee – Three-tier Panchayati Raj

81.s: The 74th Constitutional Amendment is associated with which of the following combinations?

The application of Part IX to Union Territories

81.s: In K. Krishna Murthy v. Union of India (2010), the Constitution Bench upheld the constitutional validity of provisions enabling reservation for backward classes in local bodies under:

**Art. 280(3)(bb)** is about the Union Finance Commission and panchayats.

81.s: The report of the State Finance Commission is submitted to the Governor, who is required to:

81.s: The Finance Commission may deal with which of the following matters?

Panchayats get Central money only as **FC grants routed through the state**.

81.s: Which of the following is an example of Direct Democracy? C

81.s: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave effect to which Directive Principle of State Policy?

Article 44 on a Uniform Civil Code
Article 40 on organisation of village panchayats

81.s: The Union Finance Commission is constituted by the President of India:
o: Only once during the President's term
Every five years or earlier as deemed necessary
Every ten years or earlier as decided by Parliament

The Union Finance Commission is constituted every five years or earlier. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]

81.s:

81.x: All three are correct: Madras had India's first Municipal Corporation (1688); Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj at Nagaur on 2 October 1959; Madhya Pradesh was first to implement the 73rd Amendment in its true spirit.

n: The first Municipal Corporation in India was established at Madras in 1688. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Panchayati Raj was first inaugurated on 2 October 1959 at Nagaur in Rajasthan. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj at Nagaur. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Madhya Pradesh was the first state to implement the 73rd Amendment in its true spirit. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(3)**, **I, II and III**.
I: India's first Municipal Corporation was at **Madras**, **1688**.
II: Panchayati Raj was first inaugurated at **Nagaur** (Rajasthan) by **Jawaharlal Nehru**, **2 Oct 1959**.

The Union Finance Commission deals with fiscal distribution between the Union and the States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]

xa: It also suggests measures to **augment the Consolidated Fund of a State** to supplement **Panchayats** and **Municipalities**, based on **SFC** recommendations.

n: The Gram Sabha is the village-level general assembly of all persons registered in the village electoral rolls. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]

xs: **A is true, but R is false** — option **(3)**.

Voluntary: representation of **MPs and MLAs**, reservation for **backward classes**, devolving the **29** subjects.

The Commission is constituted not by the Chief Minister but by the Governor, and it does not make recommendations only for intermediate-level Panchayats; rather, it recommends the distribution of resources among Panchayats at all levels. Panchayat audit laws are not enacted by the Union Parliament. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xs: The **incorrect** statement is option **(3)**: Panchayat audit laws are **not** enacted by the **Union Parliament**.
Under **Article 243J**, the **State Legislature** provides for maintenance and **audit** of Panchayat accounts.
⚠ Audit law is not made by the Union Parliament, the **CAG** or the **District Collector**.
xa: The municipal counterpart of 243J is **Article 243Z**.
Other pairs: **243C / 243R** composition; **243D / 243T** reservation; **243E / 243U** tenure.
**243-I / 243-Y** State Finance Commission; **243K / 243ZA** State Election Commission.

82.s:
Under the 74th Amendment, consider the following:
1. A smaller urban area has a Municipal Council.
2. A larger urban area has a Municipal Corporation.
3. The 73rd and 74th Amendment systems are linked with district planning bodies.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
82.x: All three are correct: Municipal Councils serve smaller and Corporations larger urban areas, and both systems connect to district planning.
n: The institution for a smaller urban area under the 74th Amendment is the Municipal Council. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The institution for a larger urban area under the 74th Amendment is the Municipal Corporation. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The 73rd and 74th Amendment systems are interlinked with district planning bodies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xa: A **Nagar Panchayat** serves a **transitional** area.
Rural institutions: **Gram Panchayat** (village), **Panchayat Samiti** (block), **Zila Parishad** (district).
74th: **Part IX-A**, **12th Schedule** (**18** subjects), in force **1 June 1993**.

82.s: The Constitution (Seventy-Fourth Amendment) Act, 1992 inserted which Schedule?
82.x: The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA (Articles 243P-243ZG) and the Twelfth Schedule; the Eleventh Schedule came with the 73rd.
xa: The Twelfth Schedule is linked to **Art. 243W**.
In force **1 June 1993**.

82.s: Which one of the following is NOT a compulsory provision under the 74th Amendment?
o: Reservation for backward classes in every municipality
Ward Committees in municipalities having a population of three lakh or more
Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion to population
82.x: Reservation for backward classes is voluntary and is left to the State legislature. Ward Committees for municipalities with a population of three lakh or more, five-year terms, and SC/ST reservation are compulsory provisions.
82.tq: Find the provision expressly left to State legislative discretion among otherwise mandatory features.
xs: **Reservation for backward classes** is **voluntary** — option **(1)**.
Compulsory: **Ward Committees** (**3 lakh or more**), **SC/ST reservation** by population, **5-year** term.
xa: Other voluntary items: representation of **MPs, MLAs, MLCs**; manner of electing the **Chairperson**.
Devolving the Twelfth Schedule subjects (**243W**) is also voluntary.

82.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for Ward Committees?
82.x: Article 243S provides for Ward Committees; 243Q covers types of municipalities, 243R their composition and 243T reservation.
xa: **243U** — duration (**5 years**); **243V** — disqualifications (age **21**).
**243W** — powers and the **Twelfth Schedule**.

82.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about municipal tenure and elections?
o: An election must be held within one year of the dissolution of a municipality
A municipality has a five-year term
The State Election Commission conducts municipal elections
The State Finance Commission reviews the financial position of municipalities
82.x: An election must be held within six months of dissolution, not one year.
xa: ⚠ **243K / 243ZA** = SEC; **243I / 243Y** = SFC — one body each for panchayats and municipalities.
The term runs from the **first meeting**.

82.s: Which Article provides for the powers, authority and responsibilities of municipalities, including matters in the Twelfth Schedule?
82.x: Article 243W deals with the powers, authority and responsibilities of municipalities and links them with the Twelfth Schedule.
82.tq: Test the Article by its functional subject instead of its numerical proximity.
xs: **Article 243W** covers municipal powers and the **Twelfth Schedule** — option **(4)**.
**243Z** = audit; **243V** = disqualifications; **243Y** = Finance Commission.
xa: The Twelfth Schedule has **18** functional items.
Its panchayat counterpart is **243G** (Eleventh Schedule, **29**).

82.s: Under Article 243ZA, municipal elections are conducted by the:
82.x: Under Article 243ZA, municipal elections are conducted by the State Election Commission, not the Election Commission of India.
xa: The SEC under 243ZA is the same as under **243K**.
**243ZG** bars courts in electoral matters.

82.s: Where an industrial establishment provides municipal services, the Governor may under Article 243Q specify the area as a(n):
82.x: Under the proviso to Article 243Q the Governor may specify such an area as an industrial township, and a municipality need not be constituted there.
xa: The Governor specifies area types by **public notification**.
Criteria: population, density, revenue, non-agricultural employment, economic importance.

82.s: The term of a municipality under Article 243U is calculated from the date of its:
82.x: A municipality continues for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless dissolved earlier according to law.
82.tq: Distinguish the constitutional starting point from election and notification dates.
xs: The term runs **five years** from the **first meeting** — option **(3)** (**243U**).
Not from the election result, budget session or Governor's notification.
xa: After dissolution, polls within **six months**.
The municipality is **heard** before dissolution.
Panchayat term is also **5 years** (**243E**).

82.s: Under Article 243U, before a municipality is dissolved it must be given:
o: A reasonable opportunity of being heard
Approval of the State Election Commission
82.x: Article 243U requires that a municipality be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard before its dissolution.
xa: Fresh polls within **six months** of dissolution.
Polls are run by the **SEC** (**243ZA**).

82.s: Under Article 243R, which persons may be represented in a municipality but without the right to vote in its meetings?
o: Officials of the State Election Commission
Persons with special knowledge or experience in municipal administration
Members of the State Finance Commission
82.x: State law may provide for representation of persons with special knowledge or experience in municipal administration, but they cannot vote in municipal meetings.
xa: State law may add **Lok Sabha/Assembly** members for the area.
**Rajya Sabha/Council** members **registered as electors** there may be added.

82.s: Under Article 243S of the Constitution, a Wards Committee is mandatory in a municipality having a population of:
82.x: Article 243S makes Wards Committees mandatory in municipalities having a population of three lakh or more.
82.tq: Identify the constitutional population threshold precisely.
xs: Wards Committees are mandatory in municipalities of **three lakh or more** — option **(3)** (**243S**).
It is a **compulsory** provision of the 74th; other committees are voluntary.
xa: A committee may cover **one or more wards**.
⚠ **Wards committee** = Constitution (**243S**); **Area Sabha** = **Model Nagara Raj Bill 2008**.
**MPC** threshold: **10 lakh** population.

82.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Wards Committees:
1. A Wards Committee may consist of one ward or more than one ward.
2. The State Legislature determines their composition and territorial area.
3. The councillor representing a ward is a member of that ward's committee.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
82.x: All three statements are correct. Wards Committees may cover one or more wards, while State law determines their composition and territorial area; the ward councillor sits on the relevant committee.
82.tq: Check each statement against the separate constitutional and State-law roles.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
1: a Wards Committee may cover **one or more wards**.
2: **State law** decides composition and territorial area.
3: a ward's **councillor** sits on its committee.
xa: Mandatory where population is **3 lakh or more**.
Below it sits the **Area Sabha** (Model Nagara Raj Bill **2008**).

82.s: Which of the following is NOT a Twelfth Schedule subject?
o: Street lighting, parking, bus stops and public conveniences
82.x: Technical and vocational education is an Eleventh Schedule subject; the other three are Twelfth Schedule municipal subjects.
xa: Twelfth also covers **burial and cremation grounds**, electric crematoria.
And **water supply** (domestic, industrial, commercial), **roads and bridges**.

82.s: Which one of the following best describes the present status of District Planning Committees in most States?
o: They have been abolished by subsequent constitutional amendments.
They are generally weak, and operationalising them remains a continuing mandate of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.
They function exclusively under the Union Ministry of Finance.
They have been replaced by Metropolitan Planning Committees in all districts.
82.x: District Planning Committees remain weak in most States, and operationalising them continues to be listed among the mandates of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.
82.tq: Distinguish constitutional existence from effective institutional functioning.
xs: DPCs are **weak in most States**; **operationalising** them is still an **MoPR** mandate — option **(2)**.
They have not been abolished or replaced by MPCs.
xa: It is one of the **three** mandates of the **Ministry of Panchayati Raj**.
⚠ Proposed **District Development Councils** were criticised as parallel bodies bypassing Zila Panchayats and ULBs.

82.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 73rd Amendment inserted Part IX of the Constitution.
2. Part IX contains Articles 243 to 243-O.
3. Part IX-A contains Articles 243P to 243ZG.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
82.x: All are correct: the 73rd Amendment added Part IX (Articles 243–243-O) and the 74th added Part IX-A (Articles 243P–243ZG).
n: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act inserted Part IX of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Part IX contains Articles 243 to 243-O. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act inserted Part IX-A of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Part IX-A contains Articles 243P to 243ZG. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Panchayats are the rural local self-government institutions under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Municipalities are the urban local self-government institutions under the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xa: **District Planning Committee** = **Article 243ZD**; **Metropolitan Planning Committee** = **Article 243ZE**.
73rd added the **11th Schedule** (**29** subjects); 74th the **12th Schedule** (**18** subjects).
Part IX institutions: **Gram Panchayat**, **Panchayat Samiti**, **Zila Parishad**.
**Part IX-B** (Co-operative Societies) came by the **97th Amendment, 2011**.

82.s:
Assertion (A): The minimum qualifying age for Panchayats and Municipalities is 21 years.
Reason (R): Articles 243F and 243V disqualify a person who has not attained 21 years of age from membership of a Panchayat or Municipality.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
82.x: Both are true and R explains A: Articles 243F and 243V bar anyone under 21 from membership of Panchayats and Municipalities, which is why 21 is the minimum qualifying age.
82.tq: Recall which Articles carry the disqualification rules.
n: Article 243C deals with the composition of Panchayats and Municipalities. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243R also deals with the composition of Panchayats and Municipalities. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
The minimum qualifying age for Panchayats and Municipalities is 21 years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xs: Both are true and R is the correct **explanation** of A — option **(1)**.
**Articles 243F** (Panchayats) and **243V** (Municipalities) bar anyone under **21 years** from membership.
That is why **21** is the minimum qualifying age for both.
xa: Composition: **243C** (Panchayats) and **243R** (Municipalities), regulated by the **State Legislature**.
Tenure: **243E** / **243U** — **five years**; elections within **six months** of early dissolution.
Reservation: **243D** / **243T** — women not less than **one-third** of seats and chairperson posts.

82.s:
Consider the following statements regarding premature dissolution of a local body:
I. Elections must ordinarily be held within six months of dissolution.
II. Elections are not required if the remaining term is less than six months.
III. The fixed term of a local body is seven years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
82.x: I and II are correct: after early dissolution, elections must be held within six months, unless less than six months of the term remain. III is false because the term is five years.
82.tq: Recall the five-year term and the six-month rule.
n: The fixed term of Panchayats and Municipalities is five years. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
If a Panchayat or Municipality is dissolved prematurely, elections must be held within six months. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Elections within six months are not required when the remaining term is less than six months. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xs: Statements I and II are correct — option **(3)**, **I and II only**.
After early dissolution, elections must be held **within six months**, but not if **less than six months** of the term remain.
III is false: the fixed term is **five years**, not seven.
xa: Tenure Articles: **243E** (Panchayats) and **243U** (Municipalities).
Minimum age: **21** years (**243F** / **243V**).
A municipality must be heard before dissolution.
The reconstituted panchayat serves only the **remainder** of the term.

82.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the eight types of urban local bodies listed for India?
82.x: The eight listed types are Municipal Corporation, Municipality or Municipal Council, Notified Area Committee, Town Area Committee, Cantonment Board, Township, Port Trust and Special Purpose Agency. Zonal Development Authority is not in the list.
82.tq: Check every option against the complete named classification.
xs: **Zonal Development Authority** is not among the **eight** types — option **(2)**.
The eight: Municipal Corporation, Municipality, Notified Area Committee, Town Area Committee, **Cantonment Board**, Township, **Port Trust**, **Special Purpose Agency**.
xa: Only the first type groups appear in **243Q**; the rest lie outside it.
Cantonment Boards = **Ministry of Defence**.

82.s: Under Article 243V, disqualifications for membership of a municipality are determined primarily with reference to:
o: Only rules framed by the Union Government
The law made by the municipal council itself
Only the Representation of the People Act, 1951
The law applicable to elections to the State Legislature or a State law
82.x: A person may be disqualified under the law applicable to elections to the State Legislature or under a law made by the State Legislature.
82.tq: Identify the correct level of law governing disqualification.
xs: Disqualifications follow **the law for State Legislature elections or a State law** — option **(4)** (**243V**).
Not Union rules, nor the municipal council's own law.
xa: Minimum age: **21 years**.
Same pattern as panchayats under **243F**.

82.s: Which authority is responsible for electoral rolls and all municipal elections under Article 243ZA?
82.x: Article 243ZA places the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of municipal elections under the State Election Commission, the same constitutional authority associated with Article 243K.
82.tq: Ask who would do this job and reject the similarly named Union body.
xs: The **State Election Commission** handles electoral rolls and all municipal polls under **243ZA** — option **(1)**.
It is the **same SEC** as under **Art. 243K**.
xa: AP SEC Commissioner **Anil Chandra Punetha** notified ward-wise photo rolls for **41 ULBs**.
Rolls due **22 Sep 2026**; qualifying date **1 Jan 2026**.

82.s: A Metropolitan Planning Committee is constituted for every metropolitan area with a population of:
82.x: An MPC is mandatory for every metropolitan area of ten lakh or more under Article 243ZE, and such an area may span more than one district.
xa: The 10 lakh definition is in **Art. 243P**.
The **DPC** is under **243ZD**.
⚠ **DPC four-fifths** elected vs **MPC two-thirds** elected.

82.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the composition of a Metropolitan Planning Committee?
o: Not less than two-thirds of its members are elected
Elected members are chosen from municipal members and panchayat chairpersons in the area
Elected representation reflects the ratio of urban and rural population
Elected representation is in proportion to the geographical area of urban and rural parts
82.x: Elected representation in the MPC follows the urban-rural population ratio, not area.
xa: ⚠ DPC: **four-fifths** elected, from district panchayat and municipal members.
The MPC prepares a **draft development plan** for the whole metropolitan area.

82.s: The Constitution requires not less than ____ of the members of a District Planning Committee to be elected.
82.x: At least four-fifths of DPC members must be elected; the rest are decided by State law, so the DPC is not wholly elected.
xa: ⚠ APPSC-GS 2018: "**all members elected**" is the false statement.
The elected share is in proportion to the district's **rural-urban population**.

82.s: Which of the following is correct about the plans of the DPC and the MPC?
o: The DPC prepares a plan for the metropolitan area; the MPC prepares the district plan.
The DPC consolidates panchayat and municipal plans; the MPC prepares a plan for the whole metropolitan area.
Both committees prepare plans only for rural areas.
Neither committee is concerned with local plans.
82.x: The DPC consolidates panchayat and municipal plans into a draft district plan, while the MPC prepares a draft plan for the entire metropolitan area.
xa: The MPC also considers **Union/State objectives and investments**.
Both chairpersons **forward** the plan to the **State Government**.

82.s:
With reference to the District Planning Committee (DPC) and the Metropolitan Planning Committee (MPC), consider the following statements:
1. The chairperson of the committee forwards the draft development plan to the State Government.
2. The manner of choosing the chairperson of these committees is fixed uniformly by Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
82.x: Statement 1 is correct: the chairperson of the DPC or MPC forwards the draft plan to the State Government. Statement 2 is wrong: State law, not Parliament, settles how the chairperson is chosen. Hence (a) is right; (b) and (c) wrongly accept statement 2, and (d) wrongly rejects statement 1.
82.tq: For DPC/MPC, composition and chairperson election are left to State law; the plan goes to the State Government.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
1: the **chairperson forwards** the draft plan to the **State Government**.
2 wrong: the manner of choosing the chairperson is fixed by **state law**, not Parliament.
xa: State law also settles the DPC's **composition**.

82.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
82.x: Article 243J deals with accounts and audit. 243A is the Gram Sabha, 243-I the State Finance Commission and 243ZD the District Planning Committee.
n: The District Planning Committee is associated with Article 243ZD. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243A deals with the Gram Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243-I deals with the State Finance Commission for Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243J deals with accounts and audit of Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xa: **243ZE** → **Metropolitan Planning Committee**.
The SFC is constituted by the **Governor** every **five years**; **243-Y** applies it to municipalities.
**243K** → State Election Commission (**243ZA** for municipalities).
**243G** → powers and responsibilities of Panchayats (**243W** for municipalities).

82.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the tenure and dissolution of Panchayats?
82.x: Article 243E covers tenure; 243D covers reservations, 243G powers and 243-I the State Finance Commission.
n: Article 243D deals with reservations in Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243E deals with the tenure of Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
If a Panchayat or Municipality is dissolved prematurely, elections must be held within six months. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243G deals with the powers and responsibilities of Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243-I deals with the State Finance Commission for Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xa: Municipal counterparts: **243T**, **243U**, **243W**, **243-Y**.
**243J** → accounts and audit; **243K** → State Election Commission.
The SFC is constituted by the **Governor** every **five years**.

82.s: Which Article provides for the Metropolitan Planning Committee?
82.x: Article 243ZE provides for the MPC; 243W covers municipal powers, 243Y the Finance Commission and 243Z audit.
n: The Metropolitan Planning Committee is associated with Article 243ZE. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243W deals with the powers and responsibilities of Municipalities. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243-Y deals with the State Finance Commission for Municipalities. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
Article 243Z deals with accounts and audit of Municipalities. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 94-97]
xa: Panchayat counterparts: **243G**, **243-I**, **243J**.
**243ZD** → District Planning Committee.
**243ZA** → State Election Commission for municipal elections.

82.s: Which one of the following is included in the Twelfth Schedule?
o: Cattle pounds and prevention of cruelty to animals
82.x: Cattle pounds and prevention of cruelty to animals are Twelfth Schedule subjects. Non-conventional energy, small-scale industries and technical and vocational education are Eleventh Schedule subjects used as distractors.
82.tq: Separate municipal Twelfth Schedule functions from Panchayat Eleventh Schedule distractors.
xs: **Cattle pounds and prevention of cruelty to animals** are Twelfth Schedule items — option **(3)** (APPSC-G2 2025).
⚠ **Small-scale industries**, **technical and vocational education** and **non-conventional energy** are **Eleventh** Schedule distractors.
xa: Only in Twelfth: **fire services**, **slum improvement**, **slaughter houses and tanneries**, **vital statistics**, **burial grounds**.
Twelfth has **18** items.

82.s: Which one of the following is NOT a subject in the Twelfth Schedule?
o: Regulation of slaughter houses and tanneries
82.x: Libraries and markets and fairs are listed under the Eleventh Schedule, not the Twelfth Schedule. Urban poverty alleviation, urban forestry and environmental protection, and regulation of slaughter houses and tanneries are Twelfth Schedule subjects.
82.tq: Use the municipal-versus-Panchayat list distinction to identify the excluded subject.
xs: **Libraries and markets and fairs** are **Eleventh** Schedule (panchayat) items — option **(1)**.
**Urban poverty alleviation**, **urban forestry and environment** and **slaughter houses and tanneries** are Twelfth Schedule items.
xa: Other Eleventh-only items: **PDS**, **small-scale industries**, **non-conventional energy**.
Twelfth also has **public health, sanitation, solid waste management**.

82.s:
With reference to the Kerala model of District Planning Committees, consider the following statements:
1. The DPC is chaired by the District Panchayat President.
2. The District Collector is the chairperson of the DPC.
3. The DPC integrates plans prepared through the People's Plan Campaign.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
82.x: Statement 1 is correct: in Kerala the District Panchayat President chairs the DPC. Statement 2 is wrong: the Collector is only the member-secretary (a Collector-chaired body is the AP pattern). Statement 3 is correct: the DPC integrates People's Plan Campaign plans. So (a) misses statement 3, (c) and (d) include the false statement 2; (b) is correct.
82.tq: Kerala: elected District Panchayat President chairs, Collector is member-secretary; AP: Collector chairs; Rajasthan: Zila Pramukh.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
1: Kerala's DPC is chaired by the **District Panchayat President**.
2 wrong: the **Collector** is only **member-secretary** (Collector chairs in **AP**).
3: it integrates plans from the **People's Plan Campaign**.
xa: **Rajasthan**: **Zila Pramukh** chairs the DPC.
MoPR still lists **operationalising DPCs** as a mandate.

82.s: As per the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26, how many of the State's 123 urban local bodies are Municipal Corporations?
82.x: The Survey 2025-26 lists 17 Municipal Corporations, 76 Municipalities and 30 Nagar Panchayats among AP's 123 ULBs.
xa: Year-specific keys: APPSC 2018 = **71** municipalities; G1 2019 = **17** corporations.
APPCA May 2026 gives "**113** municipalities, **7** cantonment boards" — use the Survey split.

82.s: Under G.O. Rt. No. 1065 dated 19 August 2026, the reservation provided for Backward Classes in Andhra Pradesh Urban Local Bodies is:
82.x: G.O. Rt. No. 1065 provides 33.33 percent reservation for Backward Classes in Urban Local Bodies.
82.tq: Distinguish the urban reservation figure from the rural reservation figure.
xs: **G.O. Rt. No. 1065** gives **33.33 percent** BC reservation in AP ULBs — option **(2)**.
**34%** is the figure for **rural** bodies.
xa: It is implemented under both municipal laws.
Approved by the AP Cabinet on **18 Aug 2026**.

82.s: The nodal department for Urban Local Bodies in Andhra Pradesh is the:
o: Municipal Administration and Urban Development Department
Panchayat Raj and Rural Development Department
82.x: The Municipal Administration and Urban Development (MA&UD) Department is the nodal department for ULBs in AP.
xa: Laws: **AP Municipalities Act, 1965** + corporations law.
AP has **123** ULBs.

82.s: Which pair of laws governs municipalities and municipal corporations in Andhra Pradesh respectively?
o: AP Municipalities Act, 1994 and AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1965
AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1956 and AP Municipalities Act, 2001
AP Municipalities Act, 1965 and AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994
Andhra Pradesh Panchayats Act, 1965 and AP Municipalities Act, 1994
82.x: Municipalities (and Nagar Panchayats) in AP are governed by the AP Municipalities Act, 1965, and Municipal Corporations by the AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 (as CDCA cites it; some 2026 reports name a 1955 Corporations Act). Options A and B swap or misdate the two Acts, and D names a Panchayats Act.
82.tq: Distinguish the two enactments by both subject and year.
xs: **AP Municipalities Act, 1965** and **AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994** — option **(3)**.
Options 1 and 2 swap or misdate the Acts; option 4 names a **Panchayats** Act.
xa: ⚠ CDCA cites the **1994** Corporations Act; TH cites a **1955** Act.
33.33% BC reservation is applied under **both** laws.

82.s: Who is the State Election Commissioner of Andhra Pradesh who notified ward-wise photo electoral rolls for 41 urban local bodies in 2026?
82.x: Anil Chandra Punetha is the AP State Election Commissioner who notified ward-wise photo rolls for 41 ULBs (12 corporations and 29 municipalities/nagar panchayats). The other names are not the current SEC.
82.tq: AP SEC 2026: Anil Chandra Punetha.
xs: AP SEC **Anil Chandra Punetha** notified ward-wise photo rolls for **41 ULBs** — option **(2)**.
These cover **12** Corporations + **29** municipalities/NPs.
xa: Corporations include **GVMC**, **Vijayawada**, **Guntur**, **Tirupati**, **Kurnool**.
Rolls due **22 Sep 2026**; qualifying date **1 Jan 2026**.

82.s: In August 2026, the AP Cabinet approved which method for choosing Mayors and municipal or Nagar Panchayat chairpersons?
82.x: The Cabinet approved direct election of Mayors and municipal or Nagar Panchayat chairpersons, replacing the indirect system.
xa: Under the 74th, the manner of electing the chairperson is **left to the state**.
The same meeting approved **33.33%** BC quota in ULBs.

82.s: Municipalities have Constitutional respon sibilities in respect of which of the following as per the Twelfth Schedule?
82.x: " Cattle Pounds; Cattle animals " is listed under the Twelfth Schedule (Municipal subjects). The other three options are Eleventh Schedule (Panchayat / rural) subjects instead.

82.s:
Assertion (A): The Twelfth Schedule includes functions relating to urban poverty alleviation.
Reason (R): The Twelfth Schedule is concerned exclusively with physical infrastructure such as roads, bridges and water supply.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
82.x: The Assertion is true because urban poverty alleviation is a Twelfth Schedule subject. The Reason is false because the Schedule also covers social, environmental, cultural and regulatory functions, not exclusively physical infrastructure.
82.tq: Test the absolute word “exclusively” in the Reason against the wider range of municipal functions.
xs: **A is true but R is false** — option **(3)**.
A true: **urban poverty alleviation** is a **Twelfth Schedule** item.
R false: the Schedule also covers **welfare**, **health and environment**, **culture** and civic items — not only roads, bridges and water supply.
xa: Welfare items: **weaker sections** incl. disabled; **slum improvement and upgradation**.

PESA not covered: **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram** and States like **Tamil Nadu**.

83.s: Scheduled Tribes constitute approximately what proportion of India's population as per Census 2011?
83.x: PESA covers Scheduled Tribe populations constituting approximately 8.6 percent of India's population.
83.tq: Identify the precise percentage rather than relying on approximate scale comparisons.
xs: PESA covers the ST population, about **8.6 percent** of India — option **(2)** is correct.
For this population PESA makes the **Gram Sabha**, not the Panchayat, the nucleus of self-rule.
xa: **705** ethnic groups are notified as STs.
Largest tribal population: **MP**; largest tribe: **Bhil**.
STs are notified by the **President** under **Art. 342**.
83.fixed: 8.6% is the national ST share (Census 2011), not the population 'covered by PESA'

83.s: The administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes are governed by which of the following?
o: Part X, Article 244(2) and the Sixth Schedule
Part X, Article 244(1) and the Fifth Schedule
83.x: Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes come under Part X, Article 244(1) and the Fifth Schedule. Tribal areas of the North-East come under Article 244(2) and the Sixth Schedule.
83.tq: Discriminate Article 244(1) (Fifth Schedule) from 244(2) (Sixth Schedule).
n: Scheduled Areas are governed under Part X of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
Article 244(1) governs Scheduled Areas. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Fifth Schedule governs the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Fifth Schedule relates to Scheduled Areas. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
xs: Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes are governed by **Part X, Article 244(1)** and the **Fifth Schedule** — option **(2)**.
**Article 244(2)** with **275(1)** relates to the **Sixth Schedule** — the **Tribal Areas** of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
xa: Scheduled Areas are **declared by the President** in consultation with the Governor.
Declaring a Scheduled Area does **not** make it a **Union Territory**; the State's executive power continues, subject to the Fifth Schedule.
The **Governor** reports on Scheduled Areas **directly to the President**, annually and when required.
**Art. 275(1)** provides **grants-in-aid from the Consolidated Fund of India**.

83.s:
Assertion (A): A Tribal Advisory Council is established in each State having Scheduled Areas.
Reason (R): The Tribal Advisory Council advises on matters pertaining to the welfare and advancement of Scheduled Tribes.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
83.x: Both are true: every State with Scheduled Areas must have a Tribal Advisory Council (Fifth Schedule, para 4), which advises on tribal welfare. What it does does not explain why it is required, so R does not explain A.
83.tq: Ask whether a body's function explains why it must exist.
n: A Tribal Advisory Council is mandatory in each State having Scheduled Areas. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
A Tribal Advisory Council advises on matters relating to the welfare of Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
A Tribal Advisory Council advises on matters relating to the advancement of Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
A Tribal Advisory Council is established under Paragraph 4 of the Fifth Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
xs: Both are true, but R is **not** the correct **explanation** of A — option **(2)**.
A: a **Tribes/Tribal Advisory Council** is **mandatory** in each State having **Scheduled Areas** (**Paragraph 4**, Fifth Schedule).
R: it advises on the **welfare and advancement** of Scheduled Tribes — its role, not the reason it must exist.
xa: If the **President directs**, a TAC is also set up in a State with STs but no Scheduled Areas.
Size: **not more than 20 members**, about **three-fourths ST MLAs**.
It advises only on matters **referred by the Governor**.
⚠ The Constitution's name is the **Tribes Advisory Council**.

83.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Fifth Schedule – Tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram
Sixth Schedule – Special provisions for Nagaland
Article 371-A – Scheduled Areas in other States
83.x: Article 275(1) provides grants-in-aid for tribal welfare. The Sixth Schedule covers Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, the Fifth other States, and 371-A Nagaland.
n: Article 244(1) governs Scheduled Areas. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Fifth Schedule governs the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Sixth Schedule is governed by Article 244(2). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Sixth Schedule is associated with Article 275(1). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Sixth Schedule concerns the administration of Tribal Areas. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Sixth Schedule relates to Tribal Areas. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Fifth Schedule relates to Scheduled Areas. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
xa: The Fifth Schedule covers **10** States, incl. **Andhra Pradesh** and **Telangana**.
⚠ **Manipur**, **Nagaland**, **Arunachal Pradesh** and **Sikkim** are not under the Sixth Schedule.
The Sixth Schedule is **not population-based** — "all states with ST above 40%" is wrong (APPSC-G2 2025).

83.s: Which of the following pairs relating to tribal areas is wrongly matched?
o: Autonomous District Councils – Sixth Schedule bodies with legislative, executive and judicial powers
Paragraph 5 of the Fifth Schedule – Governor's power to restrict tribal land transfer and money-lending
Tribes Advisory Council – Sixth Schedule body with legislative, executive and judicial powers
Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997) – Lease of tribal land to private miners held void
83.x: The Tribes Advisory Council is the mandatory advisory body in Fifth Schedule States, not a Sixth Schedule body with law-making powers.
n: The key governance body under the Fifth Schedule is the Tribal Advisory Council. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The key governance bodies under the Sixth Schedule are Autonomous District Councils and Autonomous Regional Councils. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Governor oversees land transfers under the Fifth Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
Autonomous District Councils exercise significant legislative powers under the Sixth Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
Autonomous District Councils exercise significant administrative powers under the Sixth Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
Autonomous District Councils exercise significant judicial powers under the Sixth Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
xa: There are **10 ADCs**: Assam 3, Meghalaya 3, Tripura 1, Mizoram 3.
An ADC has up to **30 members** — **4 nominated** by the Governor, **26 elected**; elected members serve **5 years**.
⚠ An **autonomous region** is a unit **within** an autonomous district (APPSC-G2 2017).

83.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The President declares an area as a Scheduled Area.
2. The Governor submits the administration report on Scheduled Areas to the President.
3. The Chief Minister submits the administration report to the Union Home Ministry.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
83.x: The President declares Scheduled Areas and the Governor reports to the President; the Chief Minister does not report to the Home Ministry.
n: The President of India declares an area as a Scheduled Area. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The President of India notifies an area as a Scheduled Area. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
A Tribal Advisory Council advises on matters relating to the welfare of Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
A Tribal Advisory Council advises on matters relating to the advancement of Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Governor submits a report regarding the administration of Scheduled Areas directly to the President of India. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Scheduled Areas administration report is not submitted by the Chief Minister to the Union Home Ministry. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The President is the authority for area notification. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Governor is the authority for submitting the administrative report to the President. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
xa: The President can **increase/decrease**, alter boundaries, rescind or re-declare Scheduled Areas.
Criteria include **preponderance of tribal population**, compactness, viable administrative unit and economic backwardness.
The **Union** can give directions on the administration of Scheduled Areas.

83.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh is a Fifth Schedule State.
2. Assam is a Sixth Schedule State.
3. Nagaland is a Sixth Schedule State.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
83.x: AP is under the Fifth Schedule and Assam under the Sixth; Nagaland is not covered by the Sixth Schedule.
n: The 10 States covered by the Fifth Schedule are Andhra Pradesh (AP), Telangana (TS), Jharkhand (JH), Chhattisgarh (CG), Gujarat (GJ), Himachal Pradesh (HP), Madhya Pradesh (MP), Maharashtra (MH), Odisha (OD), and Rajasthan (RJ). [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
Assam is covered by the Sixth Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
Mizoram is covered by the Sixth Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Sixth Schedule applies only to Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Sixth Schedule does not apply to Nagaland. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Sixth Schedule covers four North-Eastern States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
xa: Fifth Schedule States: AP, Telangana, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, HP, MP, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan.
PESA covers all **10** Fifth Schedule States; **Odisha** has only **draft rules** (Apr 2026).
⚠ PESA not covered: Assam, Meghalaya and **Tamil Nadu** (RPSC 2016).

83.s:
Assertion (A): Panchayats in the Fifth Schedule Areas are governed by the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996.
Reason (R): Part IX of the Constitution does not apply to the Scheduled Areas on its own; Article 243M lets Parliament extend it with modifications.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
83.x: Both are true and R explains A: Article 243M keeps Part IX out of the Scheduled Areas unless Parliament extends it, which is exactly what PESA, 1996 did, with modifications.
83.tq: Link Article 243M's exclusion to the need for the PESA law.
n: The provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act were enacted in 1996. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act is known as PESA. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 114-117]
xs: Both are true and R is the correct **explanation** of A — option **(1)**.
**Art. 243M(1)** keeps **Part IX** out of Scheduled and Tribal Areas.
**Art. 243M(4)(b)** lets Parliament extend it with modifications — done by **PESA, 1996**.
xa: Such a law is **not an amendment under Art. 368**.
PESA applies to **Fifth Schedule** areas only, not Sixth Schedule areas.
Inconsistent State laws **lapse one year** after assent.
Higher-level panchayats must not usurp **Gram Sabha** powers.

83.s: If a particular area is brought under the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution of India, which one of the following statements best reflects the consequence of it?
o: This would prevent the transfer of land of tribal people
This would create a local self-governing body in that
This would convert that area into a Union Territory
The State having such areas would be declared a
83.x: The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution defines scheduled areas as the areas defined so by the President of India. In India, there are 10 states having scheduled areas. With consultation of the governor of state, the president can alter, add or diminish the boundary of a scheduled area. The Governor can also repeal or amend any regulations with respect to the state having scheduled areas, but only with the assent of the President of India. Para (5) of the Fifth Schedule provides special power to the governor of the concerned state. Under this power, he prevents the transfer of land from tribal people to non-tribal people.

83.s: In a Scheduled Area, the Governor may direct that an Act of Parliament or of the State Legislature shall:
o: Apply only after approval of every Gram Sabha
Not apply, or apply with specified modifications
Apply only after approval of the Tribes Advisory Council
Stand repealed for that area by executive order
83.x: Under the Fifth Schedule the Governor may direct that such an Act shall not apply, or shall apply with specified modifications, to a Scheduled Area.
xa: Exam angle (**APPSC-G2 2017**): "Governor is NOT authorised to direct that an Act does not apply" is the **false** statement.
The Governor's regulations may **repeal Acts**, but need the **President's assent**.
In the Sixth Schedule, laws apply as directed by the **Governor** (Assam) or **President** (Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram).

83.s: Under PESA, a Gram Sabha in a Scheduled Area may be constituted at the level of a:
o: Habitation such as a para, majra or tola
83.x: PESA recognises habitation-level Gram Sabhas, including units such as a para, majra or tola.
xa: Its meeting is presided over by an **ST member elected by the Gram Sabha**, not the Sarpanch (**CGPSC 2015**).
AP has **2,038 notified PESA Gram Sabhas** being strengthened.
**19 model GPs** covering **43 Gram Sabhas** are being developed in AP.

83.s: If a State law is inconsistent with PESA, the inconsistent provision generally ceases to operate after:
o: Two years from publication in the Gazette
One year from the date of assent
83.x: Under PESA, any provision of a State Panchayat law inconsistent with it ceases to operate one year from the date PESA received assent (24 December 1996), unless amended earlier. Six months, two years and five years are not the stated period.
83.tq: Recall the statutory time limit and distinguish it from nearby constitutional periods.
xs: A State law inconsistent with PESA lapses **one year from the date of assent** — option **(4)** is correct.
PESA received assent on **24 Dec 1996**; six months, two years and five years are not the stated period.
xa: PESA was enacted after the **Bhuria Committee** report (**1995**).
AP followed with an amending Act in **1998** and the **AP PESA Rules 2011**.
Enabling clause: **Art. 243M(4)(b)**.

83.s: Under Paragraph 5 of the Fifth Schedule, the Governor may make regulations for which of the following purposes?
o: Establishing Autonomous District Councils in all States
Prohibiting or restricting transfer of tribal land to non-tribals and regulating money-lending to STs
Creating new Union Territories and regulating elections to Parliament
Transferring executive power over Scheduled Areas to the President
83.x: Under paragraph 5 of the Fifth Schedule, the Governor can make regulations to stop or limit tribal land passing to non-tribals and to control money-lending to Scheduled Tribes.
83.tq: Recall the Governor's regulation powers under the Fifth Schedule.
n: The Governor may make regulations prohibiting the transfer of tribal land to non-tribals. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Governor may make regulations restricting the transfer of tribal land to non-tribals. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Governor may make regulations regulating money-lending to Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
xs: Under **Paragraph 5**, the Governor may make regulations **prohibiting or restricting transfer of tribal land** to non-tribals and **regulating money-lending** to STs — option **(2)**.
These are **regulations for peace and good government** of a Scheduled Area (G2 2017 key).
**Autonomous District Councils** belong to the **Sixth Schedule**, not the Fifth; and a Scheduled Area does **not** become a **Union Territory**.
xa: Regulations may also regulate the **allotment of land**.
They are made after consulting the **TAC** and need the **President's assent**.
The Governor may direct that any Act **does not apply**, or applies with modifications, to a Scheduled Area.
AP's **Land Transfer Regulation 1 of 1959** (amended by Regulation **1 of 1970**) bars land transfers to non-tribals in Scheduled Areas.

83.s: With reference to the Sixth Schedule, which one of the following is correct regarding the composition of an Autonomous District Council?
o: Twenty-eight members are elected and two are nominated by the Governor
Twenty-four members are elected and six are nominated by the Governor
All 30 members are nominated by the Governor
Twenty-six members are elected and four are nominated by the Governor
83.x: A District Council may have 30 members, of whom 26 are elected by adult franchise and four are nominated by the Governor.
83.tq: Split the total strength into elected and nominated components.
xs: An ADC has up to **30 members**: **twenty-six elected** by adult franchise and **four nominated by the Governor** — option **(4)** is correct.
Elected members serve **5 years**.
xa: There are **10** ADCs: Assam **3**, Meghalaya **3**, Tripura **1**, Mizoram **3**.
Each **autonomous region** has its own **Regional Council**.
ADCs legislate on land, forests, **shifting cultivation**, inheritance, marriage, social customs — with the **Governor's assent**.

83.s: Which one of the following is NOT a subject within the legislative sphere of an Autonomous District Council under the Sixth Schedule?
83.x: District Councils may legislate on inheritance, village administration and social customs, among other local tribal matters. Citizenship is not included in this field.
83.tq: Find the outside subject among a cluster of genuine Sixth Schedule powers.
xs: **Citizenship of India** is not in an ADC's legislative sphere — option **(2)** is correct.
ADCs legislate on **land, forests, canal water, shifting cultivation, village administration, inheritance, marriage, social customs** — covering options (1), (3) and (4).
xa: Such laws need the **Governor's assent**.
Judicial: **village councils/courts** for suits between tribals.
Financial: assess **land revenue** and levy specified taxes; **grants-in-aid** under **Art. 275**.

83.s: Under the Sixth Schedule, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Legislative power – Village councils for suits between tribal persons
Executive and financial power – Regulation of land, forests and social customs
Judicial power – Assessment of land revenue
Constitutional financial assistance – Grants-in-aid from the Consolidated Fund of India
83.x: Article 275 grants-in-aid from the Consolidated Fund of India are the constitutional financial assistance; legislative power covers land, forests and customs, judicial power village courts, and executive power revenue and taxes.
xa: **High Court** jurisdiction over these areas is as the **Governor** specifies.
ADC laws need the **Governor's assent**.
ADC: **26 elected**, **4 nominated**; term **5 years**.

83.s: To be eligible under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must show residence for:
83.x: OTFDs must prove three generations, taken as 75 years, of residence before 2005. One or two generations is too short, and 1980 and 1950 are the wrong cut-off years.
83.tq: OTFD = 3 generations = 75 years, before 2005.
xs: **OTFDs** must show residence for **three generations (75 years) before 2005** — option **(3)** is correct.
One or two generations is too short, and **1980/1950** are the wrong cut-offs.
xa: **FRA 2006** gives individual + community rights over forest land + **ownership of MFP**.
Forest land for public utilities needs **Gram Sabha** recommendation.
NCST requisitioned FRA reports from **MoEFCC**.

83.s: Under which Schedule does the Union's executive power extend to giving directions to a State on the administration of its tribal areas?
83.x: Under the Fifth Schedule the Union may give directions to the State regarding Scheduled Areas; under the Sixth, administration stays within the State's executive authority.
xa: In the Fifth Schedule, the **Governor** reports to the President **annually or when required**.
Fifth: **President declares** areas; Sixth: **Governor organises** districts.
PESA applies only to the **Fifth Schedule** areas.

83.s: The Sixth Schedule does NOT apply to which of the following States?
83.x: Manipur is not covered by the Sixth Schedule (it has hill-area committees under Article 371-C), and neither is Nagaland. Only Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram are.
83.tq: Recall the four Sixth Schedule States.
n: Assam is covered by the Sixth Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
Meghalaya is covered by the Sixth Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
Mizoram is covered by the Sixth Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Sixth Schedule applies only to Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Sixth Schedule does not apply to Manipur. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
The Sixth Schedule covers four North-Eastern States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
xs: The Sixth Schedule does **not** apply to **Manipur** — option **(2)**.
It covers **four North-Eastern States only**: **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**.
xa: **Nagaland** is also out (**Art. 371A**); so are **Arunachal Pradesh** and **Sikkim**.
Sixth Schedule bodies: **Autonomous District Councils** and **Autonomous Regional Councils**.
Application of Acts: **Assam** → Governor; **Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram** → President.
The Sixth Schedule is **not population-based** — no ST-share threshold decides coverage (APPSC-G2 2025).

83.s: Which of the following is NOT an area of special focus associated with the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
o: Regulation of inter-State trade in agricultural commodities
83.x: The Commission focuses on minor forest produce, mineral and water rights, and rehabilitation of displaced tribals. Regulation of inter-State agricultural trade is not listed as this special focus.
83.tq: Identify the unrelated function among several functions linked to tribal safeguards.
xs: **Regulation of inter-State trade in agricultural commodities** is not an NCST focus area — option **(4)** is correct.
The NCST's extra focus is **ownership of minor forest produce**, safeguarding **mineral and water rights** and **rehabilitation** of displaced tribals — options (1), (2) and (3).
xa: The NCST (**Art. 338A**) was inserted by the **89th Amendment Act, 2003** and set up in **2004**.
It used its powers to requisition **FRA** implementation reports from **MoEFCC**.
Under **PESA**, Gram Sabhas/Panchayats get **ownership** of minor forest produce.

83.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Gram Sabha under PESA?
o: It can settle local disputes according to local practice.
It is the nucleus of village governance.
It can protect traditions and manage common property resources.
Higher-level Panchayats may take over its powers.
83.x: PESA seeks to prevent higher-level Panchayats from taking over the powers of Gram Sabhas.
xa: Seats in PESA panchayats: STs get at least **50%**; **all Chairperson posts** go to STs.
Inconsistent State laws lapse **one year** after assent.
At district level, States should follow the **Sixth Schedule pattern**.

83.s: What was held by the Supreme Court in Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997)?
o: The Fifth Schedule did not apply to tribal land used for mining.
All tribal land in Scheduled Areas could be freely transferred to private parties for mining.
Transfer or lease of tribal land in Scheduled Areas to private parties for mining was null, void and inoperative.
Only money-lending regulations in Scheduled Areas were unconstitutional.
83.x: In Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997), the Supreme Court held that transferring or leasing tribal land in Scheduled Areas to private companies for mining is void under the Fifth Schedule.
83.tq: Recall the Samatha ruling of 1997.
n: Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh was decided in 1997. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh is a landmark ruling. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]

The Supreme Court held in Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh that the transfer of tribal land in Scheduled Areas to private parties for mining operations is null, void, and inoperative under the Fifth Schedule. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 129-131]
xs: In **Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997)**, transfer or lease of tribal land in Scheduled Areas to **private parties** for **mining** was held **null, void and inoperative** — option **(3)**.
The **Supreme Court** held such leasing violates the **Fifth Schedule** and the AP Land Transfer Regulation.
The State itself was treated as a "**person**" under the Regulation.
xa: ⚠ **Niyamgiri / Orissa Mining Corporation case** (SC, **2013**): **Gram Sabhas** decided on bauxite mining.
The Niyamgiri Gram Sabhas rejected the **Vedanta** project.
**FRA 2006**: forest land for public utilities only on **Gram Sabha** recommendation.
**CNT Act 1908** was breached by the **Bharatmala** highway without PESA consent.

83.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. The Dhebar Commission was established in 1960 under U. N. Dhebar for tribal welfare.
II. The Bhuria Committee was established in 1995 under Dilip Singh Bhuria and provided the basis for the PESA Act.
III. The Xaxa Committee was established in 2013 under Virginius Xaxa to review tribal development.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
83.x: All three are correct: Dhebar (1960) dealt with tribal welfare, Bhuria (1995) laid the basis for PESA, and Xaxa (2013) reviewed tribal development.
83.tq: Arrange the tribal committees in time order.
n: The Dhebar Commission was established in 1960. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
U. N. Dhebar chaired the Dhebar Commission. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
The Bhuria Committee was established in 1995. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
Dilip Singh Bhuria chaired the Bhuria Committee. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
The Bhuria Committee provided the basis for the PESA Act. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
The Xaxa Committee was established in 2013. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
Virginius Xaxa chaired the Xaxa Committee. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
The purpose of the Xaxa Committee was to review tribal development. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(3)**, **I, II and III**.
**Dhebar Commission** — **1960**, **U. N. Dhebar**, **tribal welfare**.
**Bhuria Committee** — **1995**, **Dilip Singh Bhuria**, basis for the **PESA Act, 1996**.
**Xaxa Committee** — **2013** (also given as **2014**), **Virginius Xaxa**, to review **tribal development**.
xa: **Lokur Committee (1965)** formulated **five criteria** for scheduling STs.
Bhuria was set up by the **Ministry of Rural Development**; Xaxa by the **Prime Minister's Office**.
Xaxa recommended preventing **tribal land alienation** and strictly enforcing the **FRA, 2006**.

83.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Bhuria Committee was constituted by the Ministry of Rural Development.
II. It recommended constitutional recognition of traditional Gram Sabhas in Schedule V areas.
III. Its recommendations provided the foundation for the PESA Act, 1996.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
83.x: All three are correct: the Bhuria Committee (Ministry of Rural Development, 1995) called for recognising traditional Gram Sabhas in Schedule V areas, which led to PESA, 1996.
83.tq: Recall the Bhuria Committee.
n: The Bhuria Committee was constituted by the Ministry of Rural Development. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Bhuria Committee recommended constitutional recognition of traditional Gram Sabhas in Schedule V areas. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Bhuria Committee provided the foundation for the PESA Act, 1996. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(3)**, **I, II and III**.
The **Bhuria Committee** (**1995**) was constituted by the **Ministry of Rural Development**.
It recommended **constitutional recognition** of **traditional Gram Sabhas** in **Schedule V areas**, the **foundation** of **PESA, 1996**.

83.s:
With reference to Scheduled Areas in India, consider the following statements:
1. Within a State, the notification of an area as Scheduled Area takes place through an Order of the President.
2. The largest administrative unit forming the Scheduled Area is the District, and the lowest is the cluster of villages in the Block.
3. The Chief Ministers of the concerned States are required to submit annual reports to the Union Home Ministry on the administration of Scheduled Areas in the States.
How many of the above statements are correct?
83.x: Statement 1 is correct: In Article 244(1) of the Constitution, the expression Scheduled Areas means such areas as the President may, by order, declare to be Scheduled Areas. Statement 2 is correct: The largest administrative unit forming the scheduled areas has been the district, and the lowest is the cluster of villages in the block. Most of the districts form scheduled areas only partially. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Governor of each State having Scheduled Areas therein shall annually, or whenever so required by the President, make a report to the President regarding the administration of the Scheduled Areas in that State, and the executive power of the Union shall extend to the giving of directions to the State as to the administration of the said areas.

83.s: Scheduled Tribe status is –
83.x: According to the Constitutional (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950 the status of Schedule Tribes is religiously neutral. A follower of any religion can be included in the Scheduled Tribe Community, while by para-3 of the Constitutional (Scheduled Caste) Order, 1950 only Hindus (which includes Buddhists and Sikhs), can be included in the Scheduled Caste Community. The National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities, headed by Rangnath Mishra, had recommended repealing this para.

83.s: Who has the Constitutional Power to declare a geographical area as a ‘’Scheduled Area’’?
83.x: The President of India has the Constitutional power to declare a geographical area as a "Scheduled Area". This provision is described in the "Fifth Schedule" of the Constitution. The President may, at any time, by order – (i) Direct that the whole or any specified part of the Scheduled Area shall cease to be a Scheduled Area. (ii) Increase the area of any Scheduled Area of a State after consultation with the Governor of that State. (iii) Alter, but only by way of rectification of boundaries. (iv) On any alteration of the boundary of a State or admission into Union or establishment of new State, declare any territory not previously included in any State to be, or to form part of a, Scheduled Area.

83.s:
With reference to ‘Scheduled Areas’ in India, consider the following statements :
1. Within a State, the notification of an area as Scheduled Area takes place through an Order of the President.
2. The largest administrative unit forming the Scheduled Area is the District and the lowest is the cluster of villages in the Block.
3. The Chief Ministers of the concerned States are required to submit annual reports to the Union Home Ministry on the administration of Scheduled Areas in the States.
How many of the above statements are correct?
83.x: Part X of the Constitution, Article 244, provides for a unique administrative structure for some places classified as "scheduled areas" and "tribal areas." As per Part C of the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution, the expression Scheduled Areas means such areas as the President may, by order, declare to be Scheduled Areas. The largest administrative unit forming the scheduled areas is the district and the cluster of villages in the block is the lowest. Hence, statements 1 and 2 are correct. At present, 10 states of India have scheduled areas. These are: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha and Rajasthan. The governor has a special responsibility regarding such areas. He has to submit a report to the president regarding the administration of such areas, annually or whenever so required by the President. Hence statement 3 is not correct.

83.x: The criteria followed for the specification of a community, such as Scheduled Tribes, are indications of primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact with the community at large, and backwardness. These criteria are not spelted out in the Constitution but have become well established.

83.s: The provisions in Fifth Schedule and Sixth Schedule in the Constitution of India are made in order to
o: protect the interests of Scheduled Tribes
determine the powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats
protect the interests of all the border States
83.x: The Constitution of India provides special provisions under the Fifth Schedule and Sixth Schedule to safeguard the interests of Scheduled Tribes. The provisions of the Fifth Schedule shall apply to the administration and control of the Scheduled Areas and Tribes in any State other than the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution includes provisions for the administration of tribal areas in the states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram in northeast India. It establishes autonomous councils with legislative, judicial, executive, and financial powers to govern these areas independently.
