86.s: Media organisations are generally regarded as stakeholders of governance under which category?
86.x: Media organisations are counted among civil society stakeholders involved in governance.
86.tq: Test institutional classification through a nearby-category distinction.
xs: Media organisations are stakeholders under **civil society** — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ **Media** = civil society, not State.
xa: Stakeholders: **State** (legislature, judiciary, executive, bureaucracy), **Market**, **Civil Society**.
Civil society: **NGOs, VOs, media, trade unions, religious + pressure groups**.

86.s: Pressure groups, trade unions and NGOs belong to which set of governance stakeholders?
86.x: State, Market and Civil Society are the three broad stakeholder sets, and pressure groups, trade unions and NGOs belong to civil society.
xa: **Media** is also civil society.
Civil society also includes **VOs** and **religious** groups.

86.s: Which body, headed by the Cabinet Secretary, administers the Transaction of Business Rules?
86.x: The Cabinet Secretariat, headed by the Cabinet Secretary, works directly under the PM and administers the Transaction of Business Rules; the PMO is the PM's policy office.
xa: **NITI Aayog** (**2015**) is the apex public policy think tank, chaired by the **PM**.
AP CM's **two-month review cycle** for **₹50,999 crore** of Amaravati contracts resembles the Centre's **PRAGATI** model.

86.s: Who was appointed Vice Chairperson of NITI Aayog in 2026?
86.x: A is correct: Ashok Kumar Lahiri was appointed Vice Chairperson of NITI Aayog in 2026. B and C are earlier Vice Chairpersons, not the 2026 appointee. D, Amitabh Kant, was NITI Aayog's CEO, a different post. The Chairperson is the Prime Minister.
86.tq: NITI Aayog: Chair = PM; VC (2026) = Ashok Kumar Lahiri.
xs: **Ashok Kumar Lahiri** was appointed **Vice Chairperson** of NITI Aayog in **2026** — option **(1)** is correct.
NITI Aayog itself is **chaired by the PM**.
xa: NITI Aayog (**2015**) replaced the **Planning Commission** (**1950**).
It is **non-constitutional + non-statutory**.
NITI Aayog (with **WRI India**) launched the **second India Electric Mobility Index**.

86.s: Which of the following is identified as an accountability gap in governance?
o: Rising referral of Bills to parliamentary committees
Delays by Governors and Speakers in assent and Tenth Schedule decisions
86.x: Delays by Governors and Speakers on assent and Tenth Schedule matters are an accountability gap, along with an RTI backlog and fewer committee referrals.
xa: Other gaps: **RTI backlog** (over **4 lakh**); **fewer committee referrals** (**16%** in 17th LS).
Sri Lanka's proposed **22nd Amendment**: SC judges' retirement age from **65 to 67**.

86.s: In the legislative process, government Bills are generally drafted by the:
86.x: Parliament is the chief law-making body and the Cabinet decides the substance and timing of Bills, but the bureaucracy generally drafts them.
xa: Controls on the executive: **Question Hour** (most effective), **Zero Hour**, adjournment motions, financial control.
Committee referrals fell from **71%** (15th Lok Sabha) to **16%** (17th Lok Sabha).

86.s: Which of the following is regarded as the most effective parliamentary control over the executive among the listed devices?
86.x: Question Hour is identified as the most effective among the listed parliamentary controls over the executive.
86.tq: Recall the relative effectiveness of a parliamentary control device.
xs: **Question Hour** is the **most effective** parliamentary control over the executive — option **(2)** is correct.
Constitutional amendment and private members' bills are law-making, not executive controls.
xa: Other controls: **Zero Hour**, **half-an-hour discussions**, **adjournment motions**, **financial control**, ratification of laws.
Without a **Rajya Sabha** majority, governments must concede (**Prevention of Terrorism Bill 2002** was rejected there).

86.s: The share of Bills referred to parliamentary committees fell from about 71% in the 15th Lok Sabha to about what share in the 17th Lok Sabha?
86.x: C is correct: referral of Bills to committees fell from 71% in the 15th Lok Sabha to 16% in the 17th Lok Sabha, showing falling committee scrutiny. A, B and D are not the figures given; the drop was much steeper.
xs: Bills referred to committees fell from **71%** (**15th Lok Sabha**) to **16%** (**17th Lok Sabha**) — option **(3)** is correct.
This shows **falling committee scrutiny** (**30 Jul 2026**).
xa: ⚠ **71%** = 15th Lok Sabha; **16%** = 17th Lok Sabha.
"Fewer committee referrals" is listed as an **accountability gap**.

86.s: The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2018 was enacted by Parliament to overturn the effect of which Supreme Court decision?
86.x: B is correct: the SC/ST (PoA) Amendment 2018 followed the Subhash Kashinath Mahajan judgment. A, Shah Bano, led to the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act 1986. C, Kesavananda Bharati, laid down the basic structure limit on amendments. D, Vishaka, gave workplace sexual-harassment guidelines.
86.tq: Shah Bano gave the 1986 Act; Subhash Kashinath Mahajan gave the PoA Amendment 2018.
xs: The **SC/ST (PoA) Amendment 2018** overturned the **Subhash Kashinath Mahajan** decision — option **(2)** is correct.
**Shah Bano** led to the **Muslim Women Act 1986**; **Kesavananda Bharati** set the **basic structure** limit; **Vishaka** gave workplace harassment guidelines.
xa: A validating law must remove the **basis** of a judgment.

86.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the options available against a Supreme Court decision?
o: A review or curative petition is heard by the same Court
Parliament may amend the law to remove the basis of a judgment but cannot simply overrule it
A constitutional amendment under Article 368 must respect the basic structure
A Presidential reference under Article 143 produces a binding judgment on the dispute
86.x: A Presidential reference under Article 143 yields only an advisory opinion, not a binding judgment.
xa: Examples: **Muslim Women Act 1986** after **Shah Bano**; **SC/ST (PoA) Amendment 2018** after **Subhash Kashinath Mahajan**.
**Kesavananda Bharati** is the source of the **basic structure** limit.

86.s: In which year did Public Interest Litigation begin in India, with a case filed on behalf of prisoners?
86.x: PIL began in 1979 with a case filed on behalf of prisoners; its basis lies in Articles 32, 226 and 142.
xa: Criticism: **Upendra Baxi's** typology of fears — ideological, epistemic, management, legitimation, democratic.
PIL misuse for **publicity or political ends** draws criticism.

86.s: Which one of the following is NOT included in Upendra Baxi's typology of fears concerning judicial activism?
86.x: Upendra Baxi's typology includes ideological, epistemic, management, legitimation and democratic fears. Electoral fear is not included in the listed typology.
86.tq: Use the complete named classification to identify the outsider.
xs: **Electoral fear** is not in **Upendra Baxi's** typology — option **(4)** is correct.
His fears are **ideological, epistemic, management, legitimation, democratic** — covering options (1)–(3).
xa: Ignored **police-reform orders** → **legitimation** risk.
Overreach → **policy paralysis + backlog**.

86.s: Which of the following pairs of case and guideline subject is correctly matched?
86.x: Prakash Singh dealt with police reforms. Vishaka concerned workplace sexual harassment and T.S.R. Subramanian civil-services safeguards.
xa: Vishaka guidelines filled a legislative vacuum until the **POSH Act 2013**.
Prakash Singh: **State Security Commission**, fixed tenure for **DGP**, **Police Establishment Board**, **Police Complaints Authority**.

86.s: The Vishaka guidelines continued to operate in a legislative vacuum until the enactment of which law?
o: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
86.x: The Vishaka guidelines on workplace sexual harassment operated until the POSH Act was enacted in 2013.
86.tq: Link the judicial guideline with the later legislation that occupied the legislative field.
xs: The **Vishaka** guidelines (**1997**) filled the vacuum until the **POSH Act, 2013** — option **(1)** is correct.
They are an example of court guidelines that **acted as law**.
xa: Similar cases: **Prakash Singh (2006)** on police; **T.S.R. Subramanian (2013)** on civil servants.

86.s: The MKSS right-to-information movement led to which law?
86.x: The MKSS movement led to the RTI Act, 2005; Right to Work advocacy to MGNREGA and the Right to Food campaign to the NFSA.
xa: Right to Food rested on the **PUCL v. Union of India** PIL, **2001**.

86.s: The permanent executive in India includes:
o: All-India Services, State services, local staff and PSU staff
86.x: The permanent executive comprises All-India Services, State services, local staff and PSU staff, who help ministers formulate and implement policy.
xa: Recruitment: **UPSC + State PSCs**.
Accountability tools: **Vigilance, conduct rules, CAG, CVC, Lokpal**.

86.s: The 33.33% Backward Classes quota in Andhra Pradesh urban local bodies originated as:
86.x: The 33.33% BC quota in AP urban local bodies was an NDA 2024 poll promise, later implemented through G.O. Rt. No. 1065.
xa: It shows **manifesto → policy** in agenda setting.
Delivery tracking: **Action Taken Reports** against **seven sector white papers**.

86.s: From which date has Andhra Pradesh published Action Taken Reports on its seven sectoral white papers?
86.x: AP has published Action Taken Reports from 22 June 2026, so manifesto delivery can be tracked publicly.
xa: Manifesto example: **33.33% BC quota** (NDA **2024** promise).
ATRs + **DMEO** evaluations mark a shift to "**outcome-based**" governance.

86.s:
Assertion (A): The Press Information Bureau handles press briefings, accreditation of journalists and social-media communication.
Reason (R): The PM's Communication Wing handles publicity for the PMO and the Cabinet and gives daily newspaper feedback.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
86.x: Both are true, but they describe two separate bodies; the PM's Communication Wing's role does not explain the PIB's functions.
xa: New risk: AI-driven **foreign information manipulation** (**29 Jun 2026**).
Parties court **Gen Z (14-29)** on digital platforms (**4 Sep 2026**).

86.s: In which year was the National Innovation Council established as a Government body?
86.x: The National Innovation Council was set up in 2010; CPR, NCAER, PRS and ORF are independent bodies.
xa: Party-linked: **Syama Prasad Mookerjee Research Foundation** (BJP), **Rajiv Gandhi Foundation** (Congress).
Newer channels: **policy labs, hackathons, idea competitions**.

86.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Syama Prasad Mookerjee Research Foundation — Congress-linked body
86.x: The Syama Prasad Mookerjee Research Foundation is linked with the BJP, not the Congress. The Rajiv Gandhi Foundation is associated with the Congress.
86.tq: Look for the party affiliation that has been deliberately interchanged.
xs: **Syama Prasad Mookerjee Research Foundation — Congress-linked body** is wrong — option **(2)**; it is **BJP**-linked.
The **Rajiv Gandhi Foundation** is the **Congress**-linked body; **NCAER** is independent; **NITI Aayog** is a Government think tank.
xa: Independent: **CPR**, **PRS Legislative Research**, **ORF**.
Government: **National Innovation Council (2010)**.

86.s: NITI Aayog is chaired by the:
86.x: The Prime Minister chairs NITI Aayog, a non-constitutional, non-statutory policy think tank working on cooperative federalism.
xa: ⚠ **NITI Aayog** = **2015**; **Planning Commission** = **1950**.
It is a **Government** think tank, together with **DMEO**.
Vice Chairperson: **Ashok Kumar Lahiri** (**2026**).

86.s:
Consider the following statements regarding recruitment to the civil services:
1. Recruitment is conducted by the UPSC and the State Public Service Commissions.
2. Members of these Commissions can be removed only after an inquiry by Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
86.x: Statement 1 is correct: the UPSC and State PSCs recruit. Statement 2 is wrong: removal needs an inquiry by the Supreme Court, not Parliament. So 1 only (A); B and C include the false statement 2, D wrongly rejects statement 1.
86.tq: PSC members: removal only after a Supreme Court inquiry.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: recruitment is by the **UPSC + State PSCs**.
Statement 2 is wrong: members are removable only after a **Supreme Court** inquiry, not Parliament — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Bureaucracy concerns: **insensitivity to citizens**, **political interference**, **front-line discretion**.
Permanent executive: **All-India Services, State services, local + PSU staff**.

86.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a concern relating to bureaucracy?
86.x: Frontline implementation discretion is itself a concern, so 'complete absence of discretion' is not.
xa: **Lipsky**'s "street-level bureaucracy" is about front-line officials shaping outcomes.
Accountability tools: **Vigilance, conduct rules, CAG, CVC, Lokpal**.

86.s: Which of the following is correct about the image-building role of mass media?
o: The ideology of a media outlet can influence its treatment of news
Mass media play no part in shaping the identity of political personalities
Media treatment has no bearing on the public image of political personalities
A media outlet's ideology is irrelevant to how it treats news
86.x: Mass media shape the image of political personalities, and an outlet's ideology can colour its treatment of news.
xa: ⚠ Key (**APPSC-GS 2018**): **(A) true, (R) the correct explanation**.
Free press is necessary for a **vibrant democracy**.

86.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A free press is necessary for a vibrant democracy.
2. New media enable participatory communication.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
86.x: C is correct: both statements are true (APPSC-GS 2018 key). A free press is necessary for a vibrant democracy, and new media allow participatory, two-way communication. A and B each leave out a true statement; D wrongly rejects both.
86.tq: APPSC 2018: free press + new media statements, both true.
xs: **Both 1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)** (**APPSC-GS 2018** key).
A **free press** is necessary for a **vibrant democracy**; **new media** enable **participatory communication**.
xa: Mass media shape the **image and identity** of political personalities.
**PIB** handles press briefings, **accreditation**, social media.

86.s: What option does the government exercise and legislators have when they do not like a decision made by the Supreme Court?
o: Pass a constitutional amendment that circumvents the decision only
Pass a law challenging the decision only
Both are options pass a constitutional amendment that circumvents the decision or pass a law challenging the decision
86.x: If the legislature disagrees with a Supreme Court judgment, it may either pass a new law addressing the court's concerns or amend the Constitution to overcome the judgment. Both methods are constitutional mechanisms available to the legislature.

86.s:
Assertion:
(A) A free press necessary for a vibrant democracy.
Reason:
(B) New media technologies have facilitated participatory communication.
o: (A) is true and (B) is the correct explanation of (A)
86.x: Both statements are factually accurate on their own merits a free press is essential for democracy and new media has indeed enabled participatory communication-but the Reason does not directly explain the Assertion, only option marking both statements as simply true fits the key.

86.s:
Assertion
(A) The mass media shape the image and identity of political personalities Reason
(B) The ideology of the media outlet and treatment of news plays a significant role in creating an image.
o: (A) is true and (B) is the correct explanation of (A)
86.x: Assertion (A) is true: mass media does shape political image. Reason (B) is also true and directly explains why-media ideology and news treatment shape that image-making B the correct explanation of A.

86.s: Public Interest Litigation may attract criticism when it is used mainly for which purpose?
o: Protection of fundamental rights through judicial review
Constitutional interpretation in genuine public causes
86.x: PIL is criticised when it is misused for publicity or political purposes rather than for a genuine public cause or protection of rights.
86.tq: Distinguish the recognised constitutional purpose of PIL from its criticised misuse.
xs: PIL draws criticism when misused for **publicity or political ends** — option **(1)** is correct.
Protecting rights or helping disadvantaged groups is its proper use.
xa: PIL began in **1979**, on behalf of prisoners.

87.s: Which one is not true for good governance?
Which one of the following correctly represents the World Bank's definition of governance?
o: The manner in which power is exercised in managing a country's economic and social resources for development
The distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States
The exclusive exercise of authority by the executive branch
The process by which elections are conducted at regular intervals
87.x: The World Bank defines governance as the manner in which power is exercised in managing a country's economic and social resources for development.
87.tq: Match the exact institutional definition with the correct body.
xs: The **World Bank** defines governance as "**the manner in which power is exercised in the management of a country's economic and social resources for development**" — option **(1)** is correct.
It stresses **accountability, transparency, rule of law**.
xa: The World Bank first brought "**good governance**" into development discourse — **1989** report on **Sub-Saharan Africa**.
**UNDP (1997)**: exercise of **economic, political and administrative** authority.
**UNESCAP** stresses efficiency, effectiveness, equity, sustainability.

87.s: Which institution first brought the concept of 'good governance' into development discourse?
87.x: B is correct: the World Bank first brought 'good governance' into development discourse through its 1989 report on Sub-Saharan Africa (APPSC-GS 2018 key). A, UNDP, gave its own definition later (1997). C and D are not credited with introducing the term.
87.tq: Good governance term: World Bank, 1989, Sub-Saharan Africa.
xs: The **World Bank** first brought "**good governance**" into development discourse — option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC-GS 2018**).
It did so in its **1989** report on **Sub-Saharan Africa**; **UNDP** gave its definition later, in **1997**.
xa: World Bank stresses **accountability, transparency, rule of law**.
The World Bank's **WGI** cover **200+** countries since **1996**.

87.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the eight attributes of good governance identified in the UN/UNDP list?
87.x: Administrative centralisation is not one of the eight attributes. The list includes consensus orientation, participation, rule of law, effectiveness and efficiency, accountability, transparency, responsiveness, and equity and inclusiveness.
87.tq: Find the odd feature that is absent from the recognised list.
xs: **Administrative centralisation** is not one of the **8 attributes** — option **(3)** is correct.
The 8: **consensus oriented, participatory, rule of law, effective and efficient, accountable, transparent, responsive, equitable and inclusive**.
xa: Exam angle: in "NOT a feature" questions look for **centralisation, secrecy, discretion** or **majoritarian rule**.
Most critical three (UNDP): **transparency, accountability, responsiveness**.

87.s: Which department is identified as India's nodal department for the World Bank's Worldwide Governance Indicators?
o: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
87.x: The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, or DARPG, is India's nodal department for the WGI.
87.tq: Use the institutional-responsibility approach: identify which department handles the governance indicator.
xs: **DARPG** (**Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances**) is India's nodal department for the WGI — option **(4)** is correct.
**DPIIT** publishes **BRAP** rankings; **NITI Aayog** the **SDG India Index**.
xa: DARPG also publishes the **Good Governance Index** and **GRAI**.
DARPG tools: **NeSDA** (**2019**), **Citizen's Charter** portal, **CPGRAMS**.

87.s: The National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG) was established by upgrading the:
87.x: The NCGG was established by upgrading the National Institute of Administrative Research associated with LBSNAA.
87.tq: Identify the predecessor institution rather than the parent organisation by association.
xs: **NCGG** was set up by upgrading the **National Institute of Administrative Research** (LBSNAA) — option **(4)** is correct.
It is an **autonomous** institute.
xa: Head office **New Delhi**; branch **Mussoorie**.
⚠ **CGG** (Centre for Good Governance) is in **Hyderabad**, set up **2001**.

87.s:
Assertion (A): The World Bank stresses accountability, transparency and the rule of law in its approach to governance.
Reason (R): UNESCAP stresses efficiency, effectiveness, equity and sustainability in governance.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
87.x: Both describe different agencies' approaches correctly, but UNESCAP's emphasis does not explain the World Bank's.
xa: Governance is broader than government: it involves the **market + civil society**.
UN/UNDP list **8 attributes** of good governance.

87.s: According to the indicated UNDP emphasis, the three most critical characteristics of good governance are:
o: Rule of law, security and decentralisation
87.x: Transparency, accountability and responsiveness are identified as the three most critical characteristics.
87.tq: Recall the specifically emphasised subset within a larger list.
xs: UNDP's three most critical traits are **transparency, accountability and responsiveness** — option **(3)** is correct.
They come from the **8 attributes** of good governance.
xa: Other attributes: **consensus oriented**, **participatory**, **rule of law**, **effective and efficient**, **equitable and inclusive**.
Four pillars: **Ethos, Ethics, Equity, Efficiency**.

87.s: Among the pillars of good governance, 'Ethos' stands for:
87.x: Ethos means service; ethics means honesty and integrity, equity means empathy for weaker sections, and efficiency means speedy ICT-based delivery.
xa: Tools: **people's participation**, **RTI**, **Sevottam**, **Citizen Charters**, **e-governance**.
Second ARC's **4th Report**: "**Ethics in Governance**" (**2007**).

87.s: The Worldwide Governance Indicators have been available since:
87.x: The WGI cover more than 200 countries since 1996, with dimensions including Government Effectiveness and Rule of Law.
xa: **DARPG** is India's nodal department.
Criticism: WGI **relies on perception data**.

87.s: The Good Governance Index of DARPG, launched on Good Governance Day 2019, is to be revised every:
87.x: The GGI, which ranks States, UTs and districts, is to be revised every two years.
xa: GGI covers **10 sectors**.
⚠ **BRAP** = DPIIT; **GGI/GRAI** = DARPG.

87.s: The Worldwide Governance Indicators and V-Dem indices are mainly criticised because they:
o: Rely substantially on expert opinion and perceptions
Measure only economic growth and fiscal deficit
87.x: WGI and V-Dem are contested because, as perception-based indices, they rely substantially on expert opinion.
xa: V-Dem 2026: India **106th of 179**, "**electoral autocracy**".
India in **WGI 2023**: moderate effectiveness, **low political stability**.

87.s: Which one of the following is NOT a dimension of the World Bank's Worldwide Governance Indicators?
87.x: Human Development Index is not a WGI dimension. The WGI dimensions include Voice and Accountability, Political Stability, Government Effectiveness, Regulatory Quality, Rule of Law and Control of Corruption.
87.tq: Identify the item that belongs to another index rather than the six WGI dimensions.
xs: The **Human Development Index** is not a WGI dimension — option **(3)** is correct.

The **six** WGI dimensions: **Voice and Accountability**, **Political Stability and Absence of Violence/Terrorism**, **Government Effectiveness**, **Regulatory Quality**, **Rule of Law**, **Control of Corruption**.
xa: WGI cover **200+** countries since **1996**.
⚠ **WGI** = **6** dimensions; **GGI** = **10** sectors.

87.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the ten sectors of the Good Governance Index?
87.x: Foreign affairs and diplomacy is not one of the ten GGI sectors. The sectors include citizen-centric governance, environment, public health, agriculture and allied sectors, and others.
87.tq: Find the sector outside the prescribed domestic-governance framework.
xs: **Foreign affairs and diplomacy** is not a GGI sector — option **(4)** is correct.
The **10 sectors** include **environment**, **citizen-centric governance** and **public health**.
xa: Others: agriculture and allied, commerce and industry, human resource development, public infrastructure and utilities, economic governance, social welfare and development, judicial and public security.
GGI launched **2019**; revised every **two years**.

87.s: The Good Governance Index is published by:
87.x: DARPG publishes the Good Governance Index; NITI Aayog publishes the SDG India Index, DPIIT the BRAP rankings and PAC the Public Affairs Index.
xa: ⚠ **BRAP** = DPIIT, not NITI Aayog.
**GRAI** is also by **DARPG**.
NITI Aayog's first **Investment Friendliness Index 2026**: **Gujarat** 1st.

87.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: National MPI — NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI
SDG India Index — University of Gothenburg
87.x: The National MPI is published by NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI. V-Dem is associated with the University of Gothenburg, the Responsible Nations Index with WIF, JNU and IIM Mumbai, and the SDG India Index with NITI Aayog.
87.tq: Check the publisher before accepting an index-name association.
xs: **National MPI — NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI** is correct — option **(2)**; it uses **12 indicators**.
**Responsible Nations Index** = **WIF, JNU and IIM Mumbai**; **SDG India Index** = **NITI Aayog**; **V-Dem** = **University of Gothenburg**.
xa: **Public Affairs Index** = **Public Affairs Centre, Bengaluru**.
**BRAP** = **DPIIT**.

87.s: According to the 2026 V-Dem assessment, India was placed at:
o: 100th among 179 countries and classified as an electoral democracy
106th among 154 countries and classified as a liberal democracy
106th among 179 countries and classified as an electoral autocracy
16th among 179 countries and classified as an electoral autocracy
87.x: The 2026 V-Dem assessment placed India 106th out of 179 and described it as an “electoral autocracy.”
87.tq: Keep the country rank, total number and classification together to avoid mixing editions.
xs: **V-Dem 2026** placed India **106th of 179**, an "**electoral autocracy**" — option **(3)** is correct.
India was **100th** in **2025**; **16th of 154** is the **Responsible Nations Index** rank.
xa: V-Dem is by the **University of Gothenburg**.
Criticism: perception-based indices (**WGI, V-Dem**) rely on expert opinion.

87.s: In the Responsible Nations Index 2026, India ranked:
87.x: India ranked 16th out of 154 countries in the Responsible Nations Index 2026; Singapore ranked first.
xa: The index is by **WIF, JNU and IIM Mumbai**.
**Investment Friendliness Index 2026**: **Gujarat** 1st.

87.s: What is the name of the program launched recently by Indian Railways on ethics in public governance?
87.src: APPSC 2018 Special Qualifying Test for Appointment by Promot

87.s:
Consider the following statements about the Second Administrative Reforms Commission:
1. It was set up in 2005.
2. It submitted 15 reports.
3. Its 4th Report, 'Ethics in Governance', was submitted in 2009.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
87.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Second ARC was set up in 2005. Statement 2 is correct: it gave 15 reports. Statement 3 is wrong: the 4th Report 'Ethics in Governance' is of 2007; 2009 is the 12th Report on Citizen Centric Administration. So 1 and 2 only (A); B and C include the false statement 3, D includes all.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the **Second ARC** was set up in **2005** and gave **15 reports**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **4th Report "Ethics in Governance"** is of **2007**; **2009** is the **12th Report** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: ⚠ **4th** = Ethics (**2007**); **12th** = Citizen Centric (**2009**, Sevottam).
The 4th Report covers **codes of ethics, anti-corruption bodies, ethics in legislatures**.

87.s: The Second ARC's 12th Report, which covered Citizen's Charters, grievance redress and the Sevottam model, was titled:
o: Promoting e-Governance – The SMART Way Forward
Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance
87.x: The 12th Report (2009), 'Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance', covered Citizen's Charters, grievance redress, Sevottam and people's participation.
xa: The **Second ARC** was set up in **2005** and gave **15 reports**.
**4th Report** (**2007**): "**Ethics in Governance**".

87.s: Which of the following is regarded as the most foundational tool for implementing good governance?
87.x: People's participation is identified as the most foundational tool for implementing good governance; other tools include RTI, Sevottam, Citizen Charters and e-governance.
87.tq: Identify the foundational element rather than a supporting administrative instrument.
xs: **People's participation** is the **most foundational** good-governance tool — option **(2)** is correct.
**Secrecy, discretion** and **centralisation** run against good governance.
xa: Other tools: **RTI**, **Sevottam**, **Citizen Charters**, **e-governance**.
Democracy aids development by **encouraging citizen participation** (**APPSC-GS 2025**).

87.s: The Centre for Good Governance, set up by undivided Andhra Pradesh in 2001, is based in:
87.x: The CGG, set up with DFID (UK) and the World Bank, is in Hyderabad; New Delhi and Mussoorie are the locations of the National Centre for Good Governance.
xa: The CGG is a governance-reform **think tank**: administrative reforms, e-governance, research, training.
**NCGG** was set up by upgrading the National Institute of Administrative Research (**LBSNAA**).
The **World Bank** first brought "good governance" into development discourse — **1989** report on Sub-Saharan Africa.
DARPG tools: **NeSDA** (**2019**), **CPGRAMS**, **Citizen's Charter** portal.

87.s: Which of the following is not a feature of good governance?
87.x: Red Tapism refers to excessive regulation that hinders or prevents action or decision-making. Thus, it is not a feature of good governance. On the other hand, accountability, transparency and rule of law are features of good governance.

87.s: Which one of the following best distinguishes governance from government?
o: Governance is confined to the state, whereas government includes civil society.
Governance refers only to judicial administration.
Governance is broader and involves the market and civil society, not merely the state.
Government and governance are identical in scope and meaning.
87.x: Governance is broader than government because it involves the state together with the market and civil society.
87.tq: Focus on the scope comparison and reject the reversed relationship.
xs: **Governance is broader** — it involves the **market and civil society**, not just the state — option **(3)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses this; option (4) treats the two as identical.
xa: Stakeholders of governance: **State, Market, Civil Society**.
**UNDP (1997)**: governance manages a country's affairs **at all levels**.

87.s: Democracy aids development mainly because it encourages:
87.x: Democracy aids development by encouraging citizen participation and accountability.
87.tq: Apply the cause-effect relationship rather than choosing a general democratic feature.
xs: Democracy aids development as it **encourages citizen participation and accountability** — option **(4)** is correct (**APPSC-GS 2025**).
**Centralisation, secrecy, discretion** and **majoritarian rule** are the odd ones out in good-governance questions.
xa: **People's participation** is the **most foundational** good-governance tool.
UN/UNDP attributes include **participatory** and **accountable**.

87.s: The Centre for Good Governance (CGG) in Andhra Pradesh functions primarily as a:
o: Statutory commission for recruitment to public services
Governance-reform think tank advising the government
87.x: The CGG is a governance-reform think tank that advises the government on administrative reforms, e-governance, research and training.
87.tq: Identify the institution by its mandate rather than by its location.
xs: AP's **CGG** is a **governance-reform think tank** advising on **administrative reforms, e-governance, research, training** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is not a regulator, recruitment commission or constitutional authority.
xa: Set up by undivided AP in **2001** with **DFID (UK) and the World Bank**.
Based in **Hyderabad**.

87.s: In which report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission barriers of Good Governance in India have been identified?
87.x: In Report 12 (Citizen-Centric Administration : The Heart of Governance) of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission, barriers to good governance in India have been identified. It also describes the pre-conditions for good governance.

87.s: Which date is obscrved as the Good governance Day in India?
87.x: To mark and celebrate in the honour of the Former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee's birthday, India observes "Good Governance Day" on 25th December, every year since, It was announced in the year 2014.

87.s: In which year was the Centre for Good Governance (CGG) set up in Andhra Pradesh?
The Centre for Good Governance (CGG) was set up in Andhra Pradesh in collaboration with _________.
In which year was the Centre for Good Governance (CGG) established by the Government of Andhra Pradesh?
In which year was the Centre for Good Governance (CGG) established by the Government of Andhra Pradesh (GoAP)?

88.s: Who is associated with the five models of e-governance comprising broadcasting, critical flow, comparative analysis, e-advocacy and interactive service?
88.x: The five models listed are attributed to Arie Halachmi.
88.tq: Match the named theorist with the distinctive classification of models.
xs: The five models — broadcasting, critical flow, comparative analysis, e-advocacy and interactive service — are those of **Arie Halachmi**, so option **(3)** is correct.
Each model is a distinct way of using ICT in government, from **public-domain information** (broadcasting) to **two-way G2C services** (interactive service).
xa: **Critical flow** channels critical information to a targeted audience, e.g. corruption data to an **ombudsman**.
**Comparative analysis** means learning from **best practices** elsewhere.
**E-advocacy / mobilisation and lobbying**: online **civil-society networks** influence decisions.
⚠ Corruption data → ombudsman is **critical flow**, not broadcasting.

88.s: Information on corruption is channelled electronically to an ombudsman. This illustrates which model of e-governance?
88.x: Critical flow channels critical information to a targeted audience, such as corruption data sent to an ombudsman.
88.tq: Identify whether information is disseminated broadly or targeted to a specific recipient.
xs: Channelling corruption data to an **ombudsman** is the **critical flow** model, so option **(4)** is correct.
Critical flow sends **critical information** to a **targeted audience**.
**Broadcasting** puts information in the **public domain** for all; **comparative analysis** learns from **best practices**; **e-advocacy** uses **civil-society networks**.
xa: The model belongs to **Arie Halachmi's** five models of e-governance.
**Interactive service** = two-way **G2C** services like filing, payments and feedback.
⚠ The notes flag this trap: corruption data → ombudsman = **critical flow**, not broadcasting.

88.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Halachmi's model of e-governance is wrongly matched?
o: Comparative analysis – Learning from best practices elsewhere
E-advocacy – Online civil-society networks influencing decisions
E-advocacy – Learning from best practices elsewhere
Interactive service – Two-way G2C services such as filing, payments and feedback
88.x: Learning from best practices is comparative analysis; e-advocacy means online civil-society networks influencing decisions.
xa: The other two Halachmi models: **broadcasting / wider-dissemination** (public domain) and **critical flow** (targeted audience).
Example of critical flow: corruption data sent to an **ombudsman**.

88.s: A citizen applies online for an income certificate through UMANG or MeeSeva. This interaction is best classified as:
88.x: G2C means Government to Citizen interaction. Online birth, income and caste certificates are examples of G2C services.
88.tq: Identify the recipient of the service before classifying the interaction type.
xs: Applying online for an income certificate is a **G2C** (Government to Citizen) service, so option **(4)** is correct.
The notes list **online birth/income/caste certificates**, **UMANG** and **MeeSeva** as G2C examples.
**G2B** serves businesses (GSTN), **G2G** links departments (NIC, SWAN), **G2E** serves employees (HR tools).
xa: **UMANG** is a single app for central/state services such as tax, **EPF**, gas and passport.
**MeeSeva** ("At your service", **2011**) is AP's single-window G2C service centre.
Halachmi's **interactive service** model is also described as two-way **G2C** service.

88.s: Which of the following is an example of G2B interaction?
o: GSTN and e-Procurement services for businesses
Online HR tools for government employees
Online birth certificate services for citizens
88.x: G2B means Government to Business interaction; MCA portal, GSTN and e-Procurement are examples.
88.tq: Use the beneficiary category—businesses—to distinguish G2B from citizen, employee and inter-government services.
xs: **GSTN and e-Procurement** services for businesses are **G2B** (Government to Business), so option **(1)** is correct.
**e-Office** between departments is **G2G**; online HR tools for employees are **G2E**; online birth certificates are **G2C**.
xa: The **MCA portal** is another G2B example.
⚠ **GSTN** = G2B, while **NIC**, **SWAN** and **e-Office** = G2G.
AP's **e-Procurement** (**2003**) brought online tendering to stop collusion.

88.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about types of e-governance interaction?
o: G2G refers to interaction between departments or governments
G2E refers to interaction between different governments
NIC solutions, SWAN and e-Office are G2G examples
Online HR and administrative tools are G2E examples
88.x: G2E means services from government to its employees; interaction between governments is G2G.
xa: **G2C** examples: online certificates, **UMANG**, **MeeSeva**.
**G2B** examples: **MCA portal**, **GSTN**, **e-Procurement**.
**e-Taal** is by **NIC**; AP's **APSWAN** is the state's data backbone.

88.s: Which one of the following is the correct expansion of UMANG?
o: Universal Mobile Application for National Governance
Universal Mechanism for Administrative and New Governance
Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance
Unified Management Application for New Government
88.x: UMANG stands for Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance.
88.tq: Test the exact official expansion rather than a look-alike phrase.
xs: UMANG stands for **Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance**, so option **(3)** is correct.
It is a **single app** for central and state services such as tax, **EPF**, gas and passport.
xa: UMANG is accessible through **web, SMS and IVR**.
**DigiLocker** is a cloud locker for documents and certificates, a key **Digital India** initiative.
**MeghRaj** is the GI Cloud (Government of India cloud) hosting government applications.

88.s: Which single application gives access to Central and State Government services such as tax, EPF, gas and passport services through web, SMS and IVR?
88.x: UMANG offers multiple Central and State services through web, SMS and IVR.
xa: UMANG = **Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance**.
UMANG is a **G2C** example, alongside **MeeSeva** and online certificates.
**DigiLocker** (documents) and **MyGov** (citizen engagement) are other national platforms.

88.s: Participative governance is most directly associated with which platform?
88.x: MyGov is a citizen-engagement platform intended to promote participative governance.
88.tq: Match the governance objective with the platform designed for citizen engagement.
xs: Participative governance is most directly associated with **MyGov**, a citizen-engagement platform, so option **(4)** is correct.
**CSC** are village-level service outlets; **e-Taal** is by **NIC**; **ERSS** is the emergency system on **112**.
xa: **DigiLocker** is a cloud locker for documents and certificates.
**GI Cloud "MeghRaj"** hosts government applications.
Halachmi's **e-advocacy** model also concerns citizen voice: online **civil-society networks** influence decisions.

88.s:
Assertion (A): The Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) is linked to the single emergency number 112.
Reason (R): Common Service Centres (CSCs) are village-level service outlets.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
88.x: Both statements are true, but CSCs as village outlets have nothing to do with ERSS's link to 112.
xa: Aadhaar: launched **2009**, Aadhaar Act **2016**, amended **2019**.
**BHIM** app on UPI was launched on **30 Dec 2016**.
Grievances can be filed at **5.1 lakh CSCs**.

88.s: Aadhaar was launched in ____ and the Aadhaar Act was enacted in ____.
88.x: Aadhaar was launched in 2009; the Aadhaar Act was enacted in 2016 and amended in 2019.
xa: Aadhaar is the **biometric identity** platform.
⚠ Sequence to remember: **2009** launch → **2016** Act → **2019** amendment.
**UPI** (by **NPCI**) is another key national platform; BHIM on UPI came on **30 Dec 2016**.

88.s: In which year were the National Awards for e-Governance (NAeG) started?
88.x: NAeG, instituted by DARPG, began in 2003 and are presented at the National Conference on e-Governance.
xa: The **2025** awards (with **MoPR**) had a first-ever dedicated category for **Gram Panchayats**.
**NAeG 2026**: **17 projects in 7 categories**.
⚠ **28th** NCeG = **Visakhapatnam** (2025); **29th** = **Jaipur** (2026).

88.s: Andhra Pradesh's Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) was established in:
88.x: RTGS, AP's flagship digital-governance platform using a Data Lake and real-time dashboards, was set up in 2017.
xa: RTGS has a **Command & Control Centre**.
A **Singapore** delegation reviewed RTGS (Jul 2026).
**Mana Mitra** WhatsApp Governance came in Jan **2026**.

88.s: The objective of e-Pragati is most closely associated with:
o: A unified state service portal and state enterprise architecture
A network limited to district treasuries
88.x: e-Pragati is a unified state service portal and state enterprise architecture. It aims at faceless, paperless and cashless governance.
88.tq: Match the broad architecture-level function with the appropriate state initiative.
xs: **e-Pragati** is a **unified state service portal / state enterprise architecture**, so option **(1)** is correct.
A national consumer grievance platform is **e-Jagriti**, not e-Pragati.
xa: **45 more citizen services** were added to e-Pragati.
Its aim: "**faceless, paperless, cashless**" governance.
**APSWAN** is the separate data backbone linking state, district and mandal offices.

88.s: The primary purpose of e-Procurement in Andhra Pradesh was to:
o: Register births and deaths through village offices
Conduct online tendering and help stop collusion
Monitor consumer grievances at the national level
88.x: The e-Procurement initiative, introduced in 2003, enabled online tendering with the objective of stopping collusion.
88.tq: Infer the governance outcome from the service mechanism described.
xs: AP's **e-Procurement** (**2003**) was for **online tendering to stop collusion**, so option **(2)** is correct.
Cloud documents are **DigiLocker**; national consumer grievances are **e-Jagriti** — neither is e-Procurement.
xa: e-Procurement is also a **G2B** example nationally, with **GSTN** and the **MCA portal**.
⚠ AP sequence: **eSeva 2001** → **e-Procurement 2003** → **MeeSeva 2011** → **RTGS 2017**.

88.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
88.x: A is correct: eSeva (2001) set up integrated citizen service centres for bills and certificates. B is wrong: MeeSeva came in 2011 as single-window G2C centres, while online tendering was e-Procurement (2003). C and D pair the initiatives with wrong years and purposes.
88.tq: Use both the date and the service purpose to detect swapped pairs.
xs: **eSeva — 2001 — Integrated citizen service centres** is correctly matched, so option **(1)** is correct.
eSeva centres handled **bills and certificates**; it was a **Naidu-era pioneer** of e-governance.
**MeeSeva** came in **2011** as single-window G2C centres; online tendering was **e-Procurement** (**2003**).
xa: **RTGS** followed in **2017**.

NAeG is instituted by **DARPG** and presented at the **NCeG**.

88.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a significance of e-governance?

89.s: Which State enacted India's first Right to Services law?
89.x: Madhya Pradesh's Lok Sewa Guarantee Act, 2010 was the first; Bihar followed in 2011.

89.s: Which State passed the first law making social audit of government programmes mandatory?
89.x: Meghalaya passed the first state law making social audit of government programmes mandatory in 2017.
89.tq: Distinguish the first state law from Andhra Pradesh's pioneering implementation institution.
xs: **Meghalaya** (**2017**) passed the first state law making social audit of government programmes mandatory, so option **(1)** is correct.
**Andhra Pradesh** pioneered state-wide **MGNREGA social audits**, but not the first law; **MP** and **Bihar** are linked with RTS laws.
xa: ⚠ First RTS = **MP 2010**; first social audit law = **Meghalaya 2017**.
The **2nd ARC** wanted social audits in **all major welfare schemes**.

89.s: The Second ARC recommended that social audits be:

89.s:
Consider the following statements about the ombudsman in India:
1. The institution of ombudsman originated in Sweden in 1809.
2. The term 'Lokayukta' was coined by Morarji Desai.
3. Maharashtra set up the first Lokayukta in 1971.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statement 1 is correct: Sweden, 1809. Statement 2 is wrong: L.M. Singhvi coined the term; Morarji Desai headed the First ARC that recommended Lokpal and Lokayukta. Statement 3 is correct: Maharashtra, 1971. So 1 and 3 only (C); A and B include the false statement 2, D includes all.
89.tq: Singhvi coined the term; Desai's ARC recommended the bodies.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the ombudsman began in **Sweden, 1809**.
Statement 2 wrong: the term "Lokpal" was coined by **L.M. Singhvi**; **Morarji Desai** headed the First ARC.
Statement 3 correct: **Maharashtra** set up the first Lokayukta in **1971**.
xa: First ARC (**1966-70**) recommended **Lokpal** (Union) + **Lokayukta** (State).
Lokpal and Lokayukta are **statutory** under the **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013**.

89.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the First Administrative Reforms Commission?
o: Morarji Desai was associated with it
It recommended a Lokpal in each State and Lokayuktas at the Union level
It recommended a Lokpal at the Union level
89.x: It recommended a Lokpal for the Union and Lokayuktas for the States, not the other way round.
xa: The term "Lokpal" was coined by **L.M. Singhvi**.
First Lokayukta: **Maharashtra** (**1971**).
Ombudsman origin: **Sweden, 1809**.

89.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the six principles of the Citizens' Charter?
89.x: The six principles are quality, choice, standards, value, accountability and transparency; participation is not one. The Charter began in the UK in 1991 under John Major.
xa: India adopted the Citizens' Charter in **1997**.
⚠ **Sweden 1809** = ombudsman; **UK 1991** = Citizens' Charter.
The Right to Services idea grew out of the **UK Citizens' Charter**.

89.s: A Citizens' Charter is best described as a:
o: Constitutional guarantee enforceable in every court
Statutory code that penalises every service delay
Written commitment on service standards, time-bound delivery and grievance redress
89.x: A Citizens' Charter records commitments on service standards, time-bound delivery and grievance redress; it is not by itself legally enforceable.
xa: The **2nd ARC** recommended **statutory status** for charters.
Basic elements: **service standards**, **information about services**, **grievance redress mechanism**, **contact details** of officers.
Exam angle: its main purpose is **time-bound service delivery and grievance redress**.

89.s:
Assertion (A): The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended statutory status for Citizens' Charters.
Reason (R): Citizens' Charters in India are legally enforceable rights in their present form.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
89.x: The Second ARC did recommend statutory status, but Indian Citizens' Charters are generally non-justiciable and not presently enforceable, so R is false.
xa: The **Citizens Charter Bill 2011** sought time-bound delivery + grievance redress, but lapsed in **2014**.
A common criticism: **charters lack legal force**.

89.s: India adopted the Citizens' Charter in:
89.x: India adopted it in 1997; 1991 is its UK origin. DARPG coordinates the charters (goicharters.nic.in).
xa: DARPG also runs **CPGRAMS** (**2007**) and designs **Sevottam**.

89.s: What happened to the Citizens Charter Bill, 2011, on time-bound delivery of services and grievance redress?
o: It lapsed with the dissolution of the Lok Sabha in 2014
It was withdrawn by the Government in 2012
89.x: The Bill never became law; it lapsed when the Lok Sabha was dissolved in 2014.
xa: India adopted Citizens' Charters in **1997**; they remain **non-justiciable**.
The **2nd ARC** recommended statutory backing for charters.

89.s: The word “Sevottam” is formed from which combination?
89.x: Sevottam is derived from “Seva” and “Uttam”, conveying excellence in service.
89.tq: Use the exact word derivation rather than translating the general objective alone.
xs: Sevottam = **Seva + Uttam**, meaning **excellence in service**, so option **(1)** is correct.
It was suggested in the **2nd ARC's 12th report** (Citizen Centric Administration).
xa: Implementation in departments began in **2009**.
It has **3** modules: Citizen's Charter, Public Grievance Redress, Service Delivery Capability.
Certification follows **IS 15700:2005**; **DARPG** designs and promotes the framework.

89.s: Under Sevottam, which module is correctly matched with its focus?
o: Public Grievance Redress – Publish service standards
89.x: The Citizens' Charter module publishes service standards; Grievance Redress handles complaints and Service Delivery Capability builds organisational capacity.
xa: ⚠ Sevottam = **3** modules; standard **IS 15700:2005**.
Sevottam = **Seva + Uttam** (excellence in service).

89.s: Sevottam-compliant certification follows which standard?
89.x: Sevottam-compliant certification follows Indian Standard IS 15700:2005.
89.tq: Identify the exact standard number rather than substituting a familiar quality or information-security standard.
xs: Sevottam-compliant certification follows **IS 15700:2005**, so option **(1)** is correct.
**DARPG** designs and promotes the Sevottam framework.
xa: Sevottam was suggested in the **2nd ARC's 12th report**; departmental implementation began in **2009**.
⚠ Sevottam = **3** modules; chairman **Veerappa Moily**.

89.s: Implementation of the Sevottam model in government departments began in:
89.x: Sevottam, suggested in the Second ARC's 12th Report and promoted by DARPG, was implemented from 2009; 2005 is when the Second ARC was set up.
xa: Sevottam certification follows **IS 15700:2005**.
The 12th report's chairman was **Veerappa Moily**.

89.s: Among the following States, which enacted its Right to Services law earliest?
89.x: The order of enactment among these is Punjab, Assam, Gujarat and Maharashtra.
xa: The first RTS law overall was the **Madhya Pradesh Lok Sewa Guarantee Act, 2010**.
RTS laws provide **appeal** on delay and a **penalty on the responsible official**.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about CPGRAMS:
1. It was launched in 2007 by DARPG.
2. DARPG functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
3. It is accessible 24x7 through the web, an app and UMANG.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
89.x: Statement 1 is correct: CPGRAMS was launched in 2007 by DARPG. Statement 2 is wrong: DARPG is under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions. Statement 3 is correct: 24x7 via web, app and UMANG. So 1 and 3 only (C); A and B include the false statement 2, D includes all.
xs: Statements **1 and 3 only** are correct, so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: CPGRAMS was launched in **2007** by **DARPG**.
Statement 2 wrong: DARPG is under the **Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions**, not Home Affairs.
Statement 3 correct: it is accessible **24x7** via web, app and **UMANG**.
xa: DARPG's circular of **23 Aug 2024** cut the disposal limit from **30 to 21 days**.
Pensioners have a separate system, **CPENGRAMS**.

89.s: A circular of DARPG dated 23 August 2024 reduced the maximum disposal time for CPGRAMS grievances from:
89.x: The DARPG circular dated 23 August 2024 reduced the maximum disposal time from 30 days to 21 days.
89.tq: Retain both the original and revised limits; the reduction pair is the tested fact.
xs: The **23 Aug 2024** DARPG circular cut the maximum disposal time from **30 days to 21 days**, so option **(3)** is correct.
It applies to **CPGRAMS** grievances.
xa: Over **71,000** grievances were pending on CPGRAMS (Sep 2025).
**GRAI** ranks ministries on **11 indicators, 4 dimensions**.
CPGRAMS was launched in **2007** by **DARPG**.

89.s: Which of the following is NOT a dimension of the Grievance Redressal Assessment & Index (GRAI)?
89.x: GRAI's four dimensions (11 indicators) are efficiency, feedback, domain and organisational commitment; transparency is not one.
xa: GRAI = **Grievance Redressal Assessment & Index**.
⚠ Disposal limit **30 → 21 days** (**23 Aug 2024**).

89.s: CPGRAMS, the online grievance platform run by DARPG, stands for:
o: Central Public Grievance Registration and Management System
Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System
Citizen Public Grievance Resolution and Monitoring Scheme
Centralised Pension and Grievance Redress Monitoring System
89.x: B is the correct expansion: Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System, launched in 2007 by DARPG. A, C and D are invented expansions; D also mixes in pensions, which have a separate platform, CPENGRAMS.
89.tq: CPGRAMS: Centralised Public Grievance Redress And Monitoring System (2007, DARPG).
xs: CPGRAMS = **Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System**, so option **(2)** is correct.
It was launched in **2007** by **DARPG**; pensioners use the separate **CPENGRAMS**.
xa: Access **24x7** via web, app and **UMANG**; grievances also through **5.1 lakh CSCs**.
**CPGRAMS 7.0** works in many Indian languages.
⚠ CPGRAMS handles **service grievances** (executive); **Lokpal** handles **corruption** (statutory).

89.s: Which one of the following Andhra Pradesh initiatives provided web-based online receipt, reply and monitoring of grievances at District Collectorates?
89.x: Prajavani was an earlier Andhra Pradesh initiative for online receipt, reply and monitoring of grievances at District Collectorates.
89.tq: Match the distinctive operational function with the correct platform rather than the later statewide portals.
xs: **Prajavani** gave web-based online receipt, reply and monitoring of grievances at **District Collectorates**, so option **(4)** is correct.
**Meekosam** (**2015**) was a single-window portal; **Spandana** (**2019**) a one-stop grievance platform; **People First** was a distractor in APPSC 2018.
xa: This Prajavani description is from **APPSC 2018**.
AP sequence: **Prajavani → Meekosam → Spandana**.

89.s: Meekosam in Andhra Pradesh is a:
o: Single-window portal to lodge grievances and suggestions and track their status
Portal for social audits of MGNREGA works
89.x: Meekosam let citizens lodge grievances and suggestions through a single window and track their status.
xa: Meekosam = "**For You**", **2015**, TDP government.
**Data analytics** was added to it.

89.s: Spandana was launched in Andhra Pradesh in 2019 during the government of:
89.x: Spandana was associated with the YSRCP Government in 2019 and served as a one-stop public grievance redressal platform.
89.tq: Discriminate between the two major AP grievance platforms by matching year and government.
xs: **Spandana** was launched in **2019** under the **YSRCP** government, so option **(2)** is correct.
**TDP** is linked with **Meekosam** (**2015**).
xa: Spandana is a **one-stop public grievance redressal** platform.
**APPSC 2021** and **2018** both keyed Spandana as the AP grievance platform.

89.s: Which of the following is NOT a normal feature of Right to Services legislation?
o: Automatic abolition of all departmental grievance mechanisms
A penalty on the responsible official
A right of appeal in case of delay
Notification of services to be delivered within a fixed time
89.x: Right to Services laws provide notified services within fixed time limits, appeals against delay and penalties for responsible officials. They do not automatically abolish all other grievance mechanisms.
89.tq: Identify the option that goes beyond the stated legal features and uses an absolute institutional claim.
xs: **Automatic abolition of all departmental grievance mechanisms** is not an RTS feature, so option **(1)** is the answer.
RTS laws provide **notified services within fixed time**, **appeal on delay** and **penalty on the responsible official**.
xa: The RTS idea grew out of the **UK Citizens' Charter**.
AP too has laws mandating **time-bound delivery** of notified services with appeal and penalty.

89.s: Under Section 17 of MGNREGA, 2005, social audit of all works is conducted by the:
89.x: Section 17 makes the Gram Sabha audit all works; social audit is MGNREGA's accountability tool, not a CVC function.
xa: AP's **SSAAT** was set up in **2009** as an independent society.
AP pioneered **state-wide MGNREGA social audits**.

89.s: The AP Society for Social Audit, Accountability and Transparency (SSAAT) was set up in:
89.x: SSAAT, an independent society, was set up in 2009; 2005 is the year of MGNREGA. AP pioneered state-wide MGNREGA social audits.
xa: SSAAT = **AP Society for Social Audit, Accountability and Transparency**.
Social audit is mandated by **Section 17** of MGNREGA.

89.s: Which of the following pairs (mechanism – primary character) is wrongly matched?
o: Classic Ombudsman – Independent officer of the legislature
CPGRAMS and State portals – Service-delivery grievances
Lokpal and Lokayukta – Corruption allegations against public functionaries
CPGRAMS and State portals – Independent officer of the legislature
89.x: CPGRAMS and State portals handle service-delivery grievances; the independent officer of the legislature is the classic Ombudsman.
xa: Lokpal is **statutory** under the **Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013**.
The ombudsman originated in **Sweden, 1809**.

89.s: The following process is employed to enhance accountability in MGNREGA
89.x: Social Audit is the participatory process used under MGNREGA to enhance accountability, allowing local communities to review and verify how funds and works under the scheme are implemented.

89.s: The concept of 'Right to Service' originated in
89.x: The concept of 'Right to Service' originated in Great Britain (U.K.). Right to service refers to laws that guarantee timebound delivery of services for various public services rendered by the Government to citizens. The Right of Citizens for Time-bound Delivery of Goods and Services and Redressal of their Grievances Bill, 2011 was an attempt to start such a law in India. However, it could not be passed. Notably, Madhya Pradesh is the first state in the country to implement the Right to Services Act on 25 September,

89.s: Which e-governance initiative in Andhra Pradesh is a public grievance redressal system? n as
89.x: ' Prajavani ' is the flagship e-governance public grievance redressal platform of the Andhra Pradesh Government, allowing citizens to register and track the resolution of their grievances with various government departments online.

90.s: Sweden's Freedom of the Press Act, regarded as the world's first freedom-of-information law, dates to:
90.x: Sweden's 1766 Freedom of the Press Act was the first such law; UDHR Article 19 (1948) later recognised the right to seek information.
xa: Order (APPSC 2025): **Sweden → UN → FOI Act → RTI Act**.
⚠ **1766** = Sweden (world first); **1997** = **Tamil Nadu + Goa** (Indian state first).

90.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (MKSS):
1. It held public hearings (jan sunwais) in Rajasthan demanding access to muster rolls and bills.
2. It was led by Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey and Medha Patkar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
90.x: Statement 1 is correct: the MKSS jan sunwais on muster rolls and bills in Rajasthan started the RTI movement. Statement 2 is wrong: the MKSS leaders were Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey and Shankar Singh, not Medha Patkar. So A; B picks only the wrong statement, C accepts it, D rejects the correct statement 1.
90.tq: MKSS trio: Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey, Shankar Singh.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct, so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **MKSS** held **jan sunwais** in **Rajasthan** demanding muster rolls and bills.
Statement 2 wrong: MKSS was led by **Aruna Roy**, **Nikhil Dey** and **Shankar Singh** — not Medha Patkar.
xa: MKSS = **Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan**; its public hearings on muster rolls started the RTI movement.
The first CIC was **Wajahat Habibullah**.

90.s: The Right to Information Act, 2005 received Presidential assent and came fully into force, respectively, on:
90.x: B is correct: assent was given on 15 June 2005 and the Act came fully into force on 12 October 2005. A gives the Rajya Sabha passage date as assent; C gives the Lok Sabha passage date as assent; D gives a wrong commencement date.
90.tq: RTI: LS 11 May, RS 12 May, assent 15 June, in force 12 Oct 2005.
xs: Assent came on **15 June 2005** and full commencement on **12 October 2005**, so option **(2)** is correct.
**11 May** and **12 May 2005** are the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha passage dates.
xa: ⚠ **11 May** LS → **12 May** RS → **15 June** assent → **12 October** in force.
The Act replaced the **Freedom of Information Act, 2002**.

90.s: Under the Right to Information framework, information is provided free of cost to applicants belonging to which category?
o: All applicants below 25 years of age
All applicants belonging to rural areas
90.x: Applicants belonging to the below-poverty-line category are entitled to information without payment of the prescribed fee.
90.tq: Recall the specific beneficiary category attached to fee exemption.
xs: Information is free / fee waived for **BPL** applicants (**persons below the poverty line**), so option **(4)** is correct.
Only **citizens** can apply.
xa: Requests may be in **Hindi, English or the local official language**.
**Section 6(2)**: **no reason need be given**.

90.s: Under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act, which of the following is included within the meaning of ‘information’?
o: Information personally generated by an applicant after filing a request
Only physical records maintained by public authorities
Material in any form, including records, e-mails, opinions, contracts, samples and electronic data
Only final judicial decisions published in the Gazette
90.x: Section 2(f) covers material in any form, including records, documents, e-mails, opinions, advice, contracts, samples, models and electronic data.
90.tq: Choose the option reflecting the broad statutory wording ‘material in any form’.
xs: Under **Section 2(f)**, information is **material in any form**, including **records, e-mails, opinions, contracts, samples and electronic data** — option **(3)**.
It is not limited to physical records or judicial decisions.
xa: The list also covers **advices, press releases, circulars, orders, logbooks, models**.
It includes information on a **private body accessible to a public authority under law**.
**CBSE v Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011)**: evaluated **answer sheets** are "information".

90.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the organisations generally covered by the exemption under Section 24 and the Second Schedule of the Right to Information Act, 2005?
90.x: The IB, R&AW and CRPF are among the intelligence and security organisations covered by Section 24. The Central Information Commission is the appellate information body and is not a Section 24 exempt organisation.
90.tq: Identify the odd institutional category instead of confusing an exempt security body with the appellate authority.
xs: The **Central Information Commission** is not a Second Schedule body, so option **(2)** is the answer.
The Second Schedule lists **IB, R&AW**, DRI, ED, NCB, BSF, **CRPF**, NSG.
xa: The **CBI** was added in **2011**.
Exception: information on **corruption and human-rights violations** must still be given.

90.s: Which of the following is NOT a permissible ground associated with removal of a State Information Commissioner?
o: Conviction for an offence involving moral turpitude
Disagreement with a decision of the State Government
Proved incapacity after the prescribed inquiry
90.x: Disagreement with a State Government decision is not a stated ground for removal. Insolvency, conviction involving moral turpitude and proved incapacity are recognised grounds.
90.tq: Reject the plausible-sounding ground that is not a statutory basis.
xs: **Disagreement with a decision of the State Government** is not a removal ground, so option **(2)** is the answer.
Valid grounds: proved **misbehaviour/incapacity** (after SC inquiry), **insolvency**, **conviction (moral turpitude)**, **paid employment**, **infirmity**.
xa: Removal is by the **Governor** (Section **17**).
⚠ CIC/SIC = **up to 10** ICs; CVC = **two** Vigilance Commissioners, **4 years or age 65**.

90.s: A major institutional reason for delays in disposal of RTI matters is:
o: Chronic vacancies in the Central and State Information Commissions
90.x: Chronic vacancies in the CIC and State Information Commissions, together with a large backlog of appeals, cause long delays.
xa: Over **4 lakh** appeals/complaints pending (Jul 2026).
The **Satark Nagrik Sangathan 2025** report flagged gaps in Information Commissions.

90.s: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended that the RTI framework should be linked firmly with
90.x: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended firmly linking RTI with whistle-blower protection to prevent victimisation of those who disclose information.
90.tq: Identify the protection mechanism that directly addresses victimisation of information-seekers.
xs: The 2nd ARC wanted RTI linked firmly with **whistle-blower protection law**, to prevent victimisation — option **(4)**.
It also asked to **narrow Section 8** and **maximise Section 4** disclosure.
xa: The **Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014** is not operationalised.
The call was repeated on **30 Jul 2026**.

90.s: Which was the first Indian State to enact a Right to Information law (1997)?
90.x: Tamil Nadu enacted the first Indian State RTI law in 1997. Sweden had the world's first RTI law (1766), and Wajahat Habibullah was the first CIC.
xa: **Goa** passed its law the same year as Tamil Nadu (**1997**).
Order: **Sweden → UN → FOI Act → RTI Act**.

90.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or institutional concern relating to the functioning of the RTI regime?
o: Excessive speed in disposal of all RTI applications
90.x: The identified concerns include appeal backlogs, vacancies, misuse of Section 8 and threats to activists. Excessive speed in disposal is not listed as a criticism.
90.tq: Find the option that reverses the documented governance problem.
xs: **Excessive speed in disposal of all RTI applications** is not a concern — the problem is delay — so option **(3)** is the answer.
The listed criticisms are **backlog of appeals/delays**, **vacancies in Commissions**, misuse of **Section 8** and **threats/attacks on activists**.
xa: Over **4 lakh** appeals/complaints were pending (Jul 2026).
Another criticism: **weakened autonomy** after **2019**.
The **Satark Nagrik Sangathan 2025** report flagged gaps as the Act turns **20**.

90.s: The right to know has been judicially read into which Article of the Constitution?
90.x: Courts have read the right to know into Article 19(1)(a), and also Article 21, in cases like State of U.P. v. Raj Narain and S.P. Gupta.
xa: The RTI Act gives a **statutory right** giving effect to this fundamental right.
**CBSE v Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011)**: evaluated **answer sheets** are "information".

90.s: The Preamble of the RTI Act links an informed citizenry and transparency mainly with:
o: Containing corruption and holding governments accountable
Making every document public without exception
90.x: The Preamble ties informed citizenship and transparency to containing corruption and ensuring accountability, harmonised with other public interests.
xa: Other listed aims: participation and **better service delivery**.
Exemptions under **Section 8** carry out this balance.

90.s: Which of the following RTI Act provisions is correctly matched?
o: Section 18 – Complaints and inquiry by the Commission
90.x: Section 18 deals with complaints and inquiry by the Commission. Section 2(h) defines public authority, Section 4 proactive disclosure and Section 19 appeals.

90.s: Section 11 of the RTI Act, 2005 deals with:
o: Constitution of the State Information Commission

90.s: Under Section 2(h) of the RTI Act, public authorities include:
o: Only bodies created directly by the Constitution
Only bodies established by an Act of Parliament
Bodies set up by law or government notification, and bodies substantially financed or controlled by government
90.x: Section 2(h) covers bodies set up by law or notification and those substantially financed or controlled by government, not just constitutional bodies.
xa: NGOs **substantially financed** by government are public authorities (**DAV College Trust, 2019**).
⚠ The CIC held **BCCI is not a public authority** (May 2026).

90.s: Under Section 6(2) of the RTI Act, an applicant seeking information:
o: Must state the reasons for seeking it
Need not give any reason for seeking it

90.s: Which Section of the RTI Act, 2005 provides for the constitution of the Central Information Commission?

90.s: Under Section 24 of the RTI Act, listed intelligence and security organisations are still not excluded from disclosing information on:
90.x: Section 24 generally excludes listed organisations, but information on corruption and human-rights violations is not excluded.

90.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the ‘right to information’ under Section 2(j)?

Taking notes, extracts or certified copies
Inspection of works, documents and records

2(j) covers **inspection** of work, documents, records; **notes, extracts or certified copies**; **certified samples**; and electronic information.
xa: ⚠ **2(f)** = "information"; **2(h)** = "public authority"; **2(j)** = "right to information".

90.s: Under the RTI Act, a second appeal to the Central or State Information Commission is ordinarily filed within:

o: Section 7 and payment of RTI fees

90.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with Section 8(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005?
o: Commercial confidence and trade secrets — Section 8(1)(a)
Information held in a fiduciary relationship — Section 8(1)(e)
Information from a foreign government in confidence — Section 8(1)(j)

xs: **Fiduciary relationship — Section 8(1)(e)** is correctly matched, so option **(3)** is correct.

90.s: Section 44(3) of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 altered Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act by
o: making personal information a blanket exemption and dropping the earlier public-interest override
transferring all RTI appeals to the Data Protection Board
requiring every applicant to disclose the reason for seeking personal information
removing all exemptions relating to personal information

Constitutional right of public officials only

3 years or until the age of 65
6 years or until the age of 65

90.s: The penalty that may be imposed on a Public Information Officer under Section 20 is
90.x: Section 20 provides for a penalty of ₹250 per day, subject to a maximum of ₹25,000, along with possible disciplinary action.

weakened the autonomy of the Commissions by placing tenure and pay in executive hands
made all decisions of the Commissions subject to approval by political parties

90.x: More than 4 lakh RTI appeals and complaints were reported to be pending across Information Commissions as of July 2026.

All information held by local authorities
All records relating to public expenditure and contracts

90.s: The Right to Information is –
90.x: The Right to Information Act 2005, mandates timely response to citizen’s requests for government information. It is a legal right. The Primary object of the Right to Information Act is to empower the citizens, promote transparency and accountability in the working of the Government, prevent corruption, and make our democracy work for the people in real sense. In many of its decisions, the Supreme Court mentioned that the freedom of thought and expression also includes the right to information. However, the Right to Information is not clearly mentioned in the Indian Constitution. Thus the correct answer is an option (c).

90.s: Which of the following is not true about the objectives of the Right to Information Act?
o: To promote transparency and accountability n the
To make our democracy work for the people in real
To empower the women and weaker sections of the
90.x: The Right to Information Act, 2005, is an act to provide for setting out the practical regime of the right to information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority. The basic object of the Right to Information Act is to empower the citizens, promote transparency and accountability in the working of the Government, tackle corruption, and make our democracy work for the people in a real sense. It goes without saying that an informed citizen is better equipped to keep necessary vigil on the instruments of governance and make the government more accountable to the governed. The Act is a big step towards making the citizens informed about the activities of the Government. Hence, statement (3) is not true about the RTI Act. It is essential to mention here that the Right to Information Act, 2005, was amended in 2019.

90.s: The Right to Information Act of Parliament received the assent of the President of India on –

o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
92.x: A knowingly false complaint attracts a lighter punishment of up to 2 years and ₹30,000, so R is false.
xa: ⚠ Identity revealed = **3 years + ₹50,000**; false complaint = **2 years + ₹30,000**.
The **SPG** is excluded.

92.s: Which of the following categories is specifically excluded from the stated whistleblower rules?
92.x: The Special Protection Group (SPG) is excluded from the stated rules.
92.tq: Test the statutory exception rather than the general coverage rule.
xs: The **Special Protection Group (SPG)** is excluded, so option **(4)** is correct.
State Ministers, MPs and central employees all have named competent authorities.
xa: Union Ministers → **Prime Minister**; State Ministers → **Chief Minister**.
A weakness: "**victimisation**" is not defined.

92.s: The Whistle Blowers Protection (Amendment) Bill, 2015 lapsed with the dissolution of the:
92.x: The Bill would have barred disclosures in Section 8(1)-type categories; it lapsed with the 16th Lok Sabha in 2019.
xa: It passed the **Lok Sabha** in **May 2015**.
Weakness of the parent Act: "**victimisation**" not defined.

92.s: The 2013 central law on Lokpal and Lokayuktas required every State to set up a Lokayukta within:
92.x: The 2013 Act obliged every State to establish a Lokayukta within one year of its commencement; States then framed widely differing laws. Six months, two years and five years are not the stated period.
92.tq: 2013 Act: Lokayukta in every State within 1 year.
xs: The **2013** Act required every state to set up a Lokayukta **within a year**, so option **(2)** is correct.
States still differ widely in their Lokayukta laws.
xa: AP's law: **AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1983**.
First Lokayukta: **Maharashtra (1971)**.

92.s: The Enforcement Directorate functions primarily under which combination of laws?
o: RTI Act, 2005 and Official Secrets Act, 1923
92.x: The Enforcement Directorate operates under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, and the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999.
92.tq: Match the agency with its paired economic-enforcement statutes.
xs: The ED works under the **PMLA 2002** and **FEMA 1999**, so option **(2)** is correct.
The **DSPE Act** governs the CBI; the **CVC Act 2003** the CVC.
xa: The ED Director can **attach "proceeds of crime"** (APPSC-G1 2022).
PMLA came into force on **1 July 2005**.

92.s: The Central Vigilance Commission is best described as an:
o: Department of the Ministry of Finance under the PMLA
Independent statutory body established under the CVC Act, 2003
92.x: The CVC is an independent statutory body established under the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.
92.tq: Distinguish a statutory oversight body from a constitutional body and an international organisation.
xs: The CVC is an **independent statutory body** under the **CVC Act 2003**, so option **(4)** is correct.
The CPI is published by **Transparency International**, not the CVC.
