Dowry: minimum **5 years** + fine of at least **Rs 15,000**.

128.s: Which one of the following is correct about the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956?
o: It criminalises prostitution itself in all forms.
It penalises brothel-keeping, soliciting and living on the earnings of prostitution, but not prostitution itself.
It was enacted in 1986 to replace the Indian Penal Code provisions on trafficking.
It deals only with child marriage.
128.x: The ITPA, 1956 penalises brothel-keeping, soliciting and living on the earnings of prostitution, but does not make prostitution itself an offence. It is a 1956 law (1986 is only its amendment year) and has nothing to do with child marriage.
128.tq: ITPA 1956: punishes the trade around prostitution, not prostitution itself.
xs: The **ITPA 1956** penalises **brothel keeping, soliciting, living on earnings** — **not prostitution itself** — option **(2)**.
It dates from **1956**, not 1986, and has nothing to do with child marriage.
xa: Child marriage: **Sarda Act (1929)** fixed the minimum marriage age.
**1986** = **Indecent Representation of Women Act**.
**Dowry Prohibition Act**: **1961**.

128.s: Which Act provides for monogamy and grounds of divorce under Hindu personal law?
128.x: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 provides for monogamy and specifies grounds of divorce under Hindu personal law.
xa: **Special Marriage Act 1954**: civil marriage irrespective of religion.
**Sarla Mudgal (1995)**: a Hindu man's **conversion** cannot validate his second marriage.
**HSA 1956**: equal inheritance for women.

128.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched under the ART (Regulation) Act, 2021?
o: National registry — Regulatory record of ART institutions
Sale of gametes or embryos — Prohibited
128.x: Sex-selective ART is prohibited under the ART Act, 2021. Registered clinics and banks and a national registry are permitted regulatory arrangements.
128.tq: Locate the option that reverses a statutory prohibition.
xs: **Sex-selective ART — Permitted** is wrong — option **(2)**: the **ART Act 2021** **prohibits** it.
**Registered ART clinics and banks** and a **national registry** are permitted; **sale of gametes/embryos** is prohibited.
xa: **PCPNDT Act 1994** bans sex selection and pre-natal sex determination.
The **Surrogacy Act 2021** also prohibits **sex selection**.
Commercial surrogacy is banned.

128.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2021?
o: Termination up to 20 weeks may be done on one doctor's opinion.
Termination up to 24 weeks is available for special categories.
The woman's identity may be disclosed without restriction.
Beyond 24 weeks, a State Medical Board may permit termination for substantial foetal abnormality.
128.x: The Act prohibits disclosure of the woman's identity.
xa: Beyond 24 weeks **no gestation limit** applies.
**SC (2022)** removed **marital-status distinctions** for abortion access (**Art. 14**).
Surrogate foetus abortion needs consent + MTP Act approval.

128.s: The Code on Wages, 2019 subsumes the:
128.x: The Code subsumes the Equal Remuneration Act (along with the Minimum Wages, Payment of Wages and Payment of Bonus Acts) and provides a statutory floor wage.
xa: It also subsumes the **Minimum Wages Act 1948**, **Payment of Wages Act 1936**, **Payment of Bonus Act 1965**.
**Code on Wages (Central) Rules** notified **8 May 2026**.
**OSH Code 2020** governs women's **night shifts**.

128.s: Which of the following enactments was NOT absorbed into the Code on Wages, 2019?
128.x: The Code on Wages, 2019 absorbed the Equal Remuneration Act, Minimum Wages Act, Payment of Wages Act and Payment of Bonus Act. The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 was not among these four enactments.
128.tq: Find the statute outside the specific group of laws subsumed by the Code.
xs: The **Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017** was not absorbed — option **(4)**.
The Code subsumes the **Minimum Wages Act 1948**, **Payment of Wages Act 1936**, **Payment of Bonus Act 1965** and the **Equal Remuneration Act 1976**.
xa: The 2017 amendment raised leave to **26 weeks**.
The Code bans discrimination **including against transgender persons**.
It sets a statutory **floor wage**.

128.s: Under the OSH Code, 2020, women may work before 6 a.m. or after 7 p.m. when
o: the work is performed only in government offices
the employer gives permission without any further condition
they consent and prescribed safety safeguards are provided
the worker has completed ten years of service
128.x: The OSH Code, 2020 permits women to work during these hours with their consent and subject to safety safeguards.
128.tq: Identify the conditional permission instead of treating it as an unrestricted power of the employer.
xs: Under the **OSH Code 2020**, women may work before **6 a.m.** or after **7 p.m.** **with consent and safety safeguards** — option **(3)**.
Not unconditional employer permission, nor limited to government offices.
xa: The **Code on Wages, 2019** subsumes four wage laws.
The **Equal Remuneration Act 1976** flows from **Art. 39(d)**.
**Art. 42**: just and humane work conditions, **maternity relief**.

128.s: The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 provides for paid maternity leave of
128.x: The 2017 amendment raised paid maternity leave from 12 to 26 weeks for women with fewer than two surviving children (at most 8 weeks before delivery); from the third child it stays 12 weeks.
128.tq: Recall the exact statutory duration and distinguish it from other leave periods.
xs: The **2017 amendment** gives **26 weeks** paid leave (from **12**) — option **(2)**.
It applies to women with fewer than **two surviving children**; at most **8 weeks before delivery**.
xa: **Third child**: **12 weeks**.
**Adopting / commissioning mothers**: **12 weeks** from handing over.
⚠ "**3 months pre + 3 months post-delivery**" is wrong (UPSC **2019**).

128.s: Under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, the paid maternity leave was:
o: 26 weeks for all establishments irrespective of size
8 weeks for establishments with 20 or more employees
16 weeks for establishments with 50 or more employees
12 weeks for establishments with 10 or more employees
128.x: The 1961 Act provided 12 weeks of paid maternity leave and applied to establishments employing 10 or more persons.
128.tq: Keep the leave duration and establishment threshold together; both are required for the correct option.
xs: The **1961 Act** gave **12 weeks** paid leave in establishments with **10+** employees — option **(4)**.
**26 weeks** came only with the **2017 amendment**.
xa: The 2017 amendment: **creche** where **50+ employees**, with **4 visits** a day.
**Work-from-home** after leave **by mutual agreement**.
Contract/fellowship researchers often fall outside the Act (**19 May 2026**).

128.s: Under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, the maternity benefit for the third child onwards is:
128.x: The 2017 position provides 12 weeks of maternity benefit for the third child onwards. The longer period applies to the first two children.
128.tq: Distinguish the benefit applicable to later children from the first-two-children provision.
xs: From the **third child**, the benefit is **12 weeks** — option **(2)**.
**26 weeks** applies only to women with fewer than **two surviving children**.
xa: The **1961 Act** gave **12 weeks** to all.
Adopting (child under **3 months**) and commissioning mothers: **12 weeks**.
Up to **8 weeks before delivery**.

128.s: A woman adopting a child below three months of age is entitled under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 to maternity benefit for:
o: Six weeks from the date of adoption
Twelve weeks from the date the child is handed over to her
Twenty-six weeks from the date of adoption in every case
Eight weeks before the adoption and four weeks after it
128.x: An adopting mother of a child below three months is entitled to 12 weeks from the date the child is handed over to her. The same 12-week period applies to a commissioning mother.
128.tq: Focus on both the eligibility condition and the statutory starting point.
xs: An adopting mother (child under **3 months**) gets **twelve weeks** from the date the child is **handed over** — option **(2)**.
The same **12 weeks** applies to a **commissioning mother**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly say **26** for adopting mothers.
**26 weeks** is for biological mothers with fewer than **two surviving children**.
**Creche**: **50+ employees**, **4 visits** a day.

128.s: A crèche facility is mandatory under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 in an establishment having:
o: 20 or more employees, with two visits a day
100 or more employees, with one visit a day
30 or more employees, with three visits a day
50 or more employees, with four visits a day
128.x: The amendment requires a crèche in establishments having 50 or more employees. The woman is to be allowed four visits a day to the crèche.
128.tq: Combine the threshold number with the associated statutory frequency.
xs: A **creche** is compulsory where there are **50+ employees**, with **4 visits** a day — option **(4)**.
Other thresholds in the options are not in the Act.
xa: **Work-from-home** after leave if work allows, **by mutual agreement**.
The **1961 Act** covered establishments with **10+** employees.
**26 weeks** leave for the first two children.

128.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated cause of a low sex ratio?
128.x: Son preference, female foeticide or infanticide, dowry and neglect of girls are stated causes of a low sex ratio. Equal inheritance and universal schooling are not listed as causes.
128.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the causal group.
xs: **Equal inheritance and universal schooling** are not causes of a low sex ratio — option **(2)**.
The stated causes are **son preference**, **female foeticide/infanticide**, **dowry** and **neglect of girls**.
xa: **PCPNDT Act 1994** bans sex selection and pre-natal sex determination.
Most male-skewed: **Haryana, Punjab**; best SRB: **Kerala** and the **North-East**.
**Female Infanticide Prevention Act**: **1870**.

128.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 provides inheritance rights to Hindus.
The Indian Succession Act, 1925 applies mainly to Muslims and others.
Muslim inheritance is governed by Sharia principles under Muslim Personal Law.
The Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005 granted daughters equal coparcenary rights.
128.x: Option B is incorrect: the Indian Succession Act, 1925 applies mainly to Christians and others. Muslims follow Sharia under their personal law.
128.tq: Match each community to its inheritance law.
n: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956, provides inheritance rights to Hindus. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 54-56]
The Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005, granted daughters equal coparcenary rights. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 54-56]
The Indian Succession Act, 1925, applies mainly to Christians and others. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 54-56]
Muslim inheritance is governed by Sharia principles. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #21 · pp 54-56]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the **Indian Succession Act, 1925** applies mainly to **Muslims** — option **(2)**; it applies mainly to **Christians and others**.
**Muslim inheritance** is governed by **Sharia principles**.
The **Hindu Succession Act, 1956** gives Hindus inheritance rights; the **2005 amendment** gave daughters **equal coparcenary rights**.
xa: HSA 1956 **abolished the female heir's limited estate**.
**AP** made unmarried daughters coparceners in **1986** — well before 2005 (Assembly passed it on **24 Sept 1985** under **NTR**).
HSA does **not apply to notified STs** (**s.2(2)**).

128.s: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 declares instant Talaq-e-Biddat to be:
o: Permitted when approved by a Maintenance Tribunal
Void and illegal, with imprisonment up to three years
A civil remedy through Protection Officers only
128.x: The 2019 Act makes instant talaq-e-biddat void and illegal and a criminal offence, punishable with up to three years in prison.
128.tq: Recall the triple talaq penalty.
n: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act was passed in 2019. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act declares instant Talaq-e-Biddat void. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act declares instant Talaq-e-Biddat illegal. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act makes instant Talaq-e-Biddat a criminal offense. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act prescribes imprisonment of up to 3 years for the offense of instant Talaq-e-Biddat. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
xs: The **2019 Act** makes instant **Talaq-e-Biddat** **void**, **illegal** and a **criminal offense**, with **imprisonment of up to 3 years** — option **(3)**.
The offence is **cognisable, non-bailable** — not "non-cognizable".
**Protection Officers** belong to the **Domestic Violence Act**, not this law.
xa: It was Parliament's response to **Shayara Bano**; passed **30 July 2019**.
Enforced from **September 19, 2018** with **retrospective effect**.
⚠ **Shah Bano** → **1986** Act; **Shayara Bano** → **2019** Act.

128.s: Which Act provides a civil, secular framework for marriage irrespective of caste, religion or faith, after public notice?
128.x: The Special Marriage Act, 1954 provides civil, secular marriage for anyone, whatever their caste, religion or faith, after a public notice.
n: The Special Marriage Act was enacted in 1954. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 89-90]
The Special Marriage Act provides a civil marriage framework. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 89-90]
The Special Marriage Act provides a secular marriage framework. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 89-90]
The Special Marriage Act applies irrespective of caste. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 89-90]
The Special Marriage Act applies irrespective of religion. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 89-90]
The Special Marriage Act applies irrespective of faith. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 89-90]
The Special Marriage Act requires public notification. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #41 · pp 89-90]
xa: The Special Marriage Act came into force on **January 1, 1955**.
Hindu Marriage Act came into force on **May 18, 1955**; codifies marriage, **divorce** and **restitution of conjugal rights**.
Secular maintenance route today: **Sec. 144 BNSS**, replacing **Sec. 125 CrPC**.

128.s: Which of the following pairs (Act — year) is correctly matched?
128.x: The MTP Act dates from 1971; the Special Marriage Act is 1954, the Hindu Marriage Act 1955 and the Dowry Prohibition Act 1961.
n: The Special Marriage Act was enacted in 1954. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The Hindu Marriage Act was enacted in 1955. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The Dowry Prohibition Act was enacted in 1961. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act was enacted in 1971. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
xa: Dowry Act came into force on **July 1, 1961**; MTP Act on **April 1, 1972**.
**Maternity Benefit Act** is also of **1961**.
MTP amended on **September 24, 2021**.

128.s: Which of the following law–provision pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Hindu Marriage Act – Conditions of marriage, divorce and restitution of conjugal rights
Hindu Succession Act – Equal coparcenary rights to daughters by birth
POSH Act – Internal Complaints Committees in workplaces with 10 or more employees
Prohibition of Child Marriage Act – Equal coparcenary rights to daughters
128.x: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act makes child marriages voidable; coparcenary rights come under the Hindu Succession law.
n: The Hindu Marriage Act codified conditions of Hindu marriage, divorce, and restitution of conjugal rights. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The 2005 amendment to the Hindu Succession Act gave daughters equal coparcenary rights by birth. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
Child marriages are voidable under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act mandates Internal Complaints Committees in workplaces with 10 or more employees. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The Hindu Succession Act provides property inheritance rights. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
xa: POSH also provides **Local Committees** at the **district level**.
PCMA ages: **18 years** for females, **21 years** for males.

128.s:
With reference to the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act:
1. It replaced the Sarda Act of 1929.
2. The minimum age is 18 years for females and 21 years for males.
3. It came into force on 1 November 2007.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
128.x: All three are correct: PCMA replaced the 1929 Sarda Act, sets ages at 18 and 21 (and makes child marriages voidable), and came into force on 1 November 2007.
n: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act came into force on November 1, 2007. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act replaced the 1929 Sarda Act. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act fixes the minimum marriage age at 18 for females. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act fixes the minimum marriage age at 21 for males. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
Child marriages are voidable under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
xa: The **Sarda Act** (Child Marriage Restraint Act) set a **minimum marriage age**.
The **Hindu Marriage Act** (**1955**) also codifies **conditions of marriage**, divorce and restitution of conjugal rights.

128.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829 abolished Sati.
The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1976 prohibits dowry.
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 provides protection from domestic violence.
The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856 legalized widow remarriage.
128.x: Option B is incorrect: the Dowry Prohibition Act dates from 1961, not 1976. 1976 is the Equal Remuneration Act and the renaming of the Civil Rights Act.
128.tq: Recall the Dowry Act year, 1961.
n: The Bengal Sati Regulation was enacted in 1829. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Bengal Sati Regulation abolished Sati. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act was enacted in 1856. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act legalized widow remarriage. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Dowry Prohibition Act was enacted in 1961. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Dowry Prohibition Act prohibits dowry. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act was enacted in 2005. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act provides protection from domestic violence. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
xs: The incorrect statement dates the **Dowry Prohibition Act** to **1976** — option **(2)**; it was enacted in **1961**.
**1976** is the year of the **Equal Remuneration Act**.
The **Bengal Sati Regulation** (**1829**), **Domestic Violence Act** (**2005**) and **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act** (**1856**) are correctly dated.
xa: Dowry Act: minimum **5 years** + fine of at least **Rs 15,000** or the dowry's value.
It penalises **giving**, **taking** or **demanding** dowry.
**Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act**: **1987**.

128.s: Which of the following law–purpose pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Indecent Representation of Women Act, 1986 – Prevents child marriage
Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 – Equal wages for men and women
Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 – Prevents child marriage
128.x: The Indecent Representation of Women Act, 1986 prohibits indecent depiction of women; child marriage is dealt with by the 2006 Act.
n: The Maternity Benefit Act was enacted in 1961. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Maternity Benefit Act provides maternity protection. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Equal Remuneration Act was enacted in 1976. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Equal Remuneration Act provides equal wages for men and women. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act was enacted in 1986. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act prohibits the indecent depiction of women. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act was enacted in 2006. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act prevents child marriage. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
xa: ⚠ **1986** = Indecent Representation Act; **1987** = Sati Act.
The **2017** amendment raised paid maternity leave from **12 weeks** to **26 weeks**.
Equal Remuneration Act is now subsumed in the **Code on Wages, 2019**.

128.s: Which of the following law–feature pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: PCPNDT Act, 1994 – Regulation of ultrasound clinics
Domestic Violence Act, 2005 – Protection orders, residence rights and maintenance
Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 – Regulation of ultrasound clinics
128.x: The 2017 Maternity amendment raised paid maternity leave to 26 weeks; ultrasound clinics are regulated by the PCPNDT Act.
n: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act was passed in 2005. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act provides protection orders. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act provides residence rights. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act provides maintenance through Protection Officers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act was passed in 2013. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The POSH Act mandates Internal Complaints Committees in workplaces with at least 10 employees. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act was passed in 2017. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act enhanced paid maternity leave from 12 weeks to 26 weeks. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act was passed in 1994. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The PCPNDT Act regulates ultrasound clinics. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
xa: Domestic Violence Act is a **civil law remedy**; cases decided within **60 days**; right to reside under **Sec. 17**.
The 2017 amendment requires a **crèche** where there are **at least 50 employees**.
PCPNDT came into force on **January 1, 1996**.

128.s: Under the POSH Act, 2013, Internal Complaints Committees are mandated in workplaces having at least how many employees?
128.x: The POSH Act requires an Internal Complaints Committee in every workplace with 10 or more employees, and a Local Committee at district level for smaller ones.
128.tq: Recall the number 10.
n: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act was passed in 2013. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The POSH Act mandates Internal Complaints Committees in workplaces with at least 10 employees. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The POSH Act mandates Local Committees at the district level. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
xs: The **POSH Act, 2013** mandates **Internal Complaints Committees** in workplaces with **at least 10 employees** — option **(3)**.
**Local Committees** operate at the **district level**.
xa: ⚠ Sources differ: some notes call the district body the **Local Complaints Committee**.
The Act came into force on **December 9, 2013**.
It flows from **Vishaka (1997)** guidelines.

128.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about laws for women?
o: The Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is a civil law remedy.
The Muslim Women Act, 2019 declares instant Talaq-e-Biddat void and illegal.
The Maternity Benefit Amendment Act, 2017 mandates a crèche where there are 50 or more employees.
The PCPNDT Act, 1994 permits sex determination in ultrasound clinics.
128.x: The PCPNDT Act bans sex determination.
n: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act was passed in 2005. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act provides a civil law remedy. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act was passed in 2017. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act mandates a crèche facility for establishments with at least 50 employees. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act was passed in 2019. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act declares instant Talaq-e-Biddat void. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act declares instant Talaq-e-Biddat illegal. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act was passed in 1994. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The PCPNDT Act strictly prohibits sex determination. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
xa: PCPNDT aims to **stop female feticide** and **regulates ultrasound clinics**.
Creche: **4 visits** a day allowed.

128.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Special Marriage Act commenced on January 1, 1955.
The PCPNDT Act commenced on January 1, 1994.
The Dowry Prohibition Act commenced on July 1, 1961.
128.x: Option B is incorrect: the PCPNDT Act was passed in 1994 but came into force on 1 January 1996. The trap mixes up the year it was passed with the year it took effect.
128.tq: Discriminate the year passed from the year in force.
n: The Special Marriage Act came into force on January 1, 1955. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The Dowry Prohibition Act came into force on July 1, 1961. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act came into force on January 1, 1996. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act came into force on October 26, 2006. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
xs: The incorrect statement is that **PCPNDT** commenced on **January 1, 1994** — option **(2)**; it was passed in **1994** and came into force on **January 1, 1996**.
**Special Marriage Act**: **January 1, 1955**; **PWDVA**: **October 26, 2006**; **Dowry Prohibition Act**: **July 1, 1961** — all correct.
xa: **Hindu Marriage Act** came into force **May 18, 1955**.
**PCMA** came into force **November 1, 2007**.
**POSH Act** came into force **December 9, 2013**.

128.s: Which Act bans prenatal sex determination to stop female feticide?
128.x: The PCPNDT Act bans sex determination; the MTP Act allows abortion up to 24 weeks on set grounds.
n: The Dowry Prohibition Act strictly penalizes giving, taking, or demanding dowry. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act legalized abortion up to 24 weeks on specified therapeutic and vulnerable-group grounds. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
The Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act prohibits prenatal sex determination. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
xa: PCPNDT allows tests only for **genetic abnormality**.
MTP Act: enacted **1971**, in force **April 1, 1972**.

128.s:
Assertion (A): The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act came into force on April 1, 1972.
Reason (R): The MTP Act was enacted in 1971.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
128.x: Both are true: the MTP Act was passed in 1971 and came into force on 1 April 1972. Being passed in 1971 does not explain the 1972 start date, so R does not explain A.
128.tq: Ask whether the year passed explains the start date.
n: The Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act came into force on April 1, 1972. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #48 · pp 99-101]
xs: Both A and R are true, but **R is NOT the correct explanation of A** — option **(2)**.
The **MTP Act** was enacted in **1971** and came into force on **April 1, 1972**.
Its enactment year does not explain the commencement date.
xa: It was **amended** on **September 24, 2021**.
Under **X v. Principal Secretary** (**2022**), abortion up to **24 weeks** is available regardless of **marital status**.

128.s:
1. The National Commission for Women was established in 1992.
2. The first Equal Pay law was enacted in 1976.
3. The National Mission for Empowerment of Women was launched in 2015.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?

xa: Danial Latifi **upheld** the **Muslim Women Act, 1986**.
⚠ **Shah Bano** → **1986** Act; **Shayara Bano** → **2019** Act.
**Joseph Shine** (**2018**) struck down **Section 497** IPC (adultery).

128.s: Which judgment laid down binding guidelines against workplace sexual harassment that led directly to the POSH Act, 2013?
o: Joseph Shine v. Union of India
Saroj Rani v. Sudarshan Kumar Chadha
128.x: Vishaka's guidelines, based on Articles 14, 19 and 21, led directly to the POSH Act, 2013.
n: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan laid down binding guidelines against sexual harassment at the workplace. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
The guidelines in Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan were based on Article 14. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
The guidelines in Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan were based on Article 19. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
The guidelines in Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan were based on Article 21. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan directly led to the POSH Act, 2013. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
xa: POSH: **Internal Complaints Committees** in workplaces with **10 or more** employees.

**SHe-Box** streamlines redressal under the **POSH Act**.

128.s: Joseph Shine v. Union of India (2018) struck down which section of the IPC?
128.x: Section 497 (adultery) was struck down as archaic, patriarchal and against Articles 14 and 21.
n: Joseph Shine v. Union of India was decided in 2018. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
Joseph Shine v. Union of India struck down Section 497 of the IPC. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
Joseph Shine v. Union of India characterized adultery law as archaic. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
Joseph Shine v. Union of India characterized adultery law as patriarchal. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
Joseph Shine v. Union of India held the adultery law violative of Article 14. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
Joseph Shine v. Union of India held the adultery law violative of Article 21. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]

128.s: In X v. Principal Secretary, H&FW, GNCTD (2022), all women regardless of marital status were held entitled to safe and legal abortion up to:
128.x: The Court allowed abortion up to 24 weeks for all women, married or not, and counted marital rape under the MTP rules.

X v. Principal Secretary, H&FW, GNCTD ruled that all women are entitled to safe abortion up to 24 weeks under the MTP Act. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
X v. Principal Secretary, H&FW, GNCTD ruled that all women are entitled to legal abortion up to 24 weeks under the MTP Act. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]

MTP (Amendment) 2021: up to **20 weeks** on one doctor's opinion; **24 weeks** for special categories.

128.s: Which case recognised daughters' coparcenary rights by birth?
o: Saroj Rani v. Sudarshan Kumar Chadha
Shayara Bano v. Union of India
Joseph Shine v. Union of India

n: Saroj Rani v. Sudarshan Kumar Chadha was decided in 1984. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
Saroj Rani v. Sudarshan Kumar Chadha upheld the constitutional validity of Restitution of Conjugal Rights. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
Restitution of Conjugal Rights is provided under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma clarified the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
Daughters have coparcenary rights by birth under the principle clarified in Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
Joseph Shine v. Union of India struck down Section 497 of the IPC. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
xa: **Danial Latifi** (**2001**): maintenance not limited to the **iddat** period.

128.s:
1. Gender mainstreaming was adopted as a strategy at Beijing.
2. A gender audit checks whether policies and budgets affect women and men equally.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
128.x: Gender mainstreaming builds a gender lens into every policy and was adopted as a Beijing strategy; a gender audit checks whether policies and budgets affect women and men equally.
xa: The Beijing **Fourth World Conference on Women (1995)** adopted the **Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action**.
The Platform has **12 critical areas**, including the **girl child**.
**NPEW 2001** goals include **gender mainstreaming** and ending discrimination and violence.

128.s: The principal areas of work of the All India Women's Conference were:
o: Education, social upliftment and legal rights
128.x: The AIWC focused on education, social upliftment and legal rights.
xa: AIWC was founded in **1927**, linked with **Margaret Cousins**.
**WIA (1917)**: votes for women; **NCWI (1925)**: linked to the International Council of Women.
**Andhra Mahila Sabha (1937)**: **Durgabai Deshmukh**.

128.s: India ratified CEDAW in:
128.x: India signed CEDAW in 1980 and ratified it in 1993, both before the Beijing Conference of 1995.
xa: CEDAW was adopted by the UNGA in **1979**.

128.s: The Beijing Platform for Action (1995) identifies how many critical areas of concern?
128.x: Adopted at the Fourth World Conference on Women, it identifies 12 critical areas, including the girl child.
xa: Areas include poverty, education, health, violence, armed conflict, economy, decision-making, media, environment.
**Gender mainstreaming** is a Beijing strategy.
Earlier conferences: Mexico City **1975**, Copenhagen **1980**, Nairobi **1985**.

128.s: The UN Commission on the Status of Women (1946) functions under the:
128.x: The CSW functions under ECOSOC, not the General Assembly.
xa: **CSW-70 (2026)** adopted non-binding **Agreed Conclusions** on women's **access to justice**.
**CEDAW** was adopted by the **UNGA** in **1979**.
**International Women's Year**: **1975**.

128.s: The International Women’s Year and the First World Conference on Women were associated with
128.x: The International Women’s Year and the First World Conference on Women were held in Mexico City in 1975.
128.tq: Match the conference milestone with its city and year.
xs: **International Women's Year** and the **1st World Conference** were in **Mexico City, 1975** — option **(4)**.
**Copenhagen 1980** was the 2nd, **Nairobi 1985** the 3rd, **Beijing 1995** the 4th.
xa: The **UN Decade for Women** ran **1976-85**.
Beijing produced the **Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action**.

128.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
128.x: The Beijing Conference was held in 1995, not 1980. Copenhagen was the second World Conference in 1980, and Nairobi was the third in 1985.
128.tq: Find the shifted year in a sequence of closely spaced international milestones.
xs: **Beijing Conference — 1980** is wrong — option **(4)**: Beijing was in **1995**.
**Nairobi — 1985**, **CEDAW — 1979** and **Copenhagen — 1980** are correct.
xa: ⚠ Mexico City **1975** (1st) – Copenhagen **1980** (2nd) – Nairobi **1985** (3rd) – Beijing **1995** (4th).
India signed CEDAW in **1980**, ratified **1993**.
Beijing identified **12 critical areas**.

128.s: Sarla Mudgal v. Union of India (1995) primarily dealt with which of the following?
o: Conversion to Islam to contract a second Hindu marriage
Adultery under Section 497 of the IPC
128.x: Sarla Mudgal held that conversion to Islam cannot be used to validate a second marriage by a Hindu man and stressed the need for a Uniform Civil Code.
128.tq: Use the wrong-person or wrong-issue trap in landmark-judgment questions.
xs: **Sarla Mudgal (1995)**: a Hindu man **converting to Islam to remarry** — option **(2)**.
**Conversion cannot validate his second marriage**; the Court stressed the **UCC**.
Workplace harassment is the **2013 Act**; adultery (**s.497 IPC**) was **Joseph Shine (2018)**.
xa: **Hindu Marriage Act 1955**: **monogamy**.
**Shah Bano (1985)** also urged a UCC.
UCC vs **Art. 25/29** remains a debate.

128.s: The Gender Development Index compares females and males with respect to:
o: Health, education and command over resources
128.x: The GDI makes a female-to-male comparison in health, education and command over resources.
xa: The **GII** was proposed to fix the GDI's gaps.
⚠ The **0 (equal) to 1 (worst)** scale belongs to the **GII**, not the GDI.
**Global Gender Gap Index (WEF)**: economic participation, education, health and survival, political empowerment.

128.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the dimensions of the Global Gender Gap Index?
128.x: The Global Gender Gap Index covers economic participation, education, health and survival, and political empowerment. Military expenditure is not one of its dimensions.
128.tq: Find the unrelated dimension in a list of index components.
xs: **Military expenditure** is not a Global Gender Gap Index dimension — option **(3)**.
Its dimensions: **economic participation**, **education**, **health and survival**, **political empowerment**.
xa: The index is published by the **WEF**.
**GII** fixes GDI gaps; scale **0 (equal) to 1 (worst)**.
**Women, Peace and Security Index 2023**: India **131/177**.

128.s: The statement that “the world's welfare is impossible unless women's condition improves; a bird cannot fly on one wing” is associated with
128.x: This observation is associated with Swami Vivekananda.

xs: "A bird cannot fly on one wing" — **Swami Vivekananda** — option **(1)**.
**Ambedkar**: "progress of a **community**"; **Nehru**: "condition of a **nation**"; **Gandhi**: "weaker sex is a libel".
xa: ⚠ "**community**" = Ambedkar (APPSC-G2 **2025**); "**nation**" = Nehru (APPSC **2019**).
Vivekananda's point: the world's welfare is impossible unless women's condition improves.
**Gandhi**: calling woman the weaker sex is man's injustice to woman.

128.s: Gender mainstreaming was promoted globally at the World Conference on Women held in:
128.x: The Fourth World Conference on Women (Beijing, 1995) promoted gender mainstreaming globally.
n: Gender mainstreaming was promoted globally during the Fourth World Conference on Women. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 67-70]
The Fourth World Conference on Women was held in Beijing in 1995. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 67-70]
xa: Beijing produced the **Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action** with **12 critical areas**.
⚠ Mexico City **1975** (1st) – Copenhagen **1980** – Nairobi **1985** – Beijing **1995** (4th).
**CEDAW** (**1979**): India signed **1980**, ratified **1993**.

128.s:
Assertion (A): Gender mainstreaming aims to achieve gender equality.
Reason (R): It integrates gender perspectives into all policies, programmes, laws, and institutions.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
128.x: Both are true: gender mainstreaming works toward gender equality by bringing gender perspectives into all policies, programmes, laws and institutions. R explains A.
128.tq: Ask whether the method explains the aim.
n: Gender mainstreaming aims to achieve gender equality. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 67-70]
Gender mainstreaming aims to achieve gender equality. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 67-70]
xs: Both A and R are true and **R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
Gender mainstreaming **aims to achieve gender equality**.
It does so by **integrating gender perspectives** into all **policies**, **programmes**, **laws** and **institutions**.
xa: Other aims: **reduce gender discrimination**, **promote women's participation**, **ensure equitable development**.
It was promoted at the **Fourth World Conference on Women**, **Beijing**, **1995**.

128.s:
Gender mainstreaming aims to:
1. Reduce gender discrimination.
2. Ensure equitable development.
3. Promote inclusive governance.
Which of the above is/are correct?
128.x: Reducing discrimination, equitable development and inclusive governance (along with women's empowerment) are all aims of gender mainstreaming.
n: Gender mainstreaming aims to reduce gender discrimination. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 67-70]
Gender mainstreaming promotes women's empowerment. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 67-70]
Gender mainstreaming promotes inclusive governance. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #32 · pp 67-70]
xa: It also promotes **social justice** and **sustainable development**.
**Gender audit** = a **systematic assessment** of policies, programmes, institutions and budgets.

128.s: Which of the following statements about gender auditing is incorrect?
o: It is a systematic assessment of policies, programmes, institutions and budgets.
It excludes workplace safety from its components.
It aims to improve women's participation.
128.x: Option C is incorrect: workplace safety is one of the components of a gender audit. The audit is a systematic assessment of policies, programmes, institutions and budgets.
128.tq: Recall the components of a gender audit.
n: Gender Audit is a systematic assessment of policies. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 61-62]
Gender Audit is a systematic assessment of programmes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 61-62]
Gender Audit is a systematic assessment of institutions. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 61-62]
Gender Audit is a systematic assessment of budgets. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 61-62]
Gender Audit evaluates gender equality. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 61-62]
Gender Audit includes workplace safety. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 61-62]
Gender Audit improves women's participation. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #27 · pp 61-62]
xs: The incorrect statement is that a gender audit **excludes workplace safety** — option **(3)**; **workplace safety** is one of its components.
A gender audit is a **systematic assessment** of **policies**, **programmes**, **institutions** and **budgets**.
It **evaluates gender equality** and **improves women's participation**.
xa: Components: **gender budgeting**, **equal opportunities**, **workplace safety**, **decision-making participation**.
It also **identifies gender gaps** and **ensures gender-sensitive governance**.

128.s: The term ‘Missing women’ was coined by
128.x: Amartya Sen coined the term ‘missing women’ to refer to the consequences of discrimination against women, including intra-household discrimination.
128.tq: Use the person–concept association without confusing it with other gender scholars.
xs: **Amartya Sen** coined **'Missing women'** for intra-household discrimination — option **(2)** (APPSC **2019**).
**Uma Chakravarti**: **Brahmanical patriarchy**; **Bina Agarwal**: **A Field of One's Own**; **Gail Omvedt**: Dalit/Bahujan feminism.
xa: Sen also gave the **capability approach** and **cooperative conflict**.
Causes of a low sex ratio: **son preference**, female foeticide/infanticide, dowry, neglect of girls.
Sex ratio at birth rose from **904 (2017-19)** to **917 (2021-23)** (MoSPI, Women and Men in India **2025**).

128.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the National Policy for Empowerment of Women, 2001?
o: Promoting commercial surrogacy as an employment opportunity
Ending discrimination and violence against women
Ensuring equal access to health, education and employment
128.x: The policy objectives included advancement and empowerment, equal access to health, education and employment, ending discrimination and violence, and gender mainstreaming. Commercial surrogacy is not a policy objective listed here.
128.tq: Find the unrelated legal concept inserted among genuine policy objectives.
xs: **Promoting commercial surrogacy** is not an NPEW goal — option **(1)**; the **Surrogacy (Regulation) Act 2021** bans commercial surrogacy.
NPEW goals: **ending discrimination and violence**, **equal access to health, education, employment**, and **gender mainstreaming**.
xa: NPEW **2001**; **2001** was the **Year of Women's Empowerment**.
The **8th Plan** shifted from 'development' to **'empowerment'**.
Only **altruistic** surrogacy is allowed (medical costs, insurance).

128.s: In the Draft National Policy for Women, 2016, food security and nutrition were included under:
128.x: Food security and nutrition came under health; governance and decision-making and environment were separate priority areas.

The Draft Policy came from the **MWCD**.
Earlier: **NPEW 2001** (APPSC **2019**).

128.s: Under Section 2(2), the Hindu Succession Act does not apply to:
o: Members of Scheduled Tribes, unless the Central Government directs otherwise
128.x: Section 2(2) excludes notified Scheduled Tribes unless the Centre directs otherwise; the Supreme Court (8 Oct 2025) upheld this exclusion.
xa: HSA **1956**: equal inheritance; limited estate abolished.
**2005 amendment**: daughters equal coparceners.
**Vineeta Sharma (2020)**: daughter a **coparcener by birth**.

128.s: Which State had already made unmarried daughters coparceners through its amendment before the national Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005?
128.x: Andhra Pradesh made unmarried daughters coparceners through an earlier amendment. The Andhra Pradesh Assembly passed the relevant Act on 24 September 1985 under NTR.

xs: **Andhra Pradesh** made **unmarried daughters coparceners** well before **2005** — option **(1)**.
The AP Assembly passed its Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act on **24 Sept 1985** under **NTR**.
xa: The AP amendment is dated **1986**.
Central **2005 amendment**: daughters = **equal coparceners**.
**Vineeta Sharma (2020)**: daughter a **coparcener by birth**.

128.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021?
o: A woman can be a surrogate only once.
The couple requires certificates of essentiality and eligibility.
Sex selection is permitted if the surrogate gives written consent.
128.x: Sex selection is prohibited and cannot be permitted merely through the surrogate's consent.
xa: **Altruistic** surrogacy allowed (medical costs, insurance only).
**Abandoning the child** is also prohibited.
⚠ "Abortion of surrogate child prohibited" was **NOT** in the **2019 Bill** (APPSC **2018**).

128.s: A foetus carried through surrogacy may be aborted under the applicable law only when
o: the intending couple alone gives consent
the ART clinic recommends it without further approval
the surrogate gives written consent and authorisation is obtained under the MTP Act
the surrogate’s consent is specifically excluded
128.x: Abortion of a surrogate foetus is not prohibited outright. It requires the surrogate’s written consent and authorisation under the MTP Act.
128.tq: Apply the exception to a general prohibition instead of treating abortion as absolutely banned.
xs: A surrogate foetus may be aborted with the **surrogate's written consent** + **authorisation under the MTP Act** — option **(3)**.
It is **not banned outright**, and the couple's or clinic's say alone is not enough.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "abortion of the surrogate child is prohibited" was NOT in the **2019 Bill** (APPSC **2018**).
**MTP (Amendment) Act, 2021**: up to **20 weeks** on one doctor's opinion.
A woman can be a surrogate only **once**.

128.s: The National Commission for Women, created under the NCW Act, 1990, was constituted in:
128.x: The NCW is a statutory body under the 1990 Act and was constituted in 1992.
xa: Composition: Chairperson + **5 members** (at least one **SC**, one **ST**) + Member-Secretary.
Functions: review laws, complaints and **suo motu** notice, inspect jails/remand homes, police gender sensitisation.
⚠ NCW **Act 1990** but **set up Jan 1992**.
First women's court: **West Bengal**, **Malda, 2013** (APPSC **2019**).

128.s: Under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990, the Commission consists of a Chairperson, a Member-Secretary and:
o: three members, at least one from the Scheduled Castes
five members, at least one each from the SCs and the STs
seven members, all nominated by the Chief Justice of India
five members, all of whom must be retired judges
128.x: The NCW has a Chairperson, five members (at least one SC and one ST) and a Member-Secretary. The counts of three and seven are wrong, and there is no requirement that members be retired judges or nominated by the CJI.
128.tq: NCW = Chair + 5 (≥1 SC, ≥1 ST) + Member-Secretary.
xs: The NCW has a Chairperson, **five members (at least one SC, one ST)** and a Member-Secretary — option **(2)**.
Three or seven members, CJI nomination or retired judges are not in the **NCW Act 1990**.
xa: NCW functions: review safeguards and laws, take complaints and **suo motu** notice.
It inspects **jails/remand homes**, does research and **police gender sensitisation**.
⚠ NCW **Act 1990**, but **set up Jan 1992**.

128.s: Which of the following correctly represents the sex ratio figures reported by NFHS-4 and NFHS-5 respectively?
128.x: The sex ratio was 991 in NFHS-4 and increased to 1020 in NFHS-5.
128.tq: Read the direction of change and distinguish survey figures from census figures.
xs: Sex ratio: **NFHS-4: 991**, **NFHS-5: 1020** — option **(3)**.
Option (1) reverses them; **904 and 917** are **sex ratio at birth** figures from MoSPI.
xa: Sex ratio at birth rose from **904 (2017-19)** to **917 (2021-23)** (**Women and Men in India 2025**, **27th edition**).

Causes of low ratio: **son preference**, female foeticide/infanticide, dowry, neglect of girls.

128.s: Which of the following correctly describes the regional pattern of sex ratio in India?
o: Kerala and the North-East are the most male-skewed, while Punjab has the best sex ratio
Haryana and Punjab are the most male-skewed, while Kerala and the North-East have the best sex-ratio balance
Haryana and Punjab are the most female-skewed, while Kerala and the North-East are male-skewed
There is no marked regional variation in the sex ratio between northern and southern India

xs: **Haryana and Punjab** are most **male-skewed**; **Kerala and the North-East** have the **best** sex ratio at birth — option **(2)**.
Options (1) and (3) reverse the pattern; (4) denies a pattern that the data show.
xa: North-East best: **Arunachal, Meghalaya, Mizoram** (CRS **2024**).
NFHS-5 sex ratio: **1020** (NFHS-4: **991**).

128.s: The Female Infanticide Prevention Act was enacted during British rule in the year:
128.x: The Female Infanticide Prevention Act was passed in 1870 (APPSC 2018). 1829 is the abolition of Sati, 1856 the Widow Remarriage Act and 1929 the Sarda (Child Marriage Restraint) Act.

128.s: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 is associated with which of the following reforms?
o: Abolition of the female heir’s limited estate and equal inheritance for women
Mandatory registration of every inter-faith marriage under one uniform law
128.x: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 gave women equal inheritance and abolished the female heir’s limited estate. Civil marriage irrespective of religion is associated with the Special Marriage Act.

**Civil marriage irrespective of religion** = **Special Marriage Act 1954**; **equal pay** = **Equal Remuneration Act 1976**.
xa: **2005 amendment**: daughters = **equal coparceners**.
**AP amendment (1986)** made unmarried daughters coparceners well before 2005.
STs are excluded under **s.2(2)**.

128.s: India's first exclusive women's court was set up in which State?
128.x: The first women's court was set up in West Bengal, at Malda in 2013 (APPSC 2019). Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra are distractors.

xs: India's first women's court was set up in **West Bengal**, at **Malda** in **2013** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2019**).
Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra are not linked with the first women's court in the notes.
xa: **Family Courts Act 1984**: **953** Family Courts in **29** States/UTs (as of **31 Jul 2025**).
**NCW Act 1990**; NCW set up **Jan 1992**.
Kerala instead stands out for the **best sex ratio at birth**, with the North-East.

128.s: The 0 to 1 scale in which 0 denotes equality and 1 denotes the worst outcome belongs to the
128.x: The 0-to-1 scale, where 0 represents equality and 1 the worst outcome, belongs to the Gender Inequality Index, not the GDI.

xs: The **0 (equal) to 1 (worst)** scale belongs to the **Gender Inequality Index** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Notes that give this scale for the **GDI** are wrong.
xa: The GII was **proposed to fix GDI's gaps**.
**GDI**: female-to-male comparison on health, education, command over resources.
**Global Gender Gap Index** is the **WEF's**.

128.s: Which of the following statement–leader pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Progress of a community measured by the progress of its women – B.R. Ambedkar
Condition of a nation told by the status of its women – Jawaharlal Nehru
A bird cannot fly on one wing – Swami Vivekananda
'To call woman the weaker sex is a libel' – B.R. Ambedkar
128.x: Calling the 'weaker sex' label a libel was Mahatma Gandhi's statement.
xa: ⚠ Swapping **Ambedkar** and **Nehru** is the usual trap.

128.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Uma Chakravarti — A Field of One’s Own
Gail Omvedt — Seeing Like a Feminist
Bina Agarwal — Land rights and A Field of One’s Own
128.x: Bina Agarwal is associated with land rights and authored A Field of One’s Own. Seeing Like a Feminist is associated with Nivedita Menon, while ‘missing women’ was coined by Amartya Sen.

xs: **Bina Agarwal** — **land rights** and **A Field of One's Own** — option **(3)** is correctly matched.
**A Field of One's Own** is not Uma Chakravarti's; she wrote on **Brahmanical patriarchy**.
**Seeing Like a Feminist** is by **Nivedita Menon**, not Gail Omvedt; **'Missing women'** is **Amartya Sen's** term.
xa: **Gail Omvedt**: Dalit/Bahujan feminism.
**The High-Caste Hindu Woman**: **Pandita Ramabai**; **Stri Purush Tulana**: **Tarabai Shinde**.
**Manushi** was founded by **Madhu Kishwar**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements on the contributions of Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar:
I. His great contribution was for the upliftment of women in India.
II. He organized a powerful movement for the enactment of Widow Remarriage Act.
III. To propagate his social ideas, he published Sambad Kaumudi, a Bengali weekly newspaper.
Which of the above statements are correct?
128.x: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a major social reformer who advocated women's education and rights. He strongly supported the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856, but the newspaper Sambad Kaumudi was associated with Raja Rammohan Roy, not Vidyasagar.

128.s: Who stated that 'I measure the progress of a III. community by the degree of progress which women have achieved'?
'Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action', often seen in the news, is
o: a strategy to tackle, the regional terrorism, an outcome of a meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization
a plan of action for sustainable economic growth in the Asia-Pacific Region, an outcome of the deliberations of the
an agenda for women's empowerment, an outcome of a World Conference convened by the United Nations
a strategy to combat wildlife trafficking, a declaration of the East Asia Summit
128.x: The Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action was adopted at the Fourth World Conference on Women held in Beijing in 1995, organised by the United Nations. It serves as a comprehensive global agenda for women's empowerment, focusing on areas such as gender equality, women's rights, education, health, and participation in decision-making.

128.s: UN observed_______________as International year for Women.
128.x: The UN observed the year 1975 as the International Year for Women.

128.s: By passing, 'Triple Talaq Law' recently, the Parliament of India endorsed which year's ruling of the Supreme Court of India that had made Triple Talaq (Talaq-e-Biddat) as unconstitutional?
128.x: The Supreme Court in the Shayara Bano case (2017) had declared the Practice of Triple Talaq (Talaq-e-biddat) as unconstitutional. The Triple Talaq is considered to be a violation of Article 14 (the right to equality).

128.s: Which High Court stated that the divorce, by saying ‘Talaq’ 3 times, is illegal?
128.x: Allahabad High Court decided in the case of Rahmatullah Vs State of UP 1994 that the divorce by saying Talaq for 3 times is illegal. It violates Articles 14 and 15. It is noteworthy that under 'The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019, any pronouncement of talaq by a Muslim husband upon his wife, by words either spoken or written or in electronic form or in any other manner whatsoever, shall be void and illegal.

128.s: Which of the following was NOT proposed in the Surrogacy (Regulation) Bill, 2019?
o: The Bill prohibits commercial surrogacy, but allows altruistic surrogacy
The intending couple should have a ‘certificate of essentiality’ and a ‘certificate of eligibility’ issued by the appropriate authority
An abortion of the surrogate child is prohibited
A close relative of the intending couple can be a surrogate mother
