128.s:
Which of the following labour related Acts have been amalgamated into the 'Code on Wages, 2019'?
I. Minimum Wages Act
II. Payment of Bonus Act
III. The Contract Labour Act
IV. Equal Remuneration Act
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
128.x: The Code on Wages, 2019 replaces the following four laws: (i) The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, (ii) The Minimum Wages Act, 1948, (iii) The Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, and (iv) The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976.

129.s: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act was originally known as SITA and was amended in:
129.x: The law was enacted in 1956 as the Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act (SITA) and was renamed the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act by the 1986 amendment. 1986 is the amendment year, not the enactment year; 1961, 1994 and 2003 relate to the Dowry Act, PNDT Act and its renaming.
129.tq: Distinguish the original enactment year from the amendment year.
xs: The law was **renamed ITPA by the 1986 amendment** — option **(2)**; it began in **1956** as the **Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act (SITA)**.
**1961** = **Dowry Prohibition Act**; **1994** = **PCPNDT (PNDT) Act**; **2003** = PNDT's renaming.
xa: ⚠ ITPA is a **1956** law; "ITPA 1986" refers only to its **amendment year**.
It gives effect to the **1950 UN Convention**.
It does **not criminalise prostitution itself**; **protective homes** are run by states.

129.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act — 2006
Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act — 1987; came into force in 1988
129.x: The Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act was enacted in 1987 and came into force in 1988. The Indecent Representation Act dates to 1986, the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act to 2006 and the Muslim Women Act concerning triple talaq to 2019.
129.tq: Use neighbouring enactment years to expose swapped law-year pairs.
xs: **Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act — 1987**, in force **1988** — option **(2)**.
**Muslim Women (Marriage) Act** = **2019**, not 2006; **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act** = **2006**, not 2019.
The **Indecent Representation Act** is not of **1994** — that is the **PCPNDT Act**.
xa: The Sati Act punishes **attempt, abetment and glorification**.
The **DM** may seize property used for glorification.
The triple talaq Act was passed on **30 July 2019**.

129.s: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 came into force on:
129.x: The Dowry Prohibition Act came into force on 1 July 1961 (APPSC-G2 2025). The other dates are distractors; 26 October is the date the Domestic Violence Act came into force, in 2006.
129.tq: Dowry Act in force 1 July 1961.
xs: The **Dowry Prohibition Act** came into force on **1 July 1961** — option **(2)** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
**26 October** is the **DV Act's** commencement, in **2006**.
xa: It penalises **giving, taking or abetting** dowry.
Offences: **cognisable, non-bailable, non-compoundable**.
IPC → BNS also took effect on **1 July** (**2024**).

129.s: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 came into force on:
129.x: The PWDVA, though enacted in 2005, came into force on 26 October 2006 (UPPSC 2015). 1 July is the Dowry Act's commencement date (1961), December 2013 is when the POSH Act came into force, and 26 January 2006 is a distractor.
129.tq: PWDVA: enacted 2005, in force 26 Oct 2006.
xs: The **PWDVA** came into force on **26 October 2006** — option **(2)** (UPPSC **2015**).
**1 July** is the **Dowry Act's** date (**1961**); **Dec 2013** is when the **POSH Act** came into force.
xa: The Act is a **civil law**.
**Protection Officers** are appointed by the State Govt.
AP: **51,581** PWDVA cases (AP SES 2025-26).

129.s: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956:
o: Criminalises prostitution itself in every circumstance
Only regulates registration of protective homes
Penalises brothel-keeping, soliciting and living on prostitution earnings, but not prostitution itself
129.x: The ITPA does not criminalise prostitution itself; it penalises brothel-keeping, living on prostitution earnings, soliciting and detaining persons.
xa: Selling/buying minors for prostitution: **BNS 98/99** (IPC **372/373**).
**Shakti Sadan** (Mission Shakti) houses trafficked and destitute women.
**Ujjawala** is now part of Shakti Sadan.

129.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Monitoring under the Indecent Representation law excludes digital and AI-generated content.
The Indecent Representation of Women Act bans denigrating depiction of women in advertisements and publications.
The Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act punishes attempt, abetment and glorification of sati.
A District Magistrate may seize property used for glorification of sati.
129.x: As of 2025, monitoring under the Indecent Representation law extends to digital and AI-generated content.
xa: Sati Act: **1987**, in force **1988**.
**ITPA 1956** began as **SITA**.
**PCPNDT Act 1994** (renamed **2003**).

129.s: Under Section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, the term ‘dowry’ refers to:
o: Only property demanded by the bride’s family before marriage
Property or valuable security given or agreed to be given, directly or indirectly, in connection with a marriage
Any gift exchanged between the spouses after marriage, including mahr
Only cash or movable property given after marriage
129.x: Dowry includes property or valuable security given or agreed to be given directly or indirectly, before, at or any time after marriage, in connection with the marriage. Dower or mahr under Muslim personal law is excluded.
129.tq: Test the exact statutory definition and distinguish the excluded term.
xs: **Dowry (s.2)** = property or valuable security given or agreed to be given, **directly or indirectly**, in connection with marriage — option **(2)**.
It covers **before, at or any time after marriage**, not just one stage or only cash.
**Dower/mahr** under Muslim personal law is **excluded**.
xa: The Act came into force on **1 July 1961** (APPSC **2025**).
It penalises **giving, taking or abetting** dowry.
Amendments of **1984 and 1986**.

129.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961?
o: Section 3 — Giving, taking or abetting dowry
Section 8A — Burden of proof on the accused
Section 8B — Dowry Prohibition Officers appointed by the Central Government
129.x: Section 8B provides for Dowry Prohibition Officers appointed by the State Government, not the Central Government. Sections 3, 4 and 8A are correctly matched.
129.tq: Find the wrong authority attached to a statutory power.
xs: **s.8B — officers appointed by the Central Government** is wrong — option **(3)**: **Dowry Prohibition Officers** are appointed by the **State Govt**.
**s.3**: giving, taking or abetting; **s.4**: demanding; **s.8A**: **burden of proof on the accused** — all correct.
xa: s.3 penalty: **not less than 5 years** + fine **not less than ₹15,000** or the dowry's value, whichever is more.
s.4 penalty: **6 months to 2 years** + fine up to **Rs 10,000**.
Offences are **cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable**.

129.s: Under Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, demanding dowry is punishable with imprisonment of:
129.x: Demanding dowry attracts six months to two years; giving or taking dowry (s.3) carries a minimum of five years.
xa: ⚠ Notes saying "up to five years" are wrong.
s.3 fine: at least **₹15,000** or the dowry's value, whichever is more.
s.4 fine: up to **Rs 10,000**.

129.s: Under Section 8A of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, the burden of proof lies on the:
129.x: Section 8A places the burden of proof on the accused; the offences are also cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable.
xa: Courts may act on their **own knowledge** or on complaints by **recognised welfare bodies**.
**s.8B**: **Dowry Prohibition Officers** appointed by the State Govt.
~**20** dowry deaths a day, **6,000+** a year.

129.s: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is primarily classified as a:
129.x: The Act is a civil law protecting women from domestic violence, although other criminal provisions may also apply to related conduct.
129.tq: Discriminate between the civil character of the Act and criminal provisions dealing with particular offences.
xs: The **DV Act 2005** is a **civil law** (only civil) — option **(4)**.
⚠ CDI's list of criminal laws wrongly includes it.
xa: It protects women **irrespective of the relationship's status** with the respondent.
In force **26 October 2006** (UPPSC **2015**).
Reliefs: protection (**s.18**), residence (**s.19**), monetary (**s.20**), custody (**s.21**), compensation (**s.22**).

129.s: Section 3 of the Domestic Violence Act, 2005 covers which forms of abuse?
o: Physical, sexual and verbal or emotional abuse only
Physical, sexual, verbal or emotional, and economic abuse
Physical, verbal and economic abuse only
129.x: Section 3 covers physical, sexual, verbal or emotional, and economic abuse.
xa: The Act is a **civil law**.
Authorities: **Protection Officers**, registered **Service Providers**, the **Magistrate**.
Disposal within **60 days**.

129.s: Under the Domestic Violence Act, 2005, which pair (relief — section) is correctly matched?
129.x: Residence orders are under Section 19; protection orders are under Section 18, monetary relief under Section 20 and compensation orders under Section 22.
xa: **s.21**: temporary **custody** of children.
**Sec. 17**: **right to reside**.
Multiple reliefs in one case; disposal within **60 days**.

129.s: Which of the following pairs under the POSH Act is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Internal Committee – Workplace with 10 or more employees
Local Committee – Workplace with fewer than 10 employees
Local Committee establishing authority – District Officer
Internal Committee Presiding Officer – District Officer
129.x: The Internal Committee is presided over by a senior woman employee; the District Officer constitutes the Local Committee.
xa: LC also hears **complaints against the employer**.
IC: **2+** employees, **1 external NGO member**, half women.

129.s: Which of the following correctly states the time limits under the POSH Act?
o: Complaint within 6 months, inquiry within 60 days and employer action within 90 days
Complaint within 3 months, inquiry within 90 days and employer action within 60 days
Complaint within 90 days, inquiry within 3 months and employer action within 6 months
Complaint within 3 months, inquiry within 60 days and employer action within 30 days
129.x: The complaint is ordinarily filed within three months, the inquiry is to be completed within 90 days, and the employer is to act within 60 days.
129.tq: Keep the three separate statutory periods distinct instead of swapping their order.
xs: Complaint within **3 months**, inquiry within **90 days**, employer acts within **60 days** — option **(2)**.
The other options jumble these limits.
xa: The complaint period is **extendable by 3** months.
AP: **86 of 88** POSH cases resolved.
**SHe-Box 2.0** tracks ICs/LCs online.

129.s: SHe-Box 2.0, under Mission Shakti, is best described as:
o: A fund exclusively providing maternity benefits
An employment exchange for women in rural areas
A single-window online system for complaint and tracking of Internal and Local Committees
A criminal investigation portal for dowry deaths
129.x: SHe-Box 2.0 is a single-window online complaint and tracking system for Internal and Local Committees under Mission Shakti.
129.tq: Match the digital platform with its operational function rather than its broad women-welfare context.
xs: **SHe-Box 2.0** (MWCD, **Mission Shakti**) is a **single-window online complaint** and **tracking** system for **ICs/LCs** — option **(3)**.
It covers **public, private, organised and unorganised** sectors.
xa: **SHINE app**: launched by **Railways** for staff.
**One Stop Centres (Sakhi)**: medical, legal, counselling, shelter under one roof.
**Women Helpline 181**: emergency help and counselling.

129.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to dowry-related criminal law after the transition from the IPC to the BNS?
o: Dowry death — BNS Section 80; corresponding IPC Section 304B
Cruelty — BNS Section 80; corresponding IPC Section 498A
Presumption of dowry death — BNS Section 85; corresponding Evidence Act Section 113B
Dowry death — BNS Section 86; corresponding IPC Section 304B
129.x: Dowry death is covered by BNS Section 80, corresponding to IPC Section 304B. Cruelty is covered by BNS Sections 85 and 86, corresponding to IPC Section 498A, while the presumption is under BSA Section 118, corresponding to Evidence Act Section 113B.
129.tq: Match the new BNS provision with its former IPC counterpart.
xs: **Dowry death — BNS s.80** (IPC **304B**) — option **(1)**.
**Cruelty** is **BNS 85-86** (IPC **498A**), not s.80; dowry death is not s.86.
**Presumption of dowry death** is **BSA s.118** (Evidence Act **113B**), not BNS 85.
xa: Dowry death = death within **7 years** of marriage.
IPC → BNS from **1 July 2024**.

129.s: For the purpose of the offence of dowry death, death occurring within what period from the date of marriage is specifically relevant?
129.x: BNS Section 80, corresponding to IPC Section 304B, concerns dowry death where the death occurs within seven years of marriage, subject to the other legal requirements.
129.tq: Use the statutory time-limit as the decisive numerical clue.
xs: Dowry death covers death **within seven years** (**7 years**) of marriage — option **(2)**.
It is **BNS s.80**, the old IPC **304B**.
xa: Presumption: **BSA s.118** (Evidence Act **113B**).
The **1986** amendment brought in dowry death.
**Guntur** special court gave **life imprisonment** in a **2020** dowry-death case (**2026**).

129.s: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, stalking is dealt with under:
129.x: Stalking is BNS 78 (IPC 354D); voyeurism is 77, sexual harassment 75 and outraging modesty 74.
xa: **BNS 80**: dowry death; **85-86**: cruelty.
IPC → BNS from **1 July 2024**.

129.s: Cruelty by a husband or his relatives is covered under which provision of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
129.x: Cruelty by a husband or relatives is covered under BNS Sections 85-86, corresponding to IPC Section 498A.
129.tq: Distinguish the cruelty provision from the nearby dowry-death provision by section number.
xs: **Cruelty by husband or relatives** = **BNS sections 85-86** (IPC **498A**) — option **(4)**.
**80** is dowry death; **77-78** voyeurism and stalking; **143** trafficking.
xa: Debate: **misuse claims against 498A** vs heavy under-reporting.
The **1986** amendment linked this framework with **dowry death** (304B).

129.s: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, acid attack is covered by:
129.x: Acid attack is Section 124; rape is 63-64, trafficking 143 and selling or buying minors for prostitution 98-99.
xa: Acid attack: minimum **10 years**, extendable to life; attempt **5-7 years**.
Old IPC: trafficking **370**; minors **372/373**; acid **326A/326B**.
**RPwD Act 2016** lists acid-attack injuries as a **disability**.

129.s:
Assertion (A): Trafficking of persons is covered under Section 143 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Reason (R): Section 124 of the BNS concerns trafficking of persons.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
129.x: Trafficking is under Section 143, so A is true; Section 124 concerns acid attack, so R is false.
xa: **77**: voyeurism; **78**: stalking.
**98/99**: selling/buying minors for prostitution.
Acid attack came via **CLA 2013**.

129.s: According to UNODC trafficking findings, which one of the following countries is identified as both a high origin country and a high destination country?
129.x: Bangladesh, India, Nepal and Pakistan are identified as high origin countries, while India and Pakistan are also identified as high destination countries.
129.tq: Separate the overlapping origin-and-destination category from countries listed only as origins.
xs: **India** is both a high **origin** and a high **destination** country — option **(1)**.
**Bangladesh** and **Nepal** are origin countries only; **Sri Lanka** is not listed.
xa: High origin: **Bangladesh, India, Nepal, Pakistan**.
High destination: **India, Pakistan**.
**GLOTIP 2016**: traffickers and victims often share the same national or ethnic background.

129.s: Under BNS Section 124, the punishment for an acid attack and for its attempt is respectively:
o: Minimum ten years to life; five to seven years
Maximum three years; seven to ten years
Minimum seven years to life; five to seven years
Minimum ten years to life; one year
129.x: BNS Section 124 provides a minimum of ten years extending to life for acid attack, while attempt attracts five to seven years.
xa: Introduced by **CLA 2013**.
**RPwD Act 2016** treats acid-attack injuries as a disability.

129.s: Under the POSH Act, showing pornography is:
o: Outside the Act's definition of harassment
Harassment only if accompanied by physical contact
Itself a form of sexual harassment
Harassment only if a demand for sexual favours is also made
129.x: Showing pornography is itself listed as a form of sexual harassment, along with unwelcome contact and demands for sexual favours.
xa: **Sexually coloured remarks** are also covered.
Internal Committee: **1 external NGO member**; half the members women.
Employer's penalty for non-compliance: up to **₹50,000**.

129.s: Which of the following US Trafficking in Persons Report tiers is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Tier 1 – Fully meets the minimum standards
Tier 2 Watch List – Fully meets the minimum standards
Tier 2 – Not fully meeting standards but making significant efforts
129.x: Only Tier 1 fully meets the minimum standards; Tier 2 Watch List is a special watch-list category linked to Tier 2.
xa: The tiers come from the **US TIP Report**.
India has ratified the **UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime** + protocols.
**CLA 2013**: trafficking covers all forms, **irrespective of consent**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the definition of trafficking under the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013:
1. It covers forms such as sex trafficking, forced labour and organ removal.
2. It applies only where the victim did not consent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: Statement 1 is correct: the forms include sex trafficking, forced/bonded labour, child trafficking, slavery and organ removal. Statement 2 is wrong: the CLA 2013 definition covers all forms irrespective of consent. Hence 1 only (A); B, C and D are wrong.
129.tq: Consent is irrelevant under the CLA 2013 trafficking definition.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: forms include **sex trafficking**, **forced/bonded labour** and **organ removal** — correct.
Statement 2: the **CLA 2013** definition applies **irrespective of consent** — wrong.
xa: Other forms: **child trafficking**; **slavery and servitude**.
Bonded labour appears in agriculture, **brick kilns**, domestic work.
Trafficking now: **BNS 143** (IPC **370**).

129.s: Ujjawala, launched in 2007, covered:
o: Prosecution and conviction of traffickers only
Prevention, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of trafficking victims
Overseas employment and migration of women
129.x: Ujjawala covered prevention, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of trafficking victims.
xa: Ujjawala is now part of **Shakti Sadan** under **Mission Shakti (Samarthya)**.
AP has **26 Shakti Sadans** sheltering **950** women (AP SES 2025-26).
**Cri-MAC** gives real-time trafficking alerts across states.

129.s: Ujjawala is now part of which institutional framework under Mission Shakti?
o: Legal Services Authorities, through Women Helpline 181
129.x: Ujjawala is now part of Shakti Sadan under the Samarthya component of Mission Shakti, providing integrated relief homes for trafficked and destitute women.
129.tq: Distinguish the rehabilitation framework from emergency response, judicial and legal-aid mechanisms.
xs: Ujjawala is now part of **Shakti Sadan** under **Mission Shakti (Samarthya)** — option **(2)**.
**Cri-MAC** is an alert system; **Helpline 181** gives emergency help; **FTSCs** include **POCSO** courts — none absorbed Ujjawala.
xa: Shakti Sadans are **integrated relief homes** for trafficked and destitute women.
**SHe-Box 2.0** also falls under **Mission Shakti**.
AP: **26 Shakti Sadans**, **950** women sheltered.

129.s: What minimum compensation was directed for victims of acid attacks in Laxmi v. Union of India?
129.x: Victims of acid attacks were directed to receive compensation of at least ₹3 lakh.
129.tq: Use the statutory minimum rather than confusing it with a higher discretionary amount.
xs: **Laxmi v Union of India (2013)** directed compensation of **at least ₹3 lakh** — option **(3)**.
The case also regulated **acid sale** and ensured **free treatment**.
xa: Sale only against a **photo ID** + stated purpose; sellers keep a **sales register**.
**No sale to under-18s**.
Acid attack: **BNS s.124**, minimum **10 years**, extendable to life.

129.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the directions relating to the sale of acid in Laxmi v Union of India?
o: Maintenance of a register by sellers
No sale to persons below 18 years
Sale without recording the purchaser’s purpose
129.x: The purchaser’s stated purpose had to be recorded; sale without recording it was not permitted. The directions also included photo identification, a register and prohibition of sale to persons below 18 years.
129.tq: Find the option that reverses a specific regulatory safeguard.
xs: **Sale without recording the purpose** was not allowed — option **(4)**: acid is sold only against a **photo ID + stated purpose**.
**Sales register**, **photo ID** and **no sale to under-18s** were all directed.
xa: The **Laxmi** case also ordered at least **₹3 lakh** compensation.
Victims get **free treatment**.
Acid attack was added by **CLA 2013**.

129.s: A key reason for the continuing ineffectiveness of anti-dowry laws is:
o: Absence of any statutory prohibition of dowry
Poor enforcement, faulty FIRs and disguising cases as accidents or suicides
Excessive conviction rates in dowry cases
Exclusive jurisdiction of civil courts over dowry deaths
129.x: Poor enforcement, faulty FIRs and presenting dowry deaths as accidents or suicides are identified as major reasons for ineffectiveness.
xa: About **20** dowry deaths a day.
Dowry offences are **cognisable, non-bailable, non-compoundable**.
**s.8A**: **burden of proof on the accused**.

129.s: Under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, Protection Officers are appointed by the:
129.x: The State Government appoints them; in AP, DWCDA Project Directors and RDOs act as Protection Officers, while 55 NGOs are Service Providers.
xa: AP SES 2025-26: **51,581** cases addressed; **₹9 crore** relief to **2,207** victims.
APSES 2024-25: **47,734** petitions; **23,644** Domestic Incident Reports; **7,307** final orders.

129.s: Which of the following States are identified as leading in the incidence of dowry deaths?
o: Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan
Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand
129.x: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan are identified as the leading States in the cited assessment.
129.tq: Test the exact membership of a named group rather than a single State.
xs: **UP, Bihar, MP, Rajasthan** lead in dowry deaths — option **(2)**.
The southern, western and north-western groups are not named.
xa: About **20** dowry deaths a day, **6,000+** a year.
Laws are ineffective due to **poor enforcement** and **faulty FIRs**.
The **Dowry Prohibition Act** came into force on **1 July 1961**.

129.s: The guidelines laid down in Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997) were primarily concerned with:
o: Sexual harassment of women at the workplace
129.x: In Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan, the Supreme Court laid down guidelines concerning sexual harassment of women at the workplace.
129.tq: Use the case-name and subject association to distinguish closely related women-centric laws.
xs: **Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997)** laid down guidelines on **sexual harassment of women at the workplace** — option **(2)**.
They stood until a law was enacted, leading to the **POSH Act, 2013**.
xa: **Laxmi v Union of India (2013)**: acid sale regulation, compensation, free treatment.
POSH **Local Committee** is set up by the **District Officer**.
Complaint within **3 months**; inquiry within **90 days**.

129.s: Which information system shares real-time alerts on trafficking across States?
129.x: Cri-MAC is the Ministry of Home Affairs information technology initiative that shares real-time crime and trafficking alerts across States and supports inter-State coordination.
129.tq: Use the function-based distinction between an alert-sharing system, an emergency number and a global report.
xs: **Cri-MAC** gives **real-time alerts on trafficking across states** — option **(3)** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
**SHe-Box** handles workplace harassment complaints; **GLOTIP** is a UNODC report.
xa: Cri-MAC is an **MHA** IT initiative for inter-state coordination.
**GLOTIP 2016**: traffickers and victims often share the **same national or ethnic background**.
**Women Help Desks** in police stations; **Nirbhaya Fund** for safety projects.

129.s: The 1st joint meeting of both Houses of the Indian Parliament was held in connection with
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act came into force on –
129.x: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 was enacted by the Parliament of India to protect women from domestic violence. It came into force on 26th October, 2006.

129.s: Prevention, prohibition and Redressal Act 2013 addresses
o: sexual harassment of women at work place
129.x: sexual harassment of women at work place The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 addresses workplace sexual harassment. It mandates the constitution of Internal Complaints Committees in organisations to handle such complaints. The Act built upon the earlier Vishaka Guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court.

130.s:
Arrange the following crime heads in descending order of their share among crimes against women in 2023:
A. Assault with intent to outrage modesty
B. Cruelty by husband or relatives
C. Kidnapping and abduction
130.x: The descending order is cruelty by husband or relatives at 29.8%, kidnapping and abduction at 19.8%, and assault with intent to outrage modesty at 18.7%.
130.tq: Rank the items by the numerical values before reading the sequence options.
xs: Order **B, C, A** — option **(2)**.
**Cruelty by husband/relatives** (**29.8%**) → **kidnapping and abduction** (**19.8%**) → **assault to outrage modesty** (**18.7%**).
xa: Crimes against women, 2023: about **4.48** lakh — about **51** FIRs/hour, **81** rapes/day.
Top state by number (2023): **Uttar Pradesh**; by rate: **Telangana**.

130.s: Which of the following pairs (crime head — NCRB classification) is correctly matched?
o: Cruelty by husband or relatives — Special and Local Law
Kidnapping and abduction of women — Special and Local Law
Indecent representation of women — Special and Local Law
Protection of women from domestic violence — IPC/BNS head
130.x: Indecent representation and domestic violence (PWDVA) are SLL heads; cruelty by husband and kidnapping/abduction are IPC/BNS heads.
xa: **Assault to outrage modesty** and **insult to modesty** are IPC/BNS heads.
**ITPA 1956** and **Dowry Prohibition Act 1961** are SLL heads.

130.s: In the NCRB Crime in India 2024 data, which crime head was dominant, accounting for about 42% of crimes against women?
o: Assault with intent to outrage modesty
130.x: Cruelty by husband or relatives was the dominant head in NCRB 2024, at about 42% of crimes against women; it was also the top head in 2023 (29.8%). Kidnapping and abduction (19.8%) and assault on modesty (18.7%) ranked below it in 2023.
130.tq: Cruelty by husband = No.1 head (29.8% in 2023; ~42% in 2024).
xs: **Cruelty by husband or relatives** ≈ **42%** was dominant in **2024** — option **(2)**.
It also led in **2023** at **29.8%**, ahead of kidnapping (**19.8%**) and assault on modesty (**18.7%**).
xa: Crime in India **2024** was the first report with **BNS** data.
⚠ Don't confuse ≈ **42%** with the Opposition's claim of **+42.6% since 2013**.

130.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the causes of crimes against women?
o: Patriarchal norms and son preference reinforce unequal power relations.
Alcoholism and aggression among partners or parents may contribute to violence.
Dowry demands have no link with bride burning.
Some aggressors were themselves abused as children.
130.x: Dowry demands are listed as a cause that may escalate into bride burning.
xa: **Under-reporting**: stigma, fear, lack of awareness, economic dependence.
**Weak justice**: only **11.7%** of police are women.
Pendency over **90%** for crimes against women.

130.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a factor contributing to under-reporting of violence against women?
130.x: Stigma, fear, lack of awareness and economic dependence contribute to under-reporting. High conviction rates are not a cause of under-reporting; conviction rates are described as low.
130.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated relationship.
xs: **High conviction rates** are not a cause of under-reporting — option **(1)**; conviction rates are in fact **low**.
Under-reporting stems from **stigma, fear**, lack of awareness and **economic dependence**.
xa: **Marital rape** is not captured well in **NCRB** data.
Rape conviction rate: **22.7%** (2023).
⚠ Death penalty may **discourage reporting**.

130.s: Which State recorded the highest crime rate against women in 2023?
130.x: Telangana had the highest crime rate against women in 2023, whereas Uttar Pradesh had the highest number of cases.
130.tq: Use the number-versus-rate distinction as the key discriminator.
xs: **Telangana** had the highest **crime rate** against women in **2023** — option **(2)**.
**Uttar Pradesh** led by **number**; **Odisha** had the highest **violent-crime** rate (2024).
xa: ⚠ Number (UP) vs rate (Telangana).
**Telangana** also had the most **trafficking cases** (NCRB **2024**).
AP cases fell to **19,952** in **2024**.

130.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pendency of cases involving crimes against women — over 90%
130.x: The rape conviction rate in 2023 was 22.7%, not 42%. About 42% refers to the share of cruelty by husband as a dominant category in 2024.
130.tq: Identify the swapped percentage by matching each figure to its subject.
xs: **Rape conviction rate 2023 — 42%** is wrong — option **(2)**: it was **22.7%**.
≈ **42%** is the **cruelty by husband** share in **2024**.
**29,536** rape cases, **>90%** pendency and **4,41,534** crimes are correct.
xa: Conviction rate was **27-28%** in **2018-22**.
Opposition claim: **+42.6% since 2013**.

130.s: According to the Crime in India 2023 data, which State recorded the highest number of crimes against women?
130.x: Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest number of crimes against women in 2023. Telangana recorded the highest crime rate, which is a different measure.
130.tq: Separate absolute number from crime rate before selecting the State.
xs: **Uttar Pradesh** had the most crimes against women in **2023** — option **(2)**.
**Telangana** had the highest **rate**, a different measure.
xa: ⚠ Number vs rate is the common trap.
Dowry deaths are concentrated in **UP, Bihar, MP and Rajasthan**.

130.s: According to NCRB Crime in India 2024, fraud accounted for about what share of cybercrime cases?
130.x: Cybercrime crossed 1 lakh cases (1,01,928) for the first time, and 72.6% was fraud; sexual exploitation was only 3.1%.
xa: Reporting via **cybercrime.gov.in** and **1930**, under **I4C**.

130.s: Which group of States accounted for most dowry-death cases according to the cited data?
o: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan
Odisha, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala
West Bengal, Assam, Sikkim and Tripura
130.x: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan accounted for most dowry-death cases in the cited data.
130.tq: Recognise the complete State cluster rather than selecting a single high-population State.
xs: **UP, Bihar, MP and Rajasthan** account for most dowry-death cases — option **(1)** (**2026**).
The southern, western and north-eastern groups are not named in the data.
xa: Dowry demands escalate into **bride burning**.
Dowry deaths fall under **domestic** violence in the CDX classification.

130.s: What percentage of women were married before attaining 18 years according to NFHS-5?
130.x: NFHS-5 reported that 23.3% of women were married before the age of 18. NFHS-4 had recorded 26.8%.
130.tq: Distinguish the later NFHS-5 value from the earlier NFHS-4 value.
xs: **23.3%** of women married before **18** (NFHS-5) — option **(2)**.
**26.8%** was the **NFHS-4** figure; **18.7%** and **29.8%** are crime-head shares.
xa: Spousal violence: **32%** of ever-married women.
Physical violence: **29%** of women aged **18-49**.

130.s: According to NFHS-5, what proportion of ever-married women have faced spousal violence?
130.x: NFHS-5 reported that 32% of ever-married women had faced spousal violence.
130.tq: Distinguish the denominator—ever-married women—from the separate age-group indicator.
xs: **32%** of ever-married women faced **spousal violence** (NFHS-5) — option **(3)**.
**5.4%** is the marital rape figure (NFHS-4); **29%** is physical violence.
xa: Child marriage: **23.3%** (NFHS-5) vs **26.8%** (NFHS-4).
Cruelty by husband is the dominant NCRB head.

130.s: As per NFHS-4, what percentage of women reported marital rape?
130.x: NFHS-4 recorded 5.4%; the marital rape exception remains, and the Delhi High Court gave a split verdict on it.
xa: **Justice Verma Committee** recommended criminalising marital rape.
Critique: **rape law is not gender-neutral**.

130.s: According to Census 2011, what was the Child Sex Ratio of India and Andhra Pradesh respectively?
130.x: The Child Sex Ratio was 918 in India and 944 in Andhra Pradesh according to Census 2011.
130.tq: Separate closely related national and State figures before selecting the pair.
xs: Census **2011** Child Sex Ratio: **India 918**, **AP 944** — option **(1)**.
Option (3) reverses them; **996** and **943** are adult sex ratios.
xa: India's CSR fell from **927** (2001); provisional figure **914**.
Adult sex ratio: India **943**, AP **996**.
⚠ CSR **918** vs SRB **929** (NFHS-5) vs overall **1,020**.

130.s: As per NFHS-5, India's sex ratio at birth was:
130.x: NFHS-5 recorded a sex ratio at birth of 929, against an overall sex ratio of 1,020 (up from 991 in NFHS-4).
xa: Some notes give a child figure of **920**.
⚠ Census CSR **918** is a different measure.

130.s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched in 2015 primarily to address the decline in the:
130.x: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched in 2015 to address the declining Child Sex Ratio and related discrimination against girls. It now covers all districts.
130.tq: Link the scheme to its specifically stated demographic target.
xs: **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** (**2015**) targets the falling **Child Sex Ratio** — option **(2)**.
It now covers **all districts** (**2026**).
xa: India's CSR fell from **927** (2001) to **918** (2011).
About **3 million** girls go missing every year.

130.s:
Honour killings violate which of the following Articles?
1. Article 14
2. Article 19
3. Article 21
Which of the above is/are correct?
130.x: Honour killings violate Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21, protecting equality, freedoms and life and personal liberty.
xa: Prosecuted as murder: **BNS s.103**.
**Shakti Vahini (2018)**: preventive, remedial and punitive steps.
**Law Commission 242nd Report (2012)** drafted a law on it.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Palermo Protocol:
1. It supplements the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime.
2. India has ratified it.
3. It deals specifically with trafficking in persons, especially women and children.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: All three statements are correct. The Palermo Protocol supplements the UNTOC and addresses trafficking in persons, particularly women and children; India has ratified it.
130.tq: Check each statement against the instrument’s purpose, legal relationship and ratification status.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
The **Palermo Protocol (2000)** supplements **UNTOC**, ratified by India.
It targets trafficking in persons, **especially women and children**.
xa: **BNS s.143**: **victim's consent immaterial**.
**UNODC GLOTIP 2016**: victims and traffickers often share the **same background**.

130.s: Which provision of the Constitution of India prohibits traffic in human beings?
130.x: Article 23(1) prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour. Article 21A is the right to education, Article 24 bars child labour in hazardous employment, and Article 39(f) is a Directive Principle on protecting children from exploitation.
130.tq: Trafficking = Art. 23(1); BNS s.143.
xs: **Article 23(1)** is the constitutional provision against trafficking — option **(2)**.
Among the domestic legal framework it sits beside **BNS s.143** and the **ITPA 1956**.
xa: **BNS s.143**: **victim's consent immaterial**.
**Palermo Protocol (2000)** supplements **UNTOC**, ratified by India.
ITPA: prostitution **not a crime per se**; protective homes run by **States**.

130.s: The Supreme Court struck down the two-finger test in which case?
o: Lata Singh v State of Uttar Pradesh
Shakti Vahini v Union of India
130.x: The Supreme Court struck down the two-finger test in Lillu v State in 2013.
130.tq: Match the judicial directive with the correct case name.
xs: The **two-finger test** was struck down in **Lillu** (**2013**) — option **(1)**.
⚠ Some notes credit the **2013 Act** instead.
**Lata Singh**: adults' right to marry; **Laxmi**: acid sale; **Shakti Vahini**: khap interference.
xa: The CLA 2013 set rape investigation within **2 months**.
**ITSSO** tracks the **2-month** investigation of sexual offences.

130.s:
Which of the following are funded by the Nirbhaya Fund?
1. One Stop Centres
2. Women Helpline 181
3. ERSS 112
Which of the above is/are correct?
130.x: One Stop Centres, Women Helpline 181 and ERSS 112 are all funded by the Nirbhaya Fund.
xa: Also funded: **Mahila Police Volunteers**, **Safe City**, **FTSCs**.
181 plus 112 have helped over **9.9 million** women.

130.s: Safe City Projects include:
o: A national database of convicted sexual offenders
Free transport for women stranded at night in rural areas
CCTV and AI-based public safety measures for women in eight major cities
Only the construction of women’s prisons in every district
130.x: Safe City Projects use CCTV and artificial intelligence-based public-safety measures for women in eight major cities.
130.tq: Distinguish an urban technology project from databases, courts and transport schemes.
xs: **Safe City** projects: **CCTV and AI-based** public safety for women in **8 major cities** (**eight**) — option **(3)**.
The offender database is **NDSO**; the night pick-up scheme is AP's **Abhay** (Ongole).
xa: Funded by the **Nirbhaya Fund**.
⚠ **Abhay** = Ongole pick-up; **Abhayam** = Chittoor awareness.

130.s:
The Trishul committees in Andhra Pradesh pursue:
1. Zero drugs
2. Zero tolerance to atrocities against women
3. Zero road accidents
Which of the above is/are correct?
130.x: Trishul committees are state and district panels pursuing zero drugs, zero tolerance to atrocities against women and zero road accidents.
xa: Ordered by **CM Naidu**, with police response time of **30 minutes** (Sep **2026**).
Push for better **conviction rates**.

130.s: Which of the following was NOT credited for the further 4.4% decline in crimes against women in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Replacement of all police stations by women police stations
130.x: The decline was credited to Shakti Teams, Women's Safety Week rallies and Sexual Offender Sheets; there is no record of replacing all police stations.
xa: Chargesheets: **94.4%**.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding sex-ratio figures:
1. Andhra Pradesh has a higher adult sex ratio than India.
2. Andhra Pradesh has a higher child sex ratio than India.
3. India’s adult sex ratio and child sex ratio are 996 and 944, respectively.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Andhra Pradesh records 996 and 944 against India’s 943 and 918. Statement 3 reverses the State and national figures.
130.tq: Compare both rows of a paired State–India table before selecting the coded option.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
AP adult **996** > India **943**; AP CSR **944** > India **918**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **996 / 944** are **AP's** figures.
xa: India's CSR fell from **927** (2001).
NFHS-5 overall sex ratio: **1,020**.

130.s: The PCPNDT law prohibits:
o: Prenatal tests for detecting genetic abnormalities
Collection of census data on sex ratio
130.x: The PCPNDT law bans advertising sex determination, while it permits diagnostic procedures for genetic abnormalities.
xa: Diagnostics allowed only for **genetic abnormalities**.
Enacted in **1994**.

130.s: Honour killings are prosecuted as murder under which provision of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
130.x: Honour killings are prosecuted as murder under Section 103 of the BNS.
130.tq: Discriminate among nearby BNS section numbers by matching the offence category.
xs: Honour killings are prosecuted as murder under **BNS s.103** (**Section 103**) — option **(2)**.
**s.143**: trafficking; **s.124**: acid attack; **s.75**: sexual harassment.
xa: **Shakti Vahini (2018)**: khap interference illegal.
Rights violated: Arts **14, 15, 19, 21**.

130.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched under the 2013 criminal law amendments?
130.x: Disrobing was provided under Section 354B IPC, not Section 354E. Sections 354A, 354C and 354D relate respectively to sexual harassment, voyeurism and stalking.
130.tq: Find the wrong statutory pairing among closely numbered provisions.
xs: **Disrobing — 354E** is wrong — option **(3)**: disrobing is **354B**.
**354A** sexual harassment, **354C** voyeurism, **354D** stalking are correct.
xa: Disrobing is now **BNS 76**; sexual harassment **BNS 75**.
Voyeurism: **1-3 years**; stalking: up to **3 years**, **5** for a repeat.
Voyeurism → **BNS 77**; stalking → **BNS 78**.

130.s: Section 354C of the IPC deals with:
130.x: Section 354C covers voyeurism; 326A is acid attack, 326B attempt to acid attack and 354D stalking.
xa: Acid attack: min **10 yrs**-life; attempt **5-7 yrs**.

130.s: Which one of the following statements regarding rape under the 2013 amendment is correct?
o: Rape was confined to penile-vaginal penetration.
Penetration by objects or body parts and oral acts were included, with a minimum punishment of seven years.
The minimum punishment was reduced to five years.
Only consensual acts involving adults were covered.
130.x: The 2013 amendment widened the definition of rape to include penetration by objects or body parts and oral acts, while keeping the minimum punishment at seven years (it was raised to ten years in 2018).
130.tq: Test the expanded definition together with the associated minimum punishment.
xs: The **2013** amendment widened rape to **penetration by objects/body parts + oral acts**, keeping the minimum at **7 years** (seven) — option **(2)**.
The minimum was not cut to five; it was later raised to **10 years** (**2018**).
xa: **Age of consent** raised to **18**.
Rape investigation in **2 months**.

130.s: The 2013 provision on death for repeat rapists (IPC 376E) now corresponds to which section of the BNS?
130.x: IPC 376E is now BNS 71; acid attack is 124(1), sexual harassment 75 and stalking 78.
xa: **354C** voyeurism → **BNS 77**; **354B** disrobing → **BNS 76**.
Trafficking **370** → **BNS 143**.

130.s: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 was enacted in the context of which cases?
130.x: The 2018 amendment followed public concern arising from the Kathua and Unnao cases and was associated with the fast-track court response.
130.tq: Link the amendment to its immediate factual context without confusing it with the 2013 background.
xs: The **CLA 2018** came after the **Kathua and Unnao** cases (**2018**) — option **(3)**.
It led to the **FTSC scheme** (**2019**).
xa: Minimum for rape raised from **7** to **10 years**.
No **anticipatory bail** for rape of a girl **under 16**.

130.s: Which of the following punishment changes was made by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018?
o: Anticipatory bail became mandatory in rape cases involving minors.
All offences against children were made compoundable.
The minimum punishment for rape was reduced from seven to five years.
The minimum punishment for rape was raised from seven to ten years.
130.x: The 2018 amendment raised the minimum punishment for rape from seven years to ten years.
130.tq: Test the direction and magnitude of the statutory change rather than the offence name alone.
xs: The **CLA 2018** raised the **minimum for rape** from **7** to **10 years** — option **(4)**.
It did not reduce punishment or make offences compoundable; anticipatory bail was **barred**, not made mandatory.
xa: Timelines: **2 + 2 + 6** months.

130.s: Under the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018, rape of a girl below 16 years attracts a minimum punishment of:
130.x: The 2018 Act set a 20-year minimum for rape of a girl under 16; rape of a girl under 12 carries 20 years to life or death.
xa: No anticipatory bail for rape of a girl under **16**.
Context: **Kathua and Unnao**.

130.s: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the new offence relating to sexual intercourse by deceitful means, including a false promise of marriage or job and identity fraud, is contained in Section:
130.x: Section 69 of the BNS addresses sexual intercourse by deceitful means, including a false promise of marriage or job and identity fraud.
130.tq: Match the specific offence with its provision number, separating it from trafficking and minor-sale provisions.
xs: **BNS Section 69**: intercourse by **deceitful means**, **false promise of marriage** or job, incl. **identity fraud** — option **(1)**.
**98/99**: selling/buying minors; **143**: trafficking.
xa: BNS retained IPC provisions on **rape, stalking, voyeurism**.
Gang-rape age raised from **16 to 18**.

130.s: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita raises the age for the gang-rape provision from 16 to:
130.x: The BNS raises the age from 16 to 18 while retaining the IPC provisions on rape, stalking and voyeurism.
xa: New **s.69**: deceitful means / false promise of marriage.
**s.103**: honour killings prosecuted as murder.

130.s: Why does the Disha Act require the assent of the President of India?
o: It seeks to amend the Constitution.
It deals with subjects exclusively placed in the Union List.
It creates a new High Court in Andhra Pradesh.
Criminal law is included in the Concurrent List.
130.x: The Disha Act requires Presidential assent because criminal law falls in the Concurrent List. It has not come into force as passed.
130.tq: Ask which constitutional distribution of legislative power explains the requirement.
xs: Disha needs **President's assent** because **criminal law is in the Concurrent List** — option **(4)**.
It does not amend the Constitution, touch the Union List, or create a High Court.
xa: So it is **not in force as passed**.
Passed in **December 2019**.
**Disha police stations**: **18** dedicated women's police stations.

130.s: Under the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act, 1994, prenatal diagnostic techniques are permitted primarily for detecting:
o: The future educational needs of the child
The economic status of the family
The sex of the foetus for parental choice
130.x: The PCPNDT Act permits diagnostic procedures for detecting genetic abnormalities, while prohibiting sex selection and prenatal sex determination.
130.tq: Identify the legally permitted purpose rather than the prohibited use of diagnosis.
xs: The **PCPNDT Act 1994** allows diagnostics only for **genetic abnormalities** — option **(2)**.
Determining the foetus's **sex** for parental choice is banned.
xa: It bans **sex selection** and **pre-natal sex determination**.
It penalises **advertising** and **disclosing the sex** of the foetus.

130.s: Under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956, which of the following is correct?
o: Prostitution itself is treated as a crime in every circumstance.
Only trafficking of children is punishable.
Brothel-keeping, pimping, soliciting and living on the earnings of prostitution are punishable acts.
The Act abolishes protective homes maintained by State Governments.
130.x: The ITPA does not treat prostitution per se as a crime, but penalises activities such as brothel-keeping, pimping, soliciting and living on prostitution earnings.
130.tq: Use the distinction between the activity itself and associated exploitative activities.
xs: ITPA punishes **brothel-keeping, pimping, soliciting** and **living on earnings** — option **(3)**.
Prostitution is **not a crime per se**; protective homes are run **by States**.
xa: It is a **1956** law.
**BNS s.143** defines trafficking.

130.s:
Which of the following was recommended by the Justice J.S. Verma Committee but not adopted in the same form by Parliament?
1. Criminalisation of marital rape
2. No death penalty for rape
3. Keeping the age of consent at 16 years
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: The Verma Committee recommended criminalising marital rape, opposed the death penalty for rape and recommended retaining the age of consent at 16. Parliament raised the age of consent to 18 years.
130.tq: Separate committee recommendations from the final legislative choices.
xs: All three — option **(4)**.
The **Verma Committee** urged **criminalising marital rape**, **no death penalty for rape**, and **age of consent at 16**.
Parliament instead chose **18**; the **marital rape exception** remains.
xa: Members: **Justice J.S. Verma**, **Justice Leila Seth**, **Gopal Subramanium**.
Report in Jan **2013**; it also urged **police reforms**.

130.s: Which of the following was NOT a principal policy outcome associated with the December 2012 Nirbhaya case?
130.x: The principal listed outcomes were the Justice Verma Committee, the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 2013, the Nirbhaya Fund and the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015. The BNS was not among those immediate policy outcomes.
130.tq: Use the event’s immediate policy timeline to eliminate a later legal enactment.
xs: The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023** was not an outcome of the Nirbhaya case — option **(1)**.
Outcomes: **Justice Verma Committee**, **CLA 2013**, **Nirbhaya Fund**, **Juvenile Justice Act 2015**.
xa: The Nirbhaya Fund is a **non-lapsable corpus**.
The case: **Delhi, December 2012** gang rape and murder.

130.s: The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 permits 16–18-year-olds to be tried as adults for:
130.x: The JJ Act, 2015 permits 16–18-year-olds to be tried as adults for heinous crimes, subject to the statutory process.
xa: It was an outcome of the **Nirbhaya** case.
⚠ **BNS** raised the gang-rape age from **16 to 18**.

130.s: The Nirbhaya Fund was established in:
130.x: The Nirbhaya Fund was established in 2013 as a dedicated corpus for projects related to women’s safety.
130.tq: Link the fund’s establishment year with its purpose, not with a later scheme.
xs: The **Nirbhaya Fund** dates from **2013** — option **(2)**, created in the **Union Budget**.
It followed the **2012** Delhi case; **2018** and **2019** are later measures.
xa: It is a **dedicated corpus** for women's-safety projects.
It funds **Safe City**, **FTSCs**, **ERSS**.

130.s:
Assertion (A): SHe-Box helps streamline redressal under the POSH Act.
Reason (R): SHe-Box is a Sexual Harassment electronic Box.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
130.x: Both are true: SHe-Box is the 'Sexual Harassment electronic Box', an online portal for complaints under the POSH Act, which is how it speeds redressal. R explains A.
130.tq: Recall what SHe-Box does.
n: SHe-Box stands for Sexual Harassment electronic Box. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 79-81]
The mechanism for addressing crimes against women includes streamlined redressal under the POSH Act. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #36 · pp 79-81]
xs: Both A and R are true and **R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
**SHe-Box** is the **Sexual Harassment electronic Box**.
Being an electronic complaints box, it enables **streamlined redressal** under the **POSH Act**.
xa: **SHe-Box 2.0** (MWCD) is a single window for workplace harassment complaints in **22** languages.
**NDSO** = **National Database on Sexual Offenders**.
Nirbhaya Fund projects: **Fast Track Special Courts**, **Cyber Forensic Labs**.

130.s: The Supreme Court judgment in Shakti Vahini v Union of India (2018) dealt primarily with:
o: interference by khaps in marriages of consenting adults
the two-finger test in rape cases
130.x: Shakti Vahini addressed honour crimes and held that khap interference in marriages of consenting adults is illegal, while prescribing preventive, remedial and punitive measures.
130.tq: Match the case with its subject matter and distinguish it from other rights-related judgments.
xs: **Shakti Vahini v UOI (2018)** held **khap** interference in **adult marriages** illegal — option **(3)**.
It prescribed **preventive, remedial and punitive** steps.
Acid sale was the **Laxmi** case; the two-finger test was struck down in **Lillu**.
xa: **Lata Singh (2006)**: adults' right to marry.
Honour killings violate Arts **14, 15, 19, 21**.
Honour killings are prosecuted as murder under **BNS s.103**.

130.s: The Law Commission's 242nd Report (2012) proposed a draft law concerning:
o: Interference in matrimonial alliances in the name of honour
130.x: The 242nd Report proposed a draft law against interference in matrimonial alliances in the name of honour.
xa: **Shakti Vahini (2018)**: khap interference illegal.
Honour killings violate Arts **14, 15, 19, 21**.
**Lata Singh (2006)**: adults' right to marry.

130.s: Under Section 143 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which principle applies to trafficking?
o: Consent is relevant only if the trafficking is inter-State.
The victim’s consent is always a complete defence.
Consent matters only when the victim is an adult male.
130.x: Section 143 of the BNS treats the victim’s consent as immaterial in determining the offence of trafficking.
130.tq: Discriminate between consent as a defence and the statutory rule that consent is immaterial.
xs: Under **BNS s.143**, the **victim's consent is immaterial** — option **(4)**.
No consent-based exception applies.

**Palermo Protocol (2000)** supplements **UNTOC**.

130.s: Anti-Human Trafficking Units (AHTUs) are:

Central units of I4C issuing cyber-trafficking alerts
District-level task forces funded by MHA for trafficking intelligence, rescue and prosecution

130.s: The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and the 1930 helpline function under which organisation for reporting cybercrime?
o: CERT-In under the Ministry of Communications
Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre under the Ministry of Home Affairs

National Crime Records Bureau under the Ministry of Law and Justice

xs: The **National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal** and the **1930** helpline are under the MHA's **I4C** (**Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre**) — option **(2)**.
The portal is built especially for crimes against women and children (**CSAM**, non-consensual imagery).
xa: Cybercrime crossed **1 lakh** in **2024**: **1,01,928** cases.
Against women: rose **239%** between **2017 and 2022**.

130.s:
With reference to the Trafficking of Persons Bill, 2018, consider the following statements:

2. It subsequently lapsed.
3. It proposed the National Investigation Agency as the national investigating agency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: The 2018 Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha and later lapsed. The proposal to designate the NIA as the national investigating agency belonged to the 2021 draft Bill.
130.tq: Separate closely related legislative proposals by year and avoid transferring a feature from one draft to another.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
The **2018 Bill** passed the **Lok Sabha** and then **lapsed**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **NIA** proposal was in the **2021 draft Bill**.
xa: The 2018 Bill added **aggravated trafficking**, **aiding trafficking**.
**Cri-MAC** shares real-time trafficking alerts.

130.s:
With reference to Mission Shakti:

130.s:

3. Women Helpline 181 is being replaced by the Witness Protection Scheme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: ERSS works on the single number 112 (asked in APPSC 2018), and the Nirbhaya Fund is a non-lapsable corpus set up after the 2012 case. Statement 3 is wrong: 181 is being integrated with ERSS-112, not replaced by the Witness Protection Scheme.
130.tq: ERSS = 112; Nirbhaya Fund = non-lapsable corpus (2013).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**ERSS** uses the single number **112** (APPSC **2018**); the **Nirbhaya Fund** is a **non-lapsable corpus** created after the **2012** case.
Statement 3 is wrong: **181** is being **integrated with ERSS-112**.
xa: **Witness Protection Scheme 2018** is enforced under **Art. 141**.
181 + 112 helped over **9.9 million** women.

130.s:
Assertion (A): CCTNS links police stations across the country.
Reason (R): NDSO is a national database of convicted sexual offenders.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
130.x: Both are correct descriptions of separate systems; the NDSO database does not explain how CCTNS links police stations.
xa: ⚠ **ITSSO** = tracks investigation; **NDSO** = convicted offenders.
CCTNS is the basis of AP's **AI4AP** pilot in Chittoor, Guntur and Annamayya.

130.s: The Fast Track Special Courts (FTSC) scheme is a centrally sponsored scheme funded from the Nirbhaya Fund and primarily deals with:

It is a **centrally sponsored scheme** funded by the **Nirbhaya Fund**.
xa: **743 FTSCs** incl. **394 exclusive POCSO** courts (**31 Jul 2025**).
**773 FTSCs** functioning (**2026**).

130.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: NDSO tracks convicted and charge-sheeted sexual offenders nationwide.
ITSSO ensures mandatory two-month investigation completion in rape cases.
ITSSO is a citizen portal for reporting online financial fraud.
ITSSO provides real-time monitoring of investigations in sexual-offence cases.
130.x: Option C is incorrect: ITSSO is a police tool for tracking sexual-offence investigations against the two-month deadline. Citizens report financial fraud on the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal.
130.tq: Discriminate NCRB from BPR&D.
n: NDSO is associated with the Ministry of Home Affairs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
NDSO is associated with the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
NDSO tracks convicted sexual offenders. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
NDSO tracks charge-sheeted sexual offenders. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
NDSO tracks sexual offenders nationwide. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]

ITSSO is associated with the Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPR&D). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
ITSSO provides real-time monitoring of investigations. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
ITSSO ensures mandatory completion of rape-case investigations within two months. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
ITSSO addresses crimes against women. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
xs: The incorrect statement is that **ITSSO** is a **citizen portal for financial fraud** — option **(3)**.
**ITSSO** gives **real-time monitoring** of sexual-offence investigations and ensures completion within **two months**.
**NDSO** tracks **convicted and charge-sheeted sexual offenders nationwide**.
xa: Citizens report **financial fraud** on the **National Cybercrime Reporting Portal** (**cybercrime.gov.in**, **I4C**).
ITSSO is linked to **BPR&D**; NDSO to **NCRB** (**2018**).
⚠ **ITSSO** = tracks investigation; **NDSO** = database of offenders.

130.s: The Disha Bill of Andhra Pradesh was introduced primarily as a response to:
130.x: The Disha Bill was Andhra Pradesh’s legislative response to the 2019 Hyderabad veterinarian rape-murder case.

xs: The **AP Disha Bill** answered the **2019 Hyderabad veterinarian rape-murder** — option **(2)**.
The **2012 Delhi** case led to the **CLA 2013**; **Kathua** (**2018**) to the **CLA 2018**.
xa: Passed by the AP Assembly in **December 2019** (APPSC **2018**).
**Death sentence** for rape and gang rape.
Verdict within **21 days**.

130.s: Under the Disha Act, the prescribed time structure for investigation and trial of rape cases is:
o: Investigation in 14 days and trial in 7 days
Investigation in 14 days and trial in 21 days
Investigation in 7 days and trial in 14 days
Investigation in 21 days and trial in 14 days
130.x: The Disha Act specifies seven days for investigation and fourteen days for trial, making a total of twenty-one days.
130.tq: Separate the two components of the total time limit.
xs: **Investigation 7 days + trial 14 days** = verdict in **21 days** — option **(3)**.
The other options swap or inflate these periods.
xa: ⚠ Disha model (**21-day** verdict) vs Nirbhaya Act (**2-month** probe).
CLA 2018: investigation **2 months** + trial **2 months** + appeals **6 months**.
Disha mandates **forensic evidence**.

xs: The first women's court was set up in **West Bengal** — option **(3)** (APPSC-GS **2019**).

xs: The first all-women police station: **Kozhikode, Kerala (1973)** — option **(3)**.

xa: First women's court: **West Bengal**.

131.s: Which Articles of the Constitution provide for equal franchise in the context of women voters?
131.x: Articles 325 and 326 provide the constitutional basis for equal electoral franchise.
131.tq: Distinguish voting rights provisions from provisions concerning eligibility to contest elections.
xs: **Articles 325 and 326** provide **equal franchise** for women voters — option **(1)** is correct.
**Articles 84 and 173** only allow women to **contest** elections to Parliament and State Legislatures.
**Articles 330A and 332A** are the women's seat quotas inserted by the **106th Amendment**.
xa: The reservation Bill was needed because women were historically **under-represented in legislatures**.
**Art. 330A** = Lok Sabha quota; **Art. 332A** = State Assemblies quota.

131.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023?
o: It provides one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha.
It provides one-third reservation in State Legislative Assemblies.
It includes one-third of the seats reserved for SCs and STs.
It provides reservation for women in the Rajya Sabha.
131.x: The Act does not provide reservation in the Rajya Sabha.
xa: **No OBC/BC sub-quota**.
Duration **15 years**, extendable by Parliament.

131.s: Which Article inserted by the 106th Amendment provides the women's quota in the Lok Sabha?
131.x: Article 330A covers the Lok Sabha; 332A the State Assemblies, 239AA(2)(ba) the Delhi Assembly and 334A commencement and duration.
xa: **Art. 334A** also provides **rotation** after each delimitation.
⚠ **Art. 368** = the special majority that the **131st Bill** missed.
The Act is the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam**, passed as the **128th Amendment Bill**.

131.s: Which State is exempt from reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes in Panchayats because it has no Scheduled Caste population?
131.x: Arunachal Pradesh is exempt from SC reservation because it has no Scheduled Caste population.
131.tq: Test the specific constitutional exception rather than the general reservation rule.
xs: **Arunachal Pradesh** is exempt because it has **no SC population** — option **(4)** is correct.
Elsewhere, SC/ST seats are reserved at every level **in proportion to population**.
**Bihar** is known instead as the first State with **50%** for women in local bodies (**2006**).
xa: **73rd Amendment** in force: **24 April 1993**.
**243D(2)**: one-third of SC/ST seats go to **SC/ST women**.
SC/ST reservation ends with the **Art. 334** period, now **2030** (**104th Amendment**).

131.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the duration of reservations in local bodies?
o: Women's reservation has no such sunset provision, whereas SC/ST reservation is linked to the Article 334 period.
All local-body reservations are permanently fixed by the 73rd Amendment.
SC/ST reservation has no constitutional time limit, but women's reservation ends in 2030.
Women's reservation and SC/ST reservation both automatically end in 2030.
131.x: Women's reservation in local bodies has no equivalent sunset provision. SC/ST reservation is linked to Article 334, whose current period extends to 2030 under the 104th Amendment.
131.tq: Compare the duration clauses instead of assuming that all reservation categories have the same limit.
xs: **Women's reservation has no sunset**, whereas **SC/ST reservation** ends with the **Art. 334** period — option **(1)** is correct.
The SC/ST period now runs to **2030** under the **104th Amendment** (via **Art. 243D(5)**).
So neither "both end in 2030" nor "women's ends in 2030" is right.
xa: The women's one-third is **compulsory** and a **floor, not a ceiling**.
By contrast, the **106th Amendment** quota lasts **15 years**, extendable by Parliament.
Reserved seats and chairperson offices rotate.

131.s: Under Article 243D(3) of the Constitution, the minimum reservation for women in seats of Panchayats is:
o: One-half of the total seats, excluding SC/ST seats
One-third of the total seats, including one-third of the seats reserved for SCs and STs
131.x: Article 243D(3) provides that not less than one-third of the total seats in every Panchayat, including one-third of the seats reserved for SCs and STs, shall be reserved for women.
131.tq: Test the constitutional minimum against the higher reservation adopted by some States.
xs: **Art. 243D(3)**: not less than **one-third** of total seats, **including one-third of SC/ST seats** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is not one-half or one-fourth, and it is not limited to unreserved seats.
**243D(2)**: one-third of the SC/ST seats go to **SC/ST women**.
xa: **243D(4)** = one-third of **chairperson offices** for women.
**19 States/UTs** give women **50%** (**2026**); **Bihar** first (**2006**).
The same rule for municipalities is **Art. 243T(3)**.

131.s: Bokkasam Palem, located in Srikalahasti mandal of Tirupati, is associated with which achievement?
o: It received the first national award for tribal self-governance
It became the first girls’ Panchayat in India
It was ranked first nationally among women-friendly Panchayats
It was the first Panchayat to introduce a BC-women sub-quota
131.x: Bokkasam Palem in Srikalahasti mandal of Tirupati ranked first nationally among women-friendly Panchayats under the Deendayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas Awards.
131.tq: Link the place, administrative location and award-related achievement precisely.
xs: **Bokkasam Palem** (Srikalahasti mandal, Tirupati) ranked **1st nationally** among **women-friendly panchayats** — option **(3)** is correct.
The ranking was under the **Deendayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas Awards, 2026**.
India's first girls' panchayat (**Balika Panchayat**) was in **Kutch, Gujarat**, not here.
xa: MoPR's **Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats**: at least **one per district**, with **SHG alignment**.
**AP** gives **50%** reservation to women in local bodies.
First woman **AP Assembly Speaker**: **Pratibha Bharati** (**2004**, undivided AP).

131.s: Mahila Sabha is best described as:
o: A meeting of women officers of the Election Commission
A statutory committee of the National Commission for Women
A meeting of women members of Parliament before a joint sitting
A women-only meeting held before the Gram Sabha
131.x: Mahila Sabha refers to a women-only meeting conducted before the Gram Sabha, as exemplified in Maharashtra.
131.tq: Discriminate between a grassroots women-only forum and statutory or parliamentary bodies.
xs: **Mahila Sabha** is a **women-only meeting held before the Gram Sabha** — option **(4)** is correct.
It brings **women's issues to the Gram Sabha**; **Maharashtra** is an example.
It is not an ECI body, an NCW committee or a meeting of MPs.
xa: **Balika Panchayat** (Kutch, Gujarat, **June 2022**) trains girls in local governance.
**NCW** is a statutory body (**1992**) under the **NCW Act 1990**.
**ECI's SVEEP** targets women voters.

131.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan:

2. It includes legal-awareness and gender-justice modules.
3. It includes modules on gender-based violence.

131.x: The Abhiyan provides leadership, legal-awareness and gender-justice training, including modules on gender-based violence, for Women Elected Representatives.
131.tq: Check whether all listed components belong to the same capacity-building programme.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: it gives **leadership** training to **Women Elected Representatives**.
Statement 2: it includes **legal-awareness** and **gender-justice** training.
Statement 3: it includes modules on **gender-based violence**.
xa: It is run by the **Ministry of Panchayati Raj**.

131.s: Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats are envisaged at the rate of at least one per:
131.x: At least one per district is envisaged, providing safe spaces and gender-responsive governance aligned with SHGs.
xa: They are an initiative of the **Ministry of Panchayati Raj**.
**Bokkasam Palem** (Tirupati) ranked **1st nationally** among women-friendly panchayats.
Nearly **10 crore women** are in over **90 lakh SHGs**.

131.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The 106th Constitutional Amendment extends women’s reservation to the Lok Sabha.
The 106th Constitutional Amendment extends women’s reservation to the Legislative Assembly of NCT of Delhi.
The 106th Constitutional Amendment provides women’s reservation in the Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Councils.
The 106th Constitutional Amendment extends women’s reservation to State Legislative Assemblies.
131.x: Option C is incorrect: the 106th Amendment excludes the Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils. It covers the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly.
131.tq: Remember that the Upper Houses are excluded.
n: The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act extends not less than one-third reservation for women to the Lok Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act extends not less than one-third reservation for women to State Legislative Assemblies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]

The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act extends not less than one-third reservation for women to the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act has no provision for the Rajya Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act has no provision for State Legislative Councils. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
The Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Councils are strictly excluded from the scope of the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act applies to the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, and the Delhi Legislative Assembly. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act does not provide 33% reservation for women in the Rajya Sabha. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act does not provide 33% reservation for women in State Legislative Councils. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the 106th Amendment gives reservation in the **Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Councils** — option **(3)**; these are **strictly excluded**.

xa: The quota is **one-third**, including one-third of **SC/ST reserved** seats.

⚠ **128th** Bill = **106th** Amendment Act; the **108th** Bill only passed the Rajya Sabha (**2010**).

131.s: Which of the following pairs (body — Article on women's reservation) is correctly matched?

Article 330A governs women's reservation in the House of the People. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]

131.s:
