Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
131.x: Statement 1 is true (Delhi has no ST reservation); statement 2 is false because Delhi comes under Article 239AA(2)(ba), not 332A.
n: Article 332A governs women's reservation in State Legislative Assemblies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
Article 239AA(2)(ba) governs women's reservation in the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
Women's reservation in the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi covers directly elected seats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
Women's reservation in the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi covers Scheduled Caste-reserved seats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
xa: **Art. 330A** covers the **Lok Sabha**.

131.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to women's reservation in chronological order:
A. Constitution (106th Amendment) Act enacted
B. 108th Amendment Bill passed by the Rajya Sabha
C. 81st Amendment Bill introduced
D. 108th Amendment Bill lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha
131.x: The 81st Amendment Bill was introduced in 1996, the 108th Bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2010, it lapsed in 2014, and the 106th Amendment was enacted in 2023.
131.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest Bill and the final enacted amendment.
xs: Correct order is **C, B, D, A** — option **(1)**.
C: **81st Amendment Bill** introduced in **1996** (Deve Gowda govt).
B: **108th Amendment Bill** passed by the **Rajya Sabha** on **9 March 2010**.
D: the 108th Bill **lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha** in **2014**; A: **106th Amendment** enacted in **2023**.
xa: The 81st Bill **lapsed with the 11th Lok Sabha**; it was reintroduced in **1998, 1999, 2002-03** (Vajpayee govts) and lapsed again.
The 108th Bill was **introduced in the Rajya Sabha** in **2008**.
The 2023 measure was the **128th Amendment Bill**, passed on **21 Sept 2023**.

131.s: Which of the following correctly states the relationship between the 2023 Women's Reservation Bill and the Constitution?
o: The 108th Amendment Bill was enacted as the 106th Amendment Act in 2023.
The 106th Amendment Bill was enacted as the 128th Amendment Act.
The 81st Amendment Bill was revived and enacted without modification.
The 128th Amendment Bill was enacted as the 106th Amendment Act.
131.x: The 2023 Bill was introduced as the 128th Amendment Bill and was enacted as the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023.
131.tq: Keep the Bill number and enacted Amendment number distinct.
xs: The **128th Amendment Bill** was enacted as the **106th Amendment Act** — option **(4)** is correct.
It passed on **21 Sept 2023** and got assent in **2023**.
The **108th** Bill (**2008**) only passed the Rajya Sabha and **lapsed** in **2014**; the **81st** Bill (**1996**) lapsed with the 11th Lok Sabha.
xa: The 106th Amendment is called the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam**.
Articles inserted: **330A** (Lok Sabha), **332A** (State Assemblies), **239AA(2)(ba)** (Delhi), **334A** (commencement and duration).
Commencement only after the **first Census after the Act** and the delimitation that follows.

131.s: From 17 April 2026, the women's reservation under the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act was stated to be in force for the Assemblies of:
131.x: The reservation was stated to be in force for the Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry Assemblies from 17 April 2026.
131.tq: Match the effective date with the exact pair of Assemblies named.
xs: The quota was in force for the **J&K and Puducherry** Assemblies from **17 April 2026** — option **(2)** is correct.
For the Delhi Assembly the quota comes through **Art. 239AA(2)(ba)**, but the notes list only **J&K and Puducherry** as in force.
xa: Nationally, commencement waits for the **2027 Census** and delimitation (not before **2034**).
The same day, **17 April 2026**, the **131st Amendment Bill** was defeated in the Lok Sabha.
The quota includes **one-third of SC/ST reserved seats**.

131.s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 was defeated in the Lok Sabha on 17 April 2026 because:
o: It got fewer votes in favour than against
It got 298 votes in favour against 230, short of the 352 needed for the Article 368 special majority
The Rajya Sabha had rejected it first
It needed ratification by half the States, which was refused
131.x: It won a simple majority (298 for, 230 against, of 528 present and voting) but fell short of the 352 votes needed for the special majority under Article 368. It was not defeated on a simple vote, the Rajya Sabha did not vote first, and State ratification was not the reason.
131.tq: 131st Bill: 298-230, needed 352 (Art 368) -> defeated 17 Apr 2026.
xs: It got **298 for and 230 against**, short of the **352** needed for the **Art. 368** special majority — option **(2)** is correct.
It actually had **more votes in favour** than against, so option (1) is wrong.
**528** members were present and voting.
xa: ⚠ **Art. 368** = special majority; **Art. 334A** = rotation and duration of the 106th quota.
The Bill aimed at a quota **from 2029** with a Lok Sabha of **850** (**815** States, **35** UTs).
Defeated on **17 April 2026**.

131.s: Under Article 334A, the reservation of seats for women is to be rotated:
o: Every five years irrespective of delimitation
131.x: Article 334A provides for rotation of the reserved seats after each delimitation.
131.tq: Distinguish the constitutional trigger for rotation from the ordinary election cycle.
xs: Under **Art. 334A**, reserved seats **rotate after each delimitation** — option **(4)** is correct.
Rotation is tied to delimitation, not to every general election, a fixed five-year cycle or a referendum.
**Art. 334A** also covers the **commencement and duration** of the quota.
xa: Duration: **15 years**, **extendable by Parliament**.
⚠ **Art. 334A** = rotation + duration of the 106th quota; **Art. 368** = the special majority the **131st Bill** missed.
In panchayats, reserved seats and chairperson offices are also allotted **by rotation**.

131.s: Women's reservation under the 106th Amendment will commence after delimitation based on the:
131.x: The reservation commences only after delimitation based on the first Census after the Act, i.e. the 2027 Census.
xa: Seats **rotate** after each delimitation (**Art. 334A**).
Duration: **15 years**, extendable by Parliament.
Critics see bundling the quota with delimitation as **political cover** for reallocating seats.

131.s: Which of the following is NOT provided under the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023?
o: An OBC or BC sub-quota within the women's reservation
One-third reservation in the Delhi Legislative Assembly
Rotation of reserved seats after delimitation
One-third reservation in State Legislative Assemblies
131.x: The Act does not provide an OBC or BC sub-quota. It provides reservation in the specified legislatures and provides for rotation after delimitation.
131.tq: Look for the specific exclusion among otherwise correct features of the amendment.
xs: The Act provides **no OBC/BC sub-quota** — option **(1)** is the one NOT provided.
It does provide one-third in the **Delhi Assembly** (**Art. 239AA(2)(ba)**) and in **State Assemblies** (**Art. 332A**).
It does provide **rotation** after each delimitation (**Art. 334A**).
xa: It also excludes the **Rajya Sabha** and **State Legislative Councils**.
**AP angle:** AP Congress and BC groups demand a **BC-women sub-quota**.
In local bodies, reservation for **backward classes** is **voluntary** for States.

131.s: The reservation for women under the 106th Amendment is provided for:
131.x: The reservation is provided for 15 years and may be extended by Parliament.
xa: Seats **rotate** after each delimitation.
⚠ In panchayats, **SC/ST reservation** ends with the **Art. 334** period (**2030**), but **women's reservation has no such sunset**.
Commencement only after the **next Census and delimitation**.

131.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the proposed 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2026 is correct?
o: It proposed increasing the Lok Sabha strength from 550 to 850 on the basis of the 2011 Census.
It introduced the GST Council into Article 279A.
It restored the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha.
It proposed increasing the Rajya Sabha strength from 250 to 550 on the basis of the 2021 Census.
131.x: The 131st Amendment Bill, 2026, sought to expand the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850 seats using the 2011 Census as the basis for delimitation.
131.tq: Use the paired numerical figures and the stated Census basis to identify the proposal.
xs: The **131st Bill** proposed raising the **Lok Sabha** maximum from **550 to 850**, delimitation on the **2011 Census** — option **(1)** is correct.
Of the **850**, **815** seats were for States and **35** for UTs.
Its aim was to **fast-track the women's quota from 2029**.
xa: It was **defeated** on **17 Apr 2026** in the special session of **16-18 April**.
Vote: **298 for, 230 against** of **528** present and voting; **352** needed under **Art. 368**.
Expansion would take southern seats from **129** to **195**, keeping their **23.8%** share.

131.s: The principal legal shield against atrocities and discrimination targeting Dalit and tribal communities is:
o: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976
Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 and Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976
SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
131.x: The safeguards identified are the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.
xa: SC/ST seats in panchayats are reserved **in proportion to population**.
SC/ST reservation ends with the **Art. 334** period, now **2030** (**104th Amendment**).

131.s: Women’s groups demanded the removal of which condition attached to women’s legislative reservation?
o: The condition of reservation only in urban local bodies
The condition of approval by all State Legislatures
The condition of prior approval by the Election Commission
131.x: Women’s groups demanded removal of the Census-delimitation condition, including during the Monsoon Session.
131.tq: Identify the specific procedural condition under debate rather than a general approval requirement.
xs: Women's groups demand removing the **Census-delimitation condition** — option **(1)** is correct.
The demand is for the **Monsoon Session**, after the **131st Bill** was defeated (Apr **2026**).
xa: Under current law the quota waits for the **2027 Census** and is not enforceable before **2034**.
The 131st Bill got **298** for, **230** against — short of **352**.
Critics call bundling with delimitation **political cover** for reallocating seats.

131.s:
Assertion (A): The reservation introduced by the 106th Constitutional Amendment does not come into force immediately.
Reason (R): It takes effect only after delimitation following publication of the relevant figures of the first decennial Census conducted after the amendment.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
131.x: Both are true: the reservation does not start at once because Article 334A ties it to the delimitation after the next census. R explains A.
131.tq: Recall the census and delimitation precondition.
n: Article 334A contains the pre-condition governing the commencement of women's reservation under the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
Women's reservation under Article 334A does not come into force immediately. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
Women's reservation under Article 334A takes effect only after a delimitation exercise. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]

The delimitation exercise must follow the publication of the relevant figures of the first decennial Census conducted after the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
xs: Both A and R are true and **R is the correct explanation of A** — option **(1)**.
Under **Article 334A**, the quota does **not** come into force **immediately**.
It takes effect only **after delimitation** following the **first Census conducted after the Act**.
xa: Linked to the **2027 Census**, it is not enforceable before **2034** under current law.
Duration: an initial **15 years**, extendable by **Parliament** by law.
Reserved seats **rotate** after **every subsequent delimitation**.

131.s: The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023 is also known as:
131.x: The 106th Amendment Act, 2023, the women's reservation law, is called the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam.
131.tq: Recall the 106th Amendment's name.
n: The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act was enacted in 2023. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act is known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
xs: The **106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023** is the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam** — option **(4)**.
It extends **not less than one-third** reservation to the **Lok Sabha**, **State Assemblies** and the **Delhi** Assembly.
xa: It passed as the **128th Amendment Bill** (**21 Sept 2023**).
Local-body reservation came earlier via the **73rd and 74th Amendments, 1992**.
The **131st Amendment Bill, 2026** to fast-track it was **defeated** (**17 Apr 2026**).

131.s:
With reference to seats reserved for SCs and STs:
1. The mandatory sub-quota for SC/ST women within these seats is 50%.
2. The mandatory sub-quota for SC/ST women within these seats is one-third.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
131.x: Within SC/ST reserved seats, one-third must go to SC/ST women, not 50%.
n: The mandatory sub-quota for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe women within Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe reserved seats is one-third. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
The mandatory sub-quota for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe women within Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe reserved seats is not 50%. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
xa: SC/ST seats are reserved at every level **in proportion to population**.
SC/ST reservation ends with the **Art. 334** period (**2030**), but women's reservation has **no sunset**.
Backward-class reservation in local bodies is **voluntary** for States.

131.s: Which of the following measures came first in empowering women politically in India?
o: Setting up the National Commission for Women
Reserving seats for women in local bodies
Introducing the Women's Reservation Bill for legislatures
131.x: Reserving seats for women in local bodies came first (73rd/74th Amendments) and is the APPSC 2007 key. The NCW, SHGs and a Reservation Bill for legislatures came after, so they are not the answer.
131.tq: Local-body reservation first; legislature quota (106th) came much later.
xs: **Reserving seats for women in local bodies** came first — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC **2007** key).
The **NCW**, women's **SHGs** and the **Reservation Bill** for legislatures came after it.
Local-body reservation came through **Art. 243D(3)** (panchayats) and **Art. 243T(3)** (municipalities).
xa: The **73rd Amendment** came into force on **24 April 1993**.
**NCW** was set up in **1992** under the **NCW Act 1990**.
**Bihar** was the first State to give women **50%** in local bodies (**2006**).

131.s: The Constitution (73rd Amendment) Act, which introduced one-third reservation for women in Panchayats, came into force on:
131.x: The 73rd Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993, which is why 24 April is National Panchayati Raj Day. The other dates are not its commencement date.
131.tq: 73rd in force 24 April 1993 (Panchayati Raj Day).
xs: The **73rd Amendment** came into force on **24 April 1993** — option **(2)** is correct.
It introduced not less than **one-third** of seats for women in Panchayats (**Art. 243D(3)**).
xa: The municipal counterpart is the **74th Amendment** (**Art. 243T(3)**).
Not applicable to **Arunachal Pradesh** for SC reservation (no SC population).
SC/ST reservation ends with the **Art. 334** period (**2030**); women's has no sunset.

131.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the constitutional position regarding reservation for women in Panchayats and Municipalities?
o: The Constitution leaves women's reservation entirely to State legislatures.
The Constitution prescribes a ceiling of one-third and prohibits States from increasing it.
The Constitution prescribes a floor of one-third, and States may provide a higher proportion such as one-half.
The Constitution provides one-half reservation in every local body throughout India.
131.x: The constitutional one-third requirement is a floor, not a ceiling. States may increase women's reservation, and several States provide one-half reservation.
131.tq: Apply the floor-versus-ceiling distinction to a State reservation policy.
xs: The Constitution sets a **floor of one-third**; States may give more, such as **one-half** — option **(3)** is correct.
The one-third is **compulsory**, so it is not left entirely to States and is **not a ceiling**.
Not every local body has one-half: **19 States/UTs** give **50%** (**2026**).
xa: APPSC **2019** key: "**1/2** of the seats" in PRIs.
**Bihar** was first with **50%** (**2006**); **Andhra Pradesh** has legislated **50%** for panchayats and municipalities.
Women are **over 49.7%** of elected panchayat representatives nationally.

131.s: What percentage of seats is reserved for women in Andhra Pradesh local bodies?
131.x: Andhra Pradesh provides 50 per cent reservation for women in local bodies.
xa: **19 States/UTs** give women **50%** (**2026**); **Bihar** was first (**2006**).
**AP 2026:** Cabinet approved **34% BC** reservation in rural and **33.33%** in urban local bodies.
AP Congress and BC groups demand a **BC-women sub-quota**.

131.s: Which was the first State to raise the reservation for women in Panchayati Raj Institutions to 50%, and in which year?
131.x: Bihar was the first State to give women 50% in PRIs, in 2006. Many States followed, and 19 States/UTs now give 50%, including Andhra Pradesh. The other pairs are not the first.
131.tq: 50% for women in PRIs: Bihar first (2006).
xs: **Bihar** was the first State to give women **50%** in local bodies, in **2006** — option **(3)** is correct.
Many States followed; **19 States/UTs** now give **50%** (**2026**), including **Andhra Pradesh**.
xa: Women are **~46%** of PRI representatives (Republic Day address, **2026**).
Only **10** States/UTs exceed the quota; **4** fall short (Centre, **23 Apr 2026**).
APPSC **2019** key: "**1/2** of the seats" in PRIs.

131.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about women's reservation?
o: Local bodies have a constitutional one-third floor for women's reservation.
Half reservation for women in local bodies exists in 19 States and UTs.
Half reservation for women in local bodies is constitutionally mandatory in every State.
In legislatures, one-third reservation is to operate only after delimitation.
131.x: The constitutional floor is one-third; half reservation exists only in 19 States and UTs that chose it.
xa: **Bihar** was first with **50%** (**2006**).
The legislature quota is linked to the **2027 Census**, not enforceable before **2034**.
**AP** has legislated **50%** for women in local bodies.

131.s:
1. The constitutional baseline for women's reservation in Panchayats is one-third.
2. Bihar was the first State to grant 50% reservation for women in Panchayats, in 2006.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
131.x: Both are true: the constitutional minimum is one-third, and Bihar first raised it to 50% in 2006.
n: The constitutional baseline for women's reservation in Panchayats is one-third. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
The constitutional baseline for women's reservation in Panchayats is 33.33%. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
States have statutory discretion to increase women's reservation in Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
Bihar was the first State to grant 50% reservation for women in Panchayats. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
Bihar granted 50% reservation for women in Panchayats in 2006. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
Women's reservation in Panchayati Raj Institutions covers not less than one-third of total seats and offices. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #76 · pp 207-210]
xa: Bihar was followed by **Madhya Pradesh**, **Uttarakhand** and **Himachal Pradesh**.
**19 States/UTs** now give women **50%**; **AP** too legislated **50%**.
Women's one-third is a **floor, not a ceiling**, and has **no sunset**.

131.s: Who was the first woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
131.x: Meira Kumar was the first woman Lok Sabha Speaker; Pratibha Patil was the first woman President.
xa: ⚠ Both **Naidu** and **Kripalani** were firsts in **UP**.
**Pratibha Bharati** = first woman **AP Assembly Speaker** (**2004**).
Women's turnout exceeded men's first in **2019**.

131.s: Who was the first woman Speaker of the (undivided) Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly?
131.x: Pratibha Bharati became the first woman Speaker of the undivided AP Assembly in 2004. Meira Kumar was the first woman Lok Sabha Speaker, Sucheta Kripalani the first woman Chief Minister (UP), and Sarojini Naidu the first woman Governor (UP).
131.tq: AP Assembly first woman Speaker = Pratibha Bharati (2004).
xs: **Pratibha Bharati** became the first woman **AP Assembly Speaker** in **2004** (undivided AP) — option **(1)** is correct.
**Meira Kumar** was the first woman **Lok Sabha Speaker** (**2009**).
**Sucheta Kripalani** was the first woman **CM** (UP, **1963**); **Sarojini Naidu** the first woman **Governor** (UP, **1947**).
xa: **Pratibha Patil** = first woman **President** (**2007**).
**AP** gives women **50%** reservation in local bodies.
**Bokkasam Palem** (Tirupati) ranked **1st nationally** among women-friendly panchayats.

131.s: Who was the first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress?
131.x: Sarojini Naidu (1925) was the first Indian woman INC president; Annie Besant (1917) was the first woman president.
n: Annie Besant was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress in 1917. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress in 1925. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
Indira Gandhi was the first woman Prime Minister. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
xa: ⚠ **Sarojini Naidu** was also the first woman **Governor** (UP, **1947**) — both firsts tied to UP.
**Pratibha Patil** (**2007**): first woman **President of India**.
**Meira Kumar** (**2009**): first woman **Lok Sabha Speaker**.

131.s: Who was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court?
131.x: M. Fathima Beevi (1989) was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court. Kiran Bedi was the first woman IPS officer and Pratibha Patil the first woman President.
131.tq: Match each first to the woman who holds it.
n: M. Fathima Beevi was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
xs: **M. Fathima Beevi** was the **first woman judge of the Supreme Court** — option **(4)**.
**Kiran Bedi** was the first woman **IPS officer**; **Pratibha Patil** the first woman **President**.
**Sarojini Naidu** was the first woman **Governor**.
xa: **Jayanti Patnaik**: first **Chairperson** of the **National Commission for Women**.
**Pratibha Bharati**: AP Assembly Speaker (**2004**).
Women's turnout first exceeded men's in **2019**, and again in **2024**.

131.s: Who was the first woman Governor of an Indian State?
131.x: Sarojini Naidu became Governor of the United Provinces in 1947; Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman CM (UP, 1963).
n: Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of any State. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Sarojini Naidu was the Governor of Uttar Pradesh. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister of any State. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
Sucheta Kripalani was the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-6]
xa: **Annie Besant** (**1917**): first woman INC President.
**Pratibha Patil** (**2007**): first woman President of India.
**M. Fathima Beevi**: first woman Supreme Court judge.

131.s: The Gender Development Index primarily measures the ratio of female to male achievement in which of the following dimensions?
o: Economic participation, educational attainment, health and political empowerment
Reproductive health, political empowerment and labour market participation
Health, education and command over economic resources
131.x: GDI compares female and male HDI achievements in life expectancy, education and earned income or command over economic resources.
131.tq: Distinguish the dimensions of GDI from the sub-indices of GII and GGGI.
xs: GDI compares women and men in **health**, **education** and **command over economic resources** — option **(3)** is correct.
Indicators: **life expectancy**, **expected and mean years of schooling**, **earned income**.
Option 1 lists the **GGGI** sub-indices; option 2 is the **GII**; option 4 is the **WPS Index**.
xa: GDI is the **ratio of female to male HDI**, published by **UNDP**.
GDI parity is near **1**.
⚠ The 0-to-1 "loss" scale (1 = women fare worst) is the **GII**'s.

131.s: The 0-to-1 scale on which 1 denotes the worst position for women belongs to the:
131.x: This loss scale belongs to the GII; the GDI is read as female-to-male parity, with a value near 1 indicating parity.
xa: Both GDI and GII are published by **UNDP**.
GII dimensions: **reproductive health**, **empowerment**, **labour market**.
India's GII lags its overall HDI rank.

131.s: Which of the following indicators is included under the reproductive health dimension of the Gender Inequality Index?
o: Maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rate
Mean years of schooling and earned income
Share of women in parliamentary seats only
131.x: The reproductive health dimension of GII includes maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rate.
131.tq: Link each indicator to the correct index dimension.
xs: GII's **reproductive health** dimension = **maternal mortality ratio (MMR)** and **adolescent birth rate** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Parliamentary seats** belong to the **empowerment** dimension; **female LFPR** to the **labour market** dimension.
Mean years of schooling and earned income are **GDI** indicators.
xa: GII was introduced by **UNDP** in **2010**.
Empowerment also includes **secondary education**.
⚠ **GDI** and **GII** = **UNDP**; **GGGI** = **WEF**.

131.s: The Global Gender Gap Index is published by the:
131.x: The Global Gender Gap Index is published by the World Economic Forum.
131.tq: Use publisher-index matching to avoid confusing GGGI with UNDP indices.
xs: The **GGGI** is published by the **World Economic Forum** — option **(3)** is correct.
**UNDP** publishes the GDI and GII; the **Georgetown Institute with PRIO** publishes the WPS Index.
xa: GGGI has existed **since 2006**.
Four sub-indices: **Economic Participation & Opportunity**, **Educational Attainment**, **Health & Survival**, **Political Empowerment**.

131.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the four sub-indices of the Global Gender Gap Index?
131.x: The four GGGI sub-indices are Economic Participation and Opportunity, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, and Political Empowerment. Reproductive Health is associated with GII.
131.tq: Eliminate the GII dimension inserted into the GGGI list.
xs: **Reproductive Health** is NOT a GGGI sub-index — option **(1)**; it is a **GII** dimension.
GGGI's four sub-indices: **Economic Participation & Opportunity**, **Educational Attainment**, **Health & Survival**, **Political Empowerment**.
xa: GGGI is published by the **World Economic Forum** (since **2006**).
GII reproductive health = **MMR** and **adolescent birth rate**.
India's economic participation parity was only **36.7%** (**2023**).

131.s: Which one of the following statements about India's performance in the 2023 Global Gender Gap Index is correct?
o: Political empowerment parity was 36.7%, while economic participation parity was complete.
Economic participation parity exceeded 75%, while enrolment parity was absent at all levels.
Economic participation parity was 36.7%, while enrolment parity had been achieved at all educational levels.
India ranked 108th out of 149 countries in 2023.
131.x: In 2023, India's economic participation parity was only 36.7%, whereas parity in enrolment had been achieved at all education levels.
131.tq: Separate the education achievement from the continuing economic participation gap.

131.s: Which of the Article provide for the Reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Panchayat Raj Institutions:
131.x: 243D Article 243D of the Constitution provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Panchayati Raj Institutions. It also mandates reservation for women, ensuring inclusive representation at the grassroots level. This article was inserted by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.

131.s:
With reference to Panchayati Raj Institutions in India which of the following statements is / are correct ?
1. Tenure of Panchayati Raj Institutions shall be of 5 years.
2. In Panchayati Raj Institutions, out of the seats reserved, 1/4 of the seats shall be reserved for women belonging to Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
131.x: Statement 1 is correct. According to Article 243E(1), every Panchayat, unless dissolved earlier under any law for the time being in force, shall continue for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting. Statement 2 is incorrect. The Constitution does not provide for a one-fourth (25%) reservation for SC/ST women. As per Article 243D, not less than one-third of the seats reserved for a SCs/STs shall be reserved for women belonging to SCs/STs, and not less than one-third of the total seats to be filled by direct election in every Panchayat shall be reserved for women (and the seats reserved for SC/ST women are included within the overall women’s reservation).

131.s: In India, seats are reserved for women in –
131.x: During the question period, the seats were reserved for women in Panchayati Raj Institutions only. But now, through the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 also known as 'Women's Reservation Bill' or 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam', One-third seats are reserved for women in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, and the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, including those reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. This reservation shall come into effect after the first delimitation based on the first census after the commencement of this Amendment Act.

o: As per the requirements of circumstances
131.x: In accordance with the 73rd Amendment, Uttar Pradesh Panchayat Laws (Amendment) Act, 1994 was passed, which came into force on 22 April, 1994. It provides reservations for women on one-third of the total seats.

131.x: The local self-government in India has been formalized under the Panchayati-raj system by 73rd Amendment in 1992. According to Article 243-D Clause (2)- not less than one-third of the total number of seats reserved under Clause (1) shall be reserved for women belonging to the Scheduled Castes or as the case may be, the Scheduled Tribes. According to Clause(3), Not less than one-third (including the number of seats reserved for women belonging to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes) of the total number of seats to be filled by direct election in every Panchayat shall be reserved for women. In the Indian scenario, the reservation of seats for women in village local self-government is not a result of any demand.

Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The reservation of thirty-three percent of seats for women in Parliament and State Legislature does not require a Constitutional amendment.
Reason (R) : Political parties contesting elections can allocate thirty-three percent of seats they contest to women candidates without any Constitutional amendment. In the context of the above two statements which one of the following is correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct
131.x: Articles 330 to 334 of the Indian Constitution provide for the reservation of some special classes in the House of the People and State Legislative Assemblies. There is no provision made for women; thus the reservation of 33% of seats for women in the Parliament and State Legislature can be made only by a Constitutional Amendment. So, Assertion (A) is incorrect while the Reason (R) is correct.

131.s: Which of the following gives 'Global Gender Gap Index' ranking to the countries of the world?
131.x: The Global Gender Gap Index is an annual report produced by the World Economic Forum (WEF) that measures gender-based gaps in access to resources and opportunities in countries around the world. It is the longest-standing index, tracking progress towards closing these gaps over time since its inception in 2006. It tracks the gender gap across four key parameters:  Economic participation and opportunity,  Educational attainment,  Health and survival, and  Political empowerment. • It ranks countries on a scale from 0 to 1, with a score of 1 indicating that a country has achieved complete gender equality, while a score of 0 indicates a complete lack of equality.

Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana provides LPG connections in women's names. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]

133.tq: Distinguish local-body reservations from Parliament and State Assembly reservations.
xs: **Articles 243D and 243T** reserve SC/ST seats and chairperson posts in **Panchayats/Municipalities** — option **(3)** is correct.
**330/332** are Lok Sabha/Assemblies; **341/342** are the SC/ST lists; **244/275** concern Scheduled Areas and grants.
xa: **244** = Scheduled Areas (Fifth Schedule) and Tribal Areas (Sixth Schedule).
**275(1)** = grants-in-aid for ST welfare.
**Art. 334** time limit now till **2030**.

133.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the Articles with the lists they deal with?
133.x: Article 341 concerns the list of Scheduled Castes, Article 342 the Scheduled Tribes and Article 342A the socially and educationally backward classes.
xa: Part XVI runs from **Articles 330-342**.
**331, 333** = Anglo-Indian nomination (ended by the **104th Amendment**).
Only **Parliament by law** can include or exclude castes.

133.s: The number of seats reserved for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha was refixed on the basis of the
o: 1971 Census and 1981 Census through the 42nd and 44th Amendments
1981 Census and 1991 Census through the 73rd and 74th Amendments
1991 Census and 2001 Census through the 84th and 87th Amendments
2001 Census and 2011 Census through the 87th and 91st Amendments
133.x: The 84th Amendment refixed the seat numbers on the basis of the 1991 Census, and the 87th Amendment did so on the basis of the 2001 Census.
133.tq: Match the Census years with the corresponding amendment numbers.
xs: Seats were refixed on the **1991 Census** (**84th**) and the **2001 Census** (**87th**) — option **(3)** is correct.
The **73rd/74th** are local-body amendments; the **42nd/44th** are not listed for seat refixing.
xa: Lok Sabha SC/ST seats: **79/41** (**1971** Census) → **84/47** after the **2008** delimitation on **Census 2001**.
**51st Amendment (1984)**: ST seats for **Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal, Mizoram**.
⚠ **85th** = consequential seniority, not seat refixing.

133.s: The 51st Constitutional Amendment, 1984, provided for ST seats in the Lok Sabha for
o: Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram
133.x: The 51st Amendment, 1984, provided ST representation in the Lok Sabha for Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram.
133.tq: Test the exact four-State grouping and avoid substituting neighbouring north-eastern States.
xs: The **51st Amendment (1984)** gave ST Lok Sabha seats to **Meghalaya, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram** — option **(3)** is correct.
Assam, Tripura, Manipur, Sikkim and Goa are not in the 51st Amendment list.
xa: Sixth Schedule (**244(2)**) States: **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**.
**244A** = Autonomous State within Assam (**22nd Amendment, 1969**).

133.s: Article 16(4A), permitting reservation in promotion for SCs and STs, was inserted by the 77th Amendment (1995) mainly in response to which judicial position?
o: Indra Sawhney (1992) confining reservation under Article 16(4) to initial appointment
E.V. Chinnaiah (2004) treating SCs as a homogeneous class
133.x: Indra Sawhney (1992) held that reservation under Article 16(4) applies only at initial appointment, not promotion; the 77th Amendment (1995) responded by inserting Article 16(4A). M. Nagaraj came later and upheld the 77th; Chinnaiah concerns SC sub-classification; Janhit Abhiyan concerns EWS.
133.tq: 77th = 16(4A) promotion, answer to Indra Sawhney.
xs: The **77th Amendment (1995)** responded to **Indra Sawhney (1992)**, which confined **Art. 16(4)** to **initial appointment** — option **(1)** is correct.
**M. Nagaraj (2006)** came later and upheld the 77th; **E.V. Chinnaiah (2004)** concerns SC sub-classification.
xa: Indra Sawhney also set the **50% ceiling**.
**85th** added consequential seniority w.e.f. **17 June 1995**.
**Davinder Singh (2024)** overruled **Chinnaiah**.

133.s: The 89th Amendment (2003) created the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article:
133.x: The 89th Amendment split the joint commission into the NCSC (Article 338) and NCST (Article 338A); the Commissions report to the President.
xa: Functions: investigate safeguards, inquire into complaints, **advise on planning**.
Powers: **civil-court powers** while inquiring.
Original Art. 338 had a **Special Officer**.

133.s: In 2017, the NCRB added a separate crime head for SCs relating to:
o: Being forced to leave residence or facing social boycott
Denial of reservation in educational institutions
133.x: The 2017 NCRB crime head covered persons forced to leave their residence or facing social boycott. Uttar Pradesh recorded 57 cases under this head that year.
133.tq: Recall the exact wording of a newly introduced crime category.
xs: The **2017** NCRB head: SCs **forced to leave residence / facing social boycott** — option **(1)** is correct.
**UP** recorded **57** cases that year.
xa: Dalit labourers depend on dominant-caste landowners and **hide complaints** for fear of boycott.
⚠ **Mysore HC**: social boycott of a few individuals is **not** untouchability under Art. 17.

133.s: Which one of the following statements about constitutional reservation provisions is correct?
o: Article 16(4) formed part of the original Constitution, whereas Article 15(4) was added by the First Amendment in 1951.
Article 15(4) formed part of the original Constitution, whereas Article 16(4) was added by the First Amendment in 1951.
Both Articles 15(4) and 16(4) were inserted by the 42nd Amendment.
Both Articles 15(4) and 16(4) were inserted by the 1st Amendment.
133.x: Article 16(4) was present in the original Constitution. Article 15(4) was the first reservation clause added by constitutional amendment, through the First Amendment Act, 1951.
133.tq: Discriminate between the original provision and the later amendment-created provision.
xs: **Art. 16(4)** was in the **original Constitution**; **Art. 15(4)** was added by the **1st Amendment, 1951** — option **(1)** is correct.
Option 2 reverses them; neither came from the **42nd** Amendment.
xa: 15(4) is the basis of reserved seats in **educational institutions**.
**15(5)** covers private institutions except minority ones.

133.s: The 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill (April 2026) sought to enlarge the Lok Sabha to how many members?
133.x: The Bill sought to amend Articles 330, 332 and 334A and enlarge the Lok Sabha to 850; it was not passed.
xa: The Bill was **not passed** (Apr **2026**).
⚠ **334A** = women's reservation (**106th**, **2023**).

133.s: In the Sabarimala reference, Justice B.V. Nagarathna observed that Article 17 cannot be applied:
o: After the commencement of the Constitution
Only during the annual pilgrimage season
133.x: Justice B.V. Nagarathna stated that Article 17 cannot apply “for three days a month” in the Sabarimala reference.
133.tq: Recall the precise time-related phrase rather than replacing it with a broader limitation.
xs: Justice **B.V. Nagarathna** said Art. 17 cannot apply "**for three days a month**" — option **(2)** is correct.
It was in the **Sabarimala reference** (**8 Apr 2026**).
xa: Art. 17 binds **private persons** too (**PUDR v Union of India**, **1982**).
Haldwani "shuddhikaran" row: **32** SC/ST Congress MPs petitioned the **President** (**8 Sep 2026**).

133.s: After the Amendment in Indian Constitution by the Parliament on 14 August, 2007 the number of castes in the list of Scheduled Caste is –
133.x: After the Amendment made by Parliament in 2007, there were a total of 1206 Scheduled Castes in India. As per 'The Constitution (Scheduled Castes Amendment) Act, 2017' the total number of Scheduled Castes in India is 1261. According to the Census-2011, the Scheduled Castes form 16.6 percent of the total population.

133.s: Article 17 (abolition of untouchability) belongs to which group of Fundamental Rights?
133.x: Article 17 is in the Right to Equality group and operates against private persons too; the Constitution does not define 'untouchability'.
xa: Only **Parliament** can prescribe punishment for Art. 17 offences (**Art. 35(a)(ii)**).
**Mysore HC:** untouchability means the practice **as it developed historically**, not the literal sense.
First law enforcing Art. 17: **Untouchability (Offences) Act 1955**, renamed **Protection of Civil Rights Act** in **1976**.

133.s: Who is associated with ensuring that Article 17 made untouchability a punishable offence?
133.x: B.R. Ambedkar ensured that Article 17 constitutionally treated untouchability as a punishable offence.
133.tq: Match the constitutional contribution with the principal figure associated with it.
xs: **B.R. Ambedkar** ensured Art. 17 made untouchability a **punishable offence** — option **(3)** is correct.
He called caste "**a division of labourers**" and preferred the term **Dalit** over 'Harijan'.
xa: ⚠ **Gandhi** coined **'Harijan'** and called untouchability "**a blot on Hinduism**".
Ambedkar led the **Mahad (Chavdar Tank) Satyagraha** on **20 Mar 1927**.
Ambedkar wrote **Annihilation of Caste** (**1936**).

133.s: Under Article 35(a)(ii) of the Constitution of India, the power to prescribe punishment for offences under Article 17 belongs to
o: Both Parliament and State Legislatures concurrently
133.x: Article 35(a)(ii) gives Parliament, and not the State Legislatures, the power to prescribe punishment for offences relating to Article 17.
133.tq: Ask which authority would do this job, while distinguishing Parliament from State Legislatures.
xs: Under **Art. 35(a)(ii)**, only **Parliament** — not State legislatures — can prescribe punishment for Art. 17 offences: option **(1) Parliament alone**.
So the power is not concurrent and not with the courts.
xa: Art. 17 abolishes untouchability; its practice in any form is **forbidden** and **punishable by law**.
Laws enforcing Art. 17: **PCR Act** (**1955**/**1976**) and **SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989**.
Conviction for untouchability offences disqualifies from elections under **Sec. 8, RPA 1951**.

133.s: The Mysore High Court interpreted 'untouchability' under Article 17 as:
o: The practice as defined in the 1955 Act
Including social boycott of a few individuals
The practice as it developed historically
133.x: The Mysore HC read it as the historically developed practice, which excludes social boycott of a few individuals.
xa: **Neither the Constitution nor any Act** defines "untouchability".
Critics: because it is undefined, **new indirect forms escape penalty** (**2 Sep 2026**).
Two angles: stigma of **ritual pollution** + practices society uses to "protect" itself from it.

133.s: Which one of the following is correct about the list of Scheduled Castes of a State?
o: The President notifies it after consulting the Governor.
The State Legislature notifies it by resolution.
The Governor notifies it with the State Legislature's approval.
The National Commission for Scheduled Castes notifies it by order.
133.x: Under Article 341, the President specifies the Scheduled Castes of a State after consulting the Governor; later inclusion or exclusion can be made only by Parliament by law.
xa: **SC (July 2024)** struck down **Bihar's 2015** resolution merging **Tanti-Tantwa** into the SC list.
First SC list after the Constitution: **Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950**.
⚠ "Article **344**" (CDX) is wrong — 344 is the Official Language Commission.

133.s: In Chinthada Anand v. State of Andhra Pradesh, the Supreme Court held that a Scheduled Caste person who converts to Christianity:
o: Cannot claim SC status merely on the basis of earlier caste identity
Can claim SC status on the State Government's recommendation alone
Retains SC status because religion is irrelevant to the SC list
133.x: A Christian convert cannot claim SC status merely on earlier caste identity; reconversion requires proof of original SC status, bona fide reconversion and acceptance by the community.
xa: ⚠ By contrast, **ST status is religion-neutral**.
**K.G. Balakrishnan Commission**: SC status for Dalit converts to **Christianity and Islam**, extended to **10 June 2026**.
The Chinthada Anand ruling was in the news in **Jun 2026**.

133.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional position regarding Scheduled Tribes?
o: Scheduled Tribe status is decided exclusively by the State Legislature.
Scheduled Tribe status is religion-neutral and the list for a State or Union Territory is specified under Article 342.
Scheduled Tribe status is confined to Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists.
Scheduled Tribe status is determined by the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes without Presidential notification.
133.x: Article 342 concerns the specification of Scheduled Tribes, and ST status is not restricted by religion.
133.tq: Combine the correct Article with the key SC–ST distinction instead of choosing a familiar but misplaced authority.
xs: ST status is **religion-neutral** and the list is specified under **Article 342** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is not decided by the State Legislature or the NCST; the **President** notifies and **Parliament** alone alters.
xa: ⚠ For SCs, **Christian converts cannot claim SC status** (**Chinthada Anand**).
**366(25)** defines Scheduled Tribes.

133.s: The Usha Mehra Commission, constituted in 2007–08, recommended which of the following?
o: Amending Article 341 to enable States to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes
Including all Other Backward Classes in the Scheduled Caste list
133.x: The Usha Mehra Commission recommended amendment of Article 341 so that States could undertake sub-categorisation of Scheduled Castes.
133.tq: Match a commission with its specific recommendation.
xs: The **Usha Mehra Commission (2007-08)** recommended **amending Art. 341** to let **States sub-categorise SCs** — option **(1)** is correct.
It came after **Chinnaiah (2004)** blocked State sub-classification.
xa: **Davinder Singh (2024)** later held sub-classification **permissible** under **Arts. 14, 15, 16**.
Only **Parliament by law** can alter the SC list under **Art. 341**.
**Telangana** implemented **3** groups in **April 2025**.

133.s: The original form of Article 338 provided for—
o: a non-statutory multi-member commission appointed by the State Governments
a Special Officer designated as the Commissioner for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
a Parliamentary committee for monitoring reservations
a separate National Commission for Scheduled Castes and a separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
133.x: Originally, Article 338 provided for a Special Officer, known as the Commissioner for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, to investigate safeguards and report to the President.
133.tq: Track institutional evolution by identifying the original arrangement before later commissions were created.
xs: Original **Art. 338** provided a **Special Officer** (Commissioner for SCs and STs) — option **(2)** is correct.
He **investigated safeguards** and **reported to the President**.
Separate NCSC and NCST came only with the **89th Amendment (2003)**.
xa: **1978 Resolution**: non-statutory multi-member Commission for SCs and STs; modified in **1987**.
**1990**: the joint commission became **constitutional** (**Art. 338**).
**NCST** from **19 Feb 2004**.

133.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched regarding the status of office-bearers of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
133.x: The Chairperson of the NCST has Cabinet rank, the Vice-Chairperson has Minister of State rank, and members have Secretary rank. Therefore, describing the Chairperson as having Minister of State rank is incorrect.
133.tq: Find the single reversed rank in a hierarchy-based matching question.
xs: **Chairperson — Minister of State rank** is NOT correct — option **(4)**; the NCST Chairperson has **Cabinet rank**.
**Vice-Chairperson** = **MoS rank**; **members** = **Secretary rank**.
xa: Composition: Chairperson + Vice-Chairperson + **three** members.
The **President** fixes tenure and service conditions.
The Commission has **civil-court powers** while inquiring.

133.s: What does Article 338(9) of the Constitution provide?
o: It empowers the President to create State Commissions for Scheduled Castes
It requires the Union and every State to consult the National Commission for Scheduled Castes on all major policy matters affecting SCs
It gives the NCSC power to amend the Scheduled Caste list
It provides grants-in-aid to State SC Commissions
133.x: Article 338(9) obliges the Union and State Governments to consult the NCSC on major policy matters affecting SCs. It does not empower the President to create State commissions (a trap in CDCA); State SC Commissions are created by State law. The SC list is altered only by Parliament under Article 341, and grants-in-aid are under Article 275(1) for ST welfare.
133.tq: 338(9) = duty to consult NCSC; State SC Commissions come from State law.
xs: **Art. 338(9)** requires the **Union and every State to consult the NCSC** on major policy matters — option **(2)** is correct.
⚠ CDCA says 338(9) lets the President create State commissions — **wrong**; State SC Commissions are made by **State law**.
The SC list is altered only by **Parliament** (**Art. 341**); grants-in-aid are **Art. 275(1)**.
xa: NCSC and NCST have **civil-court powers** while inquiring.
AP has a statutory **State SC Commission** (chairman **K.S. Jawahar**).

133.s: Which of the following is NOT an offence covered by the Protection of Civil Rights law in relation to untouchability?
o: Providing reservation in public employment to an eligible Scheduled Caste candidate
Denying access to shops, hotels and places of entertainment
Barring entry to a place of public worship
Justifying untouchability on religious or traditional grounds
133.x: The Protection of Civil Rights law covers practices such as denial of temple entry, justification of untouchability and denial of access to public facilities. Providing reservation in public employment is not one of the listed offences.
133.tq: Find the item outside the statutory list rather than choosing a familiar Scheduled Caste-related provision.
xs: **Providing reservation** to an eligible SC candidate is not a PCR offence — option **(1)** is the answer.
PCR offences: barring entry to **public worship**, **justifying untouchability**, denying access to **shops, hotels, entertainment**.
xa: Insulting an SC member "on the ground of untouchability" = **Sec. 7(1)(d)**.
The PCR Act was the **Untouchability (Offences) Act 1955**, renamed in **1976**.
Conviction disqualifies from elections under **Sec. 8, RPA 1951**.

133.s: According to reports associated with the National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, which one of the following is NOT listed as a cause of caste atrocities?
133.x: Land alienation, bonded labour, indebtedness and non-payment of wages are listed causes. Religious causes are not included in the stated list.
133.tq: Find the excluded item in a familiar list rather than selecting a general social factor.
xs: **Religious causes** are NOT listed — option **(1)** (MPPSC **2015** trap).
The **National Commission for SCs & STs (1990)** listed **land alienation**, **bonded labour**, **indebtedness**, **non-payment of wages**.
xa: CDX factors: **caste hierarchy**, **upper-caste dominance**, **rising Dalit activism**, **political interference**.
NCRB (**2017**) added the head "forced to leave residence / facing **social boycott**".

133.s: “I was born a Hindu, but I will not die a Hindu” was declared by B. R. Ambedkar at:
133.x: B. R. Ambedkar made this declaration at Yeola in 1935.
133.tq: Discriminate between a leader’s quotation, place and year.
xs: Ambedkar declared "I was born a Hindu... but I will not die a Hindu" at **Yeola** in **1935** — option **(4)** is correct.
It sits with his other stands: caste is "**a division of labourers**" and **Dalit** over 'Harijan'.
xa: He wrote **Annihilation of Caste** in **1936**.
**Kalaram Temple Entry**: **1930**, Nashik.
**Mahad Satyagraha**: **20 Mar 1927**.

133.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Scheduled Caste population data in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: The SC population was 64.47 lakh and constituted 17.08% of the population.
The SC population was 84.69 lakh and constituted 24.85% of the population.
The SC population was 84.69 lakh and constituted 17.08% of the population.
The SC population was 20.14 crore and constituted 16.6% of the population.
133.x: In Andhra Pradesh, the SC population was 84.69 lakh and constituted 17.08% of the population. The other figures refer to India, a district share, or SC literacy.
133.tq: Separate absolute population, population share and literacy figures.
xs: AP SC population: **84.69 lakh** = **17.08%** — option **(3)** is correct.
**64.47%** is **SC literacy**; **24.85%** is the highest district share (**Konaseema**).
xa: Lowest district: **Alluri Sitharama Raju 2.49%**.
**Census 2011**: **1,241** caste groups notified as SCs.
AP Assembly: **29 SC + 7 ST** of **175**.

133.s: Which of the following law–purpose pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act – Prevents atrocities against SCs/STs
Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 – Eliminates manual scavenging
Protection of Civil Rights Act – Establishes NHRC
Protection of Human Rights Act – Establishes NHRC
133.x: The Protection of Civil Rights Act punishes the practice of untouchability; the NHRC was set up by the Protection of Human Rights Act.
n: The Protection of Civil Rights Act punishes the practice of untouchability. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act prevents atrocities against Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act eliminates manual scavenging. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
The Protection of Human Rights Act established the National Human Rights Commission. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #10 · pp 39-42]
xa: PCR was **renamed** in **1976** from the **Untouchability (Offences) Act**.
The Manual Scavengers Act came into force on **December 6, 2013**.
**PoA Rules 1995**: special courts and **60-day** limit for investigation.

133.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Manual Scavengers Act, 2013?
o: It prohibits hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks.
It provides for rehabilitation of manual scavengers with alternative livelihoods.
It permits hazardous manual cleaning when done by private contractors.
133.x: The 2013 Act bans hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks by anyone, including private contractors, and requires mechanisation and rehabilitation.
n: The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act was passed in 2013. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act completely prohibits hazardous manual cleaning of sewer tanks. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act completely prohibits hazardous manual cleaning of septic tanks. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act mandates mechanization. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act mandates alternative livelihood rehabilitation. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
xa: It also **totally bans** manual cleaning of **unsanitary latrines** and **open drains** without protective gear.
An earlier **1993** Act prohibited manual scavengers and dry latrines.
**SRMS** (**2007**) was subsumed in **NAMASTE**, goal **zero sanitation deaths**.

133.s: The Bhikhu Ramji Idate Commission led directly to which scheme?
133.x: The Idate Commission surveyed denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic tribes and led to the SEED scheme for their economic empowerment.
n: The Bhikhu Ramji Idate Commission led directly to the formulation of the SEED Scheme. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Bhikhu Ramji Idate Commission concerned Scheduled Castes and De-Notified Tribes (DNTs). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
xa: **Justice K.G. Balakrishnan Commission** (**2022**): SC status for Dalit converts to **Christianity and Islam**.
**Rajiv Gauba Committee** (**2024**): the **most backward SC sub-castes** (e.g. **Madigas**).

133.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Justice K.G. Balakrishnan Commission – SC status for certain converted Dalits
Bhikhu Ramji Idate Commission – Socio-economic status of Muslims
Rajiv Gauba Committee – Survey of DNTs, NTs and SNTs
Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee – Most backward SC sub-castes
133.x: The Balakrishnan Commission examined SC status for converted Dalits; Idate surveyed DNTs, NTs and SNTs, Gauba the most backward SC sub-castes and Sachar the Muslim community.
n: The Bhikhu Ramji Idate Commission surveyed De-Notified Tribes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Bhikhu Ramji Idate Commission surveyed Nomadic Tribes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Bhikhu Ramji Idate Commission surveyed Semi-Nomadic Tribes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]

The Justice K.G. Balakrishnan Commission examined the legal feasibility of according Scheduled Caste status to Dalits who converted to religions other than Hinduism, Sikhism, and Buddhism. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Rajiv Gauba Committee explored equitable administrative mechanisms for the most backward sub-castes among Scheduled Castes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee assessed the socio-economic status of the Muslim community in India. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Bhikhu Ramji Idate Commission concerned Scheduled Castes and De-Notified Tribes (DNTs). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Justice K.G. Balakrishnan Commission concerned Scheduled Castes (SCs). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Rajiv Gauba Committee concerned Scheduled Castes (SCs). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee concerned minorities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
xa: Balakrishnan examined converts to religions other than **Hinduism**, **Sikhism** and **Buddhism**.
Idate (**2017**) and Balakrishnan (**2022**) were both set up by the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment**.

133.s: Which sequence correctly represents the successive extensions of SC/ST reservation in legislatures under Article 334?
133.x: The listed extensions were made through the 8th, 23rd, 45th, 62nd, 79th, 95th and 104th Amendments; the 104th extended the reservation up to 2030.
133.tq: Track the reservation-extension series separately from promotion and service-related amendments.
xs: Correct sequence: **8th, 23rd, 45th, 62nd, 79th, 95th, 104th Amendments** — option **(1)**.
xa: **95th (2009)** took it from **60 → 70 years**.
⚠ **104th** = **2030** + end of **Anglo-Indian nomination**; **106th** = women's reservation (**334A**).

133.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Protection of Civil Rights Act?
o: It prescribes penalties for practising untouchability.
It was renamed in 1976 from the Untouchability (Offences) Act.
It came into force on 1 June 1955.
It came into force on 30 January 1990.
133.x: The Act came into force on 1 June 1955; 30 January 1990 is the commencement date of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
n: The Protection of Civil Rights Act came into force on June 1, 1955. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Protection of Civil Rights Act was renamed in 1976 from the Untouchability Offences Act. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Protection of Civil Rights Act prescribes penalties for practicing untouchability. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act came into force on January 30, 1990. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
xa: **January 30, 1990** is when the **SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act** came into force.
The PCR Act enforces **Article 17**.
Only **24 cases** were registered nationwide under the PCR Act in **2023**.

133.s: The proviso to Article 335 relating to relaxation of qualifying marks in promotion was enabled by which Constitutional Amendment?
133.x: The Eighty-Second Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000 inserted the proviso to Article 335 permitting relaxation of qualifying marks and standards in promotion for SCs and STs.
133.tq: Separate the closely placed reservation amendments by their precise subject.
xs: The **82nd Amendment (2000)** added the proviso to **Art. 335** allowing **relaxed qualifying marks** in promotion — option **(3) Eighty-Second** is correct.
**77th (1995)** = 16(4A) promotion quota; **81st** = 16(4B) carry-forward; **85th** = consequential seniority.
⚠ G2 **2024** circulated key said **89th** — that is the **NCSC-NCST bifurcation** amendment.
xa: **M. Nagaraj (2006)** upheld the 77th, 81st, 82nd, 85th but required **quantifiable data**.
⚠ **77th – 82nd – 85th** = promotion quota – relaxed marks – consequential seniority.

133.s: The 85th Constitutional Amendment is associated with
o: relaxation in qualifying marks under Article 335
backlog vacancies being treated as a separate class
consequential seniority in promotion under Article 16(4A), with effect from 17 June 1995
reservation of seats for STs in the Lok Sabha
133.x: The 85th Amendment provided consequential seniority in promotion under Article 16(4A), with effect from 17 June 1995.
133.tq: Use the effective date and the phrase “consequential seniority” as the decisive identifiers.
xs: The **85th Amendment** gave **consequential seniority** in promotion under **16(4A)**, w.e.f. **17 June 1995** — option **(3)** is correct.

133.s:

133.s: The Authority to specify as to which castes shall be deemed to be Scheduled Castes rests with the–
o: Commission of Scheduled Castes and Tribes
133.x: According to Article 341 of the Constitution, the President may with respect to any State or Union Territory, and where it is a State, after consultation with the Governor thereof, by public notification, specify the castes, races or tribes or parts or groups which shall for the purposes of this Constitution be deemed to be Scheduled Castes to that State or Union Territory, as the case may be. 5. Under which Article of the Indian Constitution does the President issue a public notification for the Scheduled Tribes for a specific state? (a) Article 340 (b) Article 349 (c) Article 342 (d) Article 338 M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2025 Ans. (c) Article 342 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to declare certain tribes or tribal communities as Scheduled Tribes for a state or union territory. This declaration is made through a public notification after consulting the state’s Governor. Parliament has the authority to add or remove tribes from the Scheduled Tribes list through legislation. Once the President issues a notification under this provision, it cannot be altered by any subsequent notification.

133.s: In India, which one of the following Constitutional Amendments was widely believed to be enacted to overcome the judicial interpretations of the Fundamental Rights?
133.x: The First Amendment was passed in 1951 by the Provisional Parliament, members of which had just finished drafting the Constitution as part of the Constituent Assembly. The First Amendment Act amended Articles 15, 19, 85, 87, 174, 176, 341, 342, 372 and 376. In Article 15, Clause 4 was added to make special provisions for the backward classes or for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. Certain restrictions were added in Article 19 by including the terms 'public order', 'friendly relations with foreign states, and 'incitement to an offence'. This amendment also added the Ninth Schedule to protect the land reforms and other laws included in it from the judicial review by adding Articles 31A and 31B. A number of rulings by the Supreme Court and High Court that declared certain sections of criminal legislation, regulations pertaining to the press, and public safety to be incompatible with the constitutional right to free expression served as the immediate impetus for the modifications.

133.s: Under which Article Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes have been granted fundamental, socioeconomic, political and cultural rights?

It is a “statement of principle” with the objective to remove humiliation and multifaceted harassment metedout to the Dalits and to ensure their fundamental, socio-economic, political and cultural rights. 38. Consider the following statements :
Statement-I : The Supreme Court of India has held in some judgements that the reservation policies made under Article 16(4) of the Constitution of India would be limited by Article 335 for maintenance of efficiency of administration.
Statement-II : Article 335 of the Constitution of India defines the term ‘efficiency of administration’. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
133.x: Article 16 (4) of the Constitution enables States to make any provision for the reservation of appointments or posts in favour of any backward class of citizens which, in the opinion of the State, is not adequately represented in the services under the State. However, the Supreme Court of India has consistently referred to the notions of "efficiency" and "merit," while adjudicating the validity of various reservation policies. The Court has held in several judgments, such as Indra Sawhney Vs Union of India 1993 and M Nagaraj Vs Union of India 2006, that the reservation policies made under Article 16(4) of the Constitution have to be interpreted in the background of Art. 335, which provides for "maintenance of efficiency of administration," while making appointments to services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union or of a State. Article 335 states that the claims of the members of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes shall be taken into consideration, consistently with the maintenance of efficiency of administration, in the making of appointments to services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union or of a State. This Article has, however, not defined the expression 'efficiency of administration'. Hence, statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect.

Dattatreya Balkrushna Kalelkar (1 Dec 1885-21 Aug 1981) Popularly known as Kaka Kalelkar, was an Indian independence activist, social reformer and journalist. He was a major follower of the philosophy and methods of Mahatma Gandhi. Kalelkar was born in Satara (Maharashtra). He was appointed as a member of Rajya Sabha from 1952 to 1964. He presided over the Gujarati Sahitya Parishad in 1959. He established Gandhi Vidyapith, Vedchhi in 1967 and served as its vice-chancellor. Mahatma Gandhi called him Savai Gujarati (a quarter more than a Gujarati).

**27%** of central civil posts were reserved in **1993** (UPSC, IYB).

135.s: Which one of the following is correct about the implementation of the Mandal Commission recommendations?
o: Implemented by the V.P. Singh Government in 1993; posts reserved in 1995
Implemented by the Morarji Desai Government in 1979; posts reserved in 1980
