135.s: President Ram nath Kovind granted assent to which Constitutional Amendment Act on 18th August, 2021?
135.x: President Ram Nath Kovind granted assent to the 105th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2021 on 18th August, 2021. It empowers states to identify and specify the Socially and Educationally Backward Class (SEBC). As per the Act, every State or Union territory may, by law, prepare and maintain, for its own purposes, a list of socially and educationally backward classes, entries in which may be different from the Central List.

135.s: Before the 102nd Constitutional Amendment, Article 338(10) provided that references to Scheduled Castes would include such backward classes as were specified by the
135.x: Before the 102nd Amendment, Article 338(10) treated references to Scheduled Castes as including such backward classes as the President specified. Consequently, complaints relating to backward classes could go to the SC Commission.
135.tq: Identify the constitutional authority named in the transitional provision.
xs: Before **2018**, **Art. 338(10)** treated references to SCs as including backward classes specified by the **President** — option **(4)**.
Hence **BC complaints** went to the **SC commission** until the **102nd Amendment**.
The **NCBC** got constitutional status only through the **102nd (2018)** under **Art. 338B**, so it could not be the specifying authority earlier.
xa: **102nd (2018)** also inserted **Art. 342A** (SEBC lists) and **Art. 366(26C)**.
The statutory **NCBC Act 1993** was **repealed** in 2018; the present (**8th**) NCBC is constitutional.
102nd = **123rd Bill**; 105th = **127th Bill**; 103rd = **124th Bill**.
**Niranjan Jyoti** was appointed **NCBC Chairperson** (2026).

135.s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the ruling in Indra Sawhney regarding carry-forward vacancies?
o: Carry-forward is allowed, but it must operate within the 50 per cent ceiling on a year-by-year basis.
Carry-forward is prohibited in every situation.
Carry-forward applies only to EWS vacancies.
Carry-forward is unlimited and is calculated only once in a decade.
135.x: Indra Sawhney permitted carry-forward of vacancies, subject to the 50 per cent ceiling being applied year by year.
135.tq: Combine the carry-forward rule with the year-by-year ceiling rather than treating either as absolute.
xs: **Carry-forward** is allowed but must stay **within the 50% ceiling**, applied **year by year** — option **(1)**.
Indra Sawhney fixed total reservation **not above 50%** except in extraordinary cases.
It is not limited to EWS; EWS (**103rd**) came much later.
xa: The **81st (2000)** made unfilled **backlog vacancies** a separate class, outside the **50%** ceiling (**Art. 16(4B)**).
**Janhit Abhiyan**: the **50% cap** applies to backward-class quotas.
The **76th (1994)** put Tamil Nadu's **69%** law in the **Ninth Schedule**.

135.s: Which amendment-clause pair is correctly matched?
135.x: The First Amendment, 1951 inserted Article 15(4). Article 16(4A) was inserted by the 77th Amendment, Article 16(4B) by the 81st, Article 15(5) by the 93rd and Article 16(6) by the 103rd Amendment.
135.tq: Start with the sure amendment-clause pair and eliminate the swapped clauses.
xs: **First Amendment — Article 15(4)** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Art. 15(4)** was added to overcome **Champakam Dorairajan**.
xa: **81st (2000)** = **Art. 16(4B)** backlog vacancies.
**85th (2001)** = **consequential seniority**, nullifying the "catch-up" rule.

135.s: Article 15(5) was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
135.x: The 93rd Amendment (2005) inserted Article 15(5), enabling reservation in educational institutions including private unaided ones, but excluding minority institutions.
xa: It overcame **P.A. Inamdar (2005)**.
It is the base for the **CEI Act, 2006** — **27% OBC** seats, in force **Jan 2007**.
GS **2007** key: the CEI Act rests on the **93rd Amendment**.

135.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: The 82nd Amendment concerns relaxation of qualifying standards in promotion for SCs and STs.
The 81st Amendment deals with unfilled backlog vacancies.
The 89th Amendment introduced the relaxation of qualifying marks under Article 335.
The 77th Amendment deals with reservation in promotion for SCs and STs.
135.x: The 89th Amendment did not introduce the relaxation of qualifying marks; that change was made by the 82nd Amendment Act, 2000. The 89th Amendment is associated with the bifurcation of the SC/ST Commission.
135.tq: Find the wrong amendment-provision association among closely related reservation amendments.
xs: The NOT-correct statement is that the **89th Amendment introduced relaxation of qualifying marks** — option **(3)**.
Relaxation (proviso to **Art. 335**) came by the **82nd (2000)**; the **89th** split the **SC/ST Commission**.
Other statements are correct: **81st** = backlog vacancies; **77th** = promotion reservation for SCs/STs.
xa: ⚠ APPSC G2 **2024** keyed relaxation to the "**89th**" — WRONG.
**85th (2001)**: consequential seniority.
**76th (1994)**: TN **69%** law in the **Ninth Schedule**.

135.s: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment–provision pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: 77th Amendment – Reservation in promotion under Article 16(4A)
81st Amendment – Backlog vacancies as a separate class
135.x: The 82nd Amendment inserted the proviso to Article 335 on relaxing qualifying marks; consequential seniority came with the 85th.
xa: The **85th (2001)** nullified the "**catch-up**" rule.
**77th (1995)** answered **Indra Sawhney**.
**81st**: backlog vacancies sit outside the **50%** ceiling.

135.s: The 76th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1994 is associated with which one of the following?
o: Inserting Article 16(4A) for reservation in promotion
Placing Tamil Nadu's 69 per cent reservation law in the Ninth Schedule
Giving constitutional status to the NCBC
135.x: The 76th Amendment (1994) placed Tamil Nadu's 69 per cent reservation law in the Ninth Schedule. Article 16(4A) came through the 77th (1995), consequential seniority through the 85th (2001), and constitutional status of the NCBC through the 102nd (2018).
135.tq: 76th = TN 69% in Ninth Schedule; 77th = 16(4A).
xs: The **76th (1994)** put **Tamil Nadu's 69%** reservation law in the **Ninth Schedule** — option **(2)**.
**Art. 16(4A)** = **77th (1995)**; consequential seniority = **85th (2001)**; NCBC status = **102nd (2018)**.
xa: Indra Sawhney: total reservation **not above 50%** except in extraordinary cases.
SC reserved verdict on TN's BC (Muslim) quota for converts (8 Aug 2026).
**103rd (2019)**: **10% EWS** — over and above existing reservation.

135.s: The 93rd Constitutional Amendment (2005), which inserted Article 15(5) enabling reservation in admissions including private institutions, was enacted to overcome which judgment?
135.x: Article 15(5) was inserted by the 93rd Amendment to overcome P.A. Inamdar (2005), which had barred quotas in private unaided institutions; it excludes minority institutions and is the basis of the CEI Act, 2006. Indra Sawhney concerns Mandal, M. Nagaraj promotion reservation, Janhit Abhiyan EWS.
135.tq: 93rd -> 15(5) -> overcame P.A. Inamdar -> CEI Act 2006.
xs: The **93rd (2005)** inserting **Art. 15(5)** overcame **P.A. Inamdar (2005)** — option **(2)**.
**Art. 15(5)** covers admissions incl. **private aided or unaided** institutions, **excluding minority institutions**.
**Indra Sawhney** concerns the Mandal quota; **Janhit Abhiyan (2022)** upheld **EWS**.
xa: Art. 15(5) is the base for the **CEI Act, 2006**.
**Jaishri Patil** → answered by the **105th (2021)**.
**Champakam Dorairajan** → answered by **Art. 15(4)**.

135.s: The Union Government opposed applying the creamy-layer principle to SCs and STs on the ground that their status flows from
135.x: In August 2026, the Union Government opposed the proposal, stating that SC/ST status flows from Articles 341 and 342.
135.tq: Discriminate between closely related constitutional provisions concerning reservations and community identification.
xs: The Union opposed SC/ST creamy layer because their status flows from **Articles 341 and 342** — option **(1)**.
**Arts. 338B and 342A** relate to the **NCBC** and **SEBC** lists (**102nd**), not SCs/STs.
**Arts. 15 and 16** are the reservation-enabling clauses.
xa: CJI **B.R. Gavai** had backed SC creamy layer (**Nov 2025**).
OBC creamy-layer income limit: **₹8 lakh** (**2017**).
**Art. 16(4A)** (**77th**) gives promotion reservation to SCs/STs.

135.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 102nd Constitutional Amendment from the 105th Constitutional Amendment?
o: The 102nd introduced EWS reservation, while the 105th abolished Article 342A.
The 102nd created constitutional status for the NCBC and inserted Article 342A, while the 105th restored States’ power to identify and list SEBCs.
The 102nd restored State power over SEBC lists, while the 105th created the NCBC.
The 102nd created the first Backward Classes Commission, while the 105th repealed the NCBC Act, 1993.
135.x: The 102nd Amendment Act, 2018 inserted Articles 338B and 342A and gave constitutional status to the NCBC. The 105th Amendment Act, 2021 restored the power of States to identify and list SEBCs.
135.tq: Separate the institutional change made by the 102nd Amendment from the federal-list change made by the 105th.
xs: **102nd** gave the **NCBC** constitutional status and inserted **Art. 342A**; the **105th** **restored States' power** to identify and list SEBCs — option **(2)**.
EWS came through the **103rd (2019)**, not the 102nd; the first BC commission was **Kalelkar (1953)** under **Art. 340**.
The 105th answered **Jaishri Patil**; it did not create the NCBC.
xa: The statutory **NCBC Act 1993** was **repealed** in **2018**.

135.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the 50 per cent ceiling referred to in the context of reservation from EWS reservation?
o: The ceiling applies to backward-class reservations, whereas EWS reservation was provided additionally under Articles 15(6) and 16(6).
The ceiling applies only to reservations in promotions.
The ceiling applies exclusively to EWS reservation.
The ceiling was abolished by the 103rd Amendment.
135.x: The 50 per cent ceiling discussed in this context relates to backward-class reservations. EWS reservation was introduced additionally through Articles 15(6) and 16(6).
135.tq: Separate the general reservation ceiling from the constitutional source of EWS reservation.
xs: The **50%** ceiling applies to **backward-class** reservations; EWS was added **additionally** under **Articles 15(6) and 16(6)** — option **(1)**.
**Janhit Abhiyan (2022)**: the **50% cap** applies to backward-class quotas.
The ceiling comes from **Indra Sawhney** and was not abolished; it is not limited to promotions.
xa: EWS is **over and above** / in addition to existing reservation.
Indra Sawhney: **carry-forward** allowed within **50%**, year by year.
**81st (2000)**: backlog vacancies sit outside the **50%** ceiling.

135.s: According to the Indra Sawhney judgment, the backward classes referred to in Article 16(4) are to be identified mainly on the basis of:
135.x: Indra Sawhney held that backward classes under Article 16(4) are identified mainly by caste and social backwardness, not by economic criteria alone.
135.tq: Indra Sawhney: caste can be the starting point for backwardness under 16(4).
xs: **Indra Sawhney**: **Art. 16(4)** backward classes are identified mainly by **caste and social backwardness** — option **(1)**.
It held **caste can be the main criterion** of backwardness, overruling **Balaji** on this.
Income alone is not the test; it is used to exclude the **creamy layer**, which Indra Sawhney introduced.
xa: Indra Sawhney fixed the **50%** ceiling except in extraordinary cases, applied year by year.
It confined reservation to **initial appointment**, not promotion → answered by the **77th** (**Art. 16(4A)**).
It directed a **permanent statutory body** for OBC lists → the **NCBC**.

135.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Indra Sawhney judgment?
o: Caste may be the main criterion for backwardness.
OBC reservation was extended to promotions as a general rule.
The creamy layer among OBCs should be excluded.
Total reservation should ordinarily not exceed 50 per cent.
135.x: Indra Sawhney confined reservation to initial appointments, not promotions.
xa: The **77th (1995)** answered it with **Art. 16(4A)** — promotion reservation for SCs/STs.
Indra Sawhney directed a **permanent statutory body** → the **NCBC**.
**Carry-forward** allowed within the **50%** ceiling, applied year by year.

135.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the categories associated with the OBC creamy layer under the Indra Sawhney framework?
o: All children of persons belonging to OBC communities, irrespective of social or economic status
Children whose parents are both Class-II officers
135.x: The framework identifies specified socially advanced categories, including children of Class-I officers and parents who are both Class-II officers. It does not exclude all OBC children irrespective of their circumstances.
135.tq: Reject the sweeping option that converts specified exclusions into a universal exclusion.
xs: NOT a creamy-layer category: **all children of OBC persons irrespective of social or economic status** — option **(2)**.
The creamy layer excludes only **socially advanced** OBCs — specified status groups and high earners.
Included: children of **constitutional post-holders**, **Class-I officers**, and parents **both Class-II**.
xa: Also excluded: senior govt and **armed-forces** officers, **property owners/large landowners**.
Income limit: **₹8 lakh a year** (**2017**).
Origin: **Indra Sawhney**; criteria via **DoPT OM Sept 1993**.

135.s: The Sukhdev case concerning backward-class reservation in Andhra Pradesh resulted in which of the following conclusions?
o: Caste alone could not be the basis, and 112 classes were identified using poverty, residence and occupation.
All reservation for backward classes was unconstitutional.
Caste alone could be the basis for identifying backward classes.
Reservation could be based only on residence.
135.x: The High Court held in the Sukhdev case that caste alone could not be the basis; consequently, 112 classes were listed using poverty, residence and occupation as considerations.
135.tq: Link the judicial principle with the resulting classification exercise.
xs: **Sukhdev case (HC)**: **caste alone** cannot be the basis → **112** classes listed on **poverty, residence and occupation** — option **(1)**.
It did not strike down all BC reservation, nor rest on residence alone.
xa: After **1956**: separate BC lists for **Andhra (86 castes)** and **Telangana**.
**1963 GO**: **25%** medical seats for **139** castes.
⚠ Contrast: **Indra Sawhney** held caste **can** be the main criterion.

135.s: The OBC creamy-layer criteria in the DoPT Office Memorandum of September 1993 were based on the report of the:
135.x: The creamy-layer criteria were framed through the DoPT Office Memorandum of September 1993, based on the Justice R.N. Prasad Expert Committee.
xa: Status exclusions: children of **constitutional post-holders**, **Class-I officers**, parents both **Class-II**.
The creamy layer itself originated in **Indra Sawhney**.

135.s: The income ceiling for determining the OBC creamy layer, after the 2017 revision and described as still current, is
135.x: The income ceiling was revised to ₹8 lakh per annum in 2017 and is stated to remain current.
135.tq: Distinguish the latest threshold from earlier figures in the revision sequence.
xs: The OBC creamy-layer ceiling since **2017** is **₹8 lakh per annum** — option **(1)**.
Earlier limits: **4.5 lakh (2008)**, **6 lakh (2013)** — now outdated.
xa: ⚠ **₹8 lakh** = OBC creamy-layer limit = **EWS** income ceiling.
**AP** aligned its State/public-sector definitions with the central threshold.

135.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Kapu reservation proposal?
o: The Justice Manjunatha Commission was constituted in 2016.
In 2019, Kapus got 5% within the EWS quota, later withdrawn.
A 2017 Bill proposed 5% reservation for Kapus as BC-F.
The Centre approved the 2017 BC-F proposal.
135.x: The Centre never approved the 2017 BC-F proposal.
xa: Kapu demand and **BC-E** Muslim quota are AP's **live issues**.
AP BC shares: **A 7%, B 10%, C 1%, D 7%, E 4%**.
EWS: enabling, **not mandatory** for States.

135.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the B.P. Mandal Commission?
o: It was the second Backward Classes Commission.
It was constituted by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
135.x: The Mandal Commission was set up through the Ministry of Home Affairs, not Social Justice and Empowerment; it identified 3,743 backward castes and recommended 27% for OBCs.
n: The B.P. Mandal Commission was the second Backward Classes Commission. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The B.P. Mandal Commission was constituted by the Ministry of Home Affairs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The B.P. Mandal Commission identified 3,743 backward castes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The B.P. Mandal Commission recommended 27% reservation for OBCs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The B.P. Mandal Commission concerned Other Backward Classes (OBCs). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
xa: It **formulated 11** social, educational and economic indicators; OBCs = **52%** of population.
The **27%** quota was implemented by **V.P. Singh** in **1990**.
The **Rohini Commission** (**2017**) was set up by Social Justice and Empowerment.

135.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Union of India v. Rohith Nathan?
o: The Court held that parental salary alone determines creamy-layer status.
The Court ordered the creation of supernumerary posts.
The verdict was delivered on 11 March 2026.
In August 2026, the Centre sought clarification on 958 CSE-2025 candidates.
135.x: The Court held that parental salary alone cannot place a candidate in the creamy layer.
xa: The SC is likely to set up a **special Bench** on it.
Creamy-layer limit: **₹8 lakh** (**2017**), via **DoPT OM** framework of **Sept 1993**.
Status exclusions include **Class-I officers** and parents both **Class-II**.

135.s: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act was introduced in Parliament as the:
135.x: It originated as the 124th Amendment Bill and inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6) for 10% EWS reservation.
xa: In force **January 2019**; upheld in **Janhit Abhiyan (7 Nov 2022)** by **3:2**.
EWS is **over and above** existing reservation.
States: enabling, **not mandatory**.

135.s: For the States, EWS reservation under the 103rd Constitutional Amendment is:
o: Mandatory only for State educational institutions
Mandatory only for State government posts
135.x: The amendment enables up to 10% EWS reservation outside SC/ST/OBC quotas but does not make it mandatory for States.
xa: EWS criteria: income **below ₹8 lakh**, **5 acres** farm land, **1,000 sq ft** flat.
Applies to jobs and education, incl. **private** central institutions.
⚠ **₹8 lakh** = OBC creamy-layer limit (**2017**) = EWS ceiling.

135.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about EWS reservation under the 103rd Amendment?
o: It applies to central educational institutions.
It applies to posts under the Central Government.
It extends to private educational institutions.
It is compulsory for State Governments.
135.x: Implementation of EWS reservation is not mandatory for State Governments.
xa: EWS is for those **not covered** by SC/ST/OBC quotas.
Upheld in **Janhit Abhiyan** by a **five-judge** bench (**3:2**).

135.s: For determining EWS eligibility, which one of the following combinations correctly represents the income and asset criteria stated for the purpose?
o: Annual family income below ₹5 lakh, land below 2 acres and flat below 800 sq ft
Annual family income below ₹8 lakh, agricultural land below 10 acres and flat below 1,000 sq ft
Annual family income below ₹8 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and flat below 1,000 sq ft
Annual family income below ₹10 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and flat below 1,500 sq ft
135.x: The stated EWS criteria include annual family income below ₹8 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and a flat below 1,000 square feet.
135.tq: Match the numerical threshold with the associated land and dwelling limits.
xs: EWS criteria: family income **below ₹8 lakh**, farm land below **5 acres**, flat below **1,000 sq ft** — option **(3)**.
Option (2) has the wrong land limit; options (1) and (4) have wrong income figures.
xa: ⚠ **₹8 lakh** is also the **OBC creamy-layer** limit since **2017**.
EWS: **10%**, over and above existing reservation.
Creamy-layer ladder: **₹1 lakh (1993)** → **₹8 lakh (2017)**.

135.s: In Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India, the 103rd Constitutional Amendment was upheld by a majority of:
135.x: The EWS amendment was upheld 3:2, with Chief Justice U.U. Lalit and Justice S. Ravindra Bhat dissenting.
xa: It held the **50% cap** applies to backward-class quotas.
103rd = **124th Amendment Bill**.

135.s:
Assertion (A): BC reservation in Andhra Pradesh local bodies was reduced to 24.15 per cent under GOs 176, 559 and 560.
Reason (R): N.T. Rama Rao introduced a 20 per cent BC quota in local bodies in 1984.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
135.x: Both are correct, but the 1984 introduction of the quota does not explain its later reduction from 34 to 24.15 per cent.
xa: The earlier **34%** was struck down for breaching the overall ceiling.
Current: **34% rural** + **33.33% urban** (19 Aug 2026).
**G.O. Rt. No. 1065** governs ULB polls.

135.s: The Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006, providing 27 per cent OBC reservation, came into force in:
135.x: Although enacted in 2006, the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act came into force in 2007.
135.tq: Separate the enactment year from the commencement year.
xs: The **CEI (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006** came into force in **Jan 2007** — option **(3)**.
It gives **27% OBC** seats in central institutions; based on **Art. 15(5)** (**93rd, 2005**).
**2006** is the enactment year, **2005** the 93rd Amendment year — not the commencement.
xa: GS **2007** key: **93rd Amendment** underlies the CEI Act.
**Oversight Committee (M. Veerappa Moily, 2006)** expanded seats (about **54%**, phased).

135.s: The BC-E category in Andhra Pradesh was added through which measure and in which year?
135.x: BC-E was added by the Andhra Pradesh Act of 2007. Earlier lists commonly included only BC-A to BC-D.
135.tq: Match the category’s introduction with the specific legal instrument and year.
xs: **BC-E** was added by the **2007 Andhra Pradesh Act** — option **(1)**.
⚠ CDX lists only **BC-A to BC-D**.
**1984** = NTR's **20%** local-body BC quota; **2010** = AP HC struck the 2007 Act down; **2019** = EWS.
xa: BC-E share: **4%**, for socially and educationally backward **Muslims**.
Earlier **5%** quotas (**2004 and 2005**) were struck down by the **AP High Court**.
The **Supreme Court** let the 2007 quota continue by **interim order** pending a **Constitution Bench**.

135.s: Which commission was the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission and framed the A-D grouping along with a 25 per cent quota?
135.x: The Anantharaman Commission was the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission; its report was submitted in 1970 and it framed the A-D grouping and a 25 per cent quota.
135.tq: Identify the commission from its distinctive first-commission and grouping role.
xs: The **Anantharaman Commission** was the first AP BC Commission (report **1970**), framing **A-D** grouping and a **25%** quota — option **(1)**.
**Mandal** was national (**1979**); **Muralidhara Rao** took charge **27 Jan 1982**; **Manjunatha (2016)** was on **Kapus**.
xa: **Muralidhara Rao** reviewed BC reservation and examined inclusion of minorities.
**BC-E** added later by the **2007** Act.
National first commission: **Kalelkar (1953)**.

135.s:
The Supreme Court’s triple test for OBC reservation in local bodies requires:
1. A dedicated commission to examine backwardness.
2. Determination of the reservation proportion local-body-wise.
3. Keeping the total reservation within the 50 per cent ceiling.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
135.x: All three requirements form the triple test: a dedicated commission, local-body-wise proportional determination, and compliance with the overall 50 per cent ceiling.
135.tq: Recognise a judicial test as a cumulative set of mandatory conditions.
xs: All three are part of the **triple test** — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
**Dedicated commission** + **local-body-wise proportion** + total **within 50%**.
xa: AP's earlier **34%** was struck down for breaching the overall ceiling.
Current AP: **34% rural**, **33.33% urban**.
**Indra Sawhney**: **50%** ceiling except in extraordinary cases.

135.s: Which of the following statements about the expression “Backward Classes” in the Constitution is correct?
o: It is exhaustively defined in Article 15.
It is defined in Article 340 itself.
It is defined only in the Fifth Schedule.
It is not defined in the Constitution.
135.x: The Constitution does not define the expression “Backward Classes”; constitutional provisions instead provide mechanisms concerning their identification and welfare.
135.tq: Test the exact constitutional status of a frequently misattributed definition.
xs: "**Backward Classes**" is **not defined in the Constitution** — option **(4)**.
APPSC G2 **2017** key: the statement saying it is "defined" was the wrong one.
**Art. 340** only lets the **President** appoint a commission to investigate their conditions — it does not define the term.
xa: Under **Indra Sawhney**, **Art. 16(4)** backward classes are identified mainly by **caste/social backwardness**.
Correct term = **Socially and Educationally** Backward Classes (SEBCs).
For the **CEI Act**, OBCs are classes "so determined by the **Central Government**".
**Art. 366(26C)** defines SEBCs by reference to **Art. 342A**.

135.s: Which clause was added to the Constitution to overcome the judgment in State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan?
135.x: Article 15(4) was inserted by the First Amendment, 1951 to overcome Champakam Dorairajan. Article 16(4) was in the original Constitution; Article 15(5) came by the 93rd Amendment (2005) and Article 16(4B) by the 81st (2000).
135.tq: Champakam Dorairajan -> 1st Amendment -> 15(4).
xs: **Article 15(4)** was added to overcome **Champakam Dorairajan** — option **(1)**.
**Art. 15(5)** = **93rd** (to overcome **P.A. Inamdar**); **Art. 16(4B)** = **81st** (backlog).
xa: Exam angle: "which article was added to overcome Champakam Dorairajan" → **15(4)**.
**Art. 16(4A)**: promotion reservation (**77th**).

135.s: Which expression correctly expands SEBC in the context of Articles 342A and the 105th Amendment?
135.x: SEBC means Socially and Educationally Backward Classes. The expression 'Socially and Economically Backward Classes' is not the constitutional expansion used here.
135.tq: Test the exact official phrase rather than a familiar but altered expansion.
xs: SEBC = **Socially and Educationally Backward Classes** — option **(1)**.
⚠ IYB's "**Socially and Economically**" is WRONG.
xa: **Art. 366(26C)** defines SEBCs by reference to **Art. 342A**.
**105th (2021)** restored **States' power** to list SEBCs.
**Art. 15(5)** covers **SEBCs, SCs, STs** in admissions.

135.s: All following statements regarding Backward Classes are correct, except?
o: The word ' Backward Classes of Citizens ' is defined in the Constitution
The Backward Classes contemplated under Art 16 (4) are mainly social. It need not be both social and educational
By clause (10) of the Article 338 " Backward Classes " are included within expression " Scheduled Caste "
Indra Sawhney case is related to " Backward Classes "

135.s: Which one of the following has a status different from the other three?
135.x: The National Human Rights Commission is a non- Constitutional body, while the other three (Appointment of a commission to investigate the condition of Backward Classes - Article 340, National Commission for Backward Classes- Article 338 B, Finance Commission- Article 280 and Election Commission- Article 324) are the Constitutional bodies. 77. Which among the following is NOT correctly matched? Bodies Establishment (a) Inter-state Council - 1990 (b) National Development - 1954 Council (c) Central Vigilance - 1964 Commission (d) National Human Rights - 1993 Commission U.P. R.O./A.R.O. (Mains) 2016 Ans. (b) The correctly matched order is as follows : Bodies Establishment (a) Inter-state Council - 1990 (b) National Development - 1952 Council (c) Central Vigilance - 1964 Commission (d) National Human Rights - 1993 Commission

135.s: By which Constitutional Amendment OBCs have been given 27 percent reservation in the admission to educational institutions?
135.x: The 93rd Amendment Act (passed in 2006) provided OBCs with 27% reservation in admission to educational institutions.

135.s: Mandal Commission, whose proposals created massive dispute, was set up by-
135.x: The Mandal Commission was constituted in India in 1979 by the Janata Party Government under former Prime Minister Morarji Desai with a mandate to “identify the socially and educationally backward persons.” It was headed by an Indian Parliamentarian, Bindheshwari Prasad Mandal.

135.s: The Report of Mandal Commission was submitted in-
135.x: In 1979, the Janta Party Government constituted the Mandal Commission presided over by Bindheshwari Prasad Mandal (B.P. Mandal). The Commission submitted its report in 1980.

135.s: Which of the following Constitutional Amendments provided rights for making provisions in favour of the SCs and STs for relaxation of qualifying marks in any examination (or) lowering the standards of evaluation and for reservation in the matter of promotions to the public services of the Centre 89. As and the State?
Under which Amendment Act was the reservation in promotion for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes ensured by inserting Clause '4A' in Article 16?
135.x: The 77th Amendment Act, 1995 ensured the reservation in promotion for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes by inserting clause (4A) in the Article- 16.

135.s: Which one of the following States has proposed reservation for Muslims in jobs and education ?
135.x: The government of Andhra Pradesh provided reservations to Muslims for jobs and education in 2004 this was cancelled by the Andhra Pradesh High Court. Later in 2007, the Government of Andhra Pradesh limited the reservation for Muslims to 4 per cent in accordance with 50% limit, but it was again cancelled by the High Court. Nevertheless, the Supreme Court', through its interim decision', accepted the reservation made by the Andhra Pradesh Government. But the final decision is still awaited as the matter is pending before the Constitutional Bench of the Supreme Court.

136.s: In tribal usage, the term ‘Diku’ refers to:
o: An outsider-exploiter such as a moneylender, trader, landlord or contractor
136.x: Diku denotes an outsider-exploiter, including a moneylender, trader, landlord or contractor.
136.tq: Distinguish the exact social meaning of a culturally specific term.
xs: **Diku** = an **outsider-exploiter** — **moneylender, trader, landlord or contractor** — option **(4)**.
**Birsa's Ulgulan** targeted British land-grabbing and the **dikus**.
xa: **Abua Raj** = aim of Birsa's **Ulgulan**; **Dharti Aaba** = title of **Birsa Munda**.
**Nistar** = a **community right** under the FRA (with grazing, fishing).
**Marang Buru** = **Parasnath Hills** as revered by **Santhals**.

136.s: The Forest Conservation Rules, 2022 became a subject of dispute between the NCST and the Environment Ministry because they:
o: Added a compulsory tribal veto over every forest diversion
Dropped the forest-dwellers’ consent clause before forest diversion
Prohibited all development projects in forest areas
Transferred all forests to Gram Sabhas
136.x: The 2022 Rules dropped the consent clause of forest-dwellers before forest diversion, leading to a dispute between the NCST and the Environment Ministry.
136.tq: Identify the precise legal change behind an institutional dispute.
xs: The **Forest Conservation Rules 2022** **dropped the forest-dwellers' consent clause** before forest diversion — option **(2)**.
This set the **NCST** against the **Environment Ministry**.
xa: MoEFCC guidelines had barred diversion until FRA processes (esp. **Gram Sabha consent**) were complete.
MoTA letter (**31 Aug 2026**): FRA has **"no provision"** for Gram Sabha consent for **Stage-II** clearance.
**Niyamgiri (2013)**: **Dongria Kondh** gram sabhas rejected bauxite mining → project cancelled.

136.s: Who identified political autonomy, recognition of identity and control over resources as objectives of modern tribal movements?
136.x: T. K. Oommen identified political autonomy, identity recognition and control over resources as objectives of modern tribal movements.
xa: Approaches: **isolation** (early **Elwin**), **assimilation** (**Ghurye**, **N.K. Bose**), **integration** (**Nehru**).
Birsa's Ulgulan aimed at **Abua Raj**.
⚠ Elwin = early **isolation**, later **integration** with Nehru.

136.s: The first principle of Nehru's Panchsheel for tribal development is to:
o: Develop tribal people along the lines of their own genius
Impose a uniform administration on all tribal areas
Measure progress by the money spent
Assimilate tribal people rapidly into mainstream culture
136.x: The first principle is to develop tribal people along their own genius, respecting their distinct capacities and culture.
xa: Principle 2: respect tribal **rights in land and forests**.
Principle 3: train **tribal people for their own administration**.
⚠ CDI lists "encourage **tribal languages**" separately; standard wording keeps it inside principle 1.

136.s: Which of the following is NOT a Panchsheel principle for tribal development?
o: Tribal rights in land and forests should be respected
Tribal people should be relied upon and trained for their own administration
Administration should be minimised and conducted through tribal institutions
Results should be judged by money spent rather than by the quality of human character evolved
136.x: Panchsheel requires results to be judged by the quality of human character evolved, not by money spent; the other three are Panchsheel principles.
xa: Principle 1: develop **along their own genius**.
Source: Nehru's foreword to Elwin's **A Philosophy for NEFA**.
Nehru's approach = **integration**.

136.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC)?
o: It was set up in 2001 by splitting the joint SC/ST corporation
It lends to STs with income up to three times the poverty line
It runs the Adivasi Mahila Sashaktikaran Yojana
136.x: NSTFDC lends to STs with income up to double, not three times, the poverty line.
xa: NSTFDC forest-dweller scheme: **90%** of cost at **6%** for FRA title-holders.
**25th Foundation Day** on **10 April 2026**.
⚠ **NSFDC** (**1989**) is for **SCs**; **NSKFDC** (**1997**) implements **NAMASTE**.

136.s: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was set up as a separate Union Ministry in:
136.x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was set up in 1999. 2001 is the year NSTFDC was set up, 2004 is when NCST began functioning, and 1989 is the year NSFDC was set up.
136.tq: MoTA 1999 -> NSTFDC 2001 -> NCST 2004.
xs: The **Ministry of Tribal Affairs** was set up in **1999** — option **(2)**.
xa: MoTA is the **nodal ministry** for the **FRA** (UPSC **2021**).
TSP monitoring moved to MoTA in **January 2017**.
**TRIFED** handles tribal marketing via "**Tribes India**".

136.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article 338A was created by the:
136.x: Article 338A was inserted by the 89th Constitutional Amendment, 2003; NCST functions from 19 February 2004 with civil-court powers.
xa: ⚠ The **89th** split the SC/ST commission into NCSC and NCST.
**2022** dispute: NCST vs Environment Ministry over **Forest Conservation Rules**.
NCST is part of the ST-inclusion chain: State → **RGI** → **NCST** → Cabinet → Parliament.

136.s: Raising farm output with improved seeds and fertilisers, planting fruit-bearing trees and other income-raising activities in tribal areas are objectives of:
136.x: Agricultural improvement, fruit-bearing plantations and other income-generating activities in tribal areas are objectives of TADP/ITDA.
xa: **ITDA Project Officers** + DSTW monitor health schemes in ITDA areas.
TSP adopted in the **5th Plan (1974)**.

136.s: Monitoring of the Tribal Sub-Plan moved from the Planning Commission to the Ministry of Tribal Affairs in:
136.x: TSP monitoring shifted to MoTA in January 2017; online monitoring now covers the ST component of 41 ministries.
xa: TSP adopted in the **5th Plan (1974)**.
Funds over and above **normal plan flows**.

136.s: PM-AJAY, launched in 2021-22, is administered as a centrally sponsored intervention by which Union Ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
136.x: PM-AJAY was launched in 2021-22 as a 100 per cent centrally funded scheme under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
136.tq: Identify the correct ministry and distinguish the SC-focused scheme from tribal-area programmes.
xs: **PM-AJAY** (**2021-22**) is under the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment**, **100% central** — option **(2)**.
⚠ It targets **SC** poverty — not STs, so MoTA is wrong (APPSC G1 **2024**).
xa: It merged **SCA to SCSP + PMAGY + BJRCY**.
**Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana** (SC hostels) is now part of PM-AJAY.
**NAMASTE** is under **MoSJE + MoHUA**.

136.s: The nodal Ministry for implementation of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 is the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
136.x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is the nodal ministry for the Forest Rights Act, 2006.
136.tq: Use the who-is-responsible test to distinguish the nodal ministry from ministries involved in implementation.
xs: The **Ministry of Tribal Affairs** is the **nodal ministry** for the **FRA 2006** — option **(1)** (UPSC **2021**).
**MoEFCC** handles forest diversion; it was asked by MoTA for **CFR funds** (**12 Jan 2026**).
xa: FRA aims to undo the "**historical injustice**" and **overrides** inconsistent laws.
MoTA letter (**31 Aug 2026**): FRA has "no provision" for Gram Sabha consent for **Stage-II** clearance.
MoTA was set up in **1999**.

136.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about processing of claims under the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
o: The Gram Sabha passes resolutions on claims
Claims are examined by Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees
Each of these committees consists of nine members
The committees include revenue, tribal and forest officials and elected panchayat members
136.x: The Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees are six-member bodies, not nine-member; the other statements are correct.
xa: FDST cut-off: occupation **before 13 December 2005**.
OTFD: **3 generations (75 years)** of residence/dependence.
Ceiling: up to **4 hectares per family**.

136.s: Which of the following is NOT recognised as a forest right under the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
o: Automatic ownership of all mineral resources beneath forest land
Habitat rights for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups
136.x: The Act recognises rights such as minor forest produce, community forest resource management and PVTG habitat rights. It does not confer automatic ownership of all mineral resources beneath forest land.
136.tq: Find the option outside the statutory list of individual and community forest rights.
xs: NOT an FRA right: **automatic ownership of all mineral resources** beneath forest land — option **(1)**.
FRA rights list: **ownership of MFP**, **habitat rights for PVTGs**, **community forest resources** management, biodiversity/traditional knowledge.
xa: Individual rights: land, **habitation**, **self-cultivation**.
Community rights: **nistar**, **grazing**, fishing, **CFR** management.
⚠ **Samatha (1997)**: mining leases in Scheduled Areas to private non-tribals are **void**.

136.s: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 sought to undo the historical injustice done to:
136.x: The Act recognises forest rights of Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers, with the stated objective of undoing historical injustice to forest dwellers.
xa: Nodal ministry: **Tribal Affairs** (UPSC **2021**).
The Act **overrides** inconsistent laws.
Beneficiaries: **FDST** and **OTFD**.

136.s: A forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribe family claims recognition of rights under the Forest Rights Act. Which date is relevant for determining occupation of forest land?
136.x: Forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes must have been occupying the forest land before 13 December 2005 for eligibility under the stated cut-off criterion.
136.tq: Treat the cut-off date as a direct numerical-recall point and reject nearby constitutional or enactment dates.
xs: The cut-off for FDSTs is occupation **before 13 December 2005** — option **(3)**.
FDSTs must be **living in, dependent on and occupying** forest land before that date.
xa: **OTFDs** need **3 generations (75 years)** of residence before **2005**.
Ceiling: up to **4 ha** per family.
Claims start with the **Gram Sabha** (**Sec. 6**).

136.s: For recognition under the Forest Rights Act, Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must establish residence in or dependence on forests for:
136.x: Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must show residence in or dependence on forests for three generations, specified as 75 years, before 2005.
136.tq: Separate the generation requirement from the ST cut-off date and convert it into the stated year equivalent.
xs: OTFDs need **three generations or 75 years** — option **(3)**.
FDSTs instead need occupation **before 13 December 2005**.
xa: OTFD = **Other Traditional Forest Dwellers**; FDST = **Forest-dwelling STs**.
Ceiling: up to **4 hectares per family**.
Committees: **six-member** Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees.

136.s: What is the maximum extent of forest rights that may be recognised per family under the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
136.x: The ceiling for forest rights is up to four hectares per family.
136.tq: Test the statutory ceiling directly using close numerical distractors.
xs: The FRA ceiling is up to **4 hectares** per family — option **(1)**.
For public utilities (schools, dispensaries), diversion is up to **1 ha per project** on **Gram Sabha** recommendation.
xa: Individual rights: land, habitation, self-cultivation.
Titles (**2025-26**): **23.92 lakh individual + 1.22 lakh community**.
AP: **2,26,651** individual titles approved (APSES **2024-25**).

136.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with an individual forest right rather than a community forest right?
136.x: Habitation and self-cultivation are individual rights. Nistar, grazing, fishing and community forest resource management are examples of community rights.
136.tq: Separate individual and community rights by identifying the beneficiary and nature of use.
xs: **Habitation and self-cultivation** are **individual** rights — option **(1)**.
**Grazing**, **fishing** and **CFR management** are **community** rights.
xa: Community rights also include **nistar**.
Other rights: **ownership of MFP**, **habitat rights for PVTGs**.
⚠ Implementation gap: focus on **individual titles over CFR**.

136.s: Which of the following correctly states the relationship between the Forest Rights Act, 2006 and inconsistent laws?
o: The Act is subordinate to every earlier forest law
The Act applies only where no State law exists
The Act overrides laws that are inconsistent with it
The Act can be overridden by an executive circular alone
136.x: The Forest Rights Act overrides laws that are inconsistent with its provisions.
136.tq: Watch for the reversed legal relationship between the Act and inconsistent laws.
xs: The FRA **overrides laws inconsistent with it** — option **(3)** (UPSC).
It is not subordinate to earlier forest laws.
xa: Purpose: undo the **"historical injustice"** to forest dwellers.
**FCA linkage**: diversion barred until FRA processes complete — upheld by the **Supreme Court**.
⚠ MoTA letter (**31 Aug 2026**): FRA has "no provision" for Gram Sabha consent for **Stage-II** clearance.

136.s: The first Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group stated to have received habitat rights under the Forest Rights Act framework was:
136.x: Bharia of Madhya Pradesh was the first PVTG mentioned as receiving habitat rights; Kamar and Baiga of Chhattisgarh followed.
136.tq: Use the first-in-sequence trap to distinguish Bharia from the later Kamar and Baiga claims.
xs: The first PVTG to get habitat rights was the **Bharia of Madhya Pradesh** — option **(1)**.
**Kamar and Baiga** (Chhattisgarh) came **after** Bharia.
⚠ The **UPSC 2018** claim that **Baigas** were first is **false**.
xa: Habitat rights follow **2014 MoTA guidelines**.
**Four** State departments (Forest, Revenue, Tribal, Panchayati Raj) coordinate, with **UNDP** help.
**PM-JANMAN** covers **75 PVTGs**.

136.s: Under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, 'nistar' is classified as a/an:
136.x: Nistar, grazing, fishing and ownership and disposal of minor forest produce are listed community rights under the FRA.
xa: **Bamboo** is an MFP under the FRA (UPSC **2019**).
**Nistar** = a community right.
**TRIFED** gives **MSP for MFP**.

136.s: Critical Wildlife Habitat under the Forest Rights Act refers to areas of national parks and sanctuaries that are to be:
o: Transferred exclusively to private conservation agencies
Kept inviolate after an open process involving affected communities
Opened for mining after approval by the Forest Department
136.x: Critical Wildlife Habitats are areas within national parks and sanctuaries to be kept inviolate, and they are notified after an open process with affected communities.
136.tq: Distinguish the legal definition from an assumed blanket exclusion of communities.
xs: **Critical Wildlife Habitats** are areas of national parks/sanctuaries **kept inviolate** after an **open process with affected communities** — option **(3)**.
They are defined and notified under the **FRA** (UPSC **2018**).
xa: ⚠ **Critical tiger habitats** (WPA) need **mandatory Gram Sabha consultation**.
**Agasthyamalai**: eviction orders ignored the FRA (**11 Aug 2026**).
The FRA overrides inconsistent laws.

136.s: Which one of the following statements regarding bamboo under the Forest Rights Act is correct?
o: Bamboo is a tree in every location and cannot be collected by forest dwellers.
Bamboo is a minor forest produce, and ownership is vested in forest dwellers.
Bamboo is excluded from minor forest produce and belongs only to the Forest Department.
Ownership of bamboo is vested only in Gram Panchayats.
136.x: The Forest Rights Act treats bamboo as a minor forest produce and vests its ownership in forest dwellers.
136.tq: Separate the FRA status of bamboo from its treatment under the Indian Forest Act amendment.
xs: **Bamboo is a minor forest produce** under the FRA, with **ownership vested in forest dwellers** — option **(2)**.
UPSC **2019** key: this was the correct statement.
xa: **IFA (Amendment) 2017** removed bamboo grown **outside forest areas** from "tree".
⚠ IFA 2017 did **not** give a right to fell bamboo in forest areas.
**TRIFED** gives **MSP for MFP**.

136.s: The Indian Forest (Amendment) Act, 2017 did which of the following?
o: Removed bamboo grown outside forest areas from the definition of “tree”.
Granted an unrestricted right to fell bamboo in forest areas.
Removed all bamboo from the definition of minor forest produce.
Transferred ownership of all bamboo to private companies.
136.x: The 2017 amendment removed bamboo grown outside forest areas from the definition of “tree”. It did not confer a right to fell bamboo in forest areas.
136.tq: Watch for the false extension from bamboo outside forests to bamboo inside forests.
xs: **IFA (Amendment) 2017** **removed bamboo grown outside forest areas** from the definition of "**tree**" — option **(1)**.
⚠ It did **not** give a right to fell bamboo in forest areas — that comes from the **FRA**.
xa: Under the FRA, **bamboo is MFP**, owned by forest dwellers.
UPSC **2019**: statement on IFA right to fell = false.
**PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission** buys MFP at **MSP**.

136.s: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding forest diversion after the Forest Rights Act?
o: Completion of FRA processes is a prerequisite before forest diversion under the FCA
Forest diversion is permissible before completion of FRA claims if the project is of public importance
Gram Sabha consent is relevant to the FRA process
Niyamgiri saw Gram Sabha rejection of bauxite mining
136.x: MoEFCC guidelines barred forest diversion under the FCA until FRA processes, especially Gram Sabha consent, were complete, a position upheld by the Supreme Court.
xa: **Forest Conservation Rules 2022** dropped the forest-dwellers' consent clause.
**Stage-II** row: MoTA said FRA has "no provision" for consent (**31 Aug 2026**).
Implementation gap: **JFMC/CAMPA** projects bypassing Gram Sabhas.

136.s: Which of the following is NOT a reported gap in Forest Rights Act implementation?
o: Excessive focus on individual titles over CFR
Strong MoTA capacity ensuring complete CFR implementation
136.x: The identified gap is weak, not strong, MoTA capacity; the other three are reported implementation gaps.
xa: Over **47,900** CFR/CFRR claims rejected.
⚠ **Forest Conservation Rules 2022** dropped prior consent.
**Agasthyamalai** evictions ignored the FRA.

136.s: Under the RFCTLARR Act, 2013, Social Impact Assessment is:
o: Required only for private projects and never for public projects
Replaced by a census of affected families
136.x: The RFCTLARR Act, 2013 makes Social Impact Assessment mandatory.
136.tq: Identify the statutory requirement without being distracted by exceptions not stated in the law summary.
xs: Under **RFCTLARR 2013**, **Social Impact Assessment** is **mandatory** — option **(2)**.
It is not optional in Scheduled Areas — there it applies along with **Gram Sabha** consent.
xa: Consent: **80% (private)**, **70% (PPP)** affected families.
Scheduled Areas: acquisition = **last resort**, with **Gram Sabha/Panchayat/Autonomous Council** consent.
**District Mineral Foundation** uses RFCTLARR's "affected" and "displaced" definitions.

136.s: In Scheduled Areas, acquisition under the RFCTLARR Act is treated as a last resort and requires consent of which body or bodies?
o: Only the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
Gram Sabha, Panchayat or Autonomous Council, as applicable
136.x: Acquisition in Scheduled Areas is a last resort and requires consent from the Gram Sabha, Panchayat or Autonomous Council, as applicable.
136.tq: Identify the local self-governing body rather than a supervisory or advisory institution.
xs: In Scheduled Areas, acquisition is a **last resort** and needs **Gram Sabha/Panchayat/Autonomous Council consent** — option **(4)**.
The **District Mineral Foundation** only uses RFCTLARR definitions of affected/displaced families.
xa: Consent: **80%** private, **70%** PPP.
**PESA** areas: at least **50%** seats to STs and **all chairpersons are STs**.
AP: **2,038** notified PESA Gram Sabhas (**AP PESA Rules 2011**).

136.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: TRIFED — 1987 — tribal marketing and MSP for Minor Forest Produce
Roshni — 2018 — residential schools for SC students
VDVKs — 2013 — skills and jobs in LWE districts
PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission — 1987 — sanitation mechanisation
136.x: TRIFED was established in 1987 and is associated with tribal marketing and MSP for Minor Forest Produce. The other options interchange the purposes or years of different programmes.
136.tq: Start from the distinctive year-purpose pair and eliminate cross-matched programmes.
xs: **TRIFED — 1987 — tribal marketing and MSP for MFP** is correctly matched — option **(1)**.
**Roshni** = skills and jobs for tribal youth in **LWE** districts (**MoRD, 2013**).
**VDVKs** = **2018**; **PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission** = **2021-22** (MFP at MSP, not sanitation).
xa: TRIFED brand: "**Tribes India**".
VDVKs: **4,172** nationally; AP **415** sanctioned.
Sanitation mechanisation = **NAMASTE**.

136.s: The PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission, associated with 2021-22, is run by TRIFED and includes which set of activities?
o: Civil Services coaching, NETS testing and residential schooling
PPE distribution, sewer profiling and sanitation stipends
Land purchase, pension payments and free electricity
Buying MFP at MSP, value addition and GI tags
136.x: The PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission is run by TRIFED and focuses on buying Minor Forest Produce at MSP, value addition and GI tags.
136.tq: Match the programme with its sector-specific activity cluster.
xs: **PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission** (**2021-22**, TRIFED): **buys MFP at MSP, value addition, GI tags** — option **(4)**.
Civil Services coaching = **DACE**; NETS = **SHRESHTA**; PPE/sewer profiling = **NAMASTE**.
xa: **VDVKs (2018)**: about **15** SHGs of up to **20** gatherers.
TRIFED brand: "**Tribes India**".
AP: **GCC Araku Valley Coffee** trademarked (**2024-25**).

136.s: Roshni is a programme for:
o: Free coaching for SC students in Central Universities
MSP procurement from all farmers in border districts
Mechanised cleaning of septic tanks in urban areas
Skills and jobs for tribal youth in Left-Wing Extremism districts
136.x: Roshni, associated with the Ministry of Rural Development and 2013, provides skills and employment opportunities for tribal youth in LWE districts.
136.tq: Use the target group, geography and purpose together to identify the programme.
xs: **Roshni** = skills and jobs for **tribal youth in LWE districts** (**MoRD, 2013**) — option **(4)**.
Free coaching for SC students in Central Universities = **DACE**; septic-tank mechanisation = **NAMASTE**.
xa: **DACE** launched **22 April 2022** at **Banaras Hindu University**.
**PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission**: MFP at MSP.
**VDVKs**: at least **60% ST**.

136.s: Eklavya Model Residential Schools are a Central Sector scheme under the:
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
136.x: EMRS is a Central Sector scheme under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.
136.tq: Apply the ministry-ownership trap to a residential education scheme.
xs: **EMRS** is a **Central sector** scheme of the **Ministry of Tribal Affairs** — option **(2)**.
It is modelled on **Navodaya Vidyalayas** and run through **NESTS**.
xa: Started **1997-98**; target **740** schools.
**511** schools with **1.68 lakh** students (Aug 2026).

136.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about scholarships for SC and ST students?
o: The Post-Matric Scholarship for SCs is the largest central scheme for SC students
ST pre-matric and post-matric scholarships are centrally sponsored schemes
National Fellowship, Top Class and National Overseas are central sector schemes
The cost of the SC Post-Matric Scholarship is shared in the ratio 75:25
136.x: The SC Post-Matric Scholarship cost is shared in the ratio 60:40, not 75:25; the other statements are correct.
xa: National Overseas: **20** awards (**17 ST + 3 PVTG**).
National Overseas income limit: **Rs 6 lakh**.
**SHRESHTA** places SC students in top residential schools via **NETS**.

136.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Stand-Up India?
o: It is meant exclusively for existing enterprises
Every bank branch is to lend to at least one SC/ST and one woman borrower
It is administered by the Ministry of Finance
136.x: Stand-Up India supports greenfield enterprises; it is not meant exclusively for existing enterprises.
xa: Loans: **Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore**; up to **85%** of project cost; repay over **7** years.
**SIDBI** refinance.
**2.75 lakh** loans worth **Rs 62,790 crore** by March 2025.

136.s: The Dr Ambedkar Centres of Excellence provide free Civil Services coaching to:
136.x: The Dr Ambedkar Centres of Excellence give free Civil Services coaching to SC students in Central Universities.
xa: Launched **22 April 2022** at **Banaras Hindu University**.
**SHRESHTA**: SC students in top residential schools via NTA's **NETS**.
**Post-Matric Scholarship for SCs**: largest central SC scheme, **60:40** cost-sharing.

136.s: Which body purchases minor forest produce at fair prices, runs PDS depots and gives credit to tribal farmers in Andhra Pradesh?
136.x: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation (GCC) purchases MFP at fair prices, runs PDS depots and provides credit to tribal farmers.
xa: GCC set up in **1956**.
"**GCC Araku Valley Coffee**" brand trademarked.
TRIFED markets via "**Tribes India**".

136.s:
Assertion (A): MoTA sought MoEFCC funds for managing Community Forest Resource areas vested in Gram Sabhas.
Reason (R): Eviction orders in Agasthyamalai were criticised for ignoring the Forest Rights Act.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
136.x: Both statements are true, but they are separate issues: the CFR funding request is not explained by the criticism of the Agasthyamalai eviction orders.
xa: STs about **9%** of population but **over 50%** of displaced.
**Forest Conservation Rules 2022** dropped prior consent.
Over **47,900** CFR/CFRR claims rejected.

136.s: In August 2026, which Ministry stated that the Forest Rights Act has no provision for Gram Sabha consent for Stage-II forest clearance?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
136.x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs stated in August 2026 that the FRA has no provision for Gram Sabha consent for Stage-II forest clearance.
xa: The **Parliamentary Committee on Public Undertakings** called consent a project bottleneck.
Opposition (**Congress**) called it an abdication of MoTA's **nodal role**.
Earlier MoEFCC guidelines barred diversion until **FRA processes** complete.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about the Forest Rights Act, 2006:
1. It recognises individual and community forest rights.
2. These rights are recognised for forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
136.x: Both are correct: the Act recognises individual and community forest rights of forest-dwelling STs and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers.
n: The Forest Rights Act was passed in 2006. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Forest Rights Act recognizes individual forest rights for forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Forest Rights Act recognizes community forest rights for forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Forest Rights Act recognizes individual forest rights for Other Traditional Forest Dwellers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Forest Rights Act recognizes community forest rights for Other Traditional Forest Dwellers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
xa: The FRA aims to undo the **"historical injustice"** to forest dwellers; nodal ministry: **Tribal Affairs**.
FDST cut-off: occupying forest land **before 13 December 2005**.
OTFDs must show **3 generations (75 years)** of dependence.
Ceiling: up to **4 hectares per family**.

136.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Forest Rights Act is correctly matched?
o: Rights vested – Individual and community forest rights
136.x: The FRA was passed in 2006, came into force on 31 December 2007, had its rules notified on 1 January 2008, and vests individual and community forest rights.
n: The Forest Rights Act was enacted in 2006. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Forest Rights Act came into force on December 31, 2007. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The rules under the Forest Rights Act were notified on January 1, 2008. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Forest Rights Act vests individual forest rights in forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Forest Rights Act vests community forest rights in forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Forest Rights Act vests individual forest rights in Other Traditional Forest Dwellers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
The Forest Rights Act vests community forest rights in Other Traditional Forest Dwellers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #50 · pp 102-103]
xa: **Sec. 6**: the **Gram Sabha** initiates determination of rights.
**Six-member** Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees examine claims.
Community rights include **nistar**, **grazing**, fishing and **CFR** management.

136.s: Which is the nodal ministry for the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan?
136.x: Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan is led by Tribal Affairs, which converges the work of several line ministries to bring basic facilities to tribal-majority villages.
136.tq: Match each scheme to its lead ministry.
n: The nodal ministry for Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan is the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan is a key scheme for Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
xs: The nodal ministry for **Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan** is **Tribal Affairs** — option **(4)**.
It seeks **comprehensive saturation** of **basic infrastructure** in about **63,000** tribal-majority villages.
xa: Launched **Sept 2024**; outlay **Rs 79,156 crore**; **17** ministries converge.
AP has **4** DAJGUA hostels.
**Birsa Munda** bore the title **Dharti Aaba**.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Sickle Cell Elimination Mission:
1. It is associated with the Ministries of Health & Family Welfare and Tribal Affairs.
2. It focuses on screening tribal populations.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
136.x: Both are correct: the Mission is run by Health & Family Welfare with Tribal Affairs and focuses on screening tribal populations.
n: The nodal ministries for the National Sickle Cell Elimination Mission are the Ministries of Health and Family Welfare and Tribal Affairs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
The National Sickle Cell Elimination Mission focuses heavily on screening tribal populations. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
The National Sickle Cell Elimination Mission is a key initiative for Scheduled Tribes. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
xa: Target: **elimination** of sickle cell anaemia by **2047**.
The **Sickle Cell Mission Portal** tracks **screening cards** in a **central registry**.

136.s:
Consider the following statements about PM-AJAY:
1. Its portal supports planning and monitoring of works in SC-majority Adarsh Grams.
2. It includes fund convergence.
3. It is a portal for tribal artisans to sell forest produce.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
136.x: 1 and 2 are correct: PM-AJAY plans, pools funds for and monitors works in SC-majority Adarsh Grams. 3 is wrong; the tribal artisans' marketplace is TRIFED/Tribes India.
n: The PM-AJAY Portal is a digital platform for Scheduled Castes (SC). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-AJAY Portal supports end-to-end planning of infrastructure works. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-AJAY Portal supports fund convergence for infrastructure works. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-AJAY Portal monitors infrastructure works. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-AJAY Portal covers SC-majority Adarsh Gram infrastructure works. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The TRIFED and Tribes India E-Marketplace are digital platforms for Scheduled Tribes (ST). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The TRIFED and Tribes India E-Marketplace provide a dedicated e-commerce gateway. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The TRIFED and Tribes India E-Marketplace connect tribal artisans directly to buyers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The TRIFED and Tribes India E-Marketplace connect forest-produce collectors directly to buyers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
xa: PM-AJAY Portal is run by the **Department of Social Justice and Empowerment**.
TRIFED also offers **MSP for Minor Forest Produce**.

136.s: Which of the following correctly represents the procedure for inclusion of a community as a Scheduled Tribe?
o: State proposal → Registrar General of India → NCST → Union Cabinet → Parliament amends the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950
NCST proposal → State Cabinet → President directly amends the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950
State proposal → Parliament → Registrar General of India → Supreme Court
Registrar General of India → State proposal → Union Cabinet → NCST
136.x: The stated sequence is proposal by the State, examination by the Registrar General of India and NCST, consideration by the Union Cabinet, and amendment by Parliament under Article 342(2).
136.tq: Follow the institutional sequence from initiation to the final constitutional amendment authority.
xs: Procedure: **State proposal → Registrar General of India → NCST → Union Cabinet → Parliament** amends the **Constitution (ST) Order 1950** — option **(1)**.
Parliament acts under **Art. 342(2)**; the President does not amend the list directly, and the Supreme Court has no role in it.
The **State** starts the process — the RGI comes second, not first.
xa: **Art. 366(25)** defines Scheduled Tribes.
ST status is **religiously neutral** (RPSC **2010** key).
**NCST** functions from **19 Feb 2004** under **Art. 338A** (**89th Amendment 2003**).

136.s: The term 'Scheduled Tribes' is defined in which provision of the Constitution of India?
136.x: Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes. Article 342(2) lets Parliament modify the ST list, Article 338A creates the NCST, and Article 244(1) applies the Fifth Schedule to Scheduled Areas.
136.tq: Definition = 366(25); list change by Parliament = 342(2).
xs: Scheduled Tribes are defined in **Article 366(25)** — option **(2)**.
**Art. 342(2)**: Parliament modifies the **ST list**; **Art. 338A**: the **NCST**.
xa: ST inclusion: State → **Registrar General of India** → NCST → Cabinet → Parliament.
The **Fifth Schedule** and **Art. 244** protect Scheduled Areas (cited in the **Parasnath Hills** debate).
ST status is **religiously neutral** (RPSC **2010**).

136.s: Which of the following contributed to tribal indebtedness and land alienation during colonial rule?
136.x: Colonial moneylenders and revenue farmers contributed to indebtedness and land alienation, while restrictive forest laws cut tribals off from their habitats.
xa: **Displacement**: STs about **9%** of population but **over 50%** of the displaced.
Other problems: **low literacy**, language barriers, **malnutrition**, **forced labour**.
AP's **Regulation 1/70** presumes land belongs to tribals and bans transfers even between non-tribals.

136.s: Birsa Munda’s Ulgulan was directed against:
o: Only forest conservation by tribal institutions
The Panchsheel principles of tribal development
136.x: Birsa’s Ulgulan was aimed at British land-grabbing and the exploitative dikus.
136.tq: Match the movement with its principal targets.
xs: Birsa's **Ulgulan** was against **British land-grabbing and the dikus** — option **(4)**.
Its issues: **land-grabbing**, **forced labour**; aim **Abua Raj**.
xa: Dates: **1899-1900**; led to the **Chotanagpur Tenancy Act 1908**.
Birsa = **Dharti Aaba**; died in **Ranchi jail** (**1900**).
**15 November** (birth anniversary) is marked by the Union.

136.s: What was the outcome of the Niyamgiri bauxite-mining proposal in 2013?
o: It was approved after the Forest Rights Act process was waived.
It was approved after consent from the State legislature.
Dongria Kondh Gram Sabhas rejected the mining under the FRA, and the project was cancelled.
It was transferred to private pumped-storage projects.
136.x: In 2013, Dongria Kondh Gram Sabhas rejected bauxite mining under the Forest Rights Act, after which the project was cancelled.
136.tq: Apply the Gram Sabha consent principle to the Niyamgiri outcome.
xs: **Niyamgiri (2013)**: **Dongria Kondh** Gram Sabhas **rejected bauxite mining** under the FRA → **project cancelled** — option **(3)**.
The FRA process was not waived; Gram Sabhas decided.
xa: MoEFCC guidelines barred diversion until **FRA processes** were complete.
AP: soil sampling for bauxite permitted in **Chintapalli and G.K. Veedhi** mandals.
**Samatha (1997)**: private mining leases in Scheduled Areas **void**.

136.s: Under the RFCTLARR Act, 2013, the consent requirement is what percentage of affected families for private projects and public-private partnership projects, respectively?
136.x: Consent of 80% of affected families is required for private projects and 70% for PPP projects.
136.tq: Keep the private-project and PPP thresholds in the correct order.
xs: RFCTLARR consent: **80% (private)** and **70% (PPP)** — option **(4)**.
Option (2) reverses the two figures.
xa: **Social Impact Assessment** is mandatory.
**PVTG** habitats get legal protection under it.
STs = about **9%** of population but **over 50%** of the displaced.

136.s: The NAMASTE scheme is implemented by:
136.x: NAMASTE, associated with MoSJE and MoHUA, is implemented by NSKFDC with an allocation of Rs 349.70 crore; TRIFED is not its implementing agency.
xa: Capital subsidy up to **Rs 7.5 lakh**; **25%** subsidy on machines.
Skilling with **Rs 3,000** stipend.
NSKFDC was set up in **1997**.

136.s: The Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation, 1959, primarily seeks to:
o: Bar transfer of land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals
Transfer all Scheduled Area land to the Union Government
Facilitate transfer of tribal land to private mining companies
136.x: Regulation 1 of 1959 bars the transfer of land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals.
136.tq: Test the core legal prohibition against a set of plausible policy reversals.
xs: **Regulation 1 of 1959** **bars land transfer in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals** — option **(2)**.
It does the opposite of facilitating transfer to private mining firms.
xa: **1/70** amendment: presumption that land belongs to **tribals**; bans transfers even between **non-tribals**.
**Samatha (1997)** enforced the **1959** Regulation (amended **1970**).
A challenge to **1/70** is **pending in the Supreme Court**.

136.s: Which one of the following correctly states the effect of the 1970 amendment to the Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation?
o: It applied only to urban municipal areas
It removed the restriction on tribal land transfers to non-tribals
It permitted all transfers if approved by a private company
It added a presumption that the land belongs to tribals and prohibited transfers even between non-tribals
136.x: The 1970 amendment added a presumption that the land belongs to tribals and prohibited transfers even between non-tribals.
136.tq: Use the precise legal consequence to reject the reversed effect.
xs: **Regulation 1 of 1970** added a **presumption that land belongs to tribals** and banned transfers **even between non-tribals** — option **(4)**.
It tightened, not removed, the restriction.
xa: Challenge to 1/70 **pending in the Supreme Court**.

136.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The definition of "Critical Wildlife Habitat is incorporated in the Forest Rights Act, of 2006.
2. For the first time in India, Baigas have been given Habitat Rights.
3. Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change officially decides and declares Habitat Rights for Primitive and Vulnerable Tribal Groups in any part of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x: Statement 1 is correct: The phrase 'critical wildlife habitat' is defined only in the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006. CWH are defined under the act as the "areas of national parks and sanctuaries where it has been specifically and clearly established, case by case, on the basis of scientific and objective criteria, that such areas are required to be kept as inviolate for the purposes of wildlife conservation". Inviolate is a general term used to indicate no human settlement or usage. Statement 2 is correct: The Baiga community in Madhya Pradesh became the first tribe in India to receive habitat rights under the Forest Rights Act of 2006. Statement 3 is incorrect: The process involves District Level Committee (DLC), Gram Sabha, State Government, and Ministry of Tribal Affairs, not MoEFCC. PMF Concept Hack: India has a dedicated Ministry of Tribal Affairs for tribal welfare, so it is highly unlikely that the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change would independently decide and declare Habitat Rights for tribal groups. Hence, Statement 3 can be eliminated. Once Statement 3 is removed, options containing 3 are also eliminated, leaving Statements 1 and 2 as correct.

136.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. As per recent amendment to the Indian Forest Act, 1927, forest dwellers have the right to fell the bamboos grown on forest areas.
2. As per the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, bamboo is a minor forest produce.
3. The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 allows ownership of minor forest produce to forest dwellers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
136.x: Statement 1 is incorrect: An amendment was made in 2017-18 in the Indian Forest Act of 1927 to remove bamboo from the category of trees. With this minor modification, bamboo grown in non-forest areas will not require a transit permit (TP) and other legal permits for felling and transportation from the forest department. However, bamboo grown in the forest would continue to require a TP and other legal permits. Statement 2 is correct: Minor Forest Produce (MFP) is a subset of forest produce and got a definition only in 2007 when the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, was enacted. Section 2(i) of the said Act defines a Minor Forest Produce (MFP) as all non-timber forest produce of plant origin and includes bamboo, brushwood, stumps, canes, Tusser, cocoon, honey, waxes, Lac, tendu/kendu leaves, medicinal plants and herbs, roots, tubers, and the like. Statement 3 is correct: The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, popularly known as the Forest Rights Act (FRA), was enacted in 2007. The Act recognises and vests individual forest-dwellers with forest rights to live in and cultivate forest land that was occupied before 13 December 2005, and grants community forest rights to manage, protect, and regenerate the forest, and to own and dispose of minor forest products from forests where they had traditional access. Individuals, communities and gram sabhas have right
