138.s: Protection of children against exploitation and moral and material abandonment is provided under:
138.x: Article 39(f) guards against exploitation and moral and material abandonment; Article 39(e) protects tender age from abuse.
xa: **National Policy for Children 2013**: everyone below **18** is a child; best interests first.
The **NCPCR** (**2007**, **CPCR Act 2005**) monitors **POCSO**, the **JJ Act** and the **RTE Act**.
The Criminal Law Amendment Act **2013** widened the trafficking definition; it is now **Section 143, BNS 2023**.

138.s: Under the POCSO Act, an offence committed by a person in a position of trust is treated as
o: an offence applicable only to institutions
138.x: The Act treats offences committed by a person in a position of trust as aggravated offences.
138.tq: Test the legal consequence attached to a special relationship of trust.
xs: An offence by a person in **trust or authority** is an **aggravated** offence — option **(4)** is correct.
Examples: **police**, **security forces**, **public servant**.
xa: POCSO offences: **penetrative** and **non-penetrative** assault, aggravated forms, **sexual harassment**, **child pornography**.
**2019**: aggravated penetrative assault minimum **20 years**, up to **life or death penalty**.
Penetrative sexual assault minimum: **10 years**.

138.s: The 21 April 2018 Ordinance relating to the POCSO Act primarily provided for
o: replacement of mandatory reporting with voluntary reporting
harsher punishment for rape of young girls
lowering the age of a child to 14 years
138.x: The Ordinance of 21 April 2018 introduced harsher punishment for rape of young girls.
138.tq: Match the dated legislative measure with its principal substantive change.
xs: The **21 April 2018** Ordinance provided **harsher punishment for rape of young girls** — option **(2)** is correct.
POCSO still keeps **mandatory reporting**, **Special Courts** and the age of **18**.
xa: **2019 Amendment**: penetrative assault minimum **10 years**; aggravated minimum **20 years**; up to **death penalty**.
**POCSO Rules 2020** replaced the 2012 Rules.
The 2018 date was asked by APPSC.

138.s: Which of the following correctly describes the 2019 amendment to the POCSO Act?
o: It introduced the death penalty for aggravated penetrative assault and prescribed a minimum punishment of 20 years
It removed the punishment of imprisonment for aggravated penetrative assault
It made all POCSO offences compoundable
It reduced the minimum punishment to 7 years
138.x: The 2019 amendment provided for the death penalty in aggravated penetrative assault cases and prescribed a minimum punishment of 20 years. The POCSO Rules were framed in 2020.
138.tq: Use the precise punishment figures to distinguish the amendment from neighbouring provisions.
xs: The **2019** amendment brought the **death penalty** for **aggravated penetrative assault** and a minimum of **20 years** — option **(1)** is correct.
It raised punishments, so options (2) and (4) are wrong; the penetrative minimum is **10 years**, not 7.
xa: ⚠ **10** = penetrative minimum; **20** = aggravated minimum.
Storing child pornography without deleting/reporting: fine at least **Rs 5,000**; repeat **Rs 10,000**.
It also punishes giving **chemicals to hasten sexual maturity**.
**POCSO Rules 2020** replaced the 2012 Rules.

138.s: Under the POCSO Act, consent of a person below ____ years is legally irrelevant.
138.x: POCSO fixes the relevant age at 18 years, so apparent consent below 18 is irrelevant.
xa: The **MP High Court** asked the Centre to lower it to **16** (APPSC **2022**).
SC in **State of UP v. Anurudh** urged a **"Romeo-Juliet" clause**.

138.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the POCSO Act is correctly matched?
o: Sections 29–30 – Burden of proof on the accused
Section 19 – Burden of proof on the accused
138.x: Sections 29–30 place the burden of proof on the accused; Section 19 concerns mandatory reporting and Section 22 false complaints.
xa: Failure to report: up to **6 months** and/or fine.
Anyone, **including a child**, who knows of an offence must report it.
⚠ Investigation **2 months**; trial **1 year**; non-reporting up to **6 months**.

138.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the trial framework under the POCSO Act?
o: Trial before the High Court within one month without compensation provisions
In-camera trial, with investigation targeted within two months and trial within one year
Open trial within two years after investigation by any police station
Trial only before a Juvenile Justice Board within six months
138.x: POCSO provides for in-camera proceedings, investigation within two months and trial within one year; special courts also address compensation and rehabilitation.
138.tq: Combine the court type and statutory time limits without reversing them.
xs: POCSO provides an **in-camera trial**, investigation within **two months** and trial within **one year** — option **(2)** is correct.
Trials are before **Special Courts**, not the High Court or a JJB, and are not open.
Special Courts also provide **compensation and rehabilitation**.
xa: Statement recorded preferably by a **woman police officer (at least SI)**, **not in uniform**.
No child kept at a police station at night; no contact with the accused.
**Disposals** of cases are up (**109%**) but convictions are falling.

138.s: The POCSO Act came into force on:
138.x: POCSO came into force on 14 November 2012; the 2019 amendment set a 10-year minimum for penetrative sexual assault.
xa: Aggravated penetrative assault: minimum **20 years**, up to **death penalty**.
The **21 April 2018** Ordinance brought harsher punishment for rape of young girls.
Full name: **Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012**.

138.s: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 retains 18 years as the age of consent under Section:
138.x: BNS Section 63 retains 18 years as the age of consent.
xa: **Standing Committee on Home Affairs, 167th Report (2012)** backed **18**.
**Law Commission 283rd Report (2023)**: lowering would make POCSO a **"paper law"**.
⚠ APPSC **2022** keyed as "true" that the committee recommended lowering the age from **18**.

138.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Supreme Court's decision on the Calcutta High Court ruling on adolescent relationships?
o: The Supreme Court set aside the Calcutta High Court ruling
The Calcutta High Court ruling had excluded consensual adolescent relationships from POCSO
The Supreme Court used Article 142 for sentencing flexibility
The Supreme Court itself excluded consensual adolescent relationships from POCSO
138.x: The Supreme Court set aside the High Court ruling that had excluded consensual adolescent relationships from POCSO; it did not create such an exclusion itself.
xa: In **State of UP v. Anurudh** the SC flagged **misuse of POCSO** and urged a **"Romeo-Juliet" clause**.
Debate: **close-in-age exemption** vs keeping the age at **18** with judicial discretion.
SC: child assessments must involve **"minimum intrusion"** where the child is an alleged abuse victim.

138.s: The age of consent under POCSO should not be confused with the legal age of marriage, which is:
o: 18 years for women and 21 years for men
21 years for women and 18 years for men
18 years for women and 18 years for men
16 years for women and 18 years for men
138.x: The age of consent under POCSO is 18 years. The legal marriage age referred to here is 18 years for women and 21 years for men.
138.tq: Separate two closely related but legally distinct age thresholds.
xs: The marriage age is **18 for women and 21 for men** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is distinct from the age of consent under POCSO, which is **18** for all.
xa: NFHS-5: over **27%** of women aged **20-24** married before **18**; newer figure **23.3%**.
Child marriage is listed as **social** abuse.
**APSES 2024-25**: **877** child marriages prevented in AP.

138.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the age of consent under POCSO?
o: The Law Commission (283rd Report, 2023) recommended lowering the age of consent
The Standing Committee on Home Affairs (167th Report, 2012) supported retaining 18 years
The Law Commission warned that lowering the age could make POCSO a 'paper law'
The Supreme Court in January 2026 urged consideration of a Romeo-Juliet clause
138.x: The 283rd Law Commission Report warned against lowering the age, saying it could make POCSO a 'paper law'.
xa: The **Justice Verma Committee** wanted **16**.
The **240th Report** (**2011**, Standing Committee on HRD) rejected minor consent.
The **MP High Court** asked for **16**, citing social-media exposure.

138.s: Special Training Centres under the National Child Labour Project cater to rescued children of which age group?
138.x: NCLP Special Training Centres serve rescued children aged 9-14 with bridge education, vocational training, mid-day meal and a stipend.
xa: NCLP started in **1988**, under **MoLE**.
Process: **identification → rescue → rehabilitation**.
**India rescues**: **40,000+** children in **2024-25**.

138.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the POCSO Act, 2012?
o: It excludes stringent punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault.
It includes capital punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault.
It provides for child-friendly special courts.
138.x: POCSO (amended 2019) has stringent punishment, including death, for aggravated penetrative sexual assault; it also has special courts and mandatory reporting.
n: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act was passed in 2012. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act was amended in 2019. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act prescribes stringent punishments. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act provides capital punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act provides child-friendly special courts. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act mandates reporting. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
xa: 2019: penetrative assault minimum **10** years; aggravated minimum **20** years.
POCSO is **gender-neutral**; it came into force **November 14, 2012**.
Non-reporting: up to **6 months** and/or fine.

138.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the RTE Act?
o: It enforces Article 21A for children aged 6–14.
It came into force on 1 April 2010.
It mandates a 25% quota in private unaided schools for disadvantaged groups.
It mandates a 20% quota in private unaided schools for disadvantaged groups.
138.x: The RTE Act reserves 25%, not 20%, of seats in private unaided schools for disadvantaged children; it came into force on 1 April 2010.
n: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act came into force on April 1, 2010. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 101-102]
The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act enforces Article 21A for children aged 6–14 years. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 101-102]
The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act mandates a 25% quota in private unaided schools for disadvantaged groups. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 101-102]
xa: It aims at **universal elementary education**.
It **protects minority educational rights** under **Article 30**.
⚠ Child = below **18** (POCSO) vs below **14** (child labour) vs **6-14** (RTE).

138.s:
Consider the following statements about the POCSO Act:
1. Its 2019 amendment added capital punishment for aggravated penetrative assault.
2. It came into force on 14 November 2012.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
138.x: Both are correct: POCSO came into force on 14 November 2012 (Children's Day), and the 2019 amendment added the death penalty for aggravated penetrative assault.
n: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act came into force on November 14, 2012. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 101-102]
The 2019 amendment to the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act added capital punishment for aggravated penetrative assault. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #49 · pp 101-102]
xa: The amendment came on **August 16, 2019**.
POCSO was drafted by **MWCD**; it is **gender-neutral**.
Special courts: investigation in **2 months**, trial within **1 year**.

138.s: Which of the following is a legal provision of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012?
o: Internal Complaints Committees in workplaces with 10 or more employees
Mandatory crèche facility in establishments with 50 or more employees
138.x: POCSO makes reporting of child sexual offences mandatory. Maintenance Tribunals belong to the Senior Citizens Act, ICCs to POSH, and crèches to the Maternity Benefit amendment.
138.tq: Match each provision to its Act.
n: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act was passed in 2012. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act mandates reporting. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The POSH Act mandates Internal Complaints Committees in workplaces with at least 10 employees. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act was passed in 2017. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act mandates a crèche facility for establishments with at least 50 employees. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act was passed in 2007. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act establishes Maintenance Tribunals. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
xs: **Mandatory reporting** of offences is a POCSO provision — option **(1)**.
Under **Section 19**, anyone who knows of an offence must report it; failure invites up to **6 months** and/or fine.
xa: **Burden of proof** lies on the accused (**Sec. 29-30**).
**False complaints** are punishable (**Sec. 22**), except good-faith ones.
The child's statement is recorded preferably by a **woman police officer**, **not in uniform**.

138.s: Which of the following statements about the abusers identified in the Study on Child Abuse: India 2007 is correct?
o: All abusers were strangers to the child
Over 50% were known to the child or were in a position of trust
Less than 10% were known to the child or held a position of trust
The study found no relationship between trust and abuse
138.x: The study found that over 50% of abusers were known to the child or were in a position of trust.
138.tq: Use the relationship-of-trust finding to reject the stranger-only assumption.
xs: **Over 50%** of abusers were **known to the child or in a position of trust** — option **(2)** is correct.
So abusers were not "all strangers", nor "less than 10%" known, and trust clearly mattered.
xa: ⚠ NCRB **2021**: **97.1%** of child sexual-abuse offenders known to the child.
The MWCD **2007** study covered **13 states** and about **12,447 children**.
**Two out of three** children faced physical abuse.

138.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position of a child below 14 years after the 2016 amendment?
o: Employment is banned in all occupations and processes, subject to specified exceptions
Employment is banned only in mines and factories
Employment is permitted in all non-hazardous occupations without restriction
Employment is regulated only through the Right to Education Act
138.x: After the 2016 amendment, employment of children below 14 years is prohibited in all occupations and processes, subject to specified exceptions.
138.tq: Separate the post-amendment blanket prohibition from the earlier listed-work model.
xs: After **2016**, a child below **14** is **banned in all occupations and processes**, subject to exceptions — option **(1)** is correct.
The ban is linked to the **RTE** age.
xa: Exceptions: helping **family/family enterprise after school hours**; child **artist** in audio-visual entertainment (not circus).
**Adolescents** (**14-18**) are banned only from **hazardous** work.
⚠ 1986 = only **18** occupations, **65** processes banned.

138.s: The original 1986 law prohibited children below 14 years from employment in how many occupations and processes, respectively?
138.x: The original law listed 18 prohibited occupations and 65 prohibited processes for children below 14 years.
138.tq: Match the two numerical components without reversing their order.
xs: The **1986** Act banned children from **18 occupations and 65 processes** — option **(1)** is correct.
Other work was merely **regulated**, which clashed with the **RTE Act 2009**.
xa: ⚠ **83** was the number of entries in the earlier hazardous list, trimmed in **2016**.
Under the 1986 Act a child = one who has not completed **14 years**.
The **1986** year was asked in APPSC **2019**.

138.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016?
o: A child may help the family or family enterprise after school hours
Offences under the Act are cognizable
The child-artist exception applies only if schooling is not affected
A child may work as an artist in audio-visual entertainment, including circus
138.x: The audio-visual entertainment exception for child artists excludes circus.
xa: Child below **14**: banned in **all** occupations; adolescent **14-18**: banned in **hazardous** work only.
Penalty: **6 months-2 years** and/or **₹20,000-50,000**.
Fund: **Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund**.

138.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about enforcement under the amended child labour law?
o: Imprisonment may range from six months to two years
Offences under the Act are non-cognizable
The fine may range from ₹20,000 to ₹50,000
A Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund is established under the Act
138.x: The amendment made offences under the Act cognizable, not non-cognizable.
xa: Enforcement: **District Magistrate**.
Rules: **Amendment Rules 2017** notified by **MoLE**.
⚠ M.C. Mehta (**1996**): employer pays **₹20,000 per child** into a rehabilitation-cum-welfare fund.

138.s: The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016 introduced the category of 'adolescent'. Which of the following correctly describes it?
o: Persons aged 14-18, barred only from hazardous occupations and processes
Persons aged 14-18, barred from all occupations and processes
Persons aged 12-16, barred only from hazardous occupations
Persons aged 16-21, allowed in all occupations with parental consent
138.x: The 2016 amendment created the adolescent category (14-18), banned only from hazardous occupations and processes; children below 14 are banned from all occupations. Option B applies the child rule to adolescents, and C and D give wrong age bands.
138.tq: Below 14: total ban; 14-18 adolescents: hazardous ban only (2016).
xs: **Adolescents** are aged **14-18** and barred only from **hazardous occupations and processes** — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) applies the **child** rule (below **14**, all work banned) to adolescents.
Options (3) and (4) give wrong age bands.
xa: The adolescent category came only in **2016**.
Hazardous list: **mines**, **inflammable substances/explosives**, **hazardous processes**.
**Mines Act 1952** bars anyone below **18**.

138.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Gurupadaswamy Committee?
o: It was associated with the Ministry of Labour.
Its recommendations led to the 1986 Child Labour Act.
It recognised that child labour is tied to poverty.
It recommended regulating hazardous child labour and banning all other forms.
138.x: The Committee recommended banning hazardous child labour and regulating other forms, the reverse of the statement; that approach led to the 1986 Act.
n: The nodal ministry for the Gurupadaswamy Committee was the Ministry of Labour. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Gurupadaswamy Committee recognized that child labour is directly tied to poverty. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Gurupadaswamy Committee recommended banning hazardous child labour. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The Gurupadaswamy Committee recommended regulating other forms of child labour. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
The dual approach recommended by the Gurupadaswamy Committee led to the 1986 Child Labour Act. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #43 · pp 92-93]
xa: The 1986 Act banned only listed hazardous work (**18 occupations, 65 processes**).
The **2016** amendment banned all work below **14**.

138.s: Which of the following case–subject pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu – Child labour in hazardous industries
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India – Child trafficking and child begging
M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu – Consensual same-sex adult relationships
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India – Human-rights oversight of Child Care Institutions
138.x: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu dealt with hazardous child labour; consensual same-sex relations was the subject of Navtej Johar.
n: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India decriminalized consensual same-sex adult relationships. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu was decided in 1996. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu banned child labour in hazardous industries. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India was decided in 2011. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India issued guidelines against trafficking. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India issued guidelines against child begging. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India mandated human-rights oversight of all Child Care Institutions. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #46 · pp 96-98]
xa: **PUDR v. UoI** (**1982**): child labour in construction violates Fundamental Rights.
**Independent Thought** (**2017**): sex with a wife below **18** is statutory rape.

138.s:
Consider the following statements about the Child and Adolescent Labour Act, as amended in 2016:
1. It prohibits employing children below 14 in all occupations, except helping in family enterprises after school hours.
2. It prohibits employing adolescents aged 14–18 in hazardous occupations and processes.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
138.x: Both are correct: the 2016 amendment bans children under 14 from all occupations except family-enterprise help after school, and bars adolescents from hazardous work.
n: The Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act was passed in 1986. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act was amended in 2016. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act completely bans employing children below 14 in all occupations. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
The Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act regulates adolescents aged 14 to 18 working in hazardous conditions. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #40 · pp 87-89]
xa: The Act came into force **December 23, 1986**; amended **September 1, 2016**.
Offences are **cognizable**; punishment **6 months-2 years** and/or **₹20,000-50,000**.
Enforcement: **District Magistrate**.

138.s: After the IPC was replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita from 1 July 2024, the POCSO Act:
o: Was subsumed entirely into the BNS
Was merged with the Juvenile Justice Act
Continues as a separate special law
138.x: The IPC was replaced by the BNS from 1 July 2024, but POCSO continues as a separate special law.
xa: **BNS (Sec. 63)** keeps the age of consent at **18**.
Trafficking is now **Section 143, BNS 2023**.
POCSO was drafted by the **MWCD** and came into force on **14 November 2012**.

138.s: The Age of Consent Act, 1891 fixed the age of consent at:
138.x: The IPC 1860 fixed 10 years, the Age of Consent Act 1891 raised it to 12, the 1925 IPC amendment to 14, and POCSO 2012 to 18.
xa: The age was raised to **16** in **1949**.
**CLA 2013** also kept **18**; **BNS (Sec. 63)** keeps **18**.
⚠ Marriage age is distinct: **18** for women, **21** for men.

138.s: According to Census 2011, the number of child labourers in the 5–14 age group in India was approximately:
138.x: Census 2011 recorded approximately 10.1 million child labourers aged 5–14. The 4.35 million figure refers only to main workers.
138.tq: Separate the overall count from the narrower main-worker figure.
xs: **Census 2011**: about **10.1 million** child labourers aged **5-14** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **4.35 million** counts **main workers only**; **8 M** is the rural share.
xa: Split: **5.6 M boys**, **4.5 M girls**; about **8 M** rural, **2 M** urban — urban child labour is rising.
Decline **2001-2011**: only **2.2% a year** (CRY).
Global: **137.6 million** in **2024** (**54 M** in hazardous work).

138.s: The POCSO e-Box was launched in 2016 by the:
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
State Commission for Protection of Child Rights alone
Ministry of Home Affairs’ Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre
138.x: The POCSO e-Box was launched in 2016 by the NCPCR for online complaints of child sexual abuse.
138.tq: Apply the ‘who launched it?’ test to distinguish the NCPCR from cybercrime authorities.
xs: The **POCSO e-Box** was launched in **2016** by the **National Commission for Protection of Child Rights** (NCPCR) — option **(2)** is correct.
It takes **online complaints** of child sexual abuse.
xa: **NCPCR** is statutory, set up in **2007** under the **CPCR Act 2005**.
NCPCR monitors **POCSO**, the **JJ Act** and the **RTE Act**.
⚠ **cybercrime.gov.in** is run under **I4C, MHA** — not the e-Box.

138.s: The National Child Labour Project was started in:
138.x: The National Child Labour Project was started in 1988.
138.tq: Distinguish the NCLP’s start year from the years of the Gurupadswamy Committee and National Policy on Child Labour.
xs: The **National Child Labour Project** started in **1988** — option **(3)** is correct.
**1979** = Gurupadswamy Committee; **1987** = National Policy on Child Labour; **1992** = India acceded to the UNCRC.
xa: NCLP is under **MoLE**, not MoSJE (UPSC **2007** key).
**Special Training Centres** serve rescued children aged **9-14** with bridge education, vocational training, mid-day meal and stipend.
NCLP was **merged into Samagra Shiksha** from **2021-22**.

138.s: Which system provides a confidential, direct digital reporting window for children and guardians to report online and physical sexual abuse?
138.x: The POCSO e-Box (NCPCR) lets children and guardians report sexual abuse, online or offline, directly and in confidence.
138.tq: Match each portal to its issue.
n: POCSO E-Box addresses child abuse, including sexual and cyber abuse. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
POCSO E-Box provides a confidential digital reporting window. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
POCSO E-Box provides a direct digital reporting window. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
POCSO E-Box enables children to report abuse. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
POCSO E-Box enables guardians to report abuse. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
POCSO E-Box enables reporting of online sexual abuse. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
POCSO E-Box enables reporting of physical sexual abuse. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #38 · pp 84-86]
xs: The **POCSO E-Box** is a **confidential**, **direct digital reporting window** for children and guardians to report **online and physical sexual abuse** — option **(4)**.
It is associated with **MoWCD** and the **NCPCR**, launched in **2016**.
xa: Cyber abuse can also be reported on **cybercrime.gov.in** (**I4C**, MHA).
⚠ **POCSO e-Box** = NCPCR (**2016**); **PENCiL** = MoLE (**2017**).
**Operation Smile / Muskaan** (**2015**) trace and rescue missing children.

138.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of forms of social child abuse?
o: Infanticide, child marriage, child prostitution and beggary
Verbal battering, educational neglect and fostering delinquency
Drug abuse, stealing, school dropout and trauma
Beating, burning, medical neglect and nutritional neglect
138.x: Infanticide, child marriage, child prostitution and beggary are identified as forms of social abuse.
138.tq: Classify all items in a group and eliminate groups containing consequences or other abuse categories.
xs: **Infanticide, child marriage, child prostitution and beggary** are all forms of **social** abuse — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) lists **emotional/non-physical** abuse; option (4) lists **physical** abuse (commission and omission).
Option (3) lists **consequences** of abuse — deviant behaviour, school dropout and trauma — not forms of abuse.
xa: **Sexual abuse (CSA)** = using a child for sexual stimulation.
**IT Rules 2021** require large platforms to detect **CSAM** automatically.
Sectors of child labour: **brick kilns**, pesticide-heavy farm work, toxic chemicals, **tea stalls**, begging.

138.s: Which of the following is a cause of child abuse rather than a consequence?
138.x: Parental alcoholism is listed as a cause. Loss of self-esteem, trauma and school dropout are consequences.
138.tq: Separate the causes column from the consequences column before selecting the answer.
xs: **Parental alcoholism** is a **cause** of child abuse — option **(2)** is correct.
**School dropout**, **trauma** and **loss of self-esteem** are listed as **consequences** of abuse.

Section 4 of the National Food Security Act, 2013
139.x: PMMVY has its legal basis in Section 4 of the National Food Security Act, 2013.
139.tq: Distinguish a statutory basis from constitutional provisions and unrelated legislation.
xs: **PMMVY**'s legal basis is **Section 4** of the **National Food Security Act, 2013** (**Sec 4, NFSA 2013**) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Article 45** is about ECCE up to age **6**, not maternity benefit.
xa: PMMVY is the only cash maternity benefit written into the **NFSA**.
Launched **1 January 2017**; ministry **MWCD** (**Samarthya**).
Purpose: **wage-loss compensation**.

139.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with its nodal ministry?
o: JSSK — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
PMSMA — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
JSY — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
PMMVY — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
139.x: PMMVY is administered by the Ministry of Women and Child Development. JSY, JSSK and PMSMA are associated with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
139.tq: Apply the ministry-swapping trap, especially between JSY and PMMVY.
xs: **PMMVY** is under **MWCD**, not MoHFW — option **(4)** is the wrong pair.
**JSY**, **JSSK** and **PMSMA** are all **MoHFW** schemes.
xa: PMMVY sits under **Samarthya** (**Mission Shakti**).
Exam angle: **JSY** sits under **NHM**, while **PMMVY** sits under **MWCD**.
JSY is **100% centrally sponsored**.

139.s:
Assertion (A): Beti Bachao Beti Padhao is administered by the Ministry of Finance as a savings scheme.
Reason (R): The Ministry of Women and Child Development is the nodal ministry for BBBP, along with the Health and Education ministries.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
139.x: MWCD is nodal for BBBP with Health and Education; the Ministry of Finance savings scheme is Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana.
xa: BBBP has **no DBT and no asset creation**.
Launched **22 January 2015** at **Panipat**.
**100% central funding**; covers **all districts**.

139.s: Palna, the National Creche Scheme, is intended for children in which age group?
139.x: Palna covers children from 6 months to 6 years. Its creches may function whether or not the mother is employed, and 17,000 Anganwadi-cum-Creches were targeted.
139.tq: Use the exact age range to distinguish Palna from preschool and school-age programmes.
xs: **Palna** covers children **6 months-6 years** — option **(3)** is correct.
**3-8** is the **NEP 2020** foundational stage.
xa: Target: **17,000 Anganwadi-cum-Creches**.
Open **whether or not the mother is employed**.
⚠ ICDS also covers children **6 months-6 years**.

139.s: Which of the following statements regarding the PMMVY Soft Portal is incorrect?
o: It is a portal for employment listings for Divyangjan.
It is associated with the Ministry of Women & Child Development.
It facilitates cash benefit payout for pregnant and lactating mothers.
It supports Direct Benefit Transfer verification.
139.x: Option A is incorrect: job listings for Divyangjan are on PM-DAKSH. The PMMVY portal (WCD) verifies DBT and pays cash benefits to pregnant and breastfeeding mothers.
139.tq: Match each portal to its function.
n: The PM-DAKSH Portal provides skill development services. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-DAKSH Portal provides vocational training. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-DAKSH Portal provides employment listings. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PMMVY Soft Portal is a digital platform for women. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The Ministry of Women and Child Development is the nodal ministry for the PMMVY Soft Portal. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PMMVY Soft Portal verifies Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PMMVY Soft Portal enables cash-benefit payouts. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PMMVY Soft Portal serves pregnant mothers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PMMVY Soft Portal serves lactating mothers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the PMMVY portal lists **employment for Divyangjan** — option **(1)**.
The **PMMVY Soft Portal** belongs to **MWCD**, **verifies Direct Benefit Transfers** and pays **cash benefits** to **pregnant and lactating mothers**.
xa: PMMVY began **1 January 2017**; legal basis **Sec 4, NFSA 2013**.
Tagline: **"Matru Shakti Rashtra Shakti"**.
⚠ **₹5,000 in 3 instalments** is the old **PMMVY 1.0** design.

139.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
A. Launch of ICDS
B. Universalisation of ICDS
C. Introduction of the Mid-Day Meal Scheme
D. Introduction of Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0
139.x: ICDS was launched in 1975, the Mid-Day Meal Scheme came in 1995, ICDS was universalised in 2006, and Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 was introduced in 2021.
xa: **POSHAN Abhiyaan** was launched on **8 March 2018** at **Jhunjhunu**.
The mid-day meal was renamed **PM POSHAN** in **2021**.
**ICDS at 50 (2025)**: **1.4 million AWCs**; over **100 million** served.

139.s: The Scheme for Adolescent Girls under Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 covers which group?
o: Girls aged 14-18 years in Aspirational Districts and the North-Eastern Region
All boys and girls aged 6-14 years
Girls aged 10-14 years in all districts
Girls aged 15-19 years only in urban areas
139.x: The Scheme for Adolescent Girls covers girls aged 14-18 years in Aspirational Districts and the North-Eastern Region.
139.tq: Check both the age band and the geographical qualification; changing either creates a false option.
xs: The **Scheme for Adolescent Girls** covers girls aged **14-18** in **Aspirational Districts and the NER** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is now merged into **Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0**.
xa: Poshan 2.0 also merges **Anganwadi Services (SNP)** and **Poshan Abhiyaan**.
Nutrition support is one of the **three verticals**, incl. adolescent girls.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0:
1. It was introduced in 2021.
2. Its nodal ministry is the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
3. It is a Central Sector Scheme with no State contribution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Statement 1 is correct: it was introduced in 2021. Statement 2 is correct: MWCD is the nodal ministry. Statement 3 is wrong: it is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with 60:40 sharing (90:10 for NE/Himalayan States and J&K). So '1 and 2 only' is right; options with 3 are wrong.
139.tq: A Centre-State ratio like 60:40 means Centrally Sponsored, not Central Sector.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: it began in **2021**.
Statement 2 is correct: its ministry is **MWCD**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it is a **CSS** with **60:40** sharing (**90:10** for NE/Himalayan States and J&K).
xa: UTs without legislature: **100%** central funding.
**2 lakh** AWCs to be upgraded as Saksham Anganwadis at **40,000 a year**.

139.s: Which one of the following funding patterns is correctly matched under Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0?
o: North-Eastern and Himalayan States and Jammu and Kashmir — 90:10
139.x: North-Eastern and Himalayan States and Jammu and Kashmir receive funding in the 90:10 pattern. Union Territories without legislature are funded 100 percent by the Centre.
139.tq: Check the category-specific ratio and reject reversed funding patterns.
xs: **NE/Himalayan States and J&K** get **90:10** — option **(3)** is correct.
General States get **60:40**, not 90:10.
**UTs without legislature** get **100%** central funding, not 50:50 or 60:40.
xa: ⚠ **PM POSHAN** also uses **60:40**.
**Mission Vatsalya** is **60:40** too.
The scheme period is **2021-22 to 2025-26**.

139.s: Which of the following was NOT merged into Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 (2021)?
139.x: PM POSHAN is a separate school-meal scheme; Poshan 2.0 merged Anganwadi Services/SNP, POSHAN Abhiyaan and the Scheme for Adolescent Girls.
xa: ⚠ PM POSHAN = **Ministry of Education**; ICDS/Poshan 2.0 = **MWCD**.
Adolescent girls covered: **14-18**, Aspirational Districts and NER.
Introduced in **2021**.

139.s: POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched on which occasion and at which place?
139.x: POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched on 8 March 2018 at Jhunjhunu in Rajasthan.
139.tq: Use the date-place combination to distinguish the launch from later campaign events.
xs: **POSHAN Abhiyaan** was launched on **8 March 2018** at **Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **BBBP** was launched at **Panipat** in **2015**; **Varanasi** hosted the **9th Poshan Maah** (**2026**).
xa: It was earlier called the **National Nutrition Mission**.
Goal: **Suposhit Bharat**, a **Jan Andolan**.
Mission goal: cut stunting to **25%** by **2022**.

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding POSHAN Abhiyaan:
1. Its mission goal included reducing stunting to 25 percent by 2022.
2. It seeks to build a Suposhit Bharat.
3. It is intended to function as a Jan Andolan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: All three statements are correct. POSHAN Abhiyaan envisages a Suposhit Bharat and a Jan Andolan, with the stated goal of reducing stunting to 25 percent by 2022.
139.tq: Check whether all statements describe the mission goal and implementation approach.
xs: **All three** statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: the goal was stunting at **25%** by **2022**.
Statements 2 and 3: it aims at a **Suposhit Bharat** as a **Jan Andolan**.
xa: Launched **8 March 2018** at **Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan**.
Full form: **Prime Minister's Overarching Scheme for Holistic Nourishment**.
Earlier name: **National Nutrition Mission**.

139.s: Which of the following POSHAN initiative–feature pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Poshan Pakhwada – Brain development in the first six years
Poshan Tracker – Real-time monitoring of Anganwadi services
Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi – ECCE and play-based pedagogy
Poshan Vatika – ECCE and play-based pedagogy
139.x: Poshan Vatika relates to nutrition gardens at Anganwadi centres; ECCE and play-based pedagogy is Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi.
xa: There are **4.35 lakh** Poshan Vatikas.
**Millets** at least once a week in supplementary nutrition.
**Rashtriya Poshan Maah** is held in **September**.

139.s: Which of the following portal–function pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: PMMVY Soft Portal – DBT verification and cash benefits for pregnant and lactating mothers
Poshan Tracker App – Panic-button distress dispatch

n: The Poshan Tracker App is a digital platform for children and infants. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The Poshan Tracker App digitally tracks Anganwadi service delivery in real time. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The Poshan Tracker App tracks stunting and wasting. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The Poshan Tracker App tracks nutrition metrics for children aged 0–6 years. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The SHe-Box Portal is a digital platform for women. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The SHe-Box Portal is a centralized platform for registering workplace sexual-harassment complaints. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The SHe-Box Portal monitors workplace sexual-harassment complaints. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The SHe-Box Portal handles complaints under the POSH Act. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The 112 India App is a digital platform for women. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The 112 India App is associated with the Emergency Response Support System (ERSS). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The 112 India App provides a unified single-number panic-button system. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The 112 India App dispatches assistance for distress situations. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The 112 India App routes distress calls to the police. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The 112 India App routes distress calls to medical services. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The 112 India App routes distress calls to fire services. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The 112 India App provides dedicated women's-safety routing. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PMMVY Soft Portal is a digital platform for women. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PMMVY Soft Portal verifies Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT). [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PMMVY Soft Portal enables cash-benefit payouts. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PMMVY Soft Portal serves pregnant mothers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PMMVY Soft Portal serves lactating mothers. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
xa: PMMVY: **₹5,000** for the first child; **₹6,000** if the second child is a girl.
**Poshan Vatikas**: **4.35 lakh** nutrition gardens.
PMMVY helpline: **1515**.

139.s: The Mid-Day Meal Scheme was introduced on 15 August 1995 under which name?
o: National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education
139.x: The scheme was introduced on 15 August 1995 as the National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education (NP-NSPE).
139.tq: Distinguish the original name from the later name PM POSHAN.
xs: The scheme began on **15 Aug 1995** as **NP-NSPE** — the **National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman** is the **2021** name (**PM POSHAN**).
xa: The mid-day meal was **first started in Tamil Nadu**.
Asked in APPSC **2025** (G2-GS 2025 key).
It is implemented under **NFSA 2013**.

139.s:
With reference to PM POSHAN, consider the following statements:
1. It covers children studying in Bal Vatika and Classes I to VIII.
2. It provides one hot cooked meal.
3. It is restricted to unaided private schools.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: PM POSHAN covers Bal Vatika and Classes I to VIII in government and government-aided schools and provides one hot cooked meal. It is not restricted to unaided private schools.
139.tq: Find the wrong coverage category by checking the type of school included.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: it covers **Bal Vatika** and **Classes I-VIII**.
Statement 2: it gives **one hot cooked meal**.
Statement 3 is wrong: it covers **government and government-aided schools**, not unaided private ones.
xa: Over **11.8 crore** children served (**29 Jun 2026**).
Primary norm: **450 kcal + 12 g protein**; upper primary **700 kcal + 20 g protein**.
Cooking cost: **₹5.45** primary; **₹8.17** upper primary.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about the nutritional norms under PM POSHAN:
1. At the primary level, the norm is 450 kcal and 12 g protein per child.
2. At the upper-primary level, the norm is 700 kcal and 12 g protein per child.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
139.x: Statement 1 is correct: the primary norm is 450 kcal and 12 g protein. Statement 2 is wrong: the upper-primary norm is 700 kcal and 20 g protein, not 12 g. So '1 only' is right; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are wrong.
139.tq: Primary 450/12, upper primary 700/20 - both calories and protein rise with the stage.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)** (**1 only**).
Statement 1 is correct: primary = **450 kcal + 12 g protein**.
Statement 2 is wrong: upper primary = **700 kcal + 20 g protein**, not 12 g.
xa: Cooking cost per child per day: **₹5.45** (primary), **₹8.17** (upper primary).
Coverage: **Bal Vatika** + **Classes I-VIII**.
Extra nutrition in **aspirational and high-anaemia districts**.

139.s: Tithi Bhojan, associated with community participation in PM POSHAN, was first introduced by which State?
139.x: Tithi Bhojan, under which communities contribute meals on special occasions, was first introduced by Gujarat.
139.tq: Test the origin State of a named community-participation practice.
xs: **Tithi Bhojan** was first introduced by **Gujarat** — option **(4)** is correct.
⚠ **Tamil Nadu** was where the **mid-day meal** first started.
xa: In Tithi Bhojan the **community contributes meals on special days**.
Other features: school nutrition gardens; **mandatory social audit** in every district.
AP runs the **Dokka Seethamma** Mid-Day Meal.

139.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Akshaya Patra Foundation—largest NGO partner in the mid-day meal programme
Tithi Bhojan—introduced first by Tamil Nadu
PM POSHAN—administered by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
139.x: The Akshaya Patra Foundation, based in Bengaluru, is identified as the largest NGO partner in the mid-day meal programme. The other pairings contain incorrect State, Ministry or year associations.
139.tq: Use the wrong-person or wrong-ministry trap to identify the only correctly matched pair.
xs: **Akshaya Patra Foundation** is the **largest NGO** mid-day meal provider — option **(2)** is correct.
NP-NSPE was renamed PM POSHAN in **2021**, not 2015; Tithi Bhojan began in **Gujarat**.
PM POSHAN is under the **Ministry of Education**, not MoHFW.
xa: Akshaya Patra: **Bengaluru**, **2000**, **Madhu Pandit Dasa**.
⚠ Mid-day meal **first** = **Tamil Nadu**; Tithi Bhojan **first** = **Gujarat**.

139.s: The nodal ministry for PM POSHAN (the renamed Mid-Day Meal Scheme) is the:
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development
139.x: PM POSHAN is run by the Ministry of Education (Department of School Education and Literacy); MWCD runs ICDS.
xa: National scheme began **15 Aug 1995** as **NP-NSPE**.
Sharing **60:40**.

139.s: Which scheme is described as one of the world’s largest SHG-based rural livelihood programmes?
139.x: DAY-NRLM, launched in 2011, is an SHG-based rural livelihoods programme described as one of the world’s largest.
139.tq: Identify the scheme from its distinctive scale and SHG-based livelihood feature.
xs: **DAY-NRLM** (**2011**) is an SHG-based rural livelihood programme, **one of the world's largest** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Swadhar** gives shelter to women in difficult circumstances.
xa: Swadhar is now inside **Shakti Sadan**.
**Swavalambini** (**2022**): MSDE-NITI Aayog entrepreneurship programme for women students in the North-East.
PM Ujjwala: **10.57 crore+** connections.

139.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the six ICDS services?
139.x: Cash maternity benefit is provided under PMMVY, now associated with Mission Shakti, and is not one of the six ICDS services.
139.tq: Use the scheme-boundary test to distinguish ICDS services from a related maternity-benefit programme.
xs: **Cash maternity benefit** is not an ICDS service — option **(3)** is correct.
It is given under **PMMVY**, now under **Mission Shakti**.
**Pre-school non-formal education**, **referral services** and **nutrition and health education** are ICDS services.
xa: The six services: **SNP**, pre-school education, nutrition and health education, **immunisation**, health check-up, referral.
PMMVY: **₹5,000** for the first child; **₹6,000** if the second child is a girl.
PMMVY is the only cash maternity benefit written into the **NFSA**.

139.s: PM POSHAN is implemented as a rights-based Centrally Sponsored Scheme under which legislation?
139.x: PM POSHAN is a rights-based Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented under the National Food Security Act, 2013.
139.tq: Use the legal-basis trap by separating the governing legislation from related education and food institutions.
xs: PM POSHAN is implemented under the **National Food Security Act, 2013** — option **(4)** is correct.
It is a rights-based **centrally sponsored scheme**.
xa: Centre-State sharing **60:40**.
⚠ **PMMVY** also rests on **Sec 4, NFSA 2013**.

139.s: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) entitles pregnant women and sick newborns to:
o: A cash incentive for institutional delivery
Free delivery, drugs, diagnostics, blood, diet and transport
Rs 5,000 maternity benefit for the first child
A free antenatal check-up on the 9th of every month
139.x: JSSK, launched in 2011 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, provides pregnant women and sick newborns free delivery, medicines, diagnostics, blood, diet and transport.
xa: **JSY** (**2005**) gives cash for institutional delivery: **₹1,400** rural, **₹1,000** urban.
**PMSMA** (**2016**): free antenatal check-up on the **9th of every month**.
**MAA** (**2016**): breastfeeding within one hour of birth.

139.s: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan is associated with which of the following?
o: Promotion of breastfeeding within one hour of birth
Free treatment exclusively for sick newborns
Free antenatal check-up on the ninth of every month and identification of high-risk pregnancies
Cash assistance for institutional delivery at rural and urban rates
139.x: PMSMA, launched in 2016 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, provides free antenatal check-ups on the 9th of every month and helps identify high-risk pregnancies.
139.tq: Use the fixed monthly date and service purpose as identifying clues.
xs: **PMSMA** gives a **free antenatal check-up on the 9th of every month** and spots **high-risk pregnancies** — option **(3)** is correct.
Breastfeeding is **MAA**; sick newborns are covered by **JSSK**; delivery cash is **JSY**.
xa: PMSMA was launched in **2016** under **MoHFW** (G2-GS **2022**).
**7.47 crore+** pregnant women examined at **22,349** facilities.
⚠ AP **ECCE day** is the **5th** of every month.

139.s: Under PMMVY 2.0 (from April 2022), which of the following correctly describes the maternity benefit?
o: Rs 5,000 for the first child, and Rs 6,000 if the second child is a girl
Rs 5,000 in three instalments for the first two children irrespective of sex
Rs 6,000 for every live birth irrespective of birth order
Rs 1,400 for institutional delivery in rural areas
139.x: PMMVY 2.0 gives Rs 5,000 for the first child and Rs 6,000 if the second child is a girl. Rs 5,000 in three instalments was the old PMMVY 1.0 design (a trap). It does not cover every birth. Rs 1,400 for rural institutional delivery is the JSY benefit.
139.tq: PMMVY 2.0: 5,000 (1st) + 6,000 (2nd girl); '3 instalments' = old 1.0.
xs: **PMMVY 2.0** gives **Rs 5,000 for the first child** and **Rs 6,000 if the second child is a girl** — option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **₹5,000 in 3 instalments** was the old **PMMVY 1.0** design.
**₹1,400** for rural institutional delivery is the **JSY** benefit.
xa: PMMVY 2.0 began in **April 2022**.
Helpline **1515**; tagline **"Matru Shakti Rashtra Shakti"**.
Legal basis: **Sec 4, NFSA 2013**.

139.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
o: It is primarily a behaviour-change campaign
It provides direct benefit transfers to every girl child
Funds for each district vary with its Sex Ratio at Birth
139.x: BBBP has no DBT component; it is a behaviour-change campaign with no asset creation.
xa: Aim: reverse falling **Child Sex Ratio**; secure the girl child's survival and education.
Girls' secondary GER **75.51% → 80.2%**.
BBBP runs under **Sambal** (Mission Shakti).

139.s: Which of the following scheme–feature pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Balika Samriddhi Yojana – Cash grant at birth and scholarships for girls of BPL families
Dhanalakshmi – Conditional cash transfer linked with birth registration, immunisation and schooling
Beti Bachao Beti Padhao – Behaviour-change campaign for survival and education of the girl child
Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana – Savings scheme with maturity at 15 years
139.x: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana matures at 21 years, not 15.
xa: Dhanalakshmi conditions: **birth registration, immunisation, schooling**.
Sukanya Samriddhi: deposits for **15 years**; at most **two girls** per family.
BBBP: **100% central funding**, all districts.

139.s: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched at which place on 22 January 2015?
139.x: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched on 22 January 2015 at Panipat in Haryana.
139.tq: Use the place-date pair to distinguish the scheme from other women-centric initiatives.
xs: BBBP was launched on **22 January 2015** at **Panipat, Haryana** — option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ **Bengaluru** is the base of the **Akshaya Patra Foundation**.
xa: ⚠ POSHAN Abhiyaan = **Jhunjhunu 2018**; BBBP = **Panipat 2015**.
BBBP runs under **Sambal** (**Mission Shakti**).

139.s: A Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana account matures after:
139.x: SSY, under the Ministry of Finance, allows up to two girls per family, deposits of ₹250 to ₹1.5 lakh a year, and matures at 21 years.
xa: **4.53 crore+** accounts.
⚠ BBBP is a **behaviour-change** campaign under **MWCD**, not a savings scheme.

139.s: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, the minimum legal age for marriage is:
o: 21 years for both girls and boys
18 years for girls and 21 years for boys
18 years for girls and 18 years for boys
21 years for girls and 18 years for boys
139.x: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 prescribes 18 years for girls and 21 years for boys.
139.tq: Directly discriminate between the two age thresholds in a commonly confused pair.
xs: Under **PCMA 2006** the minimum age is **18 years for girls and 21 years for boys** — option **(2)** is correct.
The other options swap or equalise the ages; raising women's age to **21** was only proposed in a Bill.
xa: The **Amendment Bill 2021** sought to raise women's age to **21**; it lapsed with the **17th Lok Sabha**.
A child marriage is **voidable** at the option of the minor party.
The **Allahabad HC (1 Jul 2026)** held the age limits apply to all citizens irrespective of religion.

139.s: An adult male who contracts, conducts or promotes a child marriage under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 may be punished with:
o: Rigorous imprisonment up to two years and fine up to Rs. 1 lakh
Fine up to Rs. 10 lakh only
Simple imprisonment up to five years without fine
Imprisonment up to one year and fine up to Rs. 50,000
139.x: The punishment may extend to two years of rigorous imprisonment and a fine up to Rs. 1 lakh.
139.tq: Retain both components of the penalty instead of selecting a partially correct punishment.
xs: The punishment is up to **2 years RI + fine up to Rs 1 lakh** — option **(1)** is correct.
It applies to an **adult male** who contracts, conducts or promotes a child marriage.
xa: **Child Marriage Prohibition Officers** are appointed by **State Governments**.
Minimum age: **18** (girls) / **21** (boys).
**'100-Day Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat'** campaign launched by **MWCD** in **December 2025**.

139.s: The Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill, 2021 proposed to raise the minimum marriageable age of women to 21 years. What happened to the Bill?
