**SEED** (**2022**) is the DNT welfare scheme.

144.s: Andhra Pradesh's G.O. 1065 (August 2026) provides what BC reservation in urban local body polls?
144.x: G.O. 1065 gives 33.33% BC reservation in ULB polls; AP's 138 BC communities are in Groups A-E.
xa: BCs = **43.17%** of AP's population.
A **Swarnakara** Welfare and Development Corporation has been set up.

144.s: Section 2(c) of the National Commission for Minorities Act has been criticised because it gives the Centre:
o: exclusive power to appoint State minority commissions
power to amend the Constitution without Parliament
144.x: Section 2(c) has been criticised as giving the Centre ‘unbridled power’ to notify minorities, raising concerns in the context of T.M.A. Pai.
144.tq: Match the statutory provision with the specific constitutional criticism rather than a broader unrelated power.
xs: Critics say **Section 2(c)** gives the Centre **"unbridled power"** to **notify minorities** — option **(1)**.
It sits uneasily with **T.M.A. Pai (2002)**, which made the **State** the unit for minority status.
xa: The NCM Act does not define minority; a minority = any community **notified by the Central Government**.
States may notify their own minorities — **Jains** in **11 States** before 2014.

144.s: The National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC) was established in:
144.x: NSFDC came in 1989 for SCs, NBCFDC in 1992 for Backward Classes and NSTFDC in 2001 for STs; NMDFC serves minorities.
xa: NBCFDC is under **MoSJE**; NMDFC is a **Section 8 company** under **MoMA**.
Both NBCFDC and NMDFC lend through **State Channelising Agencies**.

144.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
144.x: The Communal Award came in 1932. The National Integration Council began in 1961 and the National Foundation for Communal Harmony in 1992.
n: The National Integration Council was first established in 1961. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
Articles 29 and 30 were the first Constitutional provisions for minority rights. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Communal Award was the first Communal Award in 1932. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The National Foundation for Communal Harmony was first established in 1992. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
xa: The NIC's first Chairman was **Jawaharlal Nehru**.
**Article 51A(e)** is the first constitutional duty **promoting harmony**.
**NHRC**: first established **1993**.

144.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Article 29 – Protection of a section's distinct language, script or culture
Article 30 – Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions
Ranganath Misra Commission – First Chairman of the National Commission for Minorities
Justice Mohammed Sardar Ali Khan – First Chairman of the National Commission for Minorities
144.x: Justice Mohammed Sardar Ali Khan was the first NCM chairman; the Ranganath Misra Commission studied religious and linguistic minorities.
n: Articles 29 and 30 were the first Constitutional provisions for minority rights. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
Justice Mohammed Sardar Ali Khan was the first Chairman of the National Commission for Minorities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
Article 30 was the first Minority Educational Rights provision. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
The Ranganath Misra Commission was the first Commission on Religious and Linguistic Minorities in 2004. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #1 · pp 2-13]
xa: ⚠ **Art. 29** = all citizens; **Art. 30** = only minorities.
The **44th Amendment** added **Art. 30(1A)**.

144.s: Which of the following case–holding pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: In re Kerala Education Bill – State may regulate standards without destroying minority character
St. Stephen's College v. University of Delhi – Aided minority college may prefer its own community up to 50 per cent of seats
P.A. Inamdar v. State of Maharashtra – State cannot impose reservation on unaided professional institutions
T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka – State cannot impose reservation on unaided professional institutions
144.x: T.M.A. Pai made the State the unit for determining minority status; the bar on reservation in unaided institutions is P.A. Inamdar.
xa: **St. Xavier's (1974):** regulations only for **standards/excellence**.
**Bal Patil (2005):** Jain minority status left to the **States**.

144.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: P.A. Inamdar (2005) — Presidential reference under Article 143
In re Kerala Education Bill (1957) — 11-judge Bench and State-wise minority status
St. Xavier's College v. Gujarat (1974) — right to administer protected, subject to standards and excellence regulations
T.M.A. Pai Foundation (2002) — seven-judge Bench and no State quota in unaided institutions
144.x: C is correct: St. Xavier's College v. Gujarat (1974) protected the right to administer, allowing regulation only for standards and excellence. The others are mismatched: the Article 143 Presidential reference was the Kerala Education Bill case, not P.A. Inamdar; the 11-judge Bench and State-wise minority status belong to T.M.A. Pai; the seven-judge Bench barring State quotas in unaided institutions was P.A. Inamdar.
144.tq: Find the correctly matched case and holding by separating the four landmark decisions.
xs: **St. Xavier's College v. Gujarat (1974)** — right to administer protected; regulations only for **standards/excellence** — option **(3)**.
The **Art. 143** reference was the **Kerala Education Bill** case; the **11-judge** State-wise ruling was **T.M.A. Pai**; the **7-judge** no-quota ruling was **P.A. Inamdar**.
xa: **St. Stephen's (1992):** aided minority college may prefer its own community up to about **50%**.

144.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the decision in P.A. Inamdar (2005)?
o: A seven-judge Bench held that the State could impose its quota in unaided institutions without limitation.
A seven-judge Bench held that there could be no State quota or reservation in unaided institutions, contributing to the subsequent 93rd Amendment framework.
An 11-judge Bench abolished the distinction between aided and unaided institutions.
The Court held that minority status must be determined at the national level.
144.x: P.A. Inamdar was decided by a seven-judge Bench and held that the State could not impose its quota or reservation in unaided institutions. The decision was followed by the constitutional development associated with Article 15(5) through the 93rd Amendment.
144.tq: Combine bench strength, holding and constitutional consequence without confusing it with T.M.A. Pai.
xs: **P.A. Inamdar (2005)**, a **7-judge** bench, held the State cannot impose **reservation quotas** on **unaided** institutions, minority or non-minority — option **(2)**.
This led to Art. **15(5)** through the **93rd Amendment**.
xa: ⚠ **T.M.A. Pai (2002)** was the **11-judge** bench making the **State** the unit for minority status.
**St. Stephen's (1992)** concerned **aided** minority colleges.

144.s: The decision in Bal Patil v. Union of India (2005) is associated with which of the following?
o: Directing the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority
Imposing reservation quotas on unaided minority institutions
Declaring that minority status must be determined nationally
Declining to direct the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority and leaving the matter to the States
144.x: The Court declined to direct the Centre to notify Jains as a national minority, leaving the matter to the States and cautioning against the multiplication of minority claims.
144.tq: Discriminate between a judicial direction and a refusal to issue that direction.
xs: **Bal Patil v Union of India (2005)** **declined to direct the Centre** to notify **Jains** as a national minority, leaving it to the **States** — option **(4)**.
It also warned against **multiplying minority claims**.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** UPSC notes describe it as a linguistic-institutions case — inaccurate.
The Centre later notified **Jains** on **27 January 2014**.

144.s: The principal reason cited for the low expenditure under SEED was that:
o: States did not issue DNT certificates
the scheme covered only urban areas
the Union Government withdrew the scheme
beneficiaries were excluded from health insurance
144.x: Low expenditure was attributed to the failure of States to issue certificates for Denotified Tribes.
144.tq: Link the implementation shortfall to the administrative bottleneck rather than to the scheme’s objectives.
xs: SEED was under-spent because **States did not issue DNT certificates** — option **(1)**.
Only **Rs 69.3 crore** of **Rs 200 crore** was spent in five years.
xa: A special **DNT policy** was demanded in **Vijayawada**.
**Census 2027** will count DNTs.

144.s: The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee highlighted severe under-representation of Muslims in which areas?
144.x: The Sachar Committee found Muslims badly under-represented in public jobs and higher education, against their share of the population.
144.tq: Recall the Sachar findings.
n: The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee highlighted severe under-representation of Muslims in public employment. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee highlighted severe under-representation of Muslims in higher education. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee concerned minorities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee assessed the educational status of the Muslim community in India. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
xs: The **Sachar Committee** found **severe under-representation** of Muslims in **public employment** and **higher education** — option **(1)**.
It assessed the **socio-economic** and **educational status** of the **Muslim community**.
xa: It proposed an **Equal Opportunity Commission**, **National Data Bank** and **Diversity Index**.
**Ajlafs** need attention like Hindu OBCs; **Arzals** (Dalit Muslims) are the most deprived.
⚠ **Ajlaf** ≈ OBC; **Arzal** ≈ SC; **Ashraf** = upper.

144.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Hunar Haat / PM-VIKAS Digital Interface is incorrect?
o: It supports master trainer accreditation for traditional crafts.
It is a dashboard for 11 critical interventions across 75 PVTG communities.
It promotes artisans and provides a digital marketplace.
It is associated with the Ministry of Minority Affairs.
144.x: Option B is incorrect: the dashboard for 11 interventions across 75 PVTGs is PM-JANMAN. Hunar Haat/PM-VIKAS (Minority Affairs) promotes artisans, gives an online marketplace and accredits craft trainers.
144.tq: Match each portal to its function.
n: The PM-JANMAN Monitoring Dashboard provides an inter-ministerial saturation dashboard. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-JANMAN Monitoring Dashboard covers 11 critical interventions. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The PM-JANMAN Monitoring Dashboard covers 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group communities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The Hunar Haat and PM-VIKAS Digital Interface are digital platforms for minorities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The Ministry of Minority Affairs is the nodal ministry for the Hunar Haat and PM-VIKAS Digital Interface. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The Hunar Haat and PM-VIKAS Digital Interface promote artisans. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The Hunar Haat and PM-VIKAS Digital Interface provide a digital marketplace. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The Hunar Haat and PM-VIKAS Digital Interface provide master-trainer accreditation. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
The Hunar Haat and PM-VIKAS Digital Interface support traditional crafts. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]
xs: The incorrect statement calls Hunar Haat a **dashboard for 11 interventions across 75 PVTGs** — option **(2)**.
**Hunar Haat / PM-VIKAS Digital Interface** (**Minority Affairs**) **promotes artisans**, offers a **digital marketplace** and **master-trainer accreditation**.
xa: It also **supports traditional crafts**.
**NMDFC** offers **Virasat** loans for artisans.
**PM Vishwakarma** (**17 Sept 2023**) covers artisans in **18 trades** under **MSME**.

144.s: The Chairperson and members of the National Commission for Minorities are appointed by the:
144.x: NCM members are appointed by the Central Government, not the President; the statutory NCM dates from the 1992 Act, first constituted in 1993.
xa: The NCM is **statutory, not constitutional**, under the **Ministry of Minority Affairs**.
⚠ GS 2018 key: appointed by the **Union Government**.

144.s: The Minorities Commission became a statutory body under the NCM Act in:
144.x: The non-statutory Commission came in 1978, the NCM Act in 1992, the first statutory Commission in 1993 and the Vice-Chairperson in 1995.
xa: After 1995 the strength became **7**.
⚠ **1993** is also the year the first **five** communities were notified.

144.s: Which commission was the first to examine the condition of Denotified Tribes among the commissions mentioned below?
144.x: The Renke Commission, whose report was submitted in 2008, was the first such commission mentioned for Denotified Tribes.
144.tq: Use the ‘first’ marker to distinguish the earlier Renke Commission from the later Idate Commission.
xs: The **Renke Commission** (report **2008**) was the **first** DNT commission — option **(3)**.
The **Idate Commission** came later (**2014-17**); **J.B. Koshy** concerned **Christian minorities** in Kerala; **Sachar** concerned **Muslims**.
xa: Idate: about **1,200** DNTs already in SC/ST/OBC lists; **267-268** never classified.
DNTs were branded under the **Criminal Tribes Act 1871**.

144.s:
Consider the following statements about the Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee:
1. It was constituted in 2006.
2. It was a Prime Minister's High-Level Committee.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
144.x: The Sachar Committee was a Prime Minister's High-Level Committee set up in March 2005; it reported in November 2006.
n: The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee was constituted in 2006. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
The Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee was a Prime Minister’s High-Level Committee. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #42 · pp 90-92]
xa: Report: **November 2006**.
It was the **first national data-based committee** on minorities.
⚠ **2006** = Sachar report; **2007** = Ranganath Misra report.

144.s: In which year was the first National Foundation for Communal Harmony established?
144.x: The National Foundation for Communal Harmony was set up in 1992. 1983 is the 15-Point Programme and 2005 the Sachar Committee.
144.tq: Recall the minority firsts by year.
xs: The **National Foundation for Communal Harmony** was first established in **1992** — option **(3)**.
**1983** is the first **15-Point Programme**; **2005** is the **Sachar Committee**.
xa: **National Integration Council**: **1961**; **Communal Award**: **1932**.

144.s: The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was established in:
144.x: The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was set up in 1957.
144.tq: Distinguish the office’s establishment year from the constitutional amendment year.
xs: The office of the **Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities** was set up in **1957** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **1956** is the **7th Amendment** that inserted Art. **350B**; the office followed in 1957.
xa: HQ: **Prayagraj (Allahabad)**.
**1964** is the year of the statutory **Central Waqf Council**.

144.s: The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis Act, 1993 lapsed in:
144.x: The Act lapsed in 2004; the NCSK continues as a non-statutory body with tenure extended by resolution.
xa: Comparable finance bodies: **NSFDC** (1989, SCs), **NBCFDC** (1992, BCs), **NSTFDC** (2001, STs).

144.s:
Assertion (A): Not all seven members of the National Commission for Minorities need belong to minority communities.
Reason (R): Only five of the seven members, including the Chairperson, must be from minority communities.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
144.x: The NCM has a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and five Members; since only five must be from minorities, all seven need not be.
xa: Older notes list only a Chairperson and five Members (before the **1995** amendment).
July 2026: only **4 of 7** posts filled.

144.s: Which of the following was NOT a proposal associated with the Sachar Committee?
144.x: The Sachar Committee proposed an Equal Opportunity Commission, National Data Bank and Assessment and Monitoring Authority. A National Linguistic Minorities Commission was not listed among its proposals.
144.tq: Eliminate the option belonging to a different institutional theme.
xs: A **National Linguistic Minorities Commission** was NOT a Sachar proposal — option **(4)**.
Sachar proposed an **Equal Opportunity Commission**, a **National Data Bank** and an **Assessment and Monitoring Authority**.
xa: It also recommended a **Diversity Index**.
The **Kundu Committee** (**2013-14**) repeated the call for an Equal Opportunity Commission and anti-discrimination law.

144.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities – Amitabh Kundu
144.x: The Post-Sachar Evaluation Committee was chaired by Amitabh Kundu; the Sachar Committee by Rajinder Sachar and the minorities commission by Justice Ranganath Misra.
xa: Reports: Sachar **2006**, Ranganath Misra **2007**, Kundu **2013-14**.
Ranganath Misra suggested a **15%** quota for minorities.

144.s: The Ranganath Misra Commission was associated with which of the following recommendations?
o: Replacement of all State languages by Hindi
A 15% reservation and delinking Scheduled Caste status from religion
Creation of the National Data Bank for census purposes only
144.x: The National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities, chaired by Justice Ranganath Misra, suggested a 15% quota for minorities and delinking SC status from religion.
144.tq: Match the commission with its distinctive recommendation rather than its general subject.
xs: The **Ranganath Misra Commission** suggested a **15%** reservation for minorities and **delinking SC status from religion** — option **(3)**.
It sought concrete steps for socially and economically backward sections among religious and linguistic minorities.
xa: It reported in **2007**.
The **National Data Bank** was a **Sachar** proposal.

144.s:
Consider the following statements:

I. The Sachar Committee was established in 2005 under Rajinder Sachar to study the socio-economic status of Muslims.
II. The Ranganath Misra Commission was established in 2004 under Ranganath Misra to study religious and linguistic minorities.
III. The Gopal Singh Committee submitted its report on minorities in 1983.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: All three are correct: Sachar (2005) studied the status of Muslims, Ranganath Misra (2004) religious and linguistic minorities, and the Gopal Singh panel on minorities reported in 1983.
144.tq: Match each minority body to its chair.
n: The Sachar Committee was established in 2005. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
Rajinder Sachar chaired the Sachar Committee. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
The Ranganath Misra Commission was established in 2004. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
Ranganath Misra chaired the Ranganath Misra Commission. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
The Ranganath Misra Commission studied religious and linguistic minorities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
The Gopal Singh Committee was established in 1983. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
Gopal Singh chaired the Gopal Singh Committee. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #11 · pp 42-44]
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
I: the **Sachar Committee** (**2005**, **Rajinder Sachar**) studied the **socio-economic** status of the **Muslim community** — correct.
II: the **Ranganath Misra Commission** (**2004**) studied **religious and linguistic minorities** — correct.
III: the **Gopal Singh Committee** on **minority welfare** is dated **1983** — correct.
xa: Sachar reported in **November 2006**; Ranganath Misra in **2007**.
Ranganath Misra recommended **15%** reservation for minorities and **10%** for Muslims.
**Kundu Committee** (**2013-14**) reviewed Sachar's implementation.

144.s: The Ranganath Misra Commission was established in which year?
144.x: The Ranganath Misra Commission on religious and linguistic minorities was set up in 2004. The Sachar Committee followed in 2005.
144.tq: Arrange the minority bodies in time order.
xs: The **Ranganath Misra Commission** was established in **2004** — option **(3)**.
It is the **National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities**; ⚠ some notes say **constituted 2007** (its report year).
xa: It recommended **15%** reservation for minorities, **10%** for Muslims.
It urged **delinking SC status from religion**.
The **Sachar Committee** followed in **2005**.

144.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Hamari Dharohar — preserving the heritage of minorities
Seekho aur Kamao — skill upgradation and placement
Nai Manzil — education and skilling for school dropouts
Nai Roshni — free coaching after clearing civil services preliminaries
144.x: Nai Roshni concerns leadership training for minority women. Free coaching and post-preliminary support are associated with Naya Savera and Nai Udaan.
144.tq: Reject the option that swaps the benefits of two neighbouring minority schemes.
xs: **Nai Roshni — free coaching after prelims** is wrong — option **(4)**.
Nai Roshni is **leadership training for minority women**; coaching is **Naya Savera** and post-prelims support is **Nai Udaan**.
xa: Hamari Dharohar (**2015**), Seekho aur Kamao (**2014**), Nai Manzil (**2015**) are correctly matched.
All five merged into **PM VIKAS** (**2022**).

144.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the five schemes merged into PM VIKAS?
144.x: PM VIKAS merges Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni and Nai Manzil. PMJVK is not one of the five merged schemes.
144.tq: Find the area-based infrastructure scheme that does not belong to the merged skill and heritage package.
xs: **PM Jan Vikas Karyakram** is NOT among the five merged into PM VIKAS — option **(1)**.
PM VIKAS merges **Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni, Nai Manzil**.
xa: ⚠ **PM VIKAS** = Central Sector; **PMJVK** = Centrally Sponsored.
Critics say minority schemes lost visibility after the merger.

144.s: Which one of the following correctly describes PMJVK?
o: It is a Central Sector Scheme limited to minority students pursuing higher education.
It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for area development in minority concentration areas.
It is a constitutional programme implemented by the Election Commission.
It is a State scheme restricted to urban minority households.
144.x: PMJVK is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme aimed at area development in minority concentration areas.
144.tq: Identify the scheme from its funding pattern and broad area-development objective.
xs: **PMJVK** is a **Centrally Sponsored** infrastructure scheme for **minority-concentration areas** — option **(2)**.
It benefits **all residents**, not just minority students or urban households.
xa: Restructured in **May 2018** from **MSDP (2008-09)**.
**80%** to education, health and skills; **33-40%** for women.

144.s: PM Vishwakarma primarily targets:
144.x: PM Vishwakarma is intended for artisans and craftspeople engaged in 18 traditional trades. It is not a fishermen's scheme.
144.tq: Discriminate between the target group and the tempting but incorrect fishermen association.
xs: **PM Vishwakarma** targets **artisans and craftspeople** in **18 trades** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **Trap:** it is **not a fishermen's scheme** (APPSC G2 2023).
xa: Toolkit incentive: **Rs 15,000**.
Credit: collateral-free **Rs 1 lakh + Rs 2 lakh** at **5%**.

144.s:
Consider the following statements regarding PM-VIKAS:
I. It supports convergence of skill development.
II. It provides artisan support.
III. It supports entrepreneurship.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
144.x: All three are correct: PM-VIKAS brings together skill training, support for artisans and entrepreneurship for minorities.
144.tq: Recall the three PM-VIKAS components.
n: PM-VIKAS converges skill development, artisan support, entrepreneurship, and education. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**PM-VIKAS** **converges** **skill development**, **artisan support**, **entrepreneurship** and **education** for the **six notified minorities**.
xa: PM VIKAS (**2022**) merges **Seekho aur Kamao**, **USTTAD**, **Hamari Dharohar**, **Nai Roshni** and **Nai Manzil**.
It is a **Central Sector** scheme; **33%** of skilling seats for women.
⚠ **PMJVK** is **Centrally Sponsored**.

144.s: Which of the following statements about Naya Savera & Nai Udaan is incorrect?
o: It is meant for students clearing UPSC and SSC Main examinations.
It provides financial support to minority students.
It provides free coaching to minority students.
It is associated with the Ministry of Minority Affairs.
144.x: Option A is incorrect: Naya Savera and Nai Udaan support minority students who clear the UPSC or SSC prelims, not the mains.
144.tq: Watch for 'Main' replacing 'prelims'.
n: The nodal ministry for Naya Savera and Nai Udaan is the Ministry of Minority Affairs. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Naya Savera and Nai Udaan provide free coaching for minority students clearing UPSC prelims. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Naya Savera and Nai Udaan provide free coaching for minority students clearing SSC prelims. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Naya Savera and Nai Udaan provide financial support for minority students clearing UPSC prelims. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Naya Savera and Nai Udaan provide financial support for minority students clearing SSC prelims. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Minorities are a target group of welfare mechanisms. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Naya Savera is a key scheme for minorities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
Nai Udaan is a key scheme for minorities. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #35 · pp 76-79]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the schemes are for students clearing **UPSC and SSC Main** — option **(1)**; they support those clearing the **prelims**.
**Naya Savera** and **Nai Udaan** give **free coaching** and **financial support** to **minority students** under **Minority Affairs**.
xa: ⚠ **Nai Roshni** = women's leadership; **Nai Manzil** = dropouts; **Nai Udaan** = after prelims; **Naya Savera** = coaching.
**Seekho aur Kamao** (**2014**): skilling linked to jobs.

144.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ashraf — upper or claimed foreign origin
Ajlaf — the most deprived Dalit Muslim group
144.x: Arzal, rather than Ajlaf, was described as the Dalit Muslim group and the most deprived category. Ajlaf was identified as a backward group requiring attention similar to Hindu OBCs.
144.tq: Use the confusable-pair trap by checking the precise description of each group.
xs: **Ajlaf — the most deprived Dalit Muslim group** is wrongly matched — option **(4)**.
The most deprived **Dalit Muslims** are the **Arzal**; the **Ajlaf** are commoners/lower-caste converts comparable to **Hindu OBCs**.
xa: **Ashraf:** upper; claimed foreign/upper-caste origin.
⚠ **Ajlaf** ≈ OBC; **Arzal** ≈ SC (APPSC G2 2024).

144.s: PM VIKAS, a Central Sector scheme of 2022 merging five minority schemes, stands for:
o: Pradhan Mantri Vikas Aur Kaushal Samvardhan
Pradhan Mantri Virasat Aur Kala Sanrakshan
144.x: PM VIKAS means Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan; it merges five schemes and runs until 2025-26.
xa: Merged: **Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni, Nai Manzil**.
About **9 lakh** beneficiaries; **33%** of skilling seats for women; linked to **NMDFC** loans.

144.s: The SEED scheme, launched in 2022, has a stated outlay of:
144.x: SEED (2022) has an outlay of Rs 200 crore and covers coaching, health insurance, livelihoods and housing for incomes below Rs 2.5 lakh.
xa: Only **Rs 69.3 crore** spent in five years.
Reason: States do not issue **DNT certificates**.

144.s:
Arrange the following enactments in chronological order:
A. Waqf Act, 1954
B. Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2013
C. Waqf Act, 1995
D. Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025
144.x: The correct sequence is Waqf Act 1954, Waqf Act 1995, Waqf (Amendment) Act 2013, and Waqf (Amendment) Act 2025.
144.tq: Place the parent enactments before their later amendments.
xs: Order: **A, C, B, D** — option **(1)**.
**Waqf Act 1954** → **Waqf Act 1995** (current parent law) → **Wakf (Amendment) Act 2013** → **2025** changes.
xa: The **Central Waqf Council** became statutory in **1964**.
UMEED portal launched **June 2025**.

144.s: The Wakf (Amendment) Act, 2013 enabled which body to direct State Waqf Boards?
144.x: The 2013 amendment let the Central Waqf Council direct State Boards and barred sale, gift, mortgage, exchange and transfer of waqf property.
xa: The 2025 law put all waqf properties on a **central portal within 6 months**.

144.s: Which of the following statements about the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 is correct?
o: Only Muslim members could thereafter serve on the Central Waqf Council and State Boards.
Waqf by user was abolished even for all properties registered before the amendment.
Waqf by user survived only for properties registered before the law.
The Act prohibited the use of any central portal for waqf properties.
144.x: Under the 2025 Act, waqf by user survived only for properties registered before the law. The Act also provided for non-Muslim members and a central portal.
144.tq: Reject absolute statements by identifying the statutory qualification.
xs: Under the 2025 law, **waqf by user survives only for properties registered before the law** — option **(3)**.
It **allowed non-Muslim** members and required a **central portal**, so the other options are wrong.
xa: The **SC interim order (Sep 2025)** did not stay removal of waqf-by-user.
All waqf properties go on a **central portal within 6 months** (UMEED, **June 2025**).

144.s: Under the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, all waqf properties were to be placed on a central portal within:
144.x: The 2025 amendment required waqf properties on a central portal within six months; the UMEED portal was launched in June 2025.
xa: The **UMEED** portal was launched in **June 2025**.
⚠ The **SC (Sep 2025)** capped non-Muslims at **3** in State Boards and **4** in the Central Council.

144.s: The Central Waqf Council is best described as:
o: A temporary executive committee established in 1995 to conduct elections
A statutory body established in 1964 to advise the Centre on State Waqf Boards
A judicial body established in 2025 to decide all land disputes
A constitutional body established in 1950 to supervise courts
144.x: The Central Waqf Council is a statutory body established in 1964. Its principal role is to advise the Central Government on State Waqf Boards.
144.tq: Distinguish a statutory advisory body from constitutional and judicial bodies.
xs: The **Central Waqf Council** is a **statutory** body of **1964** that **advises the Centre on State Waqf Boards** — option **(2)**.
It was set up under Section 8A of the **1954** Act, now **Section 9(1)** of the **Waqf Act 1995**.
xa: Since **2013**, it can **direct** State Boards.
The 2025 law allows **non-Muslim** members; SC cap = **4** in the Central Council.

144.s:
Assertion (A): The Supreme Court's interim order of September 2025 stayed the five-years-practising-Islam condition in the Waqf (Amendment) Act.
Reason (R): The same order accepted the change applying the Limitation Act.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
144.x: The order stayed the five-year condition and the Collector's power and accepted the Limitation Act change; the two holdings are separate, so R does not explain A.
xa: It capped non-Muslims at **3** in State Boards and **4** in the Central Council.
⚠ The Act itself requires **at least two** non-Muslims in each Board.

144.s: Urdu was made the second official language of Andhra Pradesh under which law?
144.x: Urdu is AP's second official language under the AP Official Language (Amendment) Act, 2022. The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 bifurcated the State; the Official Languages Act, 1963 deals with the Union's official languages; the 7th Amendment, 1956 inserted Articles 350A and 350B.
144.tq: Urdu = AP second official language, 2022 amendment.
xs: **Urdu** is AP's **second official language** under the **AP Official Language (Amendment) Act, 2022** — option **(1)**.
The **7th Amendment (1956)** instead inserted Arts **350A** and **350B**.
xa: AP runs **Urdu-Ghar-cum-Shadikhanas** and **36** computer training centres across **26** districts.
AP has **6 pre-matric and 10 post-matric** minority hostels.

144.s: The Waqf Act, 1995 primarily deals with which of the following?
144.x: The Waqf Act, 1995, governs the administration of waqf properties. Tribal forest rights fall under the Forest Rights Act, and free legal aid under the Legal Services Authorities Act.
144.tq: Match each Act to its purpose.
xs: The **Waqf Act, 1995** is the parent law for the **administration of Waqf properties** — option **(4)**.
It replaced the **Waqf Act 1954**.
xa: The **Central Waqf Council** (statutory, **1964**) now sits under **Sec. 9** of the 1995 Act.
The **2013** amendment bars sale, gift or mortgage of waqf property.
All waqf properties go on a **central portal within 6 months** (**UMEED**, June **2025**).

144.s: Which Muslim group was identified as requiring attention similar to that given to Hindu Other Backward Classes?
o: All Muslim groups equally under the same classification
144.x: The Ajlaf, described as backward Muslims or commoners and lower-caste converts, were identified as requiring attention similar to Hindu OBCs.
144.tq: Separate Ajlaf from Arzal by matching the group with the specific policy concern.
xs: The **Ajlaf** (backward Muslims — commoners/lower-caste converts) need attention similar to **Hindu OBCs** — option **(1)**.
The **Ashraf** are upper/claimed foreign origin; the **Arzal** are Dalit converts, the **most deprived**.
xa: ⚠ **Ajlaf** ≈ OBC; **Arzal** ≈ SC.
This classification was asked in **APPSC G2 2024**.

144.s: PM Jan Vikas Karyakram was restructured from which earlier programme?
144.x: PMJVK was restructured from the Multi-sectoral Development Programme (MSDP), which dates from 2008-09.
144.tq: Use the predecessor-successor relationship to identify the correct programme.
xs: **PMJVK** was restructured in **May 2018** from the **Multi-sectoral Development Programme (MSDP)** of **2008-09** — option **(1)**.
The others are MoMA skilling, leadership and coaching schemes.
xa: It covers **870** minority concentration blocks + **321** towns, now all districts incl. **112 Aspirational Districts**.
**80%** of funds go to education, health and skills.

144.s: The PM-YASASVI Portal is meant for scholarship application and disbursement for which groups?
o: OBC, EBC and nomadic tribe students
144.x: The PM-YASASVI portal handles scholarship applications and payments for OBC, EBC and denotified/nomadic tribe students.
144.tq: Recall PM-YASASVI's groups.
n: The SHRESHTA Portal covers private residential schools for SC students. [Indian Society · ROCKET SHEET #37 · pp 81-84]

144.s: The Constitution of India recognises:
144.x: The term "Minority" is not defined in the Indian Constitution. However, the Constitution recognises both religious and linguistic minorities. Articles 29 and 30 of the Constitution grant protection to both religious minorities and linguistic minorities.

144.s:
Given below are two statements, in which one is Assertion and second is Reason.
Assertion (A) : The definition of term ‘Minority’ is not given in the Constitution of India.
Reason (R) : Minority Commission is not a Constitutional body. Which of the following is correct in regards to the statements above ?
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) explains (A) correctly
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not explain
144.x: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) does not explain Assertion (A) correctly. The term ‘Minority’ is not defined in the Constitution. Minority Commission is a statutory body because it is constituted under the National Minority Commission Act, 1992.

144.s: The Constitution of India recognizes –
144.x: The Constitution of India recognizes both religious and linguistic minorities. According to Article 29, citizens residing in the territory of India having a distinct language, script, or culture of its own shall have the right to conserve the same. Article 30 provides minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions whether based on religion or language.

144.s: What is not true about Rights of Minorities?
o: Minority status is determined by the demography of the State
They have right to establish their own Educational Institutions
Minority Rights aim at ensuring equality

144.s:
Consider the following statements about the minorities in India:
1. The Government of India has notified five communities, namely, Muslims, Sikhs, Christians, Buddhists and Zoroastrians as minorities.
2. The National Commission for Minorities was given statutory status in 1993.
3. The smallest religious minority in India are the Zoroastrians.
4. The Constitution of India recognizes and protects religious and linguistic minorities. Which of these statements are correct ?
144.x: With the enactment of the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992 (came into force on 17th May, 1993) the minority commission became a statutory body and was renamed as the National Commission for Minorities. Thus statement 2 is True. The first statutory National Commission was setup on 17th May, 1993, vide a Gazette notification issued on 23rd October 1993 by the Ministry of Welfare, GOI, five religious communities viz; the Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Zoroastrians (Parsis) were notified as minority communities. Further vide notification dated 27th January, 2014, Jains have also been notified as a minority community. Thus six communities have been notified as minorities, at present. Statement 1 is false. Zoroastrians are not the smallest religious minority, as there exist other smaller minorities that are not notified/recognized as minorities. The Constitution of India recognizes and protects religious and linguistic minorities.

144.s: According to which article, the right of minorities to establish and administer minorities educational institutions?

Match List I (Article of Indian Constitution) with List II (Provisions) and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists:
List I (Article of Indian Constitution)
A. Article 16(2)
B. Article 29(2)
C. Article 30(1)
D. Article 31(1)
List II (Provisions)
1. No person shall be deprived of his property save by the authority of law
2. No person can be discriminated against in the matter of public appointment on the ground of race, religion or caste
3. All minorities whether based on religion or language shall have the fundamental right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice
4. No citizen shall be denied admission into any educational institution maintained by the State, or receiving State aid, on grounds of religion, race, caste, language or any of them
144.x: Article 16(2) of the Constitution of India prohibits discrimination in public employment on grounds such as religion, race, caste, sex, descent, or place of birth. Article 29(2) ensures that no citizen is denied admission to State-maintained or State-aided educational institutions on grounds of religion, race, caste, or language. Article 30(1) grants minorities based on religion or language the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. Article 31(1), before its repeal as a Fundamental Right, provided that no person shall be deprived of property except by authority of law. Hence, the correct matching is A-2, B-4, C-3, D-1.

144.s: Which Article of the Constitution protects the 'Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice'?
144.x: Article 19- Right to Freedom Article 26- Freedom to manage religious affairs Article 29 - Protection of interests of the minority community. Article 30 - Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions.

144.s:
Consider the following statements with reference to Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities :
1. In the Constitution, there is a provision for the post of Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities for every State.
2. A new Article 350 B was added for this by the 9th Constitution Amendment Act. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
144.x: The Section 21 of the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956 added new Articles-350A and 350B which provide for ‘Facilities for instruction in mother-tongue at primary stage’ and ‘Special Officer for linguistic minorities’, respectively. According to clause (1) of Article 350B, there shall be a special officer for linguistic minorities to be appointed by the President. It provides for special officer for linguistic minorities at the Union level (for All India) and not for each State. This Officer in India is named Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities in India. Hence, both statements in the question are not correct.

144.s:
With reference to the National Commission for Minorities, consider the following statements:
I. It was set up under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.
II. Ministry of Welfare has notified five religious communities under "Minority" status, to date.
III. It can make recommendations for the effective implementation of safeguards for the protection of minorities by Central or State Governments. (B) I and II only
144.x: The National Commission for Minorities (NCM) was established under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992. It monitors safeguards for minorities and recommends measures to the government for their protection and development.

144.s: What was the key focus of the Waqf Amendment Bill introduced in April, 2025 ?
o: Enhancing transparency and ensuring better governance
144.x: The main objective of the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024, introduced in the Lok Sabha on 8 August, 2024, was to improve the management of Waqf properties, ensure transparency, governance, and accountability, and prevent mismanagement. The Bill focused on introducing technological and structural reforms in the registration, records, and administration of Waqf properties, so that their proper utilisation and protection could be ensured.

144.s: As per the recommendations of the Sachar Committee, which among the following Muslim groups needs additional attention, similar to that of Hindu OBCs?
When was the Criminal Tribes Act enacted for the first time?
144.x: In 1871, the British Government passed an Act, commonly known as the Criminal Tribes Act. It was enacted for the first time in India and was enforced in the Northern part of India which was later extended to the region of Bengal.

145.s: The e-Shram portal provides every registered unorganised worker with a 12-digit:
145.x: e-Shram, India's first Aadhaar-seeded national database of unorganised workers, gives each worker a 12-digit UAN.
xa: Registrations: **over 31.78 crore** (July 2026).
**One-Stop Solution (2024)** links **15** central schemes.

145.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched under the Code on Social Security, 2020?
o: Gig worker — work exclusively under a traditional employer-employee relationship
Platform worker — work through online platforms
Aggregator — worker registered only under EPFO
Gig worker — worker entitled automatically to government employment
145.x: A platform worker is one who works through online platforms. Gig work is performed outside a traditional employer-employee relationship, while aggregators are recognised entities under the Code.
145.tq: Separate the definitions of gig workers, platform workers and aggregators.
xs: **Platform workers** = those who **work through online platforms** — option **(2)**.
**Gig workers** work **outside** a traditional employer-employee relationship; **aggregators** are platforms, not EPFO workers.
xa: The **Code on Social Security 2020** first recognised **aggregators**, gig and platform workers.
Gig workers get **no employee status**.

145.s: The Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008 has subsequently been merged into the:
145.x: The Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008 was merged into the Code on Social Security, 2020.
145.tq: Match the earlier statute with the Labour Code that subsumed it.
xs: The 2008 Act was **merged into the Code on Social Security, 2020** — option **(3)**.
The **Industrial Relations Code** deals with layoffs, strikes and fixed-term employment instead.
xa: The Code on Social Security is the first law to recognise **aggregators**, **gig** and **platform workers**.
It provides **National and State Social Security Boards**.

145.s: Under the Social Security framework, gig workers can register from the age of:
145.x: Gig workers can register from 16, with National and State Social Security Boards; registration does not confer employee status or a minimum wage.
xa: **Rajasthan** has a Gig Workers Act (**2023**); **Karnataka** (Bill **2024**) and **Telangana** proposed.
NITI estimate: **1.43 crore** gig workers (2025-26).

145.s:
Assertion (A): Under the Industrial Relations Code, prior government permission for layoff, retrenchment and closure is needed only for establishments with 300 or more workers.
Reason (R): The contract labour threshold was raised from 20 to 50 workers.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
145.x: The permission threshold rose from 100 to 300 and the contract labour threshold from 20 to 50; these are separate changes, so R does not explain A.
xa: ⚠ **300** = layoff/closure + Standing Orders; **50** = contract labour; **60/14** days = strike notice.
**Fixed-term** workers get the **same wages and benefits** as permanent workers and gratuity after **1 year**.

145.s: Under the Industrial Relations Code, fixed-term workers become eligible for gratuity after:
145.x: Fixed-term workers get the same wages and benefits as permanent workers and gratuity after one year.
xa: Layoff permission threshold: **300** workers.
Contract labour threshold: **50** workers.

145.s: A trade union proposes to commence a strike five days after giving notice. Under the Industrial Relations Code, this proposal is:
o: Not permissible only when the establishment has more than 500 workers
Permissible if the establishment has fewer than 300 workers
Not permissible because a strike cannot occur within 14 days of giving notice
Permissible because notice has been given in writing
145.x: A strike cannot be held within 14 days of giving notice. The Code also prohibits a strike without notice within the preceding 60 days before striking.
145.tq: Apply the statutory time restriction to the facts of the situation.
xs: A strike **cannot occur within 14 days** of giving notice — so five days is **not permissible**, option **(3)**.
Nor can there be a strike without notice **within 60 days** before striking.
xa: Unions say this weakens **Article 19(1)(c)**.
The rule applies regardless of the **300**-worker threshold, which is for layoffs.

145.s: Which one of the following is NOT listed among the Schedule I schemes of the Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, 2008?
145.x: Schedule I includes the National Family Benefit Scheme, Janani Suraksha Yojana and RSBY, among others. Atal Pension Yojana is not included in the listed Schedule I schemes.
145.tq: Find the scheme outside the statutory list rather than selecting a familiar welfare scheme.
xs: **Atal Pension Yojana** is NOT in Schedule I of the 2008 Act — option **(4)**.
Schedule I lists **IGNOAPS, National Family Benefit Scheme, Janani Suraksha Yojana, Janashree Bima Yojana, Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana, RSBY**, plus schemes for weavers, artisans, fishermen.
xa: APY came in **2015**, replacing **Swavalamban**.
The 2008 Act set up a **National Social Security Board**.

145.s: The Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY), launched in 2008 for BPL families, provided hospitalisation cover of:
145.x: RSBY (2008) gave BPL families ₹30,000 hospitalisation cover and was later subsumed in AB-PMJAY.
xa: It is listed in **Schedule I** of the **2008 Act**.
⚠ **Ashraya Bima** (**2001**) = job-loss; **Swavalamban** (**2010**) = NPS-Lite.

145.s: The Swavalamban scheme for unorganised workers joining NPS-Lite was replaced in 2015 by:
145.x: Swavalamban (2010) was replaced by the Atal Pension Yojana in 2015; Ashraya Bima Yojana (2001, LIC) was for workers who lost jobs.
xa: APY gives a guaranteed **₹1,000-5,000/month** from **60**, run by **PFRDA**.
Swavalamban is distinct from **PM-SYM** (**March 2019**), which pays **₹3,000/month** from **60**.

145.s: The entry age for PM-SYM, which assures ₹3,000 a month from age 60, is:
145.x: PM-SYM entry age is 18-40 (18-50 is PMJJBY); it covers unorganised workers earning up to ₹15,000 a month.
xa: Contribution: **₹55-200/month** by entry age; launched **March 2019**.
Enrolment: **over 54 lakh** (Aug 2026), **53.1%** women.

145.s: The Atal Pension Yojana (2015) is administered by:
145.x: APY gives a guaranteed pension of ₹1,000–₹5,000 from age 60 and is run by PFRDA.
xa: Entry age: **18-40**.
It replaced **Swavalamban** (**2010**).

145.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: PMJJBY — accident death and disability cover
PMSBY — ₹2 lakh life cover for death from any cause
PMJJBY — ₹2 lakh life cover for death from any cause
Atal Pension Yojana — ₹436 annual premium for life cover
145.x: PMJJBY provides ₹2 lakh life cover for death from any cause for an annual premium of ₹436. PMSBY concerns accidental death and disability cover.
145.tq: Separate life insurance, accident insurance and pension benefits among similar abbreviations.
xs: **PMJJBY** gives **₹2 lakh** life cover for **death from any cause** — option **(3)**.
Its premium is **₹436/year**, so the APY pairing is wrong.
xa: ⚠ PMJJBY entry age is **18-50**; PM-SYM, NPS-Traders and APY are **18-40**.
PMJJBY is one of the **15** schemes linked by the **e-Shram One-Stop Solution**.

145.s: Which of the following is NOT a condition that excludes a person from PM-SYM and NPS-Traders eligibility?
o: Being a worker in the unorganised sector
145.x: Membership of EPFO, ESIC or government-funded NPS, and being an income-tax payer, excludes eligibility. Being an unorganised-sector worker is not an exclusion; PM-SYM is specifically intended for such workers.
145.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the list of exclusion conditions.
xs: **Being an unorganised-sector worker** is NOT an exclusion — option **(3)** — PM-SYM is meant for them.
Excluded: members of **EPFO, ESIC** or government-funded **NPS**, and **income-tax payers**.
xa: ⚠ **Trap:** "NPS members are also eligible" is **wrong**.
PM-SYM is for workers earning **≤ ₹15,000/month**.

145.s: Which one of the following persons is eligible for registration on the e-Shram portal?
o: A 15-year-old unorganised worker who is not an income-tax payer
A 25-year-old unorganised worker who is an income-tax payer
A 40-year-old unorganised worker who is not an income-tax payer and is not covered by EPFO or ESIC
A 62-year-old unorganised worker who is not covered by any social-security scheme
145.x: Eligibility covers unorganised workers aged 16 to 59 who are not income-tax payers and are not members of EPFO or ESIC.
145.tq: Apply all eligibility conditions together rather than relying on age alone.
xs: The **40-year-old** unorganised worker who is **not an income-tax payer** and **not in EPFO/ESIC** is eligible — option **(3)**.
Eligibility: ages **16-59**, so **15** and **62** are out; **income-tax payers** are excluded.
xa: ⚠ e-Shram age = **16-59**; gig registration under the Code = from **age 16**.
Registration gives a **12-digit UAN**.

145.s: Which of the following statements about ESIC coverage is correct?
o: It is restricted to establishments in selected States only.
It is compulsory only for units employing fewer than 10 persons.
It is pan-India and voluntary for units employing fewer than 10 persons.
It applies exclusively to government establishments.
145.x: ESIC coverage is pan-India and voluntary for establishments with fewer than 10 employees.
145.tq: Use the location and threshold qualifiers to reject overbroad statements.
xs: **ESIC** coverage is now **pan-India** and **voluntary** for units with **fewer than 10** employees — option **(3)**.
e-Shram eligibility excludes **ESIC** members.
xa: **PMVBRY:** **₹99,446 crore** for **3.5 crore** jobs.
First-time employees get **one month's wage**, up to **₹15,000**.

145.s: NCEUS was set up in 2004 under the chairmanship of:
145.x: The National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector was set up in 2004 and chaired by Arjun Sengupta.
xs: **NCEUS** was set up in **2004** under **Arjun Sengupta** — option **(3)**.
It studied enterprises in the **unorganised sector**.
xa: Its **2007** report found about **77%** of Indians living on under **₹20 a day**.
Today **over 90%** of India's ~600 million workers are informal.

145.s: Which of the following correctly represents the informal workforce situation described for India?
o: Exactly 77% of the total workforce is informal.
Over 90% of the workforce is employed only in the organised sector.
Less than 50% of roughly 600 million workers are informal.
Over 90% of roughly 600 million workers are informal.
145.x: Over 90% of India's roughly 600 million workers are informal. This is distinct from the 77% figure in the NCEUS poverty estimate.
145.tq: Separate the informal-workforce percentage from the NCEUS poverty percentage.
xs: **Over 90%** of India's ~**600 million** workers are **informal** — option **(4)**.
⚠ **77%** is the NCEUS figure for people living on under **₹20 a day**, not the informal share.
xa: Total workforce: **61.6 crore** (PLFS 2025).
**e-Shram** registrations: **over 31.78 crore** (July 2026).

145.s: At the district level, which body is responsible for identifying and releasing bonded labourers under the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976?
145.x: District-level Vigilance Committees are responsible for identifying and releasing bonded labourers under the 1976 Act.
145.tq: Identify the authority assigned the specific enforcement function.
xs: District-level **Vigilance Committees** identify and release bonded labourers — option **(4)**.
They work under the **Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976**.
xa: The Act gives effect to **Article 23**, which bans **begar** and forced labour.
A **Central Sector Scheme** for rehabilitation of bonded labourers came in **2016**.

145.s: Article 23 of the Constitution, which prohibits begar and other forms of forced labour, is given effect for bonded labour mainly through which law?
145.x: Article 23 bans begar and forced labour, and the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976 abolishes bonded labour, with district Vigilance Committees to identify and release bonded labourers. The Contract Labour Act regulates contract labour, the Minimum Wages Act fixes wages, and the 2008 Act set up the National Social Security Board for unorganised workers.
145.tq: Art 23 -> Bonded Labour Abolition Act 1976 -> district Vigilance Committees.
xs: **Article 23** is given effect by the **Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976** — option **(1)**.
The **2008 Act** set up a **National Social Security Board** for unorganised workers, not bonded labour.
xa: District **Vigilance Committees** identify and release bonded labourers.
Rehabilitation scheme: **2016**.

145.s: In the Union Budget of 2015-16 which one of the following pension schemes has been reintroduced ?

146.s: A complaint is not decided within 21 days of filing. Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, what is the consequence mentioned in the legislation?
o: It is deemed to have been dismissed
It is automatically transferred to the National Commission
It is deemed to have been admitted
146.x: A complaint not decided within 21 days is deemed to have been admitted.
146.tq: Use the precise statutory time limit and distinguish admission from dismissal.
xs: A complaint not decided within **21 days** is **deemed admitted** — option **(3)**.
It is not dismissed or transferred.
xa: Complaints may be filed where the complainant **lives or works**.
⚠ The e-commerce grievance officer must acknowledge in **48 hours** and redress in **one month**.

146.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the six consumer rights recognised under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
146.x: The six rights include safety, information, choice, hearing, redressal and consumer awareness. A right to private ownership is not included in this list.
146.tq: Find the odd legal entitlement among the recognised consumer rights.
xs: The **right to private ownership** is NOT one of the six consumer rights — option **(3)**.
The six: **safety**, be **informed**, **choose**, be **heard**, **seek redressal**, **consumer awareness**.
xa: Consumers may get **food samples tested** (UPSC 2012 key).
A **legal heir** of a deceased consumer may file a complaint.

146.s: Which one of the following persons would generally be treated as a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
o: A person purchasing services for commercial exploitation
A person purchasing goods solely for a large-scale business activity
A person purchasing goods for resale
A person making an online purchase for personal use
146.x: The definition includes online and electronic purchases for personal use. A person buying for resale or commercial use is generally excluded.
146.tq: Apply the personal-use and commercial-purpose distinction to a factual situation.
xs: A person making an **online purchase** for **personal use** is a consumer — option **(4)**.
The definition **includes online and electronic purchases**; a buyer for **resale/commercial use** is not a consumer.
xa: **"Advertisement"** includes electronic media, internet and websites.
A **legal heir** of a deceased consumer may file a complaint.

146.s: Which of the following bodies was introduced by the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
146.x: The 2019 Act introduced the CCPA, along with product liability, e-commerce rules and penalties for adulterated goods; the NCDRC dates from 1988.
xa: It also brought **e-filing** and **videoconference** hearings.
**Mediation** cells are attached to the Commissions.

146.s: Under the 2021 Rules, a consumer complaint involving consideration of ₹40 lakh falls within the original pecuniary jurisdiction of which body?
146.x: Under the 2021 Rules, the District Commission has jurisdiction over matters up to ₹50 lakh.
146.tq: Apply the lower pecuniary threshold to a concrete fact situation.
xs: **₹40 lakh** falls within the **District Commission (DCDRC)** limit of up to **₹50 lakh** — option **(1)**.
The **State** handles **₹50 lakh** to **₹2 crore**; the **National** above **₹2 crore**.
xa: Jurisdiction depends on the **value of the consideration paid**, not compensation claimed.
⚠ The original CPA 2019 slabs (**₹1 crore / ₹10 crore**) were revised in **2021**.

146.s: The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission was set up in:
146.x: The NCDRC was set up in 1988; its original orders are appealable to the Supreme Court within 30 days.
xa: There are over **35** State and **600+** District Commissions.
**Aug 2026:** the SC sought an NCDRC report on pendency — **5.7 lakh** cases.

146.s: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, the District, State and National Commissions were called:
146.x: They were Consumer Forums under the 1986 Act; they are quasi-judicial bodies, not ordinary civil courts under the CPC.
xa: District → State appeal: **45 days**; State → National: **30 days**.
**NCDRC** was set up in **1988**.

146.s: An appeal against an order of a State Consumer Commission lies to the National Commission within:
146.x: State to National is within 30 days; District to State is within 45 days and National to Supreme Court within 30 days.
xa: ⚠ Appeal days: **45** only for District → State; both others **30**.
No appeal lies against a **mediated settlement**.

146.s: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, consumer mediation cells are attached to:
146.x: Mediation cells are attached to the District, State and National Consumer Commissions, not High Courts.
xa: **No appeal** lies against a mediated settlement.
Mediation was introduced by **CPA 2019**.

146.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Consumer Helpline (NCH):
1. Its toll-free number is 1915.
2. It has convergence partners such as e-commerce companies.
3. It is a consumer court attached to the National Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
146.x: Statement 1 is correct: the toll-free number is 1915. Statement 2 is correct: e-commerce companies are convergence partners. Statement 3 is wrong: the NCH is a helpline, not a consumer court. Hence 1 and 2 only.
146.tq: NCH = helpline 1915 with convergence partners; courts are the Commissions.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: the **NCH** toll-free number is **1915**.
Statement 2 is correct: it has **convergence partners** such as e-commerce companies.
Statement 3 is wrong: it is a **helpline**, not a consumer court. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: The **2026 E-Commerce Amendment Rules** require platforms to join the **NCH convergence** process.
The awareness campaign is **"Jago Grahak Jago"**, with mascot **"Jagriti"**.

146.s: The Drug and Magic remedies Act, 1954 prohibit
o: Promotion of more expensive medicines over generic drugs
146.x: The Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 specifically prohibits the publication of advertisements that make false or misleading claims about the efficacy of drugs and remedies.

146.s: The Central Consumer Protection Authority came into existence on:
146.x: The CCPA came into existence on 24 July 2020; 24 December is National Consumer Day.
xa: **24 December** is National Consumer Day.
CCPA fined **Meta ₹10 lakh** over walkie-talkie listings.

146.s: Which body can inquire into violations of consumer rights, file class-action complaints and impose penalties?
146.x: The CCPA can inquire into violations, order recalls and refunds, file class-action complaints and impose penalties.
xa: Misleading ad penalty (**Section 21**): up to **₹10 lakh**; repeat **₹50 lakh**.
Criticism: platforms dispute **CCPA** jurisdiction.

146.s:
Consider the following statements about penalties for misleading advertisements under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019:
1. Under Section 21, the penalty may extend to Rs 10 lakh, and to Rs 50 lakh for a repeat offence.
2. An endorser may be barred from endorsing for up to 3 years for a first offence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
146.x: Statement 1 is correct: up to Rs 10 lakh, and up to Rs 50 lakh for a repeat offence. Statement 2 is wrong: the endorser ban is up to 1 year for a first offence; 3 years applies only to a repeat. Hence 1 only.
146.tq: Ban: 1 year, repeat 3 years; penalty: 10 lakh, repeat 50 lakh.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: **Section 21** penalty is up to **₹10 lakh**, and **₹50 lakh** for a repeat.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **endorser ban** is up to **1 year** for a first offence; **3 years** for a repeat. So **1 only** — option **(1)**.
xa: **June 2022 guidelines:** endorsements must reflect genuine opinion, with material connection **disclosed**.
CCPA issued advisories against celebrity endorsements of **betting apps**.

146.s: Under the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, the grievance officer of an e-commerce entity must acknowledge a consumer complaint and redress it within:
146.x: The Rules require acknowledgement within 48 hours and redressal within one month. 24 hours/15 days, 48 hours/21 days and 72 hours/one month each get at least one period wrong (21 days is the deemed-admission period of Consumer Commissions).
146.tq: 48 hours to acknowledge, one month to redress.
xs: The grievance officer must **acknowledge** within **48 hours** and **redress** within **one month** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **21 days** is the deemed-admission period for Consumer Commissions, not this.
xa: The 2026 rules require platforms to join **NCH convergence**.
The Rules were notified under **CPA 2019**.

146.s: The Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 specified how many dark patterns?
146.x: The 2023 Guidelines specified 13 dark patterns, including false urgency and basket sneaking.
146.tq: Test the exact numerical figure associated with the Guidelines.
xs: The **Dark Patterns Guidelines, 2023** specify **13** dark patterns — option **(3)**.
Examples: **false urgency**, **basket sneaking**.
xa: The 2026 rules require an **annual self-audit** and a displayed **compliance certificate**.
The Guidelines were issued under the **E-Commerce** framework of **CPA 2019**.

146.s: The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026 were gazetted on 9 September 2026 and became effective on:
146.x: The 2026 Amendment Rules were gazetted on 9 September 2026 and are effective from 1 January 2027.
146.tq: Distinguish the gazette date from the date of commencement.
xs: The **2026 Amendment Rules** were gazetted **9 Sep 2026** and are effective **1 January 2027** — option **(3)**.
**24 December** is National Consumer Day; **15 March** is World Consumer Rights Day.
xa: They require disclosure of **importer and country of origin**.
Prior price for discounts = **lowest in the preceding 30 days**.

146.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026?
o: The prior price shown with a discount must be the lowest price in the preceding 30 days
E-commerce entities must join the National Consumer Helpline convergence process
Search results must not be manipulated
Sponsored listings need not be disclosed if the product is offered at a reduced price
146.x: Sponsored listings must be clearly disclosed; there is no reduced-price exception.
xa: Dark patterns: **annual self-audit** + compliance certificate.
Platforms must also disclose **importer and country of origin**.

146.s: The e-Daakhil facility for online filing has been merged into which portal?
146.x: The e-Daakhil online filing facility has been merged into the e-Jagriti portal.
146.tq: Discriminate between similarly named digital public-service portals.
xs: **e-Daakhil** online filing is now merged into the **e-Jagriti** portal — option **(1)**.
CPA 2019 allows **e-filing** and **videoconference** hearings.
xa: ⚠ **e-Jagriti** = portal; **"Jagriti"** = mascot of **Jago Grahak Jago**.
**National Consumer Helpline**: toll-free **1915**.

146.s:
Assertion (A): The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 impose identical liabilities on marketplace and inventory entities.
Reason (R): An inventory entity owns the goods or services that it sells through the platform.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
146.x: The Rules distinguish the liabilities of the two: a marketplace entity is a platform intermediary, whereas an inventory entity owns the goods it sells.
xa: The Rules were notified by the **Department of Consumer Affairs**.
2026 rules: **importer and country of origin** must be disclosed.

146.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: FPO mark – Industrial and consumer products
146.x: Hallmark certifies gold and silver jewellery. ISI is for industrial and consumer products, Agmark for agricultural produce and FPO for processed fruit products.
xa: ISI is under **BIS** (now **BIS Act 2016**).
**Eco Mark** (**1991**, BIS) — eco-friendly products.

146.s: The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has been replaced by which of the following laws?
146.x: The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was replaced by the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The Legal Metrology Act, 2009 deals with weights and measures; the BIS Act, 2016 governs the ISI mark and hallmarking; the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 replaced the 1986 consumer law.
146.tq: PFA Act 1954 -> Food Safety and Standards Act 2006.
xs: The **Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954** was replaced by the **Food Safety and Standards Act 2006** — option **(1)**.
The **BIS Act 2016** governs the ISI mark; **CPA 2019** replaced the 1986 Act.
xa: **Legal Metrology Act 2009:** **7** sections decriminalised (**2023**); **12** more proposed in Jan Vishwas 2.0.
Consumers may get **food samples tested**.

146.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the development of the UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection?
o: Adopted in 1985, expanded in 1999 and revised in 2015
Adopted in 1999, expanded in 2005 and revised in 2015
Adopted in 1985, expanded in 2005 and revised in 2020
Adopted in 1991, expanded in 1999 and revised in 2015
146.x: The Guidelines were first adopted in 1985, expanded in 1999 to include sustainable consumption and revised in 2015.
146.tq: Use the chronological sequence to distinguish closely related revision years.
xs: The **UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection** were first **adopted** by the UN General Assembly in **1985**, **expanded** in **1999** and **revised** in **2015** — option **(1)**.
The **1999** expansion added **sustainable consumption**.
xa: The 1985 adoption was asked in the **APPSC 2025** key.
**World Consumer Rights Day** is **15 March**; **National Consumer Day** is **24 December**.
**Consumers International** was founded in **1960** (as IOCU), based in **London**.

146.s: World Consumer Rights Day commemorates the consumer-rights speech delivered by:
146.x: The day marks John F. Kennedy's 1962 speech on consumer rights.
146.tq: Discriminate between closely related political figures and years.
xs: **World Consumer Rights Day** (**15 March**) marks **John F. Kennedy's 1962** speech on consumer rights — option **(4)**.
The other presidents and years are not linked to the day.
xa: ⚠ **15 March** = World Consumer Rights Day; **24 December** = National Consumer Day (India).
**UN Guidelines** were first adopted in **1985**.

146.s: For determining the pecuniary jurisdiction of a Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, the relevant criterion is:
o: The annual income of the complainant
The compensation claimed by the complainant
The market value of the goods at the time of filing
The value of consideration paid for the goods or services
146.x: Jurisdiction is determined by the value of consideration paid for the goods or services, not by the compensation claimed.
146.tq: Apply the governing criterion to distinguish consideration from compensation.
xs: Jurisdiction depends on the **value of the consideration paid** for goods/services — option **(4)**.
It is **not** the compensation claimed.
xa: Slabs (2021): District up to **₹50 lakh**; State **₹50 lakh-₹2 crore**; National above **₹2 crore**.
⚠ Original CPA 2019 slabs were **₹1 crore / ₹10 crore**.

146.s: National Consumer Day in India is observed on:
146.x: National Consumer Day is 24 December; World Consumer Rights Day is 15 March.
xa: ⚠ **e-Jagriti** is the filing portal, not the mascot.
**15 March** marks **J.F. Kennedy's 1962** consumer-rights speech; **24 December** marks the **1986** Act.

146.s: In Indian Medical Association v. V.P. Shantha (1995), the Supreme Court held that:
o: All medical services, including wholly free services, are outside consumer law.
Medical services paid for, including services in hospitals charging some patients, constitute “service” under the Consumer Protection Act.
Medical negligence can never be considered by consumer fora.
Only services provided in government hospitals are covered by consumer law.
146.x: The 1995 decision held that paid medical services, including services in hospitals that charge some patients, fall within the definition of service under consumer law. Wholly free services are excluded.
146.tq: Use the paid-versus-wholly-free distinction to identify the holding.
xs: **IMA v. V.P. Shantha (1995):** **paid medical services**, including those in hospitals charging some patients, are a **"service"** under the Consumer Protection Act — option **(2)**.
So **medical negligence** can go to consumer fora; only **wholly free** services are excluded.
xa: A **legal heir** of a deceased consumer may file a complaint.
CPA 2019 brought **product liability** of service providers.

146.s:
With reference to consumer remedies, consider the following statements:
1. A consumer may get food samples tested.
2. The legal heir of a deceased consumer may file a consumer complaint.
3. A legal heir can file a complaint only when the deceased consumer had received wholly free medical services.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
146.x: Consumers may get food samples tested, and the legal heir of a deceased consumer may file a complaint. Statement 3 is false because the right is not confined to wholly free medical services.
146.tq: Retain the two recognised consumer remedies and reject the restrictive condition.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: consumers may get **food samples tested**, and the **legal heir** of a deceased consumer may file a complaint (**UPSC 2012** key).
Statement 3 is wrong: the heir's right is not limited to free medical services. So **1 and 2 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: ⚠ Under **V.P. Shantha (1995)**, **wholly free** medical services are outside consumer law.
Complaints may be filed where the complainant **lives or works**.

146.s:
With reference to consumers rights/privileges under the provisions of law in India, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
1. Consumers are empowered to take samples for food testing.
2. When a consumer files a complaint in any Consumer Forum, no fee is required to be paid.
3. In the case of death of a consumer, his/her legal heir can file a complaint in the Consumer Forum on his/her behalf.
Select the correct answer using the code given below
146.x: In 1986, the Government of India passed the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 to protect the consumer rights. Under this Act, the consumers are empowered to take samples for food testing. A consumer can file his complaint in the Consumer Forum on any malfunction or failure of the product. He has to pay a small fee for that. In the case of the death of a consumer, his/her legal heir can file a complaint in the Consumer Forum on his/her behalf. The Consumer Protection Act, 2019, which received the President's assent on 9 August, 2019 has replaced the Consumer Protection Act, 1986.

146.s: In which year did the United Nations first adopted the Guidelines for Consumer Protection ?

147.s: Setting up Bhilai with the USSR and Rourkela with West Germany illustrates which determinant of India's foreign policy?
147.x: Taking aid and technology from both blocs reflects the economy as a determinant; Himalayan frontiers reflect geography.
xa: ⚠ **Bhilai** = USSR; **Rourkela** = West Germany.
After **1991**, the economic determinant meant a push for investment.
**History:** the freedom struggle produced anti-colonialism and Asian solidarity.

147.s:
Consider the following statements about the historical roots of India's foreign policy:
1. The freedom struggle produced anti-colonialism.
2. It contributed to Asian solidarity.
3. Nehru's broadcast of 7 September 1946 expressed independence from power blocs.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
147.x: All three describe the historical influence on India's foreign policy, including Nehru's 7 September 1946 broadcast.
xa: Leadership: **Nehru's idealism**, **Indira's realism**.
ICWA hosted the **Asian Relations Conference, 1947**.

147.s: Article 51 of the Constitution directs the State to encourage settlement of international disputes by:
147.x: Article 51 directs the State to encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration.
147.tq: Match the constitutional directive with its precise operative term.
xs: **Article 51** (DPSP) directs the State to encourage settlement of disputes by **arbitration** — option **(4)**.
Asked in **UPPSC 2016**.
xa: Art. 51 also asks the State to promote **international peace and security** and **just and honourable relations** between nations.
**Article 73:** treaties are made by the **executive**.

147.s: Foreign affairs is listed in which entry of the Union List?
147.x: Entry 10 is foreign affairs; Entry 14 treaties, Entry 15 war and peace, and Entries 11–13 diplomatic representation and the UN.
xa: These are in **List I** of the **Seventh Schedule**.
**Article 73** lets the executive make treaties.

147.s: India's demand for UNSC reform is summed up in its call for:
147.x: India seeks UNSC reform and advocates 'reformed multilateralism', strengthening rather than weakening multilateral bodies.
xa: **Article 51** encourages settlement of disputes by **arbitration**.
India pressed for **nuclear disarmament** at **Belgrade (1961)**.

147.s:
Consider the following statements about Panchsheel:
1. It was set out in the preamble of the Agreement on Trade and Intercourse between India and the Tibet Region of China.
2. That agreement was signed on 29 April 1955.
3. Burma adopted Panchsheel in a joint declaration later in 1954.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
147.x: Statement 1 is correct: the source is the preamble of the India-Tibet Region of China trade agreement. Statement 2 is wrong: it was signed on 29 April 1954 (1955 is Bandung). Statement 3 is correct: Burma adopted it later in 1954. Hence 1 and 3 only.
147.tq: Panchsheel and its Burma adoption are both 1954; 1955 is Bandung.
xs: Statement 1 is correct: Panchsheel comes from the preamble of the **Agreement on Trade and Intercourse between India and the Tibet Region of China**.
Statement 2 is wrong: it was signed on **29 April 1954**, not 1955.
Statement 3 is correct: **Burma** adopted it later in **1954**. So **1 and 3 only** — option **(2)**.
xa: ⚠ **1955** is **Bandung**, where it was absorbed into the **Ten Principles**.
⚠ Don't confuse with Nehru's **Tribal Panchsheel (1952)**, drafted with **Verrier Elwin**.

147.s: Nehru's Tribal Panchsheel (1952) was drafted with:
147.x: Nehru's Tribal Panchsheel was drafted with Verrier Elwin in 1952 and dealt with tribal policy, unlike the international Panchsheel.
xa: International Panchsheel became a core NAM principle at **Belgrade (1961)**.
**UNGA** recognised it as a principle of international law in **1957**.
