157.s:
India is a member of which of the following?
1. Asian Development Bank
2. Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation
3. Colombo Plan
4. Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD)
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
157.x: India is a member of the Asian Development Bank and the Colombo Plan. However, India is not a member of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) or the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).

158.s: The Uruguay Round (1986–1993/94), which led to the creation of the WTO, was the ____ round of GATT negotiations.
158.x: The Uruguay Round was the eighth GATT round; it involved 123 countries and created the WTO.
xa: It produced **TRIPS**, **GATS** and the **AoA**.
⚠ **Marrakesh** = WTO agreement; **Uruguay** = round that created it; **Geneva** = HQ.
**Dunkel Draft**: **20 Oct 1991**, by **Arthur Dunkel**.

158.s: Non-tariff barrier codes are associated with which GATT round?
158.x: Non-tariff barrier codes came from the Tokyo Round; the Uruguay Round produced TRIPS, GATS and the Agreement on Agriculture.
xa: **TRIPS** = minimum standards for all forms of IPR; **GATS** = trade in services; **AoA** = market access, domestic support, export subsidies.
The **Kennedy Round** (**1964-67**) gave the first **Anti-Dumping Code**.
Since then only two new agreements: **Trade Facilitation** and **Fisheries Subsidies**.

158.s: Which GATT Article permits free trade agreements as exceptions to the MFN principle, if they cover substantially all trade?
158.x: GATT Article XXIV allows FTAs as MFN exceptions provided they cover substantially all trade.
xa: India has **15 FTAs** and **6 PTAs**; latest **EFTA TEPA** and **UK CETA**.
The **India-EU FTA** covers **97.5%** of EU tariff lines.
GATT survives as an **integral WTO agreement**.

158.s: The World Trade Organization was established on 1 January 1995 under which agreement?
o: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
158.x: The WTO was established on 1 January 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement after the Uruguay Round.
158.tq: Use the founding agreement and date as the identifying pair.
xs: The WTO was established on **1 January 1995** under the **Marrakesh Agreement** — option **(2)**.
**GATT** was the predecessor system; **Doha** is a later round; **Singapore** hosted **MC1** (**1996**).
xa: ⚠ **Marrakesh** = WTO agreement; **Uruguay** = round; **Geneva** = HQ.
WTO membership: **166** (Mar **2026**).
Decision-making is **one-country-one-vote**, by consensus.

158.s:
Consider the following statements about the World Trade Organization:
1. It had 166 members as of March 2026.
2. Comoros and Timor-Leste joined it in 2024.
3. It is headquartered at Vienna.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
158.x: Statement 1 is correct: 166 members in March 2026 (older sources say 164). Statement 2 is correct: Comoros and Timor-Leste are the latest members (2024). Statement 3 is wrong: the WTO is headquartered at Geneva. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, C and D include statement 3.
158.tq: WTO = Geneva; 164 is the outdated count, 166 the current one.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: **166** members (Mar **2026**); older notes say **164**.
Statement 2: **Comoros and Timor-Leste** joined in **2024**.
Statement 3 wrong: the WTO is headquartered at **Geneva**, not Vienna.
xa: The WTO was set up on **1 January 1995** (**Marrakesh Agreement**).
**MC12** was also held in **Geneva** (**June 2022**).
Decision-making: **one-country-one-vote**, consensus-based.

158.s:
Assertion (A): Developing countries can obtain bargaining space in WTO negotiations.
Reason (R): The WTO follows a one-country-one-vote principle.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
158.x: Both are true, and the one-country-one-vote principle explains the bargaining space developing countries get.
xa: WTO decisions are **consensus-based**.
⚠ Consensus can also cause **paralysis**, pushing countries to **FTAs**.
WTO membership: **166** (Mar **2026**).

158.s: The Dunkel Draft (1991), prepared under Arthur Dunkel, belonged to which round of trade negotiations?
158.x: The Dunkel Draft of 1991, associated with Arthur Dunkel, was part of the Uruguay Round.
xa: ⚠ The Dunkel Draft belongs to the **Uruguay Round**, not Doha.
The Uruguay Round ran **1986-1993/94** with **123** countries.
It created the **WTO** with **TRIPS, GATS, AoA**.
158.fixed: Dunkel Draft (Draft Final Act) was tabled 20 December 1991, not 20 October

158.s: Which GATT round was held during 1964–67?
158.x: The Kennedy Round ran 1964–67; the Tokyo Round 1973–79, Uruguay 1986–93/94 and Doha was launched in 2001.
xa: GATT held **8 rounds** in all; Uruguay was the **8th**.
Kennedy = **first Anti-Dumping Code**; Tokyo = **non-tariff barrier codes**.
Uruguay created the **WTO**.

158.s: Which WTO Ministerial Conferences are specifically associated with a breakdown of negotiations?
158.x: The Seattle Ministerial Conference of 1999 and the Cancún Ministerial Conference of 2003 broke down.
158.tq: Separate failed negotiating conferences from conferences identified mainly by their locations or dates.
xs: **Seattle (1999)** and **Cancún (2003)** Ministerials **broke down** — option **(1)** "**Seattle and Cancún**".
**Singapore** was **MC1 (1996)**; **Geneva** hosted **MC12 (2022)**; **Abu Dhabi** hosted **MC13 (2024)**.
xa: **MC12** adopted a limited **TRIPS waiver** for vaccine patents.
At **MC14** (Yaoundé, **2026**), the **e-commerce** and **TRIPS non-violation** moratoria lapsed.
The **Doha Development Agenda** (**2001**) has stalled.

158.s: The Director General of World Trade Organization is
158.x: Pascal Lamy served as the Director- General of the World Trade Organization (WTO) during this period, overseeing global trade negotiations and dispute resolution. A French politician and economist, he previously served as EU Trade Commissioner. His tenure focused on advancing the stalled Doha Development Round.

158.s: Which of the following WTO bodies is wrongly matched with its function?
o: General Council – Runs the WTO between Ministerial Conferences
Dispute Settlement Body – Deals with panel and Appellate Body rulings
Trade Policy Review Body – Highest decision-making body
158.x: The Trade Policy Review Body conducts periodic reviews of members' trade policies; the Ministerial Conference is the highest decision-making body.
xa: The Ministerial Conference must meet **at least once every two years**.
The **Council for Trade in Goods** oversees **GATT** (committees on agriculture, market access, **TBT**, **SPS**).
The US **blocked Appellate Body appointments**, paralysing the two-tier system.

158.s:
Consider the following statements about the WTO Ministerial Conference:
1. It must meet at least once every two years.
2. MC14 was held at Yaounde, Cameroon, in March 2026.
3. MC13 was held at Geneva in 2022.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
158.x: Statement 1 is correct: the MC, the highest decision-making body, must meet at least once every two years. Statement 2 is correct: MC14 was at Yaounde, Cameroon (March 2026). Statement 3 is wrong: MC13 was at Abu Dhabi (Feb 2024); Geneva 2022 was MC12. So 1 and 2 only.
158.tq: MC12 Geneva 2022, MC13 Abu Dhabi 2024, MC14 Yaounde 2026.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 2 only**".
Statement 1: the **Ministerial Conference** must meet **at least once every two years**.
Statement 2: **MC14** was held at **Yaoundé, Cameroon (March 2026)**.
Statement 3 wrong: **MC13** was at **Abu Dhabi (Feb 2024)**; **Geneva (June 2022)** was **MC12**.
xa: **MC1** = **Singapore 1996**.
Seattle (**1999**) and Cancún (**2003**) broke down.
MC14 left **PSH** and **fisheries Phase 2** unresolved.

158.s: In India, which body handles anti-dumping, countervailing and safeguard investigations under WTO rules?
158.x: The Directorate General of Trade Remedies handles anti-dumping, countervailing and safeguard investigations in India.
158.tq: Ask which domestic authority performs the specified trade-remedy function.
xs: The **Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR)** handles **anti-dumping, countervailing and safeguard** investigations — option **(3)**.
The **TPRB** is a WTO body reviewing members' trade policies, not an Indian investigator.
xa: **Anti-dumping** = duties on goods sold below **normal value**.
Countervailing duties target **actionable** subsidies under **SCM**.
India raised the **UK steel safeguard** at the **Council for Trade in Goods** (**May 2026**).

158.s: The present crisis in the WTO dispute-settlement system primarily resulted from:
o: The African Group rejecting all panel reports
The General Council refusing to meet between Ministerial Conferences
India withdrawing from the Marrakesh Agreement
The United States blocking appointments to the Appellate Body
158.x: The United States blocked Appellate Body appointments, paralysing the WTO’s two-tier dispute-settlement system.
158.tq: Identify the actor responsible for the institutional blockage rather than the affected body.
xs: The crisis arose because the **United States blocked appointments to the Appellate Body** — option **(4)**.
This paralysed the WTO's **two-tier** dispute system.
xa: India's appeals now sit "**into the void**".
The crisis, with consensus paralysis, pushes countries towards **FTAs**.
The **DSB** handles panels and **Appellate Body** rulings.

158.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Anti-dumping — Duties on goods sold below normal value
TRIPS — Minimum standards for all forms of intellectual property rights
TRIMS — Investment measures that distort trade
GATS — Subsidies that are prohibited, actionable and non-actionable
158.x: GATS deals with trade in services. The classification of subsidies as prohibited, actionable and non-actionable belongs to the SCM Agreement.
158.tq: Detect the agreement-subject swap among neighbouring WTO agreements.
xs: **GATS — prohibited, actionable and non-actionable subsidies** is NOT correctly matched — option **(4)**.
**GATS** covers **trade in services** (banking, insurance); that subsidy classification belongs to **SCM**.
The others are correct: **Anti-dumping** — goods below normal value; **TRIPS** — minimum IPR standards; **TRIMS** — trade-distorting investment measures.
xa: **SCM** non-actionable subsidies: **R&D, regional, environment**.
**TRIMS** example: **local content** requirements.
**AoA** covers market access, domestic support and export subsidies.

158.s: To meet its TRIPS obligations, India enacted the Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act in:
158.x: The GI Act, 1999 was enacted to meet TRIPS obligations; the Patents Act was amended in 2005 for the same purpose.
xa: **TRIPS (1995)** sets **minimum global IPR standards**.
India's flexibilities: **Section 3(d)** (anti-evergreening) + **compulsory licensing**.
First compulsory licence: **Natco-Bayer** (**2012**).

158.s: The Doha Declaration on TRIPS and public health affirmed that TRIPS:
o: Prevents members from regulating medicines in public interest
Must not stop members from protecting public health
Eliminates compulsory licensing by developing countries
158.x: The Doha Declaration of 2001 affirmed that TRIPS must not prevent members from taking measures to protect public health.
158.tq: Test the public-health flexibility principle against restrictive distractors.
xs: The **Doha Declaration (2001)** said TRIPS **must not stop members from protecting public health** — option **(3)**.
So it supports, not eliminates, flexibilities like **compulsory licensing**.
xa: First compulsory licence in India: **Natco-Bayer** (**2012**).
**India-South Africa** proposed a **COVID TRIPS waiver** (**2020**); **MC12** adopted a limited waiver (**2022**).
**Section 3(d)** is India's anti-evergreening clause.

158.s:
Consider the following statements about the COVID-19 TRIPS waiver:
1. It was proposed jointly by India and Brazil in 2020.
2. MC12 (2022) adopted a limited waiver for vaccine patents.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
158.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the proposal (2020) came from India and South Africa, not Brazil. Statement 2 is correct: MC12 at Geneva in 2022 adopted a limited waiver for vaccine patents. So 2 only (B); A and C accept the wrong statement 1, D rejects the correct statement 2.
158.tq: COVID waiver = India + South Africa; outcome only a limited vaccine-patent waiver at MC12.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — option **(2)** "**2 only**".
Statement 1 wrong: the **2020** waiver proposal came from **India and South Africa**, not Brazil.
Statement 2 correct: **MC12 (2022)** adopted a **limited waiver for vaccine patents**.
xa: MC12 was held at **Geneva (June 2022)**.
The **Doha Declaration (2001)** on TRIPS and public health.
First compulsory licence: **Natco-Bayer** (**2012**).

158.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about WTO disputes involving India?
o: The USA challenged the JNNSM solar domestic-content rules and India lost in 2016
The EU, Japan and Chinese Taipei won a panel against India's ICT tariffs in 2023
The dispute over India's export subsidy schemes (MEIS, SEZ) was brought by the EU
The panel in the export subsidy (MEIS, SEZ) dispute ruled in 2019
158.x: The MEIS/SEZ export subsidy case was brought by the USA, not the EU (panel 2019).
xa: India's appeals sit "**into the void**" as the **Appellate Body** lacks members.
The US **blocked Appellate Body appointments**.
**SCM** classes subsidies as prohibited, actionable or non-actionable.

158.s: The WTO moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions lapsed on:
158.x: The moratorium lapsed on 31 March 2026 after MC14 failed to extend it; 66 members then signed a plurilateral agreement banning such duties.
xa: The moratorium had run since **1998**.
The **TRIPS non-violation** moratorium (since **1995**) also lapsed at MC14.
**Investment Facilitation for Development** has **120+** backers.

158.s:
Consider the following statements about Special and Differential Treatment (SDT) at the WTO:
1. The US wants to deny SDT to China, India, Brazil and Indonesia.
2. India supports withdrawing SDT from developing countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
158.x: Statement 1 is correct: the US wants to deny SDT to China, India, Brazil and Indonesia. Statement 2 is wrong: India defends SDT. So 1 only (A); B and C accept the wrong statement 2, D rejects the correct statement 1.
158.tq: India is on the defending side of SDT, the US on the denying side.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)** "**1 only**".
Statement 1: the **US** wants to deny **SDT** to **China, India, Brazil, Indonesia**.
Statement 2 wrong: **India defends SDT**.
xa: India's core food-security demand: a **permanent solution for PSH**.
India **opposes** bringing **plurilaterals** into the WTO rulebook.
**One-country-one-vote** gives developing countries bargaining space.

158.s: India's core demand in the WTO food-security negotiations is a permanent solution for:
158.x: India's core food-security demand is a permanent solution for public stockholding (PSH).
xa: **AoA** governs market access, **domestic support** and **export subsidies**.
India also defends **SDT** for developing countries.
**Fisheries Phase 2** was deferred to the **General Council**.

158.s: India opposes bringing which of the following plurilateral initiatives into the WTO rulebook?
158.x: Investment Facilitation for Development, backed by more than 120 members, is a plurilateral initiative that India opposes bringing into the WTO rulebook.
xa: **66 members** signed the plurilateral E-commerce Agreement banning duties on electronic transmissions.
The multilateral e-commerce moratorium lapsed on **31 March 2026**.
The only new multilateral agreements: **Trade Facilitation** + **Fisheries Subsidies**.

158.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the WTO's 14th Ministerial Conference (Yaoundé, March 2026)?
o: A permanent solution on public stockholding was agreed
No fisheries subsidies Phase 2 deal was reached
158.x: MC14 ended without a permanent solution on public stockholding; both moratoria lapsed and no fisheries Phase 2 deal was reached.
xa: The e-commerce moratorium dated from **1998**; the TRIPS one from **1995**.
Fisheries Phase 2 (overcapacity, overfishing) was **deferred to the General Council**.
**MC13** was at **Abu Dhabi (Feb 2024)**.

158.s: Which two agreements are identified as the only new WTO agreements concluded in the first 30 years of the organisation?
o: Trade Facilitation Agreement and Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
158.x: The Trade Facilitation Agreement and the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies are identified as the only new WTO agreements in that period.
158.tq: Use the word “only” carefully to identify the complete pair rather than older Uruguay Round agreements.
xs: The only new WTO agreements in **30** years are the **Trade Facilitation Agreement** and the **Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies** — option **(1)**.
**AoA, TRIPS, GATS, TRIMS, SPS, TBT** all came with the **Uruguay Round** package.
xa: **Fisheries Phase 2** (overcapacity, overfishing) remained unresolved at **MC14** → deferred to the **General Council**.
The WTO began on **1 January 1995**.
Plurilaterals like **Investment Facilitation for Development** are disputed; **India opposes** bringing them in.

158.s: Section 3(d) of India's Patents Act, used as a TRIPS flexibility, is aimed against:
158.x: India used Section 3(d) against evergreening, along with compulsory licensing, as TRIPS flexibilities for public health.
xa: First compulsory licence: **Natco-Bayer** (**2012**).
The **Doha Declaration (2001)** backs public-health measures under TRIPS.
India amended the **Patents Act** in **2005** to comply with TRIPS.

158.s: Phyto sanitary condition is a
158.x: Phytosanitary requirements (plant health / safety standards) are a form of non-tariff barrier, used by countries to regulate imports of agricultural products without imposing direct tariffs.

159.s: Which one of the following organisations was established through the Bangkok Declaration of 1967?
159.x: ASEAN was established in 1967 through the Bangkok Declaration.
159.tq: Identify the organisation from its founding declaration and year.
xs: **ASEAN** was set up by the **1967 Bangkok Declaration** — option **(3)**, by Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore and Thailand.
**SAARC** came from the **Dhaka** Charter (**1985**); **BIMSTEC** from a **1997** Bangkok Declaration; **SCO** from **Shanghai** (**2001**).
xa: ASEAN Secretariat: **Jakarta**; members now **11** with **Timor-Leste** (**2025**).
⚠ Two "Bangkok Declarations": **1967** = ASEAN; **1997** = BIMSTEC (as BIST-EC).
**Myanmar** is the only ASEAN state bordering India.

159.s: BIMSTEC, set up through the 1997 Bangkok Declaration, has its Secretariat at:
159.x: BIMSTEC originated through the 1997 Bangkok Declaration and its Secretariat is in Dhaka.
xa: It began as **BIST-EC**: Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Thailand.
BIMSTEC has **7** members; **Nepal + Bhutan** joined in **2004**.
⚠ BIMSTEC Secretariat = **Dhaka**; ASEAN = **Jakarta**.

159.s: The Council of Europe, founded in 1949, is headquartered at:
159.x: The Council of Europe sits at Strasbourg; Brussels is the seat of the EU.
xa: Council of Europe: **47** members (asked **2019**); **Russia expelled March 2022**.
EU: **27** members; last to join **Croatia (2013)**.
**Article 50** TEU (Lisbon Treaty) = exit clause, used for **Brexit**.

159.s: How many members does SAARC have?
159.x: SAARC comprises eight members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
159.tq: Recall the exact membership count and verify it against the member list.
xs: SAARC has **8** members — option **(3)**.
It includes **every land neighbour of India except China** (and Myanmar).
xa: SAARC Charter: **Dhaka, 8 Dec 1985**; Secretariat: **Kathmandu**.
SAARC observers: **China, Japan, USA, EU, Iran**.
⚠ "Number of members" is a favourite: SAARC **8**, BIMSTEC **7**, ASEAN **11**, Council of Europe **47**.

159.s: With the admission of Timor-Leste in 2025, the membership of ASEAN became:
159.x: Timor-Leste joined ASEAN in 2025, taking its membership to 11.
xa: GCC (**1981**, Riyadh): Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman.
⚠ Newest: ASEAN = **Timor-Leste**; EU = **Croatia**; NATO = **Finland + Sweden**.
The **East Asia Summit** has **19** members, incl. all **11** ASEAN states.

159.s: The headquarters of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation is located at
159.x: The SAARC Secretariat is located in Kathmandu, while its Charter was signed in Dhaka.
159.tq: Use the location trap involving the Charter venue and Secretariat headquarters.
xs: The SAARC Secretariat is at **Kathmandu** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Trap: the Charter was signed at **Dhaka** (**1985**), which also hosts the **BIMSTEC** Secretariat.
**Thimphu** hosts the **SAARC Development Fund**; **Colombo** hosted the **5th BIMSTEC Summit**.
xa: The **18th SAARC summit** (Kathmandu, **2014**) is the last one held.
The **19th** (Islamabad, **2016**) was cancelled after **Uri**.
**SAFTA** replaced **SAPTA**; in force **1 Jan 2006**.

159.s: Which one of the following is NOT an observer of SAARC?
159.x: SAARC's observers include China, Japan, the USA, the EU and Iran. Russia is not a SAARC observer.
159.tq: SAARC observers incl. China, Japan, USA, EU, Iran - not Russia.
xs: **Russia** is NOT a SAARC observer — option **(4)**.
SAARC observers: **China, Japan, USA, EU, Iran**.
xa: ⚠ China is a SAARC **observer** but **not** a member of **BIMSTEC**.
Russia was **expelled** from the **Council of Europe** (**March 2022**).
Russia is in the **East Asia Summit**'s **19** members.

159.s: The Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) is associated with which of the following organisations?
159.x: RATS is the counter-terrorism structure of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.
159.tq: Identify the organisation from the specialised institutional function.
xs: **RATS** is the counter-terror structure of the **Shanghai Cooperation Organisation** — option **(4)**.
RATS is located at **Tashkent**, while the SCO HQ is **Beijing**.
xa: SCO was founded in **2001** at **Shanghai**.
India and Pakistan became full SCO members in **2017 (Astana)**.
⚠ IORA's Secretariat is at **Ebene, Mauritius**; NATO dates from **1949**.

159.s: Which one of the following is not an ASEAN member?
159.x: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) consists of Southeast Asian countries such as Cambodia, Laos, and the Philippines. China, however, is not a member of ASEAN; it is a separate major Asian power and only maintains a dialogue partnership status with ASEAN.

159.s: Which of the following is not a member of the 'Gulf Cooperation Council'?
159.x: The GCC is a political, economic, social, and regional organisation. It was formed to address regional challenges faced by the Arab States of the Gulf. Members: Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and UAE.

159.s: Which of the following countries has taken membership of the European Union in July, 2013?
159.x: In July 2013, Croatia took membership of the European Union. The number of EU member states increased to 28 with Croatia joining the European Union. The European Economic Community established under the Treaty of Rome in the year 1957 was converted into the European Union in the year 1993. It is headquartered in Brussels (Belgium). Currently, there are 27 member countries in European Union after Brexit.

159.s: Which country was expelled from the Council of Europe in March 2022?
159.x: Russia was expelled from the Council of Europe, which had 47 members in 2019, in March 2022.
xa: Council of Europe: founded **1949**, HQ **Strasbourg**.
⚠ **Strasbourg** = Council of Europe; **Brussels** = EU.
**NATO** also dates from **1949**.

159.s:
Assertion (A): The United Kingdom's withdrawal from the European Union (Brexit) was carried out under Article 50 of the Treaty on European Union.
Reason (R): Article 50 of the Treaty on European Union is the EU's exit clause.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

160.x: The NDB was established at Fortaleza in 2014 and its headquarters is located in Shanghai.
160.tq: Match an institution with its founding venue and headquarters rather than confusing the two.
xs: The **NDB**, set up at **Fortaleza** in **2014**, is headquartered at **Shanghai** — option **(3)**.
**Fortaleza** is where it was agreed, not its HQ.
xa: The BRICS **Contingent Reserve Arrangement** (**2014**) is a **$100 billion** liquidity pool.
**Johannesburg** hosted the **2025** G20 meetings.
BRICS in **2011** had **20%** of GDP but only **11%** of IMF votes.

160.s: The BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement, created in 2014, has a liquidity pool of:
160.x: The BRICS CRA (2014) has a liquidity pool of 100 billion dollars.
xa: The **NDB** was also set up in **2014** (Fortaleza); HQ **Shanghai**.
⚠ The CRA is a **BRICS** body, not a Quad initiative.
India **avoids de-dollarisation** within BRICS.

160.s: Consider the following statements about IBSA: 1. It was founded in 2003 through the Brasilia Declaration. 2. The IBSA Trust Fund is managed by the World Bank. 3. IBSAMAR is its naval exercise. Which of the statements given above are correct?
160.x: Statement 1 is correct: IBSA was founded in 2003 by the Brasilia Declaration. Statement 2 is wrong: the IBSA Trust Fund (operational 2004, funds LDC projects) is managed by UNOSSC, not UNDP. Statement 3 is correct: IBSAMAR is the IBSA naval exercise. So 1 and 3 only (B); A misses statement 3, C and D include statement 2.
160.tq: IBSA Fund = UN Office for South-South Cooperation (UNOSSC).
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)** "**1 and 3 only**".
Statement 1: **IBSA** was founded in **2003** via the **Brasilia Declaration**.
Statement 2 wrong: the **IBSA Trust Fund** is managed by **UNOSSC**, not UNDP.
Statement 3: **IBSAMAR** is IBSA's naval exercise.
xa: The IBSA Trust Fund became operational in **2004** and funds **LDC** projects.
IBSA = **India, Brazil, South Africa**.
India's IBSA proposals (**Nov 2025**): **Fund for Climate-Resilient Agriculture**, **Digital Innovation Alliance**, **NSA-level dialogue**.
160.fixed: UNOSSC (manager of IBSA Fund) is hosted by UNDP, so 'managed by UNDP' is arguably true; replace with clearly false body, key unchanged

160.s: The Colombo Security Conclave began in 2011 as a maritime trilateral of India, Sri Lanka and:
160.x: The Colombo Security Conclave originated in 2011 as an India-Sri Lanka-Maldives maritime trilateral.
xa: Members now: **India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius, Bangladesh**; observer **Seychelles**.
Secretariat: **Colombo**.
Five pillars include **maritime safety and security** and **HADR**.

160.s: Which of the following is an observer, not a member, of the Colombo Security Conclave?
160.x: Seychelles is an observer; India, Mauritius and Bangladesh are members.

Secretariat: **Colombo**.

160.s: In climate negotiations, the BASIC grouping upholds the principle of:

Exclusive reliance on private climate finance
Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC)
Carbon border taxes on developing countries

160.s: The G20 accounts for approximately:
o: More than 40% of global GDP, 46% of trade and 55% of population
40% of global GDP, 50% of trade and one-third of population
85% of global GDP, more than 75% of trade and two-thirds of population
20% of global GDP, 11% of trade and half of population
160.x: The G20 represents approximately 85% of global GDP, more than 75% of global trade and two-thirds of the world's population.
160.tq: Keep the three indicators together and reject figures belonging to other groupings or periods.
xs: The **G20** accounts for **~85%** of GDP, **>75%** of trade and **two-thirds** of population — option **(3)**.
Option 1 mixes **BRICS** figures (**>40%** GDP, **55%** population) with the false "**46%** of trade" claim.
xa: G20 = **19 countries + EU + AU**.
BRICS in **2011**: **20%** of GDP but only **11%** of IMF votes.
G20 first leaders' summit: **Washington D.C., 2008**.

160.s: Which of the following correctly describes the share of the expanded BRICS grouping?
o: More than 40% of global GDP on a PPP basis and about 50% of the world's population
Exactly 46% of global trade and one-third of the world's population
About 85% of global GDP and more than 75% of global trade
About 20% of global GDP and 11% of the world's population
160.x: The expanded BRICS grouping accounts for more than 40% of global GDP on a PPP basis and approximately 50% of the world's population. The exact estimates vary by source.
160.tq: Distinguish BRICS indicators from the G20 figures and avoid an unsupported exact percentage.
xs: The expanded **BRICS** has **>40%** of global GDP (**PPP**) and ~**50%** of population — option **(1)**.
Another source gives **nearly 40%** of GDP and **55%** of population; **85%** GDP / **>75%** trade is the **G20**.
xa: ⚠ "BRICS = **46%** of global trade" was the **wrong** statement in UKPSC **2024**.
BRICS in **2011**: **20%** of GDP but **11%** of IMF votes.
BRICS has **10** members (+ **Saudi** ambiguous).

160.s: The G20 troika consists of:
o: The three largest economies of the G20
The current, previous and next presidencies
The G7, BRICS and European Union
The three permanent members of the G20 Secretariat
160.x: The G20 troika comprises the previous, current and next presidencies (B). In 2022 it was Italy (previous, 2021), Indonesia (current, 2022) and India (next, 2023). The G20 has no permanent secretariat, and the troika is not based on economic size or on G7/BRICS/EU.
160.tq: Resolve a terminology trap by identifying the institutional meaning of troika.
xs: The **G20 Troika** = **past, current and next presidencies** — option **(2)**.
In **2022** it was **Indonesia**, **Italy** and **India**.
The G20 has **no permanent secretariat or HQ**, so option 4 is wrong.
xa: India's presidency summit: **New Delhi, 9-10 Sep 2023**.
The presidency **rotates annually**.
**2025** G20: **Johannesburg, South Africa**.

160.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with India's 2023 G20 presidency?
o: Creation of a permanent G20 headquarters
Admission of the African Union as a permanent member
Launch of the Global Biofuels Alliance
160.x: India's presidency produced the New Delhi Declaration, admitted the African Union as a permanent member and launched the Global Biofuels Alliance. The G20 has no permanent headquarters.
160.tq: Find the institutional statement that conflicts with the G20's non-permanent structure.
xs: A **permanent G20 headquarters** was NOT created — option **(1)**; the G20 has **no permanent secretariat or HQ**.
The **New Delhi Declaration (2023)** admitted the **African Union** and launched the **Global Biofuels Alliance**.
xa: The G20 runs on an annual **rotating presidency** and a **Troika**.
⚠ Two **New Delhi Declarations**: G20 (**2023**) admitted AU; BRICS (**2026**) sought IMF/WB + UNSC reform.
Theme: "**Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam**".

161.s:
Match List I (Organisation) with List II (Headquarters) and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists:
List I (Organisation)
A. International Atomic Energy Agency
B. International Telecommunication Union
C. Council of the European Union
D. Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development
List II (Headquarters)
1. Brussels
2. Geneva
3. Paris
4. Vienna
161.x: The International Atomic Energy Agency is headquartered in Vienna, the International Telecommunication Union in Geneva, the Council of the European Union in Brussels, and the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development in Paris.

161.s: The Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG) was formed in 1975 in response to:
161.x: The NSG was formed in 1975, popularly known as the London Club, in response to India's 1974 Pokhran-I test.
161.tq: Match the organisation's origin with the triggering event.
xs: The **NSG** was formed in **1975** in response to India's **1974 Pokhran-I** test — option **(3)**.
It was popularly called the **"London Club"**.
The **CTBT** came later (**1996**) and North Korea's NPT exit was in **2003**, so neither could have triggered a 1975 body.
xa: The NSG is **voluntary, consensus-based**, with **no permanent secretariat** and **48 members**.
It controls **nuclear materials and technology**.
India got the **India-specific NSG waiver in 2008** (India-US Civil Nuclear Deal).
IAEA DG **Rafael Grossi** chaired the NSG in **2016**.

161.s:
Consider the following statements about the NSG:
1. It is voluntary and consensus-based.
2. It has a permanent secretariat.
3. It has 48 members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
161.x: The NSG is voluntary and consensus-based and has 48 members. Statement 2 is false because it has no permanent secretariat.
161.tq: Use the institutional-structure trap involving a permanent secretariat.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2) 1 and 3 only**.
Statement 1: The NSG is **voluntary and consensus-based** — correct.
Statement 2: It has **no permanent secretariat** — wrong.
Statement 3: It has **48 members** — correct.
xa: ⚠ **MTCR = 35** members (**500 kg / 300 km**); **Wassenaar = 42** (Vienna); **NSG = 48**.
The NSG ("**London Club**") was formed in **1975** after India's **1974 Pokhran-I**.
The NSG controls **nuclear materials and technology**.

161.s: The Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) is headquartered at:
161.x: The OPCW is headquartered at The Hague and implements the CWC.
161.tq: Use location-based elimination among the headquarters of treaty organisations.
xs: The **OPCW** is headquartered at **The Hague** — option **(3)**.
**Vienna** hosts the **IAEA**; **Paris (OECD)** hosts the **FATF** secretariat.
xa: The OPCW **implements the CWC**, **monitors the chemical industry** and inspects destruction.
Organs: **Conference of States Parties**, **Executive Council**, **Technical Secretariat**.
⚠ It is **not an EU body** (UPSC 2016); it won the **Nobel Peace Prize 2013**.

161.s: Which of the following is wrongly matched?
o: MTCR – 1987 – Missiles and drones (500 kg over 300 km)
161.x: The NSG (1975) controls nuclear materials and technology; missiles and drones fall under the MTCR (1987).
xa: ⚠ **MTCR = 35** members; **NSG = 48**; **Wassenaar = 42**, Vienna.
The **Australia Group** (**1985**) covers **chemical and biological weapon precursors**.
The **Hague Code of Conduct** (**2002**) deals with **ballistic missile proliferation** (transparency).

161.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Wassenaar Arrangement – Chemical and biological weapon precursors
Hague Code of Conduct – Transparency on ballistic-missile proliferation
Australia Group – Conventional arms and dual-use goods
161.x: The Hague Code of Conduct (2002) concerns ballistic-missile transparency; Wassenaar covers conventional arms and dual-use goods and the Australia Group covers chemical and biological precursors.
xa: Wassenaar sits at **Vienna** and has **42** members.
**MTCR** (**1987**, **35** members) controls missiles/drones — **500 kg over 300 km**.
**China + Pakistan** are outside Wassenaar and MTCR; **North Korea** is outside MTCR.

161.s: The NPT, which entered into force in 1970, was extended indefinitely in:
161.x: The NPT (signed 1968, in force 1970) was extended indefinitely in 1995.
xa: ⚠ UPSC 2015 trap: only **China** and **France** among the options were NPT nuclear-weapon states.
India calls the NPT **discriminatory ("nuclear apartheid")** and won't sign until nuclear powers accept a **time-bound disarmament plan**.
**North Korea** left the NPT in **2003**; Review Conferences are held **every 5 years**.
Criticism: the NPT lets recognised powers **modernise without disarmament deadlines**.

161.s: India's principal objection to the NPT is that it:
o: does not contain any provision on nuclear energy
is discriminatory and perpetuates nuclear apartheid
recognises India as a nuclear-weapon state without conditions
161.x: India rejects the NPT as discriminatory, describing its structure as nuclear apartheid. India also seeks a time-bound disarmament plan from the nuclear powers before signing.
161.tq: Identify the stated policy objection rather than a consequence of the treaty.
xs: India rejects the NPT as **discriminatory**, calling it **"nuclear apartheid"** — so option **(3)** is correct.
India won't sign until the nuclear powers accept a **time-bound disarmament plan**.
The NPT recognises only the **P5** as nuclear-weapon states, so it does not recognise India as one.
xa: India is also **not a signatory to the CTBT** and **did not sign the TPNW**.
⚠ India is a party to **PTBT, CWC, BWC, CCW**; not to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.
India is called a **"de facto responsible nuclear state"** — **NFU doctrine**, export controls, entry into **3 of 4 regimes**.
The **2008 NSG India-specific waiver** opened civil nuclear trade despite India staying outside the NPT.

161.s: India has not signed the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT) primarily because it:
o: lacks a time-bound disarmament commitment and permits subcritical tests
does not ban any form of nuclear explosion
161.x: India objects to the CTBT because it lacks a time-bound disarmament plan and still permits subcritical tests. The CTBT bans all nuclear explosions and was adopted in 1996.
161.tq: Separate India's objection to the treaty from the treaty's stated prohibition.
xs: India has not signed the **CTBT** because it has **no time-bound disarmament** and still **allows subcritical tests** — option **(1)**.
The CTBT (**1996**) **bans all nuclear explosions**, so option (3) is wrong; it is a nuclear, not chemical, treaty.
It says nothing about recognising nuclear-weapon states — that is the **NPT**, which recognises the **P5**.
xa: The CTBT is **not in force**.
The **PTBT (1963)** bans tests **except underground**; **India is a party** to it.
India **did not sign the TPNW** (in force **2021**) — it "adds nothing to customary law".
⚠ India is not a party to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.

161.s: India, which has not signed the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW), holds that the treaty:
o: Is backed by all nuclear-armed states
Adds nothing to customary international law
161.x: India did not sign the TPNW and has stated that it adds nothing to customary international law.
xa: The TPNW entered into force in **2021**.
⚠ India: party to **PTBT, CWC, BWC, CCW**; not to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.
India supports **FMCT** negotiation at the **Conference on Disarmament**.

161.s: The Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW) entered into force in:
161.x: The TPNW, a binding treaty banning nuclear weapons, entered into force in 2021.
xa: **India did not sign** the TPNW — it **adds nothing to customary law**.
The **CTBT** (**1996**) bans all nuclear explosions but is **not in force**.
**US + Russia** hold about **90%** of global arsenals.

161.s: India supports negotiation of the Fissile Material Cut-off Treaty (FMCT) at the:
161.x: India supports FMCT negotiations at the Conference on Disarmament, for a treaty that does not cap existing stocks.
xa: India's other FMCT conditions: **universal, verifiable, non-discriminatory**.
India **did not sign the TPNW** — it **adds nothing to customary law**.
India is **not a signatory to the CTBT** — no time-bound disarmament; subcritical tests still allowed.

161.s: India is party to how many of the protocols of the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW)?
161.x: The CCW deals with inhumane conventional weapons, and India is party to all five of its protocols.
xa: ⚠ India is a party to **PTBT, CWC, BWC, CCW**; not to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.
The **Wassenaar Arrangement** (**1996**) controls **conventional arms and dual-use goods**.
The **BWC** has **no verification organisation**; India is a party.

161.s: North Korea withdrew from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) in:
161.x: North Korea left the NPT in 2003.
161.tq: Recall the specific withdrawal year rather than a nearby nuclear-crisis date.
xs: **North Korea** left the **NPT** in **2003** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The NPT was signed in **1968**, came into force in **1970** and was extended indefinitely in **1995**.
xa: The NPT recognises only the **P5 — US, Russia, UK, France, China** as nuclear-weapon states.
**NPT Review Conferences** are held **every 5 years**; the consensus rule lets a single state block outcomes.
**North Korea** is also outside the **MTCR**.
**Iran's Parliament** weighed an **NPT exit** in **Mar 2026** after US-Israel strikes on its nuclear sites (**June 2025**).

161.s:
Consider the following statements about the JCPOA:
1. The United States withdrew from it in 2018.
2. Iran dropped all limits under it on 5 January 2020.
3. It was concluded in 2010.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
161.x: The United States withdrew in 2018 and Iran dropped all limits on 5 January 2020. Statement 3 is false because the JCPOA dates from 2015.
161.tq: Use the treaty's year and subsequent-status dates to reject a swapped date.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: The **US quit the JCPOA in 2018** — correct.
Statement 2: Iran **dropped all limits on 5 Jan 2020** — correct.
Statement 3: The JCPOA dates from **2015**, not **2010** (2010 is **New START**) — wrong.
xa: JCPOA parties: **Iran** with **P5+1** (US, UK, France, Russia, China, Germany) and the **EU**.
**June 2025:** US + Israel struck Iran's nuclear sites.
IAEA DG **Rafael Grossi** voiced worry over hits on Iran's nuclear sites (**Apr 2026**).

161.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. New START (2010) was a treaty between the USA and China.
2. The INF Treaty (1987) was concluded between the USA and the USSR, and the US withdrew from it in 2019.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
161.x: Statement 1 is wrong: New START was between the USA and Russia (Russia suspended it in 2023). Statement 2 is correct: INF (1987) was a USA-USSR treaty and the US withdrew in 2019. So 2 only (B); A, C and D misjudge one of the two.
161.tq: Both New START and INF are US-Russia/USSR bilateral treaties; China is party to neither.
xs: Only statement 2 is correct — option **(2) 2 only**.
Statement 1: **New START (2010)** was between the **USA and Russia**, not China — wrong.
Statement 2: The **INF Treaty (1987)** was **USA-USSR**, and the **US withdrew in 2019** — correct.
xa: Russia **suspended New START in 2023**; its expiry **removed all binding limits**.
New START's expiry is cited (**2026**) as a sign of **treaty erosion**.
**US + Russia** hold about **90%** of global nuclear arsenals.

161.s: The headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is located at:
161.x: The IAEA is headquartered in Vienna and was established in 1957.
161.tq: Separate the locations of the IAEA, FATF and OPCW.
xs: The **IAEA** is headquartered at **Vienna** — option **(2)**.
**The Hague** hosts the **OPCW**; **Paris (OECD)** hosts the **FATF** secretariat.
The IAEA was established in **1957** and verifies that civil nuclear material is **not diverted to weapons**.
xa: **India joined the IAEA in 1957** as a **founding member**.
⚠ **Vienna** is also the seat of the **Wassenaar Arrangement** (**1996**, **42** members).
IAEA DG **Rafael Grossi** voiced worry over hits on Iran's nuclear sites (**Apr 2026**); he chaired the **NSG in 2016**.

161.s: India joined the IAEA as a founding member in:
161.x: India joined the IAEA in 1957 as a founding member.
xa: ⚠ NSG waiver = **2008**; safeguards agreement = **2009**; **Additional Protocol** = **2014**.
The IAEA is headquartered at **Vienna**, established **1957**.
India-Canada uranium (**10,000 tonnes, 2027-2035**) is for PHWRs **under IAEA safeguards**.

161.s: India completed the destruction of its declared chemical-weapon stockpile under the CWC in:
161.x: India, a party to the CWC (in force 1997), completed destruction of its declared stockpile in 2009.
xa: The CWC is implemented by the **OPCW** at **The Hague** (Nobel Peace Prize **2013**).
The **BWC** (**1972**, in force **1975**) has **no verification organisation**; India is a party.
⚠ India: party to **PTBT, CWC, BWC, CCW**; not to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.

161.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the OPCW?
o: It implements the Chemical Weapons Convention
It inspects the destruction of chemical weapons
It is an institution of the European Union
It received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2013
161.x: The OPCW is not an EU body; it implements the CWC, monitors the chemical industry and won the 2013 Nobel Peace Prize.
xa: HQ: **The Hague**.
Organs: **Conference of States Parties**, **Executive Council**, **Technical Secretariat**.
The **CWC** was signed **1993**, in force **1997**; India finished destroying its stockpile in **2009**.

161.s: The Biological Weapons Convention, adopted in 1972 and to which India is a party, entered into force in:
161.x: The BWC was adopted in 1972, entered into force in 1975 and has no verification organisation.
xa: The **CWC** (signed **1993**, in force **1997**) is implemented by the **OPCW**.
⚠ India: party to **PTBT, CWC, BWC, CCW**; not to **NPT, CTBT, TPNW**.
The **Australia Group** (**1985**) controls **chemical and biological weapon precursors**.

161.s: The secretariat of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) is located at:
161.x: The FATF secretariat is at Paris (OECD); Vienna hosts the IAEA.
xa: FATF keeps a **grey list** (increased monitoring) and a **black list** (call for action).
India's **mutual evaluation** (adopted **June 2024**) → **"regular follow-up"**; India is also in the **APG**.
**Pakistan** was on the grey list **June 2018 to Oct 2022** for failing a **27-point action plan**.

161.s:
Assertion (A): Placement on the FATF grey list does not necessarily mean that a jurisdiction faces a call for action.
Reason (R): A call for action applies to the FATF black list of high-risk jurisdictions, while the grey list covers jurisdictions under increased monitoring.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
161.x: The grey list means increased monitoring; a call for action characterises the black list, which explains why grey-listing alone does not mean a call for action.
xa: **Pakistan** was grey-listed **June 2018 to Oct 2022** (failing a **27-point action plan** on terror financing).
**FATF** was set up in **1989** by the **G7**; secretariat at **Paris (OECD)**.
India's **June 2024** mutual evaluation placed it in **"regular follow-up"**.

161.s: India's Additional Protocol to its IAEA safeguards agreement came into force in:
161.x: India's Additional Protocol came into force in 2014.
xa: ⚠ Sequence: **NSG waiver 2008** → **safeguards agreement 2009** → **Additional Protocol 2014**.
The safeguards agreement covers **civilian facilities, excludes military**.
The **2008 waiver** stemmed from the **India-US Civil Nuclear Deal** → uranium/reactor imports.

161.s: The India-specific NSG waiver of 2008, associated with the India-US Civil Nuclear Deal, permits India to:
o: trade in civilian nuclear material and import uranium and reactors
join the NPT as a nuclear-weapon state
161.x: The 2008 waiver permits civil nuclear trade and the import of uranium and reactors by India. It does not make India an NPT member.
161.tq: Distinguish the practical effect of a waiver from formal membership in another treaty.
xs: The **2008 NSG waiver** lets India carry out **civil nuclear trade** and **import uranium and reactors** — option **(1)**.
It came through the **India-US Civil Nuclear Deal**; it does not make India an NPT member or give it a veto.
The NSG is **consensus-based**, so no member holds a special veto through the waiver.
xa: ⚠ NSG waiver = **2008**; safeguards agreement = **2009**; Additional Protocol = **2014**.
Uranium deals followed: **Canada (10,000 tonnes, 2027-2035)** and **Australia (July 2026)**.
The **India-Specific Safeguards Agreement** covers civilian facilities and **excludes military** ones.

161.s: Which of the following pairs (nuclear-weapon-free-zone treaty – region) is correctly matched?
161.x: Rarotonga covers the South Pacific; Tlatelolco covers Latin America, Bangkok Southeast Asia and Pelindaba Africa.
xa: The fifth NWFZ treaty, **Semipalatinsk**, covers **Central Asia**.
The **TPNW** (in force **2021**) is the first binding global ban on nuclear weapons.
⚠ **Pelindaba** (Africa) vs **Bangkok** (SE Asia) — easy swaps in matching questions.

161.s: Pakistan was kept on the FATF grey list from June 2018 to October 2022 mainly for failing to complete:
o: a 27-point action plan on terror financing

164.s:
With reference to Home Guards, consider the following statements:
1. Home Guards are raised under the Home Guards Act and Rules of the Central Government.
2. The role of the Home Guards is to serve as an auxiliary force to the police in maintenance of internal security.
3. To prevent infiltration on the international border/coastal areas, the Border Wing Home Guards Battalions have been raised in some States.
How many of the above statements are correct?
164.x: Statement 1 is incorrect: Home Guards are raised under the Home Guards Act and Rules of the States/Union Territories. They are recruited from amongst all classes of people and walks of life, who give their spare time to the organisation for betterment of the community. Amenities and facilities given to Home Guards include free uniform, duty allowances and award for gallantry, distinguished and meritorious services. Members of Home Guards with three years' service in the organisation are trained in policing, in maintenance of law and order, prevention of crime, anti-dacoity measures, border patrolling, prohibition, flood relief, fire-fighting, election duties and social welfare activities. Statement 2 is correct: The role of Home Guards is to serve as an auxiliary Force to the Police in maintenance of internal security situations, help the community in any kind of emergency such as an air-raid, fire, cyclone, earthquake, epidemic etc., help in maintenance of essential services, promote communal harmony and assist the administration in protecting weaker sections, participate in socio-economic and welfare activities and perform Civil Defence duties. Statement 3 is correct: Home Guards are of two types – rural and urban. In the border States, Border Wing Home Guards (BWHG) have been raised to serve as an auxiliary to the Border Security Force. The organisation is spread across all States and Union Territories except Kerala.

(b) Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) - Indo-China Border (c) Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) - Indo-Nepal and Indo-Bhutan (d) Assam Rifles - Indo-China and Indo-Myanmar Border.
